title: perf: btrfs_read_file scans ALL inode extents per read (O(extents)/read regardless of read size)
description: btrfs_read_file (ffs-core lib.rs ~7837, the COW/writable read path) ranged the inode's EXTENT_DATA items over [offset 0 .. u64::MAX] on EVERY read, cloning+parsing every extent of the inode even for a small read of a fragmented file -> O(extents) per read. The kernel seeks to the covering extent (btrfs_lookup_file_extent) instead. LEVER: cap the upper key at the read window end (offset+size); extents keyed at/after the window start after the last byte read and cannot overlap (the assembly loop already skips non-overlapping extents and the output buffer is pre-zeroed for holes), so the read result is identical. Lower bound stays 0 so the covering extent is always included. Isomorphic; ffs-core suite + bench subset-assert prove it. A/B bench (ffs-btrfs extent_fetch, 1024-extent file, 4KiB prefix read): 19.6us -> 123ns (159x). FOLLOW-ON: a floor/predecessor query on InMemoryCowBtrfsTree would also bound the LOWER edge (reads not near the file start), making it O(log+overlap) for all read positions.
notes: LOWER-BOUND COMPLETED (3372d7b6): added InMemoryCowBtrfsTree::floor_key (O(log N) predecessor descent, proven by floor_key_matches_bruteforce proptest) + btrfs_read_file now seeks the fetch lower bound to the covering extent. btrfs_read_file extent fetch is now O(log N + overlapping) at ALL read positions (upper bound c98b5291 + lower bound 3372d7b6). Bench: EOF-read 22.8us->188ns (121x). floor_key is also the primitive the rejected bd-4xeew needed.
close_reason: shipped c98b5291: btrfs_read_file COW read-path extent fetch bounded to the read window [offset, offset+size] instead of [0, MAX]; A/B bench 19.6us->123ns (159x, 1024-extent prefix read); isomorphic (1092 ffs-core tests green + bench subset-assert). title: btrfs RW: root_tree EXTENT_ITEMs not written to disk during commit
description:
## Problem

During btrfs commit, root_tree allocations happen AFTER extent_tree is serialized. This means:
- root_tree metadata blocks get EXTENT_ITEMs inserted into extent_tree in memory
- But these EXTENT_ITEMs never reach disk because extent_tree was already written

## Impact

- Mounted-FUSE durability is correct (resolver doesn't depend on extent_tree consistency)
- `btrfs check` flags root_tree tree blocks as missing EXTENT_ITEMs
- Not a data loss issue, but structural inconsistency

## Potential Fixes

1. Iterate commit to quiescence (like kernel btrfs does)
2. Reserve maximum upper bound for root_tree allocations and write extent_tree last
3. Accept the inconsistency as acceptable for V1

## Notes

Earlier attempt to reorder root_tree allocation before extent_tree serialization
regressed durability because EXTENT_TREE ROOT_ITEM patch CoW'd root_tree and
invalidated the pre-computed root_tree allocation map.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `btrfs check --readonly` on FFS-written images shows no root_tree EXTENT_ITEM errors
- [ ] OR document as acceptable V1 gap with clear guidance

title: perf(btrfs): binary-search InMemoryCowBtrfsTree descent (child_slot + leaf find)
description: InMemoryCowBtrfsTree (production btrfs COW write tree: fs_tree/root_tree/csum_tree/extent_tree, ffs-core 5984/6009/6163) descends internal nodes via child_slot which linear-scans up to max_items keys (=(nodesize-101)/25 ~= 651 for 16KB nodesize) with .iter().position; find_in's leaf arm linear .iter().find over up to ~651 sorted items. Both keys and leaf items are sorted (insert uses partition_point @3389). child_slot is called by find_in + insert_into + delete_from (every COW op, per descent level). Replace with partition_point (correct predicate: key_cmp(key,sep) != Less) and binary_search_by -> O(log N) per node. Isomorphic on sorted unique keys.
close_reason: Shipped 797937db: binary-search InMemoryCowBtrfsTree descent. child_slot O(N)->O(log N) via partition_point (correct predicate key_cmp(key,sep)!=Less; Explore's was inverted), find_in leaf via binary_search_by. N up to ~651 (16KB nodesize); called per descent on every COW find/insert/delete. A/B (N=651): child_slot 2.79us->418ns=6.7x, leaf find 7.87us->255ns=30.9x. Isomorphic (sorted unique keys; bench asserts old==new); 344 ffs-btrfs tests green, clippy clean.

title: [parity][corruption] ext4 encrypted-file read returns ciphertext and write stores plaintext into encrypted blocks
description: EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_ENCRYPT is in Ext4IncompatFeatures::ALLOWED_V1, so FrankenFS mounts encrypted (fscrypt) filesystems. FrankenFS has NO fscrypt support (no key handling, no AES-XTS), yet the regular file read path (FsOps::read, lib.rs:20561) and ext4_write (12681) never check inode.is_encrypted() (EXT4_ENCRYPT_INODE_FL): read() falls through after the is_dir/is_symlink/COMPRBLK/inline checks and returns the raw on-disk bytes = CIPHERTEXT presented as plaintext (wrong data); ext4_write writes the caller's PLAINTEXT directly into the encrypted file's data blocks, so when the real kernel later reads with the fscrypt key it decrypts that plaintext into garbage = silent DATA CORRUPTION of the encrypted file. is_encrypted() IS guarded in move_ext (20073) and symlink-read (20629) but NOT on the main read/write/fallocate paths. A real kernel without the encryption key returns ENOKEY on open/read/write; FrankenFS instead silently returns ciphertext / corrupts. Same accepted-at-mount-but-unhandled class as bd-4y9ca (inline_data). Reachable on any encrypt-enabled image with an encrypted file. FIX: an ext4_reject_encrypted(inode) guard on read, ext4_write, and ext4_fallocate returning UnsupportedFeature (FrankenFS cannot decrypt, so erroring is the only safe + parity-defensible behavior, matching a keyless kernel). PROOF: set EXT4_ENCRYPT_INODE_FL on a file inode (persist_ext4_inode_for_testing) and assert read/write/fallocate return UnsupportedFeature rather than ciphertext/plaintext-corruption.
close_reason: Fixed in add38979. ext4_reject_encrypted guards read/ext4_write/ext4_fallocate -> UnsupportedFeature for any EXT4_ENCRYPT_INODE_FL inode, instead of returning raw ciphertext-as-plaintext (read) or storing plaintext into encrypted blocks = corruption (write). FrankenFS has no fscrypt key/AES-XTS, so erroring is the only safe + parity-defensible behavior (a keyless kernel returns ENOKEY). Same accepted-at-mount-but-unhandled class as bd-4y9ca (inline_data). Test encrypted_file_content_io_fails_loudly_bd_4sfty. ffs-core 907/907, clippy/fmt clean. Full fscrypt support (AES-XTS + key mgmt) would be the parity-complete enhancement but is out of scope; erroring is correct for a no-key implementation.

title: perf(methodology): the admission contract bounds within-invocation error only — cross-window reproducibility is 9.15% measured, 3x the margin, and lands on the incumbent arm
description:
Every banked mounted-comparator row is published with a within-invocation bootstrap median
95% CI, typically +/-0.5% to +/-1%, and admitted against a twice-widest-null margin of
about 1.01x-1.05x. Both quantities describe error INSIDE one invocation. Neither says
anything about whether the same ELF, on the same host and kernel, re-measures to the same
ratio in the next window -- and that is the number every reader actually uses when they
compare a row to a later run or to another row.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED (bd-2i2ez step 1, 2026-08-06): bulk durable write reproduces to
9.15% across two windows. Two 2,048-pair runs of the IDENTICAL candidate ELF bcf2bc80...,
PGO 5c6530a0..., kernel 6.17.0-41-generic, performance/performance governor, both admitted
HONEST_LOSS under the same contract, measured 2.898298x [2.874382, 2.920502] and 2.655365x
[2.641224, 2.672899]. The intervals do not overlap and the gap is about 3x that row's own
1.035235x admission margin.

The mechanism is on the INCUMBENT side and is the part that generalizes. Across four runs
of that one ELF, FrankenFS held 232.11 / 225.22 / 225.31 / 222.39 ms while the kernel ext4
arm held 77.05 / 77.31 / 78.42 ms and then moved to 83.69 ms. Between the two admitted
runs our arm moved -1.30% and the incumbent moved +8.26%. A ratio row is a quotient, so
incumbent volatility lands in the published number even when our own cost is stable -- and
the A/A nulls cannot see it, because both nulls are taken inside the same invocation as the
ratio and are blind to what the host does between invocations.

CONSEQUENCE: at least six of the eight scorecard rows have never had cross-window spread
characterized at all. The only two figures that exist are 4.71% (another workload, cited in
bd-2i2ez) and 9.15% (this one). Until a row has a second same-ELF run, its published
interval is a lower bound on its true uncertainty and must not be used to call a later
measurement a regression, an improvement, or a disagreement.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS
1. For each admitted ext4 row, a second same-ELF, same-kernel run in a distinct window;
   publish the observed spread beside the CI. Bulk durable write already has its pair.
2. State the rule in the scorecard admission text: a row's quotable precision is
   max(its own CI, its measured cross-window spread), and a row with no second run is
   quoted to the campaign's worst observed spread until it has one.
3. Record the incumbent arm's ABSOLUTE median in every ledger row, not only the ratio. The
   2026-07-31 bulk-durable row could not be diagnosed from its own ledger entry because
   only the ratio was transcribed and the report has since been deleted (bd-v0igv); had the
   kernel-arm median been in the row, step 1 would have been arithmetic instead of a rerun.

Item 3 is cheap, applies to every future row, and is the one that stops this class of
question from recurring. Item 1 is the expensive one and should be spent on the rows that
carry campaign decisions first.

comments.author: PlumRiver
comments.text:
The harness's own quiet-window gate does not bound this, and that is worth stating
explicitly because it is the obvious first thing a reader will reach for.

Both admitted runs printed `core_contention_preflight,...,verdict=clear` with
`driver_busy_fraction=0.000000` and `fuse_busy_fractions=0.000000`, five consecutive clear
host-wide samples required and met, `host_quiet_timeout_ms=300000`. The 21:46 run cleared
the gate and measured a 77.31 ms kernel arm; the 22:57 run cleared the same gate and
measured 83.69 ms. So an 8.26% move in the incumbent passed a gate designed to certify the
window was quiet.

That is not a defect in the gate. The gate samples CPU busy fractions on the placement CPUs
immediately before the run; it cannot see page-cache state, writeback backlog on the backing
device, thermal/boost history, or anything else that carries across invocation boundaries.
It certifies "no competing load on these CPUs right now", which is a strictly weaker claim
than "this window will reproduce the last one".

The practical consequence for the retry predicate: do not treat `verdict=clear` as evidence
that a new run is comparable to a banked one. The only thing that establishes comparability
between windows is a second measurement of the same ELF, which is what item 1 of this bead
asks for.

comments.author: PlumRiver
comments.text:
PROMOTED TO A GENERAL RULE AND PUBLISHED (PlumRiver, 2026-08-06, 1ea814fa). Both scorecards now
carry it as a header, not a per-row caveat, because it is not specific to bulk durable write and
not specific to this repo.

THE RULE AS PUBLISHED:
`core_contention_preflight ... verdict=clear` certifies that no competing load sat on the
placement CPUs at the moment sampling started. It is NOT evidence that a run is comparable to a
previously BANKED one, and must never be cited as if it were.

THE MEASUREMENT BEHIND IT, which is what makes it a rule rather than an opinion: two 2,048-pair
runs of the IDENTICAL candidate ELF, PGO profile, kernel and governor both printed verdict=clear
with five consecutive clear samples and driver_busy_fraction=0.000000. The incumbent arm still
moved 8.26% between them (77.31 ms -> 83.69 ms), carrying the published ratio from 2.898298x to
2.655365x: a 9.15% swing, non-overlapping intervals, roughly 3x the row's own 1.035235x admission
margin. FrankenFS's own arm moved -1.30%. The entire difference was the incumbent.

WHY THE GATE CANNOT SEE IT, which is the part that generalises: it samples CPU busy fractions on
the placement CPUs immediately before the run. It is structurally blind to page-cache state,
writeback backlog on the backing device, thermal and boost history, and everything else that
carries ACROSS invocation boundaries. No amount of tightening the sample count fixes that; five
clear samples were already required and observed.

CONSEQUENCE, applying to every banked row in every repo:
- A/A nulls and the twice-null margin bound WITHIN-invocation error only.
- Cross-window reproducibility is a separate, UNMEASURED quantity unless a second same-ELF run
  exists. Only two figures exist so far: 4.71% on one workload, 9.15% on bulk durable write.
- A later measurement disagreeing with a banked row by less than that is NOT a regression, an
  improvement, or a disagreement. It is unresolved.
- Quote a row to its measured cross-window spread where one exists, and to the campaign's worst
  observed spread where none does — never to its own CI.

ALSO LANDED IN THE SAME COMMIT, because it is the same class of problem (a number that no longer
describes the thing it names): both scorecards now state that NO row in them describes FrankenFS
at HEAD. Every row was measured on an ELF predating the current tree — the bank on f44b3dc4, warm
stat on 9e32e28f, xattr and bulk durable on bcf2bc80, verified against each file's own provenance
sections — and three btrfs correctness commits have landed since the newest of them, one of which
(7fac4779) removes a read and an allocation from every overwrite-split and so can move the numbers
in either direction.

STILL OPEN ON THIS BEAD: items 1 and 3 of its own plan. Item 3 — record the incumbent arm's
ABSOLUTE median in every ledger row, not just the ratio — remains the cheapest thing here and the
one that would have made bd-2i2ez step 1 arithmetic instead of a rerun. Item 1, a second same-ELF
run per admitted row, is the expensive one and should be spent on rows that carry campaign
decisions first. Neither is done.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ITEM 3 IS DONE (2026-08-08). Item 2 was already published as scorecard headers; item 1 (a second same-ELF run per admitted row) is untouched and remains the expensive half. This bead stays OPEN for item 1 only.

WHAT LANDED
1. Both scorecards now carry an "Absolute arm medians - REQUIRED per row, never a gate" section covering EVERY row, replacing the ext4 file's optional "Diagnostic side numbers" framing. Not a gate (gate_input=false unchanged), but a required record - a different obligation.
2. scripts/perf_ledger_preflight.py enforces it. A row whose incumbent_denominator() is live_same_invocation must record an absolute median for BOTH arms, via the harness fields (kernel_median_wall_ns / fuse_median_wall_ns) or prose naming each arm with a duration. New Row.missing_absolute_arm_medians() + a contract_violations() entry, so it fires in --lint --staged (the pre-commit path). 7 new self-test cases, 32/32 pass. Deliberately exempts internal A/B rows: they have no incumbent arm to separate.
3. Backfilled what was recoverable and MARKED what was not, rather than leaving gaps silent. ext4: 7 of 8 rows complete (warm stat 4.42/21.30 ms and bulk durable write 77.31/225.31 ms moved into the table). btrfs: 2 of 6 complete.

WHAT IS PERMANENTLY LOST - the concrete cost of not having had this rule
- ext4 xattr get/list (5.749816x) and FOUR of the six btrfs rows have NO absolute median for either arm, in the tree or in any surviving log. Their reports were deleted with the comparator scratch (bd-v0igv). Those ratios are now un-decomposable into "our cost" vs "the incumbent's cost" until re-run. Worst-placed is the btrfs parallel-read row - the campaign's only honest_win - exactly the row where a reader asks "did we get faster or did the incumbent get slower?".
- The btrfs scorecard's Provenance section claimed "Reports retained at /data/tmp/frankenfs-mounted-btrfs/run_*/mounted-kernel-report.json". That claim was FALSE as of 2026-08-08: the path does not exist and a /data/tmp-wide search finds exactly ONE surviving mounted-kernel-report.json anywhere, belonging to an unrelated bd-2i2ez ext4 window. Corrected in place. Relevant to bd-v0igv: the cleanup has already eaten the reports once.

NEW EVIDENCE recovered from the one surviving log, which STRENGTHENS this bead's thesis
A fifth run of the bulk-durable-write shape exists in /data/tmp/frankenfs-bd2i2ez/w1.log: same workload shape (64 ops/observation, 2048 pairs, 512 crossover blocks), same kernel 6.17.0-41-generic, same performance/performance, verdict=clear with driver_busy_fraction=0.000000 and fuse_busy_fractions=0.000000, admitted HONEST_LOSS. Kernel arm 91.43 ms, FrankenFS arm 222.22 ms, ratio 2.430234x.

Read half of that and not the other half. Its candidate ELF is d34b21c0..., NOT bcf2bc80..., so its RATIO is not a same-ELF replicate and must NOT be folded into the 9.15% figure - that number still rests on the two bcf2bc80 runs alone. But the kernel arm does not execute our binary, so its absolute median IS a legitimate third observation of the incumbent: 77.31 -> 83.69 -> 91.43 ms, a monotone +18.3% across three gate-clear windows on one kernel, while our arm sat at 225.31 / 222.39 / 222.22 ms and agreed to 1.4%. Named confound: the arms run interleaved in the crossover, so a different candidate could in principle change the interference the kernel arm sees - but our arm measured 222.22 ms here, inside the banked 222-232 ms band, so the co-load was comparable.

So the incumbent-side drift is roughly TWICE what this bead was filed with, and recorded absolute medians are what made it visible. That is the argument for item 3 stated in its own evidence.

SIDE EFFECT ON THE WHOLE-LEDGER CENSUS: --lint now reports 925 violations where it reported 911, the 14 new ones being exactly the live-same-invocation competitive rows that banked only a ratio. Whole-ledger --lint already exited 2 before this change; unchanged. --lint --staged is clean on this commit.

Two admitted, same-ELF, same-kernel, same-governor runs of ext4 `readdir-stat-8t` at the banked shape (operations=32768, pairs=32, repeats=3), candidate `913c36a4…`, PGO `b30de364…`, both `verdict=clear`, both `HONEST_LOSS`:

| 1 | `4.052605x` | [4.034231, 4.108783] | 28.976 ms | 117.003 ms | `1.032372x` |
| 2 | `4.163402x` | [4.106308, 4.196759] | 27.991 ms | 115.616 ms | `1.038028x` |

    spread            2.73%
    run 1 CI width    1.84%
    run 2 CI width    2.17%
    intervals overlap by a sliver (4.106308 < 4.108783)

THIS IS THE BEAD'S THESIS, REPRODUCED ON A THIRD WORKLOAD. The spread (2.73%) EXCEEDS run 1's own within-invocation CI width (1.84%) and is comparable to its twice-null admission margin (3.24%). Anyone who had quoted run 1 to its own CI would have called run 2 a disagreement. It is not; it is the same row.

AND THE VARIANCE LANDS ON THE INCUMBENT AGAIN, which is the part that generalises. Between the two runs the kernel arm moved −3.40% while FrankenFS moved −1.19%. That is now three independent observations of the same asymmetry: bulk durable write (+8.26% incumbent vs −1.30% ours), the +18.3% incumbent-only climb across three windows, and now readdir+stat. The campaign's ratio noise is predominantly the incumbent's, not ours.

HONEST LIMIT, stated because it changes how this figure may be used: these two runs were BACK TO BACK in one session, so they share thermal history, page-cache state and boost history. 2.73% is therefore a LOWER BOUND on this row's true cross-window spread, not a measurement of it. It does not retire item 1 for this row — a genuinely distinct window would — but it is strictly more than any row had before, and it is enough to forbid quoting the row to its own CI.

PUBLISHED: docs/MOUNTED_KERNEL_SCORECARD.md now carries the row as ≈`4.1x` with both runs, both margins, both A/A pairs and both arms' absolute medians, and states "quote the 2.73% spread, not either CI". The header rule is updated from "only two same-ELF figures exist" (4.71%, 9.15%) to three.

FOR THE REST OF ITEM 1: the six remaining ext4 rows still have no second run, and for five of them a same-ELF repeat is now IMPOSSIBLE — their candidate ELFs (`f44b3dc4…`, `9e32e28f…`, `bcf2bc80…`) and the banked PGO profile `5c6530a0…` were destroyed with the comparator scratch (bd-v0igv). Item 1 as literally written ("a second same-ELF run") cannot be satisfied for them. The achievable version is: re-measure on a CURRENT ELF, twice, and bank the pair — which is exactly what readdir+stat just did, and what bd-plkzd/bd-c5210/bd-o6iiw will each produce as they land.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CORRECTED GATE VERIFIED TO DISCRIMINATE — including by refusing me a third time, correctly.

    negative test (synthetic sustained)   23/23 = 100.0%   REFUSED  (correct)
    warm-stat run A                        8/67 =  11.9%   REFUSED  (correct — over the 10% limit,
                                                            max_consecutive=2, so the FRACTION rule fired)
    warm-stat run 1                        2/71 =   2.8%   would now PASS (unit-tested)
    warm-stat run 2                        1/70 =   1.4%   would now PASS (unit-tested)

So the policy separates cleanly across four real datasets spanning 1.4% to 100%, and the two rules do different work: run A tripped the fraction rule with `max_consecutive_over_limit=2`, under the consecutive limit of 3, which is exactly the case the fraction rule exists for.

I did NOT relax the threshold again to make run A pass. The box was genuinely busier (load ~4.1 versus ~0.4 in the earlier quiet window, my own rebuilds plus peers), so refusing was right.

⭐ AN OBSERVATION THAT ARGUES AGAINST ONE GLOBAL THRESHOLD, recorded rather than acted on. Across the three warm-stat attempts the ratios barely moved despite contention varying 8x:

    run              contended    ext4        btrfs
    r1                    2.8%    4.878463    4.812203
    r2                    1.4%    4.880928    4.789771
    rA                   11.9%    4.859600    4.812585
    spread across all three:      0.44%       0.48%

Warm stat is ~1-thread, ~4.5 ms kernel / ~22 ms FUSE per batch, and its ratio is dominated by per-request FUSE round-trip cost. It looks robust to socket-level contention at this magnitude. Parallel read, by contrast, FLIPPED VERDICT under comparable load (bd-ws9dg).

CONCLUSION, and the reason not to touch the threshold: contention sensitivity is WORKLOAD-DEPENDENT, so any single global limit is necessarily conservative for robust workloads and possibly still permissive for sensitive ones. The correct response is not to loosen the global limit for warm stat's benefit — it is to accept that a robust workload will occasionally be refused on a busy box, because the same limit is what protects the sensitive ones. A per-workload sensitivity calibration would be the principled alternative, and it is not something to invent from three data points.

NOT DELIVERED THIS TURN: bd-4sull item 1 for warm stat. Three attempts, all refused, none bankable. The numbers above are recorded ONLY as evidence about the gate's behaviour and the workload's robustness — they are from refused runs and must not be quoted as rows or used to supersede the banked ext4 4.812194x / btrfs 4.977803x. Re-run when the box is genuinely idle.

the control that would let anyone act on that. (DarkMeadow, 2026-08-14.)

WHY THIS EXISTS. Every mounted row attempted on this host today was refused by
`external_load_during_run` (>2 off-placement CPUs above 25% busy for >10% of samples), while the
estimator's OWN A/A nulls came out clear each time. That gate is an absolute quietness precondition
layered on a design that is already a balanced crossover, so whether it protects the verdict is an
empirical question rather than a matter of principle. This measures it.

METHOD: five runs of the IDENTICAL workload and ELF (ext4, large_directory_readdir_stat_8t, 32,768
entries, pairs=12, 8 observed client threads, candidate a53bfa88…, x86-64-v3, PGO 6a22cfcf…,
BUILT_IN_PLACE, host thinkstation1, kernel 6.17.0-41-generic), taken back to back while the box's
foreign load varied on its own. Each run records its own load metrics, so the x-axis is measured
rather than assumed.

    run  ratio      max_busy_cpus  peak_off_placement_busy  kernel ms  FUSE ms
     1   3.941912        20              25.6%               32.36     126.19
     2   3.882481        29              35.7%               32.53     127.29
     3   3.866605        44              37.1%               31.76     122.58
     4   4.116410        17              23.7%               31.64     128.50
     5   3.870034         9              16.4%               31.34     120.46

RESULT:
  * external load varied 4.9x (9 -> 44 busy CPUs; peak off-placement mean busy 16.4% -> 37.1%)
  * ratio median 3.882481, range 3.866605-4.116410 = 6.46% spread
  * Pearson r(busy_cpus, ratio) = -0.35 — weak, and the WRONG SIGN: more load, slightly LOWER
    ratio. If socket contention were biasing the FUSE arm the correlation would be strongly positive.
  * the two EXTREME-load runs, 44 busy CPUs and 9 busy CPUs, differ by 0.09%
  * per arm: r(busy, kernel arm) = +0.32, r(busy, FUSE arm) = +0.01. Neither arm tracks load, and
    the arm that moves most (FUSE, 6.67% spread vs kernel's 3.81%) is the one NOT correlated with it.

⚠ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH, and it is the reason I am not proposing a gate change on it.
`contended_fraction` was 1.0000 in ALL FIVE runs — by the gate's own definition every one of them
was fully contended. So this series compares CONTENDED against CONTENDED and contains no quiet
anchor. It refutes "the ratio degrades progressively with load across the contended range"; it
cannot refute "contended runs differ systematically from quiet ones", which is what the veto
actually asserts. n=5 with no repeats at fixed load is also weak: r=-0.35 at n=5 is not significant.

WHAT WOULD FINISH IT: the same five runs plus at least two taken in a genuinely quiet window
(contended_fraction near 0), so the contended cluster can be compared against a clean anchor. If the
quiet runs land inside the contended cluster's spread, the veto is discarding rows whose verdict
does not depend on what it measures, and the integrity check is already favourable — every row it
vetoes for these workloads is an HONEST_LOSS, so admitting them cannot manufacture a win. If the
quiet runs sit outside, the veto is vindicated and that should be written into the scorecard as a
measured fact rather than an assumption.

SECONDARY OBSERVATION, relevant to this bead's own subject. The 6.46% spread across five same-ELF
runs is larger than the 1.36% cross-window spread the btrfs scorecard tells readers to quote (though
these are pairs=12 against the bank's 32, so wider intervals are expected). It is another instance
of the bd-4sull rule: a row's quotable precision is max(its own CI, its measured spread), and five
runs of one ELF in one hour already exceed what a single run's CI would have implied.

title: btrfs BTRFS_IOC_DEFRAG_RANGE ioctl support
description:
## Summary

Implement `BTRFS_IOC_DEFRAG_RANGE` ioctl for file defragmentation.

Used by `btrfs filesystem defragment` to defragment file extents.

## Kernel reference

- `fs/btrfs/ioctl.c: btrfs_ioctl_defrag()`
- `BTRFS_IOC_DEFRAG_RANGE` = `_IOW(0x94, 16, struct btrfs_ioctl_defrag_range_args)`

## Implementation scope

1. Add ioctl constant and dispatch in ffs-fuse
2. Add trait method in ffs-core/vfs.rs
3. Implement defrag logic or return EOPNOTSUPP for read-only mounts

## Notes

For V1 read-only mode, returning EROFS is acceptable. For RW mode with
`--btrfs-rw-ephemeral-ok`, actual defrag would require extent tree manipulation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit tests for argument validation
- EOPNOTSUPP or EROFS returned appropriately
close_reason: done

title: ext4 FC recovery: free a zero-link inode + blocks on link-count-to-zero (follow-on to bd-w6fxn)
description: Follow-on to bd-w6fxn (all 4 FC dir-ops CREAT/LINK/UNLINK/DEL_RANGE now apply, see 531ae295). REMAINING GAP: when an UNLINK drops a file's last link, recovery removes the dir entry and the accompanying InodeUpdate writes links_count=0, but the inode slot + data blocks are NOT released, so e2fsck reports a zero-link in-use inode (repairable leak, NOT corruption/data-loss; namespace is correct). PRIMITIVE EXISTS: ffs_inode::delete_inode(cx,block_dev,geo,groups,ino,inode,csum_seed,tstamp_secs,pctx) — used by ext4 orphan recovery (lib.rs ~3467 deleted action) to release inode bitmap + all blocks. PLAN: in apply_fast_commit_inode_update, when the FC raw inode has links_count==0, load_ext4_alloc_state + parse to Ext4Inode + delete_inode (react to FC-recorded links==0, do NOT compute a delta, to avoid rename-half corruption). UNCERTAINTY: confirm ext4 fast-commit emits an INODE tag with links=0 for a freed inode vs falling back to full JBD2 commit. Validate via e2fsck on a single-link create+write+remove FC recovery. Also defer-noted: DEL_RANGE on depth>0/legacy-indirect inodes, mid-file punch growing a full inline root (i_blocks off-by-one metadata), htree leaf-full CREAT (split needs alloc).
close_reason: done

title: perf(btrfs): compressed random read 48x slower than kernel — needs a decompressed-extent cache (kernel caches decompressed pages)
description: MEASURED (CrimsonFox cc/opus 2026-06-22, binary-only warm HEAD 9dbdb38e, btrc:/c.bin 10k x 4KiB 16t): COMPRESSED btrfs random read = frankenfs 321 MiB/s vs kernel-loop 15485 MiB/s = ~48x SLOWER, byte-identical (0c981e24). LARGEST warm read loss in the scorecard (far worse than the ~2x copy tax on uncompressed). ROOT CAUSE: the kernel page-cache caches DECOMPRESSED pages, so a warm compressed random read is a page-cache hit (15 GB/s, no decompression); frankenfs RE-DECOMPRESSES the whole 128 KiB compressed extent on every 4 KiB random read (zstd can't partial-decompress -> 32x amplification + zstd CPU per read), with no decompressed-extent cache. The btrfs read path (ffs-core lib.rs:9047) DELIBERATELY drops each decompressed Vec to bound memory on large compressed sequential reads. FIX = a bounded-LRU decompressed-extent cache keyed by extent disk_bytenr -> Arc<[u8]> (the decompressed bytes), gated read-only, so repeated 4 KiB random reads of the same 128 KiB extent skip re-decompression. TRADEOFF/risk: re-introduces retained decompressed Vecs the current design avoids -> must be a bounded LRU sized to capture random-read locality WITHOUT bloating the sequential-compressed path; byte-identity across zstd/zlib/lzo codecs; inside the parallel decompress job (thread-safe). Deep-swing, needs disk headroom to build+conformance-gate (currently DISK-constrained, no builds). Uncompressed btrfs random read is already at ~ext4 parity (b4b9f331), so this is decompression-specific. Reproduce: ffs-cli rand-read <compressed-btrfs-img> /c.bin --count 10000 --size 4096 --parallel vs the loop-mounted file. Real workload: a database on compressed btrfs.
notes: SHIPPED RO decompressed-extent cache (btrfs_decompressed_extent_cache, ShardedCache<disk_bytenr,Arc<[u8]>>, bounded 4096/env FFS_BTRFS_DECOMP_CACHE_ENTRIES, gated btrfs_alloc_state.is_none(), partial-slice path only so sequential .413 path keeps bounded mem). Clean env-toggle A/B on 50MiB zstd:3 comp.bin: SINGLE-THREAD 520->800 MiB/s =1.55x, narrows vs-kernel gap 3.15x->2.05x (residual=universal userspace copy-tax). PARALLEL 64t median-NEUTRAL (1634 vs 1604; raises worst floor 1165 vs 557) — parallel compressed-read wall is rayon/per-read COORDINATION not decompression (~11x vs kernel 17GB/s, cache-insensitive; separate lever, .414 family). Byte-identical (unit test btrfs_ro_decompressed_extent_cache_hit_matches_miss_bd_4tw2n + sha256==kernel). Headline '48x' was a parallel measurement on a different fixture; decompression is only the single-thread component.
close_reason: Decompressed-extent cache implemented + shipped (single-thread 1.55x, byte-identical, RO-gated, bounded). Parallel residual is coordination-bound (separate .414-family lever), not decompression.

title: Epic: evidence promotion control plane hardening
description:
Idea-wizard Phase 2/3 selected theme: FrankenFS has extensive feature and readiness machinery, but the remaining user risk is evidence promotion rather than another filesystem primitive. The project must make it hard for agents, docs, release gates, or operator handoff packets to mistake local smoke, stale artifacts, tracker pollution, or RCH artifact-retrieval quirks for authoritative readiness evidence.

This epic turns that theme into a self-contained control-plane backlog. It deliberately complements, rather than duplicates, the existing tracker hygiene epic bd-cj0bo and the permissioned execution beads bd-rchk3.3 / bd-rchk0.53.8.

The intended outcome is an operator and agent workflow where: remote cargo evidence is fail-closed and centrally enforced; proof-bundle lanes carry provenance strong enough to distinguish dry-run handoff from executed product evidence; xfstests failures can be minimized into durable sparse fixtures and narrow beads; docs wording is compiled or checked from release-gate state; and future agent swarms can choose safe work without inflating readiness claims.

Every child bead must include focused unit tests, an E2E/logging path where practical, artifact-schema checks, and explicit release-gate or proof-bundle consumers. Do not execute permissioned xfstests or large-host campaigns in this epic; those remain blocked on their existing acknowledgement boundaries.
close_reason: Completed: all evidence promotion control-plane child beads bd-4v16z.1 through bd-4v16z.10 are closed with proof-bundle, readiness-dashboard, permissioned campaign, artifact index, redaction, RCH, and large-host calibration coverage in place.

title: Standardize direct-RCH capture helper and accepted-marker guardrail
description:
Problem: many E2E scripts grew copy-pasted RCH wrappers. Recent hardening removed the most misleading accepted-marker paths, but duplicated helper logic makes regressions likely and makes future agents patch scripts one by one.

Scope: design and implement a shared direct-RCH capture contract for scripts/e2e. The contract must reject local fallback and non-compilation wrapper output, require remote success evidence before returning success, preserve command-tagged stopped-after-remote-exit evidence when artifact retrieval is intentionally terminated after remote exit=0, and ban any RCH_ARTIFACT_RETRIEVAL_*ACCEPTED marker.

Implementation guidance: prefer extending scripts/e2e/lib.sh or a similarly established helper if it already owns E2E primitives; migrate a representative subset first, then expand mechanically but manually in narrow reviewed patches. Do not introduce hidden local cargo execution. Keep each migrated script behavior-isomorphic aside from marker wording and fail-closed checks.

Acceptance: unit or harness tests scan every scripts/e2e/*.sh helper for accepted markers, local fallback acceptance, and missing remote evidence; fixture tests exercise remote exit=0 plus artifact retrieval stop, remote nonzero, timeout without remote exit, local fallback, and non-compilation wrapper output; an E2E smoke proves at least three migrated scripts still pass through RCH; ubs and bash -n run on touched scripts; docs in scripts/e2e/README.md explain the canonical helper contract for future agents.
close_reason: Implemented canonical fail-closed e2e_rch_capture helper in scripts/e2e/lib.sh, migrated invariant_oracle/OQ/verification_runner E2E scripts to delegate to it, documented the contract, and added ffs-harness guardrail tests. Validation: bash -n touched scripts; git diff --check touched files; cargo fmt --check -p ffs-harness; rg accepted-marker scan clean; RCH remote exit=0 for cargo test -p ffs-harness rch_capture -- --nocapture (3 passed, local wrapper timed out only during .rch-target artifact retrieval); UBS only reports pre-existing e2e.rs inventory findings outside this slice.

title: Build operator readiness dashboard over proof and evidence state
description:
Problem: operators and agents have to inspect many JSON reports to answer a simple question: what evidence is current, what claims are blocked, and what command should be run next? A compact dashboard would make the control plane understandable without weakening the underlying strict validators.

Scope: add a read-only CLI/TUI summary over proof-bundle validation, release-gate output, artifact index, permissioned campaign packets, and tracker follow-up beads. It should show claim state, controlling lane, freshness, host class, missing artifacts, remediation bead, and next safe command. It must never infer readiness outside validator outputs.

Acceptance: unit tests cover rendering for all claim states and missing-data combinations; an E2E fixture renders JSON and terminal/Markdown output from synthetic proof reports; the dashboard links every recommendation to a validator report or bead id; operator docs make clear that this is a display layer over strict validators, not a separate source of truth.
close_reason: Completed: added read-only readiness-dashboard CLI over proof-bundle, release-gate, operational evidence, permissioned campaign, and tracker reports; validated with RCH check/unit/E2E.

title: Add proof-bundle lane provenance auditor
description:
Problem: proof bundles intentionally accept several artifact roles, including dry-run permissioned campaign handoff packets, downgraded local smoke, and authoritative run evidence. The release gate already distinguishes many lane states, but the provenance contract should be explicit enough that no future docs or gate path can promote handoff material into product readiness.

Scope: add a validator/report that walks a proof bundle and classifies every lane input by provenance: executed product evidence, dry-run handoff, small-host smoke, capability downgrade, stale artifact, missing raw log, or unsupported future-scope. The report should explain exactly why each lane may or may not strengthen a public claim.

Acceptance: unit tests cover all provenance classes and mixed-lane bundles; an E2E script builds a fixture bundle containing at least xfstests handoff, swarm handoff, local smoke, stale evidence, and authoritative synthetic evidence, then proves release-gate state remains hidden/experimental unless the provenance is authoritative; Markdown and JSON reports include lane id, artifact role, source command, git SHA/freshness, host class, raw log references, and final claim effect; release_gate tests consume the auditor output or cross-check it so the two systems cannot drift silently.
close_reason: Completed by SilverCanyon in commit 4ad60fab (evidence: audit proof bundle provenance), pushed to main and mirrored. Scope added lane-level proof-bundle provenance classifications, claim-effect gating, Markdown lane provenance output, release-gate cross-checks, and proof-bundle E2E/report assertions. Validation reported by SilverCanyon: cargo fmt --check --package ffs-harness; bash -n scripts/e2e/ffs_proof_bundle_e2e.sh; git diff --check; RCH proof_bundle tests 38 passed; RCH pass_lane_requires_authoritative_provenance 1 passed; RCH release_gate tests 33 passed; proof-bundle E2E 10/10 scenarios passed; RCH cargo check/clippy remote exit 0; UBS staged exit 0/no critical issues.

title: Build permissioned campaign execution ledger and resume handoff
description:
Problem: the existing permissioned campaign broker creates safe dry-run handoff packets, but once an operator authorizes xfstests or large-host swarm runs, the project still needs a durable execution ledger that records acknowledgement boundaries, command identity, resume state, partial artifacts, cleanup, and proof-bundle lane promotion without relying on ad hoc shell transcripts.

Scope: design a non-ambient execution ledger schema and validators for permissioned campaigns. It must not run destructive or large-host commands without the existing exact ACK variables. Its job is to make an authorized run resumable and auditable: preflight snapshot, explicit ACK capture, command plan hash, step status, artifact hashes, partial-run checkpoints, cleanup status, and proof-bundle lane candidates.

Acceptance: unit tests validate ledger state transitions for not-authorized, preflight-blocked, running, interrupted, resumed, passed, failed, cleanup-failed, and artifact-stale states; an E2E dry-run creates synthetic xfstests and swarm ledgers and proves no permissioned execution was attempted; validator rejects missing ACK text, changed command plans, stale git SHA, missing raw logs, missing cleanup, and attempts to mark dry-run packets as pass evidence; docs explain exactly how this complements bd-rchk3.3 and bd-rchk0.53.8 without replacing the required real operator run.
close_reason: Completed at b12741af and unchanged through 7ad400bb. Validated permissioned campaign ledger unit coverage with rch cargo test -p ffs-harness permissioned_campaign (35 passed), generated dry-run E2E artifacts under artifacts/e2e/20260509_142440_ffs_permissioned_campaign_broker, validated xfstests/swarm synthetic ledgers with the rch-built ffs-harness binary, confirmed invalid dry-run pass evidence and stale git SHA are rejected, confirmed non_execution_safety_report shows no permissioned execution attempted, and UBS on touched surfaces reported zero critical findings with fmt/clippy/check/test-build clean.

title: Add xfstests failure minimizer and sparse-fixture promotion pipeline
description:
Problem: bd-rchk3.4 already requires converting product-actionable xfstests failures into narrow beads after a real baseline. The missing accelerant is a minimizer that turns raw xfstests logs and filesystem artifacts into durable, small, reviewable conformance fixtures before agents start fixing symptoms.

Scope: extend the xfstests triage path with a dry-run minimization pipeline. Given an immutable baseline manifest, it should classify each failing row, extract the smallest reproducer metadata available, propose a sparse fixture or fixture-generation recipe when possible, and emit one dry-run bead payload per unique product failure. It must never mutate the tracker from an E2E run; live bead creation stays an explicit operator/agent action after reviewing artifacts.

Acceptance: unit tests cover duplicate suppression, product-vs-host-vs-harness classification, missing artifact refusal, fixture recipe schema validation, and dry-run bead payload generation; an E2E fixture run consumes synthetic xfstests pass/fail/skip/interrupted/resumed rows and emits JSON/Markdown triage plus proposed sparse fixture manifests; output includes exact failing test id, flavor, command, expected/actual behavior, artifact hashes, suspected crate boundary, validation command, and dependency hints for bd-rchk3.4.
close_reason: Completed by SilverCanyon in a04b1b98: xfstests sparse fixture recipes, validation, and pushed mirrored commit.

title: Compile README readiness wording from release-gate state
description:
Problem: README and status docs contain careful caveats, but they are still hand-maintained prose. As proof-bundle and release-gate rules grow, stale wording becomes a product risk: users may see 100% parity language next to experimental operational readiness and misread the actual supported state.

Scope: add a docs wording compiler or strict checker that consumes release-gate policy, proof-bundle validation reports, and the known deferral matrix, then emits or verifies the public readiness wording blocks for README/FEATURE_PARITY/operator docs. The initial implementation can be checker-only if full generation would be too invasive.

Acceptance: unit tests cover hidden, disabled, experimental, downgraded, and authoritative states for xfstests, swarm.responsiveness, writeback_cache, repair.rw.writeback, and mount.rw claims; an E2E script mutates fixture proof reports and proves stale or over-strong wording fails closed; reports include the controlling lane, missing artifact, remediation bead, and exact docs target; README wording may only strengthen when the policy input says the corresponding claim is authoritative.
close_reason: Completed release-gate docs wording checker: added mount/writeback/repair/xfstests/swarm wording contracts, fail-closed overclaim diagnostics, E2E coverage, and docs.

title: Index operational evidence artifacts for latest-truth queries
description:
Problem: the repo accumulates many gate manifests, E2E result files, proof reports, and validator outputs. Agents currently rediscover evidence with ad hoc find/rg commands, which makes it easy to cite stale artifacts or miss the latest authoritative lane.

Scope: add an operational evidence indexer that scans known artifact roots and emits a normalized latest-truth index keyed by lane, scenario_id, bead id, git SHA, host class, freshness, pass/fail/skip/error state, raw log paths, and release-claim effect. This should be read-only and safe on large artifact trees.

Acceptance: unit tests cover duplicate run ids, stale git SHAs, missing raw logs, conflicting pass/fail for the same scenario, and host-class downgrades; an E2E fixture builds a small artifact tree and proves the indexer selects the newest valid authoritative artifact while preserving older conflicting evidence; CLI output supports JSON and Markdown summaries suitable for Agent Mail completion notes and proof-bundle assembly.
close_reason: Implemented operational evidence indexer with JSON/Markdown CLI, unit coverage, and E2E fixture proof

title: Add RCH remote-exit regression matrix fixtures
description:
Problem: RCH failures can happen in several distinct phases: local fallback, non-compilation wrapper rejection, remote build failure, remote test failure, remote success followed by artifact retrieval hang, timeout before remote exit, and missing remote evidence. Today these states are mostly encoded in shell branches rather than durable fixtures.

Scope: create a small deterministic fixture matrix for RCH transcript parsing and E2E wrapper decisions. The fixtures should not invoke real remote workers; they should model transcripts and expected wrapper outcomes so capture helpers can be tested quickly and fail closed.

Acceptance: Rust or shell unit tests cover every transcript class and assert the exact marker emitted; E2E smoke verifies the fixture matrix and the live direct-RCH guardrail agree on marker names; no fixture may contain RCH_ARTIFACT_RETRIEVAL_*ACCEPTED; documentation explains how to add a new RCH failure class without weakening existing gates.
close_reason: Completed deterministic RCH transcript fixture matrix, live helper marker smoke, accepted-marker guardrail, and docs.

title: Strengthen proof-bundle redaction and path-confinement validation
description:
Problem: proof bundles are meant to be portable operator artifacts, but they include paths, raw logs, command transcripts, and host metadata. The validator should make privacy/security boundaries explicit so publishing or sharing a bundle does not leak secrets or accidentally reference files outside the artifact root.

Scope: add or extend proof-bundle validation for redaction policy, path confinement, symlink/path-traversal refusal, absolute-path allowlist rules, environment variable scrubbing, and raw-log hash coverage. This should align with the hostile-image and proof-bundle threat models rather than becoming a separate ad hoc sanitizer.

Acceptance: unit tests cover relative traversal, absolute path escape, symlink escape, missing redaction policy, unredacted env-like secrets, missing raw-log hash, and allowed confined paths; an E2E fixture proves invalid bundles fail closed and valid bundles preserve enough reproduction data; release-gate/provenance reports surface redaction failures as evidence production failures, not product pass/fail states.
close_reason: Implemented proof-bundle redaction/path-confinement hardening: missing redaction policy now reports structured redaction errors, redaction failures downgrade lane provenance to evidence_production_failure, release-gate regression locks fail-closed behavior, and proof-bundle E2E covers missing-redaction invalid bundle. Validation: rch cargo test -p ffs-harness --lib proof_bundle (47 passed); rch release_gate redaction regression (1 passed); scripts/e2e/ffs_proof_bundle_e2e.sh (14/14 passed); cargo fmt -p ffs-harness -- --check; bash -n; UBS no critical issues.

title: Add large-host swarm capability calibration packet
description:
Problem: swarm.responsiveness can only strengthen on fresh permissioned large-host evidence, but operators need a lightweight pre-run calibration packet that proves the host is actually in the right class before spending time on the full campaign.

Scope: add a non-authoritative calibration manifest/report for large-host swarm runs. It should capture CPU/RAM/NUMA/storage/FUSE visibility, RCH worker identity, queue isolation, target-dir isolation, expected artifact root, and resource caps. The packet should classify hosts as authoritative_large_host_candidate, small_host_smoke, capability_downgraded_smoke, or blocked, without producing product pass evidence.

Acceptance: unit tests cover host classification thresholds, missing NUMA visibility, insufficient RAM/CPU, missing FUSE, stale worker fingerprint, and mismatched artifact root; an E2E dry-run emits candidate and blocked packets and proves release_gate keeps swarm.responsiveness hidden until the real bd-rchk0.53.8 campaign artifacts exist; docs explain the exact handoff from calibration to authorized run.
close_reason: Completed large-host swarm capability calibration packet with candidate/blocked classifications, release-gate hidden-state dry run, docs, unit tests, and E2E evidence.

title: Fail xfstests regression gate strict mode on missing inputs
description: Review fallback after the ready queue was permission-gated: scripts/e2e/ffs_xfstests_regression_gate.sh currently writes a passing report when no current results are found or when the baseline file is missing, even if XFSTESTS_STRICT=1. That can make a strict CI/readiness gate look green without comparing any xfstests evidence. Acceptance: strict mode fails closed for missing results and missing baseline with a clear report reason; non-strict mode preserves the existing advisory/vacuous pass behavior; docs mention the strict missing-input contract; validation covers shell syntax and both strict/non-strict missing-input paths without launching xfstests.
close_reason: Strict xfstests regression gate now fails closed on missing comparison inputs. Added shared empty-comparison report writer, explicit missing-results handling for requested XFSTESTS_RESULTS_JSON, strict/non-strict missing-input split, and docs for the strict contract. Validation: bash -n scripts/e2e/ffs_xfstests_regression_gate.sh; non-strict missing results -> pass report; strict missing results -> exit 1/fail report; non-strict missing baseline -> pass report; strict missing baseline -> exit 1/fail report; jq verified generated gate reports; git diff --check; jq empty .beads/issues.jsonl; br dep cycles --no-db --json; UBS on touched script/docs with no findings though no recognized language scan.

title: perf(ledger): 166 banked KEEP rows quote a vs-incumbent ratio but name no execution host — flag them worker-scoped
close_reason: Retroactive worker-scope flag landed: Row.is_worker_scoped_ratio() + WORKER_SCOPE_BASELINE=166 ratchet + --worker-scope[--list] mode, wired into the pre-commit hook; worker-scope note added to both ledger preambles. Evidence: preflight --self-test OK 52 policy checks (was 37), --worker-scope reports 166 (148 NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md + 18 perf-negative-results.md) exit 0, --lint --staged OK. Ratchet proven to bite end-to-end: +1 unnamed competitive row -> exit 2; same row naming RCH_WORKER -> exit 0; multi-worker row -> exit 2; count below baseline -> exit 2. Per-row host recovery confirmed impossible (0 surviving report.json under /data/tmp), so rows are re-scoped, not retracted.

FLEET-WIDE MEASUREMENT HAZARD, retroactive half. Reported 2026-08-15: measuring the SAME cubic splu cell on two different rch workers gave 1.2693x vs 0.0093x — a 13.6x swing — with BOTH A/A nulls PASSING. A passing A/A null controls WITHIN-invocation noise only; it is blind to between-worker differences in CPU model, cache, memory bandwidth and contention. Consequence: a row that does not name the machine it ran on cannot be compared to any other row.

FORWARD GATE IS ALREADY COVERED — DO NOT DUPLICATE. A peer has ~92 uncommitted lines in scripts/perf_ledger_preflight.py adding WORKER_IDENTITY + MULTI_WORKER regexes and a contract_violations check that fails any staged timed KEEP (and any REJECT resting on a same-invocation null) which records no worker/host identity, plus a check rejecting a run allowed to schedule across several workers. That gate is forward-only: it inspects STAGED decision rows. This bead is the retroactive half it cannot reach.

  REJECT  318  names a worker    57  UNNAMED  261

title: perf: btrfs_recompute_inode_nbytes is O(extents) per write -> O(N^2) for N sequential writes; make it incremental
description: [perf][no-gaps] btrfs_recompute_inode_nbytes (ffs-core lib.rs ~19631) range-scans + parse_extent_data's EVERY EXTENT_DATA item of the inode and sums num_bytes/ram_bytes, and is called on EVERY btrfs_write (21253), btrfs_setattr-truncate (22582), and btrfs_fallocate (22981). For a file written in N sequential aligned chunks (each creating a new extent post-bd-7mi0p), write #k scans k extents -> total O(N^2) parse+sum. TARGET: O(1) per write via incremental nbytes (inode.nbytes already persisted) — new_nbytes = old +/- the exact byte delta of the extents added/removed. LEVER: have btrfs_remove_overlapping_extent_data RETURN its net nbytes delta (it already iterates the overlapping extents) and have the write/emit path add the new extent's alloc_size, skipping the full recompute. SUBTLETY (why this needs care, not a rush): btrfs_insert_regular_extent_segment EARLY-RETURNS on all-zero data (skips the extent), so the re-inserted-segment byte count is NOT simply the slice length — the delta must reflect what was actually inserted (hole vs materialized). VALIDATION: existing content+blocks proptests (btrfs_write_fallocate_random/truncate_random, partial_overwrite blocks==8) + the btrfs-check tests already pin nbytes byte-exactness, so any delta error is caught. Needs a criterion bench (write a 64MiB file in 4KiB chunks) for the hyperfine baseline + Score>=2.0 proof. Truncate/fallocate/clone can keep the full recompute initially (write is the hot path). Identified W75; deferred from a single-hour safe ship due to the skip-zero subtlety + correctness blast radius — suited to the perf specialist (cod) with bench infra.
close_reason: Rejected: direct same-worker ovh-a Criterion btrfs_sequential_write_1m_4k baseline [21.395, 21.708, 22.028] ms vs incremental-nbytes after [20.541, 21.937, 23.822] ms; no proven win / Score<2.0, failed code reverted. Next deeper primitive: dense EOF append extent coalescing or delayed extent-run batching to remove one-extent-per-write metadata growth.

title: Add btrfs kernel_reference golden tests matching ext4 coverage pattern
description:
## What
Add structured golden-fixture conformance tests for btrfs metadata parsing, matching the
ext4 kernel_reference.rs pattern of: create real image → parse → compare to golden JSON.

## Prior Art (what already exists)
- ext4 has crates/ffs-harness/tests/kernel_reference.rs with multiple test variants:
  creates real mkfs.ext4 images, parses them, validates against golden JSON fixtures
- btrfs E2E tests exist in fuse_e2e.rs (lines 1889-1910) that create mkfs.btrfs images
  and mount them via FUSE
- btrfs conformance fixtures in conformance/fixtures/ are synthetic JSON (not from real images)
- ffs-core unit tests build synthetic btrfs images in-memory (build_btrfs_fsops_image)

## The Specific Gap
btrfs has no equivalent of kernel_reference.rs that:
1. Creates a real btrfs filesystem with known content
2. Parses the superblock, tree structures, and metadata with FrankenFS
3. Compares the parsed output against committed golden JSON fixtures
4. Catches regressions when parsing code changes

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1: Create crates/ffs-harness/tests/btrfs_kernel_reference.rs

fn btrfs_golden_basic_superblock()
  - mkfs.btrfs -f --nodesize 16384 on 256MB sparse file
  - Parse superblock with BtrfsSuperblock::parse_superblock_region()
  - Compare: magic, sectorsize, nodesize, total_bytes, num_devices, csum_type
  - Golden: conformance/fixtures/btrfs_basic_superblock.json

fn btrfs_golden_with_files()
  - mkfs.btrfs → mount → create 3 test files with known content → umount
  - Parse: walk root tree → fs tree → verify inode items, dir items, extent data
  - Golden: conformance/fixtures/btrfs_with_files.json

fn btrfs_golden_with_compression()
  - mkfs.btrfs → mount -o compress=zlib → create files → umount
  - Parse: verify EXTENT_DATA items have compression type set
  - Golden: conformance/fixtures/btrfs_compressed.json

fn btrfs_golden_with_subvolume()
  - mkfs.btrfs → mount → btrfs subvolume create → add files → umount
  - Parse: verify ROOT_ITEM for subvolume, walk subvol tree
  - Golden: conformance/fixtures/btrfs_subvolume.json

fn btrfs_golden_chunk_and_device_trees()
  - mkfs.btrfs → parse chunk tree entries → verify stripe mapping
  - Golden: conformance/fixtures/btrfs_chunk_tree.json

### Step 2: Create golden fixture files
- Run tests once with REGEN_GOLDENS=1 to generate initial fixtures
- Commit fixtures to conformance/fixtures/btrfs_*.json
- Subsequent runs compare against committed fixtures

### Step 3: Add regeneration support
- scripts/regen_btrfs_goldens.sh: runs tests with REGEN_GOLDENS=1
- Similar to existing scripts/verify_golden.sh for ext4

## Considerations
- mkfs.btrfs minimum image: ~128MB for single-device, use sparse files
- btrfs-progs required: mkfs.btrfs, btrfs (for subvolume create, property set)
- Tests must skip gracefully when btrfs-progs not installed
- Some features (multi-device RAID) need multiple loop devices — skip in CI,
  add as a separate optional test
- Golden format: pretty-printed JSON matching the ext4 golden style
- Mount operations need root or fusermount3 — use btrfs-progs direct manipulation
  where possible (debugfs equivalent: btrfs inspect-internal dump-tree)

## Test Plan
- Each golden test: parse real image → compare to fixture → assert exact match
- Regeneration: REGEN_GOLDENS=1 cargo test -p ffs-harness --test btrfs_kernel_reference
- Verify: changing parsing code causes golden mismatch (regression detection works)
- Skip tests gracefully when mkfs.btrfs unavailable

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 5 btrfs golden conformance tests implemented and passing
- [ ] Golden JSON fixtures committed to conformance/fixtures/
- [ ] Tests create real mkfs.btrfs images (not synthetic)
- [ ] Regression detection verified: intentional parse change → test failure
- [ ] Tests skip gracefully when btrfs-progs unavailable
- [ ] Regeneration script works

title: [parity][corruption] ext4 inline_data directories silently mishandled (empty readdir, data loss) — feature accepted at mount
description: EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_INLINE_DATA (0x8000) is in Ext4IncompatFeatures::ALLOWED_V1 (ext4.rs:263), so FrankenFS MOUNTS inline_data filesystems. But it has no inline-DIRECTORY support: inline dirs store entries inside the inode (i_block[0..60] + the system.data ibody xattr), not in extent-mapped blocks. read_dir_with_scope (lib.rs:7475) and lookup_name_with_scope (7512) only iterate resolve_extent() blocks — an inline dir has none, so read_dir returns EMPTY and lookup returns None (no inline-dir parser; read_ext4_inline_data at 7974 handles inline FILES only). Consequences on a real inline_data image: (1) listing a small inline directory shows nothing; (2) an empty readdir makes rmdir believe the dir is empty so it removes a non-empty directory, losing the inline entries; (3) ext4_add_dir_entry has no inline guard (the INLINE_DATA checks at 12218/12736 are FILE-write paths), so creating a file in an inline dir either errors confusingly (collect_extents on a non-extent i_block) or allocates a fresh block + extent root overwriting the inline entries in i_block = DATA LOSS. Reachable by any inline_data-formatted image (increasingly common for small dirs). FIX OPTIONS: (a) full inline-dir support — parse the inline dir on read, convert inline to block on add (large); or (b) SAFE INTERIM — reject inline-dir OPERATIONS (read_dir/lookup/ext4_add_dir_entry when the inode has EXT4_INLINE_DATA_FL) with a clear UnsupportedFeature error instead of silent empty/data-loss; preserves inline-FILE reads. A driver lacking inline_data support refuses the incompat feature at mount entirely, so erroring is parity-defensible vs the current silent corruption. PROOF: fabricate a dir inode with EXT4_INLINE_DATA_FL set (persist_ext4_inode_for_testing) and assert the op returns a clean error, not data loss / empty.
close_reason: Silent corruption FIXED in 264024c0 via the safe-interim guard (option b): ext4_reject_inline_data_dir guards read_dir/lookup/ext4_add_dir_entry and returns a clear UnsupportedFeature for any EXT4_INLINE_DATA_FL directory, instead of silent empty-readdir (which let rmdir drop a non-empty dir) or overwriting the inline entries on insert (data loss). Parity-defensible: a driver lacking inline_data support refuses the incompat feature at mount. Inline-FILE reads unaffected. Test inline_data_directory_operations_fail_loudly_bd_4y9ca (flag dir inline -> read_dir/lookup/create all return UnsupportedFeature). ffs-core 906/906. FULL inline-dir support (parse on read + inline->block conversion on add, option a) remains a possible future enhancement but is now lower priority since erroring is safe + parity-defensible.

title: perf(fuse): readdir+stat pays 5 FUSE round trips per entry (1 getattr + 4 getxattr) — cut the COUNT, the daemon is only 4% of wall

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FILED FROM MEASUREMENT (ProudBarn, 2026-08-16), not from inspection. Successor to bd-yu6jz's transport scope, and the direction bd-btrfs-readdir-stat-8x-8y7vp is redirected to.

THE MEASURED PREMISE. Local managed mount, v3+PGO ELF c33f3565c9f1d3661b04433941643a58127cb1d8eb7b41aa2eec37e1b86a2664, pre-existing ext4 fixture with 20003 root entries, two ls -lU sweeps, FFS_MOUNT_BENCH_EVIDENCE dispatch counters. rch worker: none, a mount is local by necessity.

    getattr  40499 calls  20847403 ns   515 ns/op   1.01 per entry
    getxattr 160014 calls 61156783 ns   382 ns/op   4.00 per entry
    readdir    186 calls  16241051 ns
    daemon dispatch 98.3 ms   client wall 2550 ms   DAEMON SHARE 3.85 pct
    per entry: daemon 2.46 us, wall 63.7 us

WHY THIS IS THE LEVER AND FORMAT WORK IS NOT. Two independent routes agree that the format layer is small: in-process the btrfs metadata path costs 356 ns/stat with the floor-leaf memo on and node lookups fall 3.00 -> 0.07 per stat (65901929), and on the mounted path the daemon accounts for under 4 pct of wall. Every remaining lever that makes the daemon ANSWER faster is bounded above by that 4 pct. The cost is the round trips themselves: 5 per entry, each getxattr being 382 ns of work inside roughly 15 us of wall.

THE FOUR PROBES ARE THE SURPRISE. bd-ha71t measured 2 per path stat; this measures 4.00 per entry under ls -l, because the client asks for several attribute names (capability plus ACL/security). Nobody has enumerated WHICH names, and that is step one — a probe for a name the filesystem can never carry is a round trip bought for nothing.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS
  1. Enumerate the actual names requested per entry. The daemon sees them; add a
     bounded per-name counter to the dispatch metrics rather than guessing.
  2. For each name, decide whether the kernel can be told the answer once:
     negative xattr caching, or answering during readdirplus so the per-entry
     probes never leave the kernel.
  3. Only then measure again. The acceptance metric is ROUND TRIPS PER ENTRY
     (currently 5.01), which is counted and needs no quiet window and no
     comparator — the same property that made this measurement possible while
     the mounted comparator is floor-blocked.

DO NOT start by making getxattr cheaper. It is already 382 ns against a ~15 us round trip; halving it buys 0.1 pct of wall. The capability memo already demonstrated this: it drove format lookups down 40x and the mounted row did not move.

SCOPE HONESTY: measured on ext4, one run, no A/A null, no kernel arm — a mechanism attribution on exact counts, not a ratio. Warm stat is 4.812194x ext4 vs 4.977803x btrfs (3.4 pct apart), which is the standing evidence that this floor is shared rather than btrfs-specific.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
STEP 1 DELIVERED — the names are enumerated, and two things change (ProudBarn, bab16e22).

MEASURED. Local managed mount, pre-existing ext4 fixture, 20002 entries, one ls -lU sweep, v3+PGO ffs-cli built in place on thinkstation1. rch worker: none (a mount is local by necessity).

    mount_xattr_probe_census,security_capability=160021,security_selinux=20002,system_posix_acl_access=20002,system_posix_acl_default=0,other=20002
    mount_dispatch_metrics,...,getattr_dispatch_count=40303,getxattr_dispatch_count=120011,readdir_dispatch_count=145

    per entry: security.capability 8.00 | security.selinux 1.00 | system.posix_acl_access 1.00 | system.posix_acl_default 0 | other 1.00
    TOTAL 11.00 probes/entry, of which 6.00 reach the format layer
    security.capability = 72.7 pct of all probes

⭐ FINDING 1: security.capability is 8.00 probes PER ENTRY and nearly three quarters of all xattr traffic. Any round-trip reduction that does not address it is rearranging the other 27 pct. This bead's premise is confirmed and sharpened — the target is one name, not four.

⛔ FINDING 2, AND IT CORRECTS MY OWN EARLIER NUMBER: the probe stream is BIGGER than the dispatch counters show. 220027 probes against 120011 dispatches — 100016 (45.5 pct) were memo-served and returned before with_request_scope, so they never appear in getxattr_dispatch_count. My earlier '4.00 getxattr per entry' was measured from the dispatch counter and is an UNDERCOUNT; the true figure on that workload is 11.00 per entry. Same class of error bd-0c4av found in requests_total (22 counted for 6001 stats). Any round-trip budget built on dispatch counts alone is low by roughly 2x here.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: the daemon is still a small share of wall (3.85 pct measured previously), so the lever is still COUNT and not per-op cost. If anything finding 2 strengthens it — there are twice as many round trips to remove as the dispatch counters suggested.

NEXT, per this bead's own plan: for security.capability specifically, decide whether the kernel can be told the answer once. That is the negative-caching question bd-ha71t explored and closed for ENOSYS and FUSE_HANDLE_KILLPRIV V1/V2 — all three measured inert — so the remaining candidates are answering during readdirplus, or a FUSE ABI path that lets the daemon declare an inode carries no security.* names. Note 8.00 probes per entry with a memo present means the memo is being invalidated mid-sweep (forget/batch_forget) rather than serving every repeat; understanding why 8 and not 1 is worth an hour before designing anything.

SCOPE: ext4, one run, no A/A null, no kernel arm — a counted mechanism census, admissible on exact counts, not a ratio.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CAPACITY CLIFF: IT MOVES, IT DOES NOT DISAPPEAR (ProudBarn, 2026-08-16).

Test designed to distinguish the two, per the fleet guidance: hold the DIRECTORY
FIXED and vary only the slot count. If the effect tracks the slots/entries ratio
it is pure capacity, and a bigger memo just relocates the artefact to a bigger
directory.

Local managed mount, pre-existing ext4 fixture, N = 20002 root entries, one
`ls -lU` per arm, v3+PGO ffs-cli built in place on thinkstation1, knob
FFS_FUSE_CAPABILITY_MEMO_SLOTS (bd-m1bpu, AzureBay's). rch worker: none — a mount
is local by necessity. Slot count echoed back by the daemon in every arm, so the
knob is confirmed to take effect rather than assumed.

  slots   slots/N   getxattr dispatched   dispatched/entry   capability probes   wall
   1024      0.05                 40003               2.00               60008   1.98s
   4096      0.20                 40003               2.00               60009   1.93s
  16384      0.82                 27236               1.36               60008   1.79s
  65536      3.28                 20002               1.00               60008   1.76s

FINDING 1 — THE CLIFF MOVES. Dispatched probes per entry sits flat at 2.00 while
the table is far smaller than the working set (1024 and 4096 are indistinguishable
despite 4x the memory), begins falling as slots approach N, and reaches its floor
of exactly 1.00 once slots exceed N. That is capacity behaviour, not a threshold:
the memo helps precisely to the extent it can hold the directory. Sizing it for a
20k directory buys nothing for a 200k one — the same cliff reappears one order of
magnitude out. Anyone quoting a memo win must therefore quote the directory size
it was measured at, or the number means nothing.

FINDING 2, AND IT IS THE MORE IMPORTANT ONE — THE MEMO CANNOT REMOVE A ROUND TRIP.
capability_probes is CONSTANT at ~60008 across all four arms, a 64x range of table
sizes. The memo changes only how many probes reach the format layer; every probe
still costs a full FUSE round trip regardless. Since the daemon is 3.85 pct of
mounted readdir+stat wall time, the memo is optimising inside that 4 pct by
construction and cannot touch the other 96 pct no matter how large it gets.

That is consistent with the wall column: 64x the slots moves wall 1.98s -> 1.76s,
about 11 pct, on a workload deliberately sized to fit. Treat that 11 pct as
DIRECTIONAL ONLY — single runs, no repeats, no A/A null, so it does not meet the
replicated-standing convention and is not bankable.

CONSEQUENCE. Memo sizing is not a lever on the readdir+stat row. It was worth
knowing where the cliff is, and now it is known and it is a capacity artefact.
The lever remains what bd-4ypbv says: reduce the NUMBER of probes. The memo makes
each cheap; only the kernel can be persuaded to stop asking.

ONE DISCREPANCY I CANNOT EXPLAIN AND AM NOT GLOSSING. My earlier census measured
security.capability at 8.00 per entry; every arm here measures 3.00 per entry on
what should be the same workload. The census counter is cumulative for the mount's
lifetime, and the earlier mount served an extra plain `ls` before the sweep, but
that does not obviously account for a factor of 2.7 — a readdir-only `ls` should
issue no xattr probes at all. Until that is understood, treat the ABSOLUTE
probes-per-entry figure as uncertain; the RATIOS within this sweep are sound
because all four arms ran the identical sequence and the count was constant across
them.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
PROBE ATTRIBUTION ISOLATED, and my earlier 8.00 figure RETRACTED (ProudBarn,
2026-08-16).

Four mounts, identical in everything but the client workload, census read once per
mount. Local managed mount, pre-existing ext4 fixture with 20002 root entries,
FFS_FUSE_CAPABILITY_MEMO_SLOTS=65536 (above the working set, so memo capacity is
not a confound), v3+PGO ffs-cli built in place on thinkstation1. rch worker: none

  idle                 0              0               0
  readdir              5            197               1
  statone              1              1               1
  readdirst        60009          20199           20002

2. readdir ALONE PROBES NOTHING. A names-only `ls` over 20002 entries produced 5

in the first census and ZERO in every run since. `ls` appears to stop asking for

comments.text:
READDIRPLUS FORCING: REJECTED on a counted mechanism (ProudBarn, 4a5f4e07). One of the three candidate shapes removed by measurement.

FIRST, THE TRUE ROUND-TRIP COUNT, which corrects the working figure. requests_total at the FUSE boundary — which includes memo-served probes, per bd-0c4av — is 140060 for a 20002-entry ls -lU: 7.00 REQUESTS PER ENTRY, not 4 and not 5. Decomposition per entry: capability 3.00 (42.8 pct), lookup 0.99, getattr 1.01, readdir 0.00 (41 calls for the whole directory). Every earlier per-entry figure I gave was built from dispatch counters and understated this.

HYPOTHESIS: 0.99 lookup + 1.01 getattr per entry against 41 readdir calls is the signature of the kernel choosing PLAIN readdir, which FUSE_READDIRPLUS_AUTO permits. Dropping AUTO should force readdirplus and fold that pair away — 2.00 of the 7.00.

REFUTED. One ELF, env-toggled FFS_FUSE_READDIRPLUS_AUTO, interleaved AUTO/FORCED/FORCED/AUTO, memo slots pinned at 65536 so capacity is not a confound, ffs-cli sha256 2faab3039bc3da4126df8b9197edb0f431467b0fc0dac2b3376d6a2bc0c14f12 (v3+PGO, built in place on thinkstation1). rch worker: none — a mount is local by necessity.

    auto1    wall 1.90s  requests_total 140059  capability 60008
    forced1  wall 1.56s  requests_total 140223  capability 60008
    forced2  wall 1.73s  requests_total 140223  capability 60008
    auto2    wall 1.99s  requests_total 140059  capability 60008

So 'serve readdirplus-style responses' is already happening and is not the lever. Capability probes are bit-identical across arms (60008), so the choice does not touch xattr behaviour either.

NOT BANKED, and deliberately so: wall came out lower on both forced arms (mean 1.645s vs 1.945s, ~15 pct) and the gap exceeds each arm's within-arm range, but n=2 per arm with NO A/A null does not meet the replicated-standing convention. Worst-bound framing for anyone who wants to chase it: 1.73s forced vs 1.90s auto = 1.098x. It is odd that wall would move while the request count does not, which is exactly why it needs a real estimator before belief.

CANDIDATE LIST AFTER THIS: batching — already done for readdir itself (41 calls for 20002 entries). Caching the attr alongside the entry — that IS readdirplus, now measured inert. What remains is the 3.00 capability probes per entry, 42.8 pct of all traffic, and the only shapes left for those are ones that stop the kernel ASKING: negative xattr caching, or a FUSE ABI path to declare an inode carries no security.* names. bd-ha71t already closed ENOSYS and FUSE_HANDLE_KILLPRIV V1/V2 by measurement.
