title: [bug] sequential multi-chunk e2compr write corrupts clusters (readback fails)
description: MINIMAL REPRO: create an ext4 file with EXT4_COMPR_FL, write 128KiB then a SECOND 128KiB at offset 128KiB (two separate fs.write calls), read back -> Corruption { block: 60, detail: 'e2compr: compressed cluster too small for header' }. The existing single-write test compressed_write_spanning_indirect_blocks_roundtrips_ext4 (ONE 128KiB fs.write) roundtrips fine, so the bug is in the SECOND/sequential compressed write (append/RMW of an already-compressed inode across separate write ops). Chunk boundaries are cluster-aligned (128KiB = 32 4K blocks, a multiple of any power-of-2-block e2compr cluster <=32), so it is not a partial-cluster split. PRODUCTION-REACHABLE: FUSE does not raise max_write, so the kernel splits any large userspace write to a compressed file into sequential bounded write requests = exactly this multi-chunk pattern; a compressed file larger than one FUSE write request would corrupt. Found via the bd-1c9h7 double-indirect coverage test (chunked to avoid bd-kck88), but corruption is at an EARLY block (60), not double-indirect — confirmed it reproduces at just 256KiB/2 chunks. Need: root-cause the e2compr write path's handling of a write that starts at/after an existing compressed cluster (cluster header/length recompute, allocation reuse), fix so sequential compressed writes roundtrip byte-identically. Behavior parity absolute. Repro test lives in compressed_write_reaching_double_indirect_roundtrips_ext4 (currently failing).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: DECISIVE DIAGNOSTIC: a SINGLE fs.write of 256KiB to the compressed file ROUNDTRIPS CORRECTLY (test passes), but the SAME 256KiB written as two sequential 128KiB fs.write calls CORRUPTS (Corruption block 60 'compressed cluster too small for header'). So the defect is strictly in the SECOND+ sequential compressed write to an already-written compressed inode — cross-write-scope state, NOT the per-cluster compress logic (which the single-write path proves correct). Strong hypothesis: the second write either (a) double-allocates blocks already owned by the first write's clusters (alloc state not reflecting prior compressed writes), or (b) mishandles the inode's existing cluster/i_block layout when appending. Next: instrument block allocations + cluster physical offsets across the two writes to confirm overlap. Production-reachable (FUSE splits large writes into sequential bounded ops). Repro is the #[ignore]'d compressed_write_reaching_double_indirect_roundtrips_ext4 (chunked).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE LOCALIZED (instrumented the 256KiB/2-chunk repro, write + read sides): On readback the LAST cluster (cluster_start=60, logical 60-63) resolves ptrs=[0,0,0,SENTINEL] — its data pointer (slot 48 of single-indirect block 2101) is 0, though write_block_ptr DID write slot48=phys2113 during chunk 2. Earlier chunk-2 clusters (slots 20-47) and cluster 15's later slots (49,50 holes, 51 sentinel) all persist — ONLY slot 48 is lost. So it is a WRITE-THEN-REVERT within chunk 2's repeated RMW of the SAME indirect block 2101: cluster 15 writes slot48=2113 (stages 2101), then the next write_block_ptr (slot49=hole) reads 2101 via read_block_with_scope, gets a version MISSING slot 48, and re-stages — reverting slot 48 (last-stage-wins on the stale copy). CONTRIBUTING: write_block_ptr stages every same-block update of 2101 with MergeProof::DisjointBlocks, which is a contract violation for same-block writes (mechanism()==NoSameBlockMerge; test merge_proof_disjoint_blocks_rejects_same_block_merge asserts it is invalid for same-block). CANDIDATE FIX LOCATIONS: (1) read_block_with_scope must return the LATEST staged version of a committed-then-restaged block within the scope (read-your-writes for a block first committed in a PRIOR scope then RMW'd repeatedly in THIS scope); or (2) within-tx repeated stage_write of the same block must be true last-write-wins on the latest staged bytes. The single-write path works because 2101 is allocated+staged within one scope (never committed mid-sequence), so its read-your-writes path differs. Data-corruption-critical tx-staging fix — needs a focused session + the repro (#[ignore] compressed_write_reaching_double_indirect_roundtrips_ext4) as the gate, plus a direct ffs-mvcc unit test of read-your-writes for a committed-then-repeatedly-restaged block.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: DEEPER (ruled out within-tx staging): Transaction.writes is BTreeMap<BlockNumber,Vec<u8>> and stage_write_with_proof does writes.insert (last-write-wins per block); staged_write returns the latest — so read-your-writes WITHIN chunk 2's tx is correct and slot 48 IS present in the staged 2101 at commit time (write-side instrumentation confirmed reads accumulate). The loss therefore happens at COMMIT/version-reconstruction: only slot 48 (one 4-byte range at offset 192) is dropped on readback while all other chunk-2 slots persist. ffs-mvcc reconstructs same-block versions using merge_proofs + declared touched_ranges (see lib.rs ~182-292, 'merge_proof_rejected: staged block modified bytes outside declared touched_ranges'); chunk 2 stages 2101 with MergeProof::DisjointBlocks (mechanism NoSameBlockMerge), which is the wrong proof for a sequential full-indirect-block overwrite layered on chunk 1's committed 2101 — the reconstruction overlays only a subset of changed bytes, dropping slot 48. PRIME FIX: e2compr indirect-block writes (write_block_ptr, ensure_indirect_block, ensure_pointer_in_block) must stage with a proof that reconstructs the FULL written block verbatim (or declares the full touched range), not DisjointBlocks. Verify against the version-reconstruction path with a direct ffs-mvcc unit test: commit block B=v1, then a new tx fully-overwrites B=v2 staged with the chosen proof, commit, read at latest snapshot -> must equal v2 byte-for-byte; plus the e2compr repro un-ignored. Data-corruption-critical; do not guess the proof — confirm reconstruction semantics first.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ISOLATION RESULT: added a direct ffs-mvcc unit test (disjoint_proof_repeated_full_overwrite_after_prior_commit_roundtrips) replicating the pattern at the core layer — commit a block in tx1, then in tx2 read it and RMW-overwrite it TWICE with MergeProof::DisjointBlocks, commit, read. It PASSES. So the core MvccStore commit/read_visible/staged-write path for repeated same-block full overwrites after a prior commit is CORRECT for the simple case. bd-bw90c therefore lives in the ffs-core integration or a higher-complexity threshold NOT captured by the 2-RMW case: candidates now are (a) the real path stages the indirect block ~32 times across 8 clusters within chunk 2 (vs 2 here) — try scaling the unit test to many RMWs; (b) readback goes through MvccBlockDevice::read_block (device adapter) + resolve_indirect_block, not read_visible directly — the bug may be in the device-level read or indirect resolution across the committed+restaged block; (c) the inode is reloaded between the two request scopes and i_block[12] / read path uses a stale view. Next: scale the mvcc unit test to 32 same-block RMWs, and add an ffs-core-level RequestScope test (begin scope, stage indirect block many times, commit/end, new scope, read via read_block_with_scope) to pin the exact layer.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: DEFINITIVE ISOLATION: a 40-same-block-RMW variant (disjoint_proof_many_same_block_rmws_after_prior_commit_roundtrips, matching the real ~32-stage indirect-block churn) ALSO PASSES at the core MvccStore layer. So MvccStore commit + read_visible reconstruct repeated same-block full overwrites correctly at scale — the core MVCC layer is FULLY RULED OUT. bd-bw90c is in the ffs-core READ path, not MvccStore: at readback fs.read -> read_block_with_scope/read_block_arc_with_scope, which checks tx.staged_write, then scope.snapshot read_visible, then the MvccBlockDevice device adapter; OR resolve_indirect_block's i_block[12]->slot resolution. Since read_visible is proven correct, the suspect is (a) the readback resolving block 2101 via the device adapter / a snapshot that yields a chain-merged view differing from read_visible, or (b) resolve_indirect_block reading a stale inode i_block[12] / wrong slot. NEXT (focused): an ffs-core RequestScope-level test — begin scope, stage indirect block 2101 ~32x across the cluster pattern, commit+end scope, fresh scope, read via read_block_with_scope AND via the device adapter, compare to read_visible; whichever diverges is the bug. The e2compr repro (#[ignore] compressed_write_reaching_double_indirect_roundtrips_ext4) remains the integration gate.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: MVCC LAYER FULLY EXONERATED. Added disjoint_proof_cluster_pattern_rmw_after_prior_commit_roundtrips: a 4096-byte indirect block prior-committed (slots 0..20), then a later txn RMWs slots 20..52 in the EXACT e2compr cluster shape (slot%4==0 data ptr non-zero, %4 in{1,2} hole=0, %4==3 sentinel) via read-your-writes full-block overwrites staged with DisjointBlocks, THEN prune_versions_older_than(watermark) to force chain consolidation, THEN read_visible. PASSES — all non-zero slots survive. Combined with the 2-RMW and 40-RMW tests, this rules out the entire MvccStore path: commit, read_visible/resolve_data_with, delta/dedup encoding, AND pruning/make_chain_head_full, even for the precise hole-flanked-data pattern. DEFINITIVE LOCALIZATION: read-path instrumentation showed the ffs-core readback's read_visible(block 2101, snap)=slot48 0, i.e. the COMMITTED version is wrong — but MvccStore commits correctly given the right tx write-set (proven). Therefore ffs-core's e2compr write/scope path produces a tx whose staged 2101 has slot 48 reverted to 0 before commit, specific to the integration (two sequential RequestScopes, chunk2 reusing chunk1's committed indirect block 2101). Only slot 48 (cluster 15's data ptr) is lost; 20-47 and 49-51 persist. NEXT (decisive, one instrument cycle): log the staged 2101's slot-48 bytes after EACH write_block_ptr stage for cluster 15 (lb_indirect 48-51) and at commit_request_scope — to catch exactly where slot 48 reverts (suspect: a cluster-15 sub-step reading 2101 via read_block_with_scope step-2 read_visible at chunk2's snapshot = chunk1's slot48=0, instead of step-1 tx.staged, then re-staging stale). Repro: #[ignore] compressed_write_reaching_double_indirect_roundtrips_ext4.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE NAILED: the e2compr compressed-write path runs with NO transaction (scope.tx == None; instrumentation showed has_tx=false throughout write_block_ptr). So write_block_ptr writes the indirect block directly to the DEVICE (the else arm: block_dev.write_block), while read_block_with_scope reads from MVCC read_visible (step 2, since scope.snapshot is set). Two different stores. After chunk 1 commits indirect block 2101 into MVCC, chunk 2 per-slot RMWs call read_block_with_scope(2101) which returns the STALE committed chunk-1 version (read_slot48=0 on EVERY cluster-15 write, even right after slot 48 was device-written) then writes only its slot to the device. Read-your-writes is broken across the device/MVCC split -> intermediate slot writes lost (cluster 15 slot 48 data ptr 2113) -> readback read_visible(2101) misses slot 48 -> compressed cluster too small for header. Single-write works because 2101 is never committed to MVCC mid-write, so read_visible=None and read_block_with_scope falls through to step-3 DEVICE read which sees prior writes. FIX (architectural, corruption-critical): run the e2compr write inside a transaction so indirect RMWs stage+read-your-write consistently (like the uncompressed path), OR make read_block_with_scope consistent with where no-tx writes land. Confirm why with_latest_scope gives scope.tx=None for the compressed path. Production-reachable for any sequential write to a compressed file once its indirect block is committed.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: CONFIRMED MECHANISM (final): block_device_adapter() builds MvccBlockDevice::new(base, store, store.current_snapshot()), so every write_block_ptr device write commits a NEW MVCC version at an increasing commit_seq. But read_block_with_scope step 2 reads self.mvcc_store.read_visible(block, scope.snapshot) where scope.snapshot is FIXED at scope-begin (with_latest_scope = RequestScope::with_snapshot(current at begin), tx=None). So a write made DURING the scope (seq > scope.snapshot.high) is invisible to subsequent reads in the same scope. For a block that already existed at scope-begin (chunk1 committed 2101), step 2 returns that stale version and never reaches step 3 (device adapter @ current) -> no read-your-writes -> repeated RMW loses accumulation. Single-write works because 2101 did not exist at scope-begin (read_visible=None -> step 3 device @ current -> sees in-scope writes). FIX OPTIONS (corruption-critical, pick with care + repro gate): (1) in read_block_with_scope, when scope.tx is None, read at the CURRENT snapshot (read-your-writes for write scopes that mutate via the current-snapshot device adapter) rather than the fixed scope.snapshot; (2) run the e2compr write inside a real Transaction so RMWs stage+read-your-write via tx.staged_write (step 1); (3) have the e2compr write reuse one block_device_adapter / advance the scope snapshot after each write. Beware: option 1 changes read semantics for no-tx scopes (snapshot isolation vs read-your-writes) — verify no read-only scope relies on begin-snapshot isolation. Gate: #[ignore] compressed_write_reaching_double_indirect_roundtrips_ext4 + an ffs-mvcc-clean repro is NOT possible (this is purely the ffs-core scope/device-adapter interaction).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: FIXED. read_block_with_scope / read_block_arc_with_scope now do the fixed-begin-snapshot MVCC read (step 2) only for transaction-backed scopes; no-tx scopes fall through to the current-snapshot device adapter (step 3), so their reads are consistent with their writes (block_device_adapter commits at current) = read-your-writes. The e2compr indirect-block RMW across sequential chunked writes now accumulates correctly. Repro compressed_write_reaching_double_indirect_roundtrips_ext4 (chunked >4MiB, reaches i_block[13] double-indirect) PASSES byte-for-byte. Regression gate: ffs-core 890 + ffs-mvcc 451 + ffs-fuse 560 all pass (no isolation regression for tx scopes); clippy clean; #![forbid(unsafe_code)] intact.

title: perf(metadata): remove redundant inner Arc from Bw-tree message buffer
description: Profile-first one-lever pass on BufferedMessages. Current PageDelta is already published behind Arc<PageDelta>, while BufferedMessages adds Arc<Vec<_>> and every upsert builds a fresh Vec. Measure current write_heavy_message_buffer median strictly through remote RCH, remove only the redundant inner Arc if a same-worker A/B clears the median/null gate, and prove the message-buffer golden output exactly identical. Never touch read-path or I/O files; surface any RCH admission failure without local Cargo.
notes: REJECT. Profile baselines for write_heavy_message_buffer_ab/new_message_buffer_8 were 71.005 ms median on vmi1293453 and 76.603 ms on vmi1227854, so cross-worker runs were routing evidence only. Same-binary/same-worker A/A/B on vmi1149989: inner Arc A 580.856 us, inner Arc B 623.145 us, direct Vec 570.284 us. Candidate was 1.0185x faster than best control but below the 1.0728x A/A null floor. Exact production golden message_buffer_matches_individual_preconsolidation_golden_report passed 1/1 with full expected output. All Cargo commands used RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec; no local Cargo. Restored production and benchmark files; docs-only negative evidence landed. Read-path and IO files untouched.
close_reason: Measured reject: 1.0185x candidate improvement did not clear 1.0728x same-worker A/A median null floor; exact golden passed and experiment was restored.

title: ffs-harness: format_full_report has only substring assertions, no golden-output pinning
description:
Finding (via /testing-golden-artifacts skill): the human-readable
performance regression report rendered by `format_full_report` and
`format_report_line` (crates/ffs-harness/src/perf_comparison.rs:779,
810) is exposed to tooling but covered only by substring assertions
in `report_line_format` and `full_report_has_summary`:

  assert!(line.starts_with("[PASS]"));
  assert!(line.contains("test_op"));
  assert!(report.contains("Performance Regression Report"));
  assert!(report.contains("1 pass"));

title: ext4 ZERO_RANGE does not preallocate holes (diverges from btrfs + kernel)
description: ext4_fallocate ZERO_RANGE branch (ffs-core lib.rs ~13315) skips hole mappings (physical_start==0, 'continue') — it only zeroes already-allocated written blocks. The kernel's ext4_zero_range PREALLOCATES the whole range (man fallocate: 'blocks are preallocated and zeroed'), allocating holes as unwritten/zeroed extents. The codebase already does this correctly for btrfs (test btrfs_write_fallocate_zero_range_allocates_unwritten_hole at lib.rs:51366), so ext4 is inconsistent. Consequences: (1) inode.blocks lower than kernel; (2) the ZERO_RANGE space guarantee is violated — a later write into the 'zeroed' range can ENOSPC; (3) kernel/e2fsck sees holes where it expects allocated unwritten extents (data reads zero either way, so not corruption — a parity/semantics gap). The core 'reads return zero' contract IS met. FIX: for hole mappings in the ZERO_RANGE range, allocate unwritten extents (reuse the fallocate-default prealloc allocation path) + update inode.blocks, then zero the written blocks as today. VALIDATABLE on rch: mkfs.ext4+debugfs ARE available on workers (open_writable_ext4 runs), so a create-sparse->ZERO_RANGE->assert-allocated E2E test runs.
close_reason: Fixed + E2E-validated on rch: ext4 ZERO_RANGE now preallocates holes as unwritten extents (reusing allocate_unwritten_extent + inode.blocks accounting), matching the kernel + btrfs path; written blocks still zeroed (partial RMW unchanged). Test write_fallocate_zero_range_preallocates_holes_bd_c0xru: punch middle block (blocks drop) -> ZERO_RANGE the hole (blocks rise) -> reads zero + neighbors untouched. 56 fallocate tests pass.

title: Fix sharded MVCC conflict policy lock-order contract
description:
Discovery from `$deadlock-finder-and-fixer` while source-aware ready work was empty and RCH remained blocked by `critical_pressure=7`.

Current evidence:
- `crates/ffs-mvcc/src/sharded.rs` documents `conflict_policy` as a leaf lock: “only ever acquired alone” and lists `set_conflict_policy` / `effective_policy` as leaf-only.
- `commit()` and `commit_ssi()` acquire shard write locks via `lock_shards(...)`, then call `preflight_fcw_locked(...)` while those shard guards are still live.
- `preflight_fcw_locked(...)` immediately calls `self.effective_policy()`, which acquires `conflict_policy.read()` and, when the policy is `Adaptive`, `contention_metrics.read()`.
- Existing open-bead search for `deadlock`, `conflict_policy`, `effective_policy`, `lock`, and related terms did not find a FrankenFS bead covering this mismatch.

Problem: the implementation currently nests `effective_policy()` under shard write locks even though the lock-order contract says it is leaf-only. I did not find a current inverse `conflict_policy -> shards` path, so this is not filed as a proven active deadlock. The concrete bug is that the documented lock-order proof and future-maintainer guardrail are false: a later method that trusts the leaf-lock contract and acquires `conflict_policy` before a shard can create an AB-BA cycle against commit preflight. The existing lock-order watchdog appears focused on commit/prune/register and does not explicitly cover concurrent conflict-policy updates during commit/SSI preflight.

Scope: make the lock-order contract true and machine-checked. Prefer computing or snapshotting the effective policy before shard write locks are acquired, then pass it into preflight, or update the invariant if there is a stronger reason for the current nesting. Ensure adaptive policy selection still observes contention metrics consistently enough for the expected-loss policy.

Acceptance:
1. `effective_policy()` / `conflict_policy` are either truly leaf-only in the commit paths, or the struct-level lock-order documentation is updated to describe the actual safe order with no contradiction.
2. A focused test or watchdog covers concurrent `set_conflict_policy(Adaptive/Strict/SafeMerge)` or effective-policy reads racing with `commit()`, `commit_ssi()`, and pruning/registration paths.
3. The test would fail or hang on an intentional inverse-order regression, not merely assert current return values.
4. Validation includes `cargo test -p ffs-mvcc sharded` or a tighter targeted test through `rch`, plus `cargo check -p ffs-mvcc --all-targets` through `rch`, `git diff --check`, `jq empty .beads/issues.jsonl`, `br dep cycles --no-db --no-auto-import --json`, and source-aware hygiene. If RCH remains blocked, keep this bead blocked on `bd-oowwx` and do not use local cargo as proof.
close_reason: Completed: commit and commit_ssi snapshot the effective conflict policy before acquiring shard write locks; focused tests prove policy waits do not pin shard locks and the lock-order watchdog now races policy updates/effective reads with commit, SSI, prune, and snapshot registration paths.

title: the mounted comparator's ext4 parallel-read fixture is also NOT htree-indexed — the same mke2fs -d defect bd-plkzd fixed for readdir+stat, found by completing its audit
description:
The mounted comparator's `parallel-read` fixture carries the SAME `mke2fs -d` htree defect bd-plkzd fixed for `readdir-stat-8t`, and it was found by completing bd-plkzd's own un-done audit item ("whether any OTHER workload whose fixture is populated by create_fixture_tree and consumed through mke2fs -d shares the defect").

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Reproducing the comparator's ext4 construction verbatim at the parallel-read fixture's real shape (256 entries named `read-%06d.bin`), against a second arm that creates the identical entries THROUGH a kernel mount:

  parallel-read   n=256   baked dir Size: 8192
      mke2fs -d : htree_dump: Not a hash-indexed directory
      thru mount: Hash Version: 1

So a real ext4 DOES index this directory and the comparator's does not. 8192 bytes = 2 directory blocks, i.e. the fixture crosses ext4's single-block threshold, which is why the mount arm converts and `mke2fs -d` does not.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, so this is not just "mounting always indexes": at 3 entries (the xattr fixture's shape) NEITHER arm indexes — `Not a hash-indexed directory` on both. The discriminator tracks directory size, as it should.

WHY IT IS IN THE TIMED REGION. `parallel_read_batch` (crates/ffs-harness/src/bin/ffs_mounted_kernel_bench.rs) starts its clock, then `fs::read_dir` + sort, then each of 8 workers does `File::open(path)` per file — 256 full path-based lookups inside the measured window. A linear 2-block directory resolves those by scan; an indexed one does not. And as with readdir+stat, btrfs has no analogue (`mkfs.btrfs -r` produces a normally indexed directory), so the two arms are again built by mechanisms with different indexing outcomes.

MAGNITUDE — stated honestly, and it is NOT the readdir+stat story. This is 2 blocks, not 8192. In the warm `parallel-read-8t` arm the whole directory is page-cached after the readdir that immediately precedes the opens, so the expected effect is small and could plausibly be inside the row's own noise. The arm where it should actually bite is `parallel-read-8t-cold-cache`, which drops caches, so the lookups become real I/O against an unindexed directory. Neither is measured; do not quote a size for this until it is.

ROWS POTENTIALLY AFFECTED
- ext4 `Multi-file parallel read, 256 x 256 KiB` — `1.287862x` (docs/MOUNTED_KERNEL_SCORECARD.md)
- btrfs `Multi-file parallel read` — `0.894290x` / replicate `0.830537x` (docs/MOUNTED_BTRFS_SCORECARD.md). This one deserves attention out of proportion to the defect's likely size: it is the campaign's ONLY honest_win against a real kernel incumbent, so any construction asymmetry that inflates the ext4/kernel side of it must be eliminated before it is defended, not after.

DIRECTION. An unindexed ext4 directory inflates the KERNEL ext4 arm... and also inflates the FrankenFS arm, since both arms read the same fixture shape. That is exactly why it must be measured rather than argued: unlike readdir+stat (where the bd-3zx2x cross-format ratio-of-ratios made the direction analyzable), here both arms of the ext4 comparison see the same unindexed directory, so the ratio effect is second-order and its SIGN is not predictable from the mechanism. Do not assume it cancels.

FIX. The mechanism already exists: bd-plkzd added `seed_readdir_fixture_through_mount`, which seeds through a kernel mount of the base image before `clone_images`, plus `ensure_ext4_large_directory_is_htree_indexed` as a fail-closed control. Extend both to the parallel-read fixture. One complication readdir+stat did not have: these files have CONTENT (256 KiB of deterministic per-index payload from `write_fixture_file`), and the workload asserts a content digest — so the through-the-mount seeding must reproduce those bytes exactly or the digest parity check fails. That is the whole of the extra work.

NOT DONE HERE ON PURPOSE. bd-plkzd asked for the audit; this is the audit's result. Fixing it invalidates two more banked rows and needs its own re-measurement window, so it is filed rather than folded into that bead.

ACCEPTANCE
- the comparator's ext4 parallel-read fixture reports a Hash Version under `debugfs htree_dump`;
- the harness FAILS CLOSED if it does not, by the same control as the large-directory fixture;
- the fixture files' bytes are unchanged (content digest parity holds across the change);
- both parallel-read rows re-measured on a current ELF, old values marked superseded rather than silently replaced.

Probe: /data/tmp/claude-1000/-data-projects-frankenfs/854a9d54-8847-4406-9662-2268b74a5d4f/scratchpad/plkzd_audit.sh (two-arm baked-vs-mounted discriminator with the 3-entry negative control). Worth committing next to scripts/cmp_fixture_probe.sh if this is picked up.
close_reason: All acceptance items delivered. Code fix landed 284f24f2 (SeededFixture generalizes the through-the-mount seeding to both parallel-read variants; payload byte-identical, pinned by test; htree control generalized and its one-block threshold corrected). Pre-measurement confounds cleared by probe rather than assumption: ext4 extent layout identical under both constructions (44909ba3), btrfs layout DIFFERS in ordering — the -r seeder inherits the host's htree hash order (c7a1e6fd) — which disqualifies banked-vs-new comparison but not run-to-run. Rows re-measured on a current ELF: ext4 0.986316x/0.978203x both HONEST_NEUTRAL (a banked LOSS of 1.287862x is actually a TIE; the flip is ~80% incumbent movement, not ours, and the fixture is excluded by direction since an htree makes the 256 lookups cheaper); btrfs 0.893282x/0.927352x both HONEST_WIN in a verified-quiet window, confirming the campaign's only win at 0.11% from its banked value. Both scorecards updated with absolutes and spreads. The btrfs stability question was resolved under bd-ws9dg (closed): the earlier opposite-verdict pair was co-tenant contention, not the fixture.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CODE FIX LANDED. The bead stays OPEN: the re-measurement half is not done, exactly as on bd-plkzd.

WHAT LANDED (crates/ffs-harness/src/bin/ffs_mounted_kernel_bench.rs)
- `create_fixture_tree` now leaves `parallel-read` EMPTY and caller-owned, the same shape bd-plkzd gave `large-directory`. Caller ownership is load-bearing for the same reason: a fresh mkfs root is uid 0 and `mke2fs -d` preserves the host tree's ownership, which is what lets the seeding step write into it without root.
- The seeding path was GENERALIZED rather than copy-pasted. `SeededFixture` (LargeDirectory | ParallelRead) carries the directory name and the per-index entry factory; `seed_readdir_fixture_through_mount` became `seed_fixture_through_mount` and takes it. Both fixtures now go through one code path, so the next fixture that needs this cannot get a subtly different one.
- `SeededFixture::for_workload` maps BOTH parallel-read variants (`ParallelRead8`, `ParallelRead8ColdCache`) onto the shared fixture. Missing the cold-cache variant would have left the arm where the defect actually bites — cold lookups against an unindexed directory are real I/O — still broken.
- The parallel-read payload is byte-for-byte unchanged: the factory calls the SAME `write_fixture_file(path, PARALLEL_READ_FILE_BYTES, index)` the baked path called. This is not incidental — `parallel_read_batch` folds those bytes into a content digest that four-arm parity compares.

THE HTREE CONTROL WAS GENERALIZED AND, IN THE PROCESS, CORRECTED
`ensure_ext4_large_directory_is_htree_indexed` became `ensure_ext4_directory_is_htree_indexed(image, dir)`. It now reads the directory's size from `debugfs stat` first and only REQUIRES an htree when the directory exceeds one 4096-byte block.

That precondition is the control's correctness, not a loophole. ext4 converts a directory to an htree only once it outgrows a single block, so a small directory is legitimately unindexed and a real ext4 would leave it that way. Measured, in the audit: a 3-entry directory reports "Not a hash-indexed directory" whether baked by `mke2fs -d` OR created through a mount, while the 256-entry parallel-read shape (8192 bytes, two blocks) differs between them. The previous unconditional assertion would therefore have FAILED a legitimately small `--operations` run and called a correct filesystem broken. Below the threshold it now prints a note rather than passing silently, because a skipped control that looks like a passing one is the failure mode this whole bead family is about.

TESTS (`cargo test -p ffs-harness --bin ffs-mounted-kernel-bench`: 51 passed, 0 failed, up from 49)
- `only_the_indexable_fixture_directories_are_seeded_through_the_mount_bd_c5210` pins the mapping in BOTH directions: the three affected workloads map to a fixture, and the other six map to None with the reason recorded per workload. The negative half is the point — it encodes the audit result so a future workload cannot quietly join the list without someone deciding it should.
- `seeding_parallel_read_through_the_mount_writes_the_same_bytes_as_before_bd_c5210` compares the factory's output against the verbatim pre-change call at four indices, asserting byte-identical payloads, unchanged size, and unchanged names.

ACCEPTANCE STATUS
  [x] the harness FAILS CLOSED if the ext4 parallel-read directory is not hash-indexed (above the one-block threshold where that is the correct expectation)
  [x] the fixture files' bytes are unchanged — pinned by test, not asserted in prose
  [ ] the comparator's ext4 parallel-read fixture OBSERVED reporting a Hash Version in a real run
  [ ] both parallel-read rows re-measured, old values marked superseded

The two open items need the full gated comparator run, which is the same blocker bd-plkzd, bd-4sull item 1 and bd-o6iiw all sit behind. Note that bd-o6iiw's recipe turns out to be stale — the banked PGO profile is gone, so that build is a full ~20 min train, not ~5.

Until the run lands, the banked ext4 `1.287862x` and btrfs `0.894290x` / `0.830537x` parallel-read rows remain measured on the old fixture path. The btrfs one is the campaign's only honest_win, so it should not be defended until it is re-measured on the corrected fixture.

MAGNITUDE STILL UNMEASURED, deliberately unguessed. 2 directory blocks, not 8192; page-cached in the warm arm; and both ext4 arms read the same unindexed fixture, so the sign of the ratio effect does not follow from the mechanism.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
PRE-MEASUREMENT CHECK: the fixture change does NOT alter the ext4 extent layout, so the index is the only variable on the ext4 side.

WHY THIS NEEDED CHECKING AND readdir+stat DID NOT. The readdir+stat fixture is 32,768 ZERO-BYTE entries — there is no file data, so moving creation from `mke2fs -d` to a mount can only change the directory index. The parallel-read fixture is different: 256 files of 256 KiB each, and the workload is a READ benchmark. If through-the-mount creation laid the data out differently, any re-measurement would carry a second, independent confound on top of the index, and I would not be able to separate them afterwards.

MEASURED (probe: /data/tmp/ffs-extent-layout-probe/probe.sh, four 256 KiB files, same names the harness uses):

    read-000000.bin  baked  (mke2fs -d)   EXTENTS: (0-63):2160-2223
                     seeded (thru mount)  EXTENTS: (0-63):32896-32959
    read-000001.bin  baked                EXTENTS: (0-63):2224-2287
                     seeded               EXTENTS: (0-63):32960-33023

Both constructions produce ONE contiguous 64-block extent per file, with consecutive files physically adjacent. Fragmentation is identical (1 extent each); only the absolute starting offset differs, because `mke2fs -d` packs near the start of the device and the mount allocates further in. On an SSD-backed loop file that offset difference is immaterial, and it is not a difference in structure.

CONCLUSION FOR THE UPCOMING RE-MEASUREMENT: on ext4, the directory index is the ONLY thing bd-c5210's fix changes for this workload. A movement in the ext4 parallel-read row can be reasoned about as an indexing effect (plus the usual ELF/PGO/kernel/window confounds that apply to every re-measurement).

⚠ NOT VERIFIED FOR BTRFS, and it matters more there. `debugfs` is ext4-only, so this probe says nothing about `mkfs.btrfs -r` versus through-the-mount allocation, and btrfs is COW with its own extent allocator — a layout difference is more plausible there than on ext4. The btrfs parallel-read row is the campaign's ONLY honest_win, so if that number moves, the layout question must be settled before anything is concluded. Do not assume this ext4 result transfers.

The seeded layout is PERFECTLY ASCENDING in name order. The baked layout is scrambled.

WHY THAT MATTERS FOR THIS SPECIFIC WORKLOAD: `parallel_read_batch` does `read_dir`, then SORTS the paths by name, then 8 workers pread them in that sorted order. So under the seeded fixture the read sequence walks the disk forwards; under the baked fixture it jumps around. For a read benchmark with kernel readahead in play, those are materially different jobs.

MECHANISM, verified rather than guessed: `mkfs.btrfs -r` copies the seed tree in HOST READDIR order, and the host directory here is ext4 with an htree, so readdir returns HASH order. Listing the seed tree with `ls -U` gives read-000001, read-000002, read-000000, read-000003 ... — scrambled exactly as the physical layout is. The btrfs image therefore inherits the host filesystem's hash order as its physical layout.

NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WITH EXT4, which is why the earlier ext4 probe did not predict this: `mke2fs -d` lays the same files out in ascending name order under BOTH constructions (2160-2223 then 2224-2287 baked; 32896-32959 then 32960-33023 seeded). The two mkfs tools differ, so the ext4 result genuinely did not transfer — as flagged.

CONSEQUENCES, split precisely:

1. FOR THE 6.09% RUN-1-vs-RUN-2 SPREAD: cause 3 is ELIMINATED. Both new runs used the seeded construction and therefore byte-identical images with identical layout. Layout cannot explain a disagreement between two runs that shared a fixture. That leaves cause 1 (co-tenant load) and cause 2 (intrinsic row variance), and cause 1 remains the leading candidate.

2. FOR THE BANKED WINS vs THE NEW NUMBERS: cause 3 is CONFIRMED as a disqualifying confound. The banked 0.894290x / 0.830537x were measured against a physically SCRAMBLED fixture; the new 1.019622x / 0.961107x against a SEQUENTIAL one. Those are not the same benchmark, so the movement from "win" to "unresolved" cannot be read as a change in FrankenFS at all. The old numbers should be treated as describing a workload the harness no longer runs.

WHICH CONSTRUCTION IS RIGHT? The seeded one, and this is not a close call — a real btrfs filesystem populated by writing files has them laid out in write order, not in some other filesystem's hash order. bd-c5210's fix made the fixture more realistic on btrfs as well as fixing ext4's index. But it means the btrfs parallel-read row must be re-baselined from scratch rather than compared to its predecessor.

STILL OPEN on bd-ws9dg: the quiet-window re-run (cause 1) and, if the spread survives it, the question of whether this row is decidable by this instrument at 128 pairs (cause 2).

title: fuzz: no dedicated fuzz target for ext4 casefold key/collide/diagnostics
description:
Finding (via /testing-fuzzing skill, NEW target): fuzz/fuzz_targets/ has 47 targets but NONE dedicated to the ext4 casefold collision contract — ext4_casefold_key, ext4_casefold_names_collide, ext4_casefold_name_diagnostics. fuzz_ext4_checksums covers casefold tangentially via lookup_in_dir_block_casefold (it constructs a single fixed search key b"Test_File" and asserts determinism for that key against block-shaped input), but the casefold *function itself* — the byte-level fold — never receives arbitrary fuzzed input.

The casefold fold has UTF-8/ASCII-fallback branching, multi-codepoint sharp-s expansion (ß/ẞ -> 'ss'), and produces a Vec<u8> that the directory-lookup path treats as the canonical comparison key. A bug in any branch would silently mis-classify directory entries on case-folded ext4 filesystems.

The newly-shipped bd-6rsow proptest verifies the equivalence-relation laws on 32 random byte sequences. A dedicated fuzz target lifts that to >1M iterations with libfuzzer corpus learning across mutations of multi-byte UTF-8 boundaries, ASCII edge cases, and byte sequences that look almost-but-not-quite UTF-8.

Acceptance: new fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_ext4_casefold.rs that, for arbitrary byte input, asserts:
  * ext4_casefold_key(name) never panics
  * ext4_casefold_names_collide(name, name) is reflexive
  * ext4_casefold_key(ext4_casefold_key(name)) == ext4_casefold_key(name) (idempotence)
  * ext4_casefold_name_diagnostics(name).folded_key == ext4_casefold_key(name)
  * ext4_casefold_name_diagnostics(name).source_len == name.len()
  * Symmetry on a split-input pair: collide(a, b) == collide(b, a)
Plus a [[bin]] entry in fuzz/Cargo.toml so cargo-fuzz can drive it.
close_reason: done

title: [MOCK-FINDER] btrfs_ino_lookup only supports root objectid; non-root returns ENOENT with 'not implemented yet' comment
description:
# Mock-finder audit finding

`FsOps::btrfs_ino_lookup` at crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:16062-16082 only returns a path for `objectid == BTRFS_FIRST_FREE_OBJECTID (256)` and falls through to `Err(FfsError::Io(libc::ENOENT))` for every other inode, with the comment: `// Full back-reference walking not implemented yet.`

## Context

The prior bead bd-jfsga ('add BTRFS_IOC_INO_LOOKUP ioctl support') was closed 2026-04-21 as 'done' with acceptance criterion 'BTRFS_IOC_INO_LOOKUP returns correct path for known inodes'. The current implementation satisfies that criterion only for the single well-known root objectid; every other known inode returns ENOENT indistinguishable from 'inode does not exist'. Callers (btrfs-progs, user scripts) cannot tell the difference between 'this inode genuinely doesn't exist' and 'this file doesn't implement lookup for non-root inodes'.

## Evidence

- Backend: crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:16062-16082
- FUSE dispatcher wiring: crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:2100-2125 (correctly routes the ioctl)
- Comment verbatim: 'Full back-reference walking not implemented yet.'

## Why this is a real stub, not an intentional scope limit

Unlike write-participating MMP (crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:6531) and e2compr lzv1/lzrw3a/bzip2 (6989, 7955), which surface a bespoke `UnsupportedFeature` error with a clear scope message, this path returns a generic ENOENT that masks the limitation from callers and from conformance tools.

## Fix direction

Walk the btrfs INODE_REF / INODE_EXTREF back-references chain from the target objectid up to the tree root, assembling path components in reverse. Reference implementation: fs/btrfs/ioctl.c::btrfs_search_path_in_tree in Linux v6.19. For v1 scope, supporting only same-subvolume paths (no cross-subvolume) is acceptable if documented.

## Acceptance

- Non-root objectid that exists in the subvolume tree returns its reconstructed path.
- Non-existent objectid returns a structured NotFound / FfsError that the FUSE layer maps to ENOENT (current behavior preserved for truly-missing inodes).
- Unit + mounted-path test that resolves a file created at runtime and asserts the returned path matches.
- If cross-subvolume resolution is out of scope, emit `UnsupportedFeature('cross-subvolume btrfs_ino_lookup not implemented')` with a distinct errno mapping instead of ENOENT.
close_reason: Implemented in commit f70dcca. btrfs_ino_lookup (crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:16051) now walks INODE_REF back-references from the target objectid up to the subvolume root, assembling a /-separated path with trailing / before the terminating NUL (matches fs/btrfs/ioctl.c::btrfs_search_path_in_tree). Algorithm extracted as pure helper btrfs_build_path_from_inode_refs for unit-testability; 6 new tests cover subvolume root, single hop, multi-hop a/b/c/, missing back-ref → NotFound, cycle → Corruption, and hard-link first-wins determinism. Cross-subvolume (ROOT_REF) remains out-of-V1-scope but now returns UnsupportedFeature with a clear message rather than silent ENOENT. All 6 new tests + existing ffs-core suite pass via rch; workspace clippy green.

title: [HIGH] build_btrfs_readdir_image still computes invalid tree_block_csum after explicit stamping
description:
# Review finding

The current `build_btrfs_readdir_image()` fixture already writes explicit CRC32C values into both synthetic tree blocks, but `rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_frankenfs_cod cargo test --workspace --all-targets` still fails the six btrfs directory-walk tests with `Format("invalid field: tree_block_csum (CRC32C checksum mismatch)")`.

## Evidence
- Builder already stamps both blocks: `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:23225-23378`.
- It computes `csum_root` and `csum_fs` over `image[tree + 0x20 .. tree + nodesize]` and writes them to bytes `0..4`.
- After `br-bd-o5114 repair btrfs default-root smoke fixture`, the remaining red frontier is exactly:
  - `walk_btrfs_dir_entry_items_includes_dir_index_items`
  - `btrfs_readdir_mixed_types`
  - `btrfs_readdir_empty_directory_returns_dot_dotdot`
  - `btrfs_readdir_sorted_by_index`
  - `btrfs_readdir_offset_pagination`
  - `btrfs_readdir_special_characters_in_names`
- All six still fail on the same checksum mismatch, so the root cause is no longer "missing stamp calls".

## Why this is high severity
This keeps the full workspace test gate red and shows the older broad review bead is now under-specified. The next implementation pass needs to debug the actual checksum semantics, not just add stamp writes.

## Expected fix direction
Audit the exact checksum window, node header fields, and final byte mutations for the 16 KiB synthetic readdir fixture. Verify the bytes being hashed match what the parser later validates.
close_reason: Already shipped; targeted btrfs readdir repros now pass

title: btrfs fiemap reports explicit hole extents (disk_bytenr==0) as physical-0 extents instead of gaps
description: btrfs_fiemap (lib.rs ~25198) iterates every EXTENT_DATA item and pushes a FiemapExtent for each, including explicit hole extents (Regular, disk_bytenr==0) found on kernel-created images WITHOUT the NO_HOLES feature. A hole is then reported as a real extent with physical==0 and no flags, so filefrag / cp --sparse / tar / qemu-img see the hole as data backed by physical block 0 instead of an unmapped gap. Linux fiemap never reports holes — they are simply gaps between returned extents (fiemap_fill_next_extent is only called for real extents). Inconsistent with btrfs_read_file (zero-fills disk_bytenr==0) and the just-fixed SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE (bd-pb6bs). Prealloc (BTRFS_FILE_EXTENT_PREALLOC, disk_bytenr!=0) is correctly reported FIEMAP_EXTENT_UNWRITTEN. FrankenFS-written files use IMPLICIT holes (punch/insert remove/shift extents, no disk_bytenr==0 item) so this only bites kernel images. FIX: filter disk_bytenr==0 hole extents (Self::btrfs_extent_is_hole) before the map loop so holes become gaps and FIEMAP_EXTENT_LAST lands on the last real extent. ext4 unaffected (implicit-gap holes).
close_reason: Fixed in 40fef847: btrfs_fiemap filters disk_bytenr==0 explicit hole extents (btrfs_extent_is_hole) before mapping, so holes are gaps not physical-0 extents, and FIEMAP_EXTENT_LAST lands on the last real extent. Matches btrfs_read_file + SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE (bd-pb6bs). Prealloc stays FIEMAP_EXTENT_UNWRITTEN. Regression btrfs_fiemap_skips_explicit_hole_extent_bd_cfjvh. ffs-core 1046/0; clippy clean.

title: btrfs commit: loaded chunk/dev/uuid/free_space tree extents lose backrefs across load+rewrite (bd-x36qn lever B)
description: On a real-image commit, btrfs check reports 'tree extent[X] root N has no backref item' + 'ref mismatch extent item 0, found 1' for N in {3=chunk_tree, 4=dev_tree, 9=uuid_tree, 10=free_space_tree, -9=data_reloc} — i.e. the trees FrankenFS does NOT rewrite. Their blocks (X BELOW FrankenFS's alloc range, e.g. 22036480) exist in the original on-disk extent tree with proper EXTENT_ITEM+backref, but after FrankenFS loads the extent tree (load_btrfs_alloc_state walks EXTENT_TREE ROOT_ITEM.bytenr) and fully rewrites it at commit, btrfs check finds no extent item for them -> they appear to be DROPPED across load+reserialize. HYPOTHESES to check (instrument load): (1) the extent-tree walk loads few/zero items (extent_root resolution or walk_btrfs_tree fails silently -> empty rewritten extent tree); (2) load inserts items with .is_ok() and silently drops on key collision; (3) walk_btrfs_tree returns METADATA_ITEM values truncated to 24 bytes, dropping inline refs; (4) the rewrite omits loaded items. NEXT: add a temporary count (loaded EXTENT_ITEM/METADATA_ITEM + TREE_BLOCK_REF item counts) in load_btrfs_alloc_state and in the extent_tree right before serialize, run the harness, compare to the original tree's item count. If load is dropping them, fix the load/preserve; then the 'root N' no-backref errors should clear. Note: prerequisite format fixes already landed — skinny key offset=level (d3f7f552) + inline TREE_BLOCK_REF (33389555). Sibling lever: bd-x36qn lever A (self-allocated tree-node EXTENT_ITEMs).
notes: ROOT-CAUSED + partially fixed via btrfs-progs dump-tree ground truth (4d87d924). The 'loaded extents lose backrefs' framing was WRONG: dump-tree shows FrankenFS's committed extent tree items are PERFECTLY formed with correct inline TREE_BLOCK_REFs (chunk/dev/uuid/free-space all present and correct). The real defect: FrankenFS rewrites root/extent/fs/csum wholesale at fresh addresses each commit but never removed the OLD nodes' extent items — so the tree carried stale backrefs for unreferenced blocks (e.g. a gen-8 EXTENT_TREE self-item at one addr while the live extent leaf is at another), POISONING btrfs check's refcount walk so it reported 'no backref' even for the correctly-described unchanged trees. FIX: remove_metadata_items_owned_by_roots drops the to-be-rewritten trees' old items at commit start. Verified via dump-tree: stale gen-5/7/8 items gone, extent tree now describes only live blocks. The 5 'loaded-extent no backref' errors were thus a CASCADE, now traced to its source. Residual is purely bd-myrgc (the 2 self-nodes). Closing as the cascade is understood + the orphan source fixed; the remaining count reduction is bd-myrgc's self-node completion.

title: Restore btrfs multi-device RAID corpus and degraded-mode proof
description:
Fresh review follow-up from the closed bd-nzv3.24 lane. That historical bead was closed with the note that the multi-image layout corpus was deferred and single-device tests covered the read path. That is not enough for users if docs, parity reports, proof bundles, or future agents infer multi-device readiness from the closed status.

Scope: restore the missing multi-device corpus and degraded-mode evidence as explicit work. The target is a reproducible btrfs multi-image proof surface for healthy profile assembly, degraded or missing-device handling, unsupported-profile refusal, deterministic device ordering, chunk/stripe mapping visibility, repair/scrub interaction boundaries, and operator remediation. The goal is not to overclaim full btrfs RAID parity; it is to make the supported and unsupported envelope measurable and safe.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/schema tests validate a multi-device scenario manifest with profile, device count, device ids, device order, image hashes, chunk layout, stripe mapping, missing/degraded state, expected read/write boundary, repair/scrub boundary, unsupported-profile classification, cleanup policy, and artifact requirements.
2. Unit tests cover healthy profile assembly, device-order permutations, missing device, duplicate device id, stale superblock/device metadata, unsupported RAID/profile, degraded read where declared supported, write refusal where unsupported, and remediation text generation.
3. E2E or harness smoke builds or consumes at least one reproducible healthy multi-image fixture, one missing-device fixture, and one unsupported-profile fixture; it emits pass/fail/skip/error artifacts without requiring destructive host operations by default.
4. Logs include scenario id, profile, device ids, image hashes, chunk/stripe mapping summary, mount or parser mode, degraded-state decision, expected outcome, observed outcome, remediation id, artifact paths, cleanup status, and reproduction command.
5. README, FEATURE_PARITY, release gates, and proof bundles cannot claim multi-device support from single-device tests alone; missing or deferred multi-image evidence must downgrade the claim or link this bead as the owning gap.

title: ffs-mvcc: WalWriter::append_commit + rollback_failed_append have implicit append-only reasoning mode
description:
Finding (via /modes-of-reasoning-project-analysis skill, third
visit, different target): `WalWriter::append_commit`
(crates/ffs-mvcc/src/wal_writer.rs:310) has inline `// ── D1 ──`,
`// ── D8 ──`, etc. dividers naming individual invariants
(strict monotonicity, sentinel rejection, backpressure, etc.) but
**no function-level doc block** that names the OVERARCHING
reasoning mode the function implements:

  **Append-only with strict-monotonic sequence check, plus
  atomic-rollback on any failure between encoded-write and synced
  state.**

The partner helper `rollback_failed_append` (l. 627) reverts THREE
state pieces on failure but is private with no doc:

  1. `write_pos` — reset to the pre-append offset
  2. file length — truncated via `set_len(write_offset)` (best-
     effort, ignored result)
  3. `appends_since_sync` — restored to pre-append value

There is also an INLINE rollback path inside `append_commit` for
verify failure (l. 411-412) that resets only `write_pos` and
truncates the file — NOT `appends_since_sync`, because the
`increment_pending_sync_count` happens AFTER verify (l. 419). This
is intentional but easy to miss — a future contributor moving the
verify check after the increment, or adding new pre-sync state,
might forget to reset it on verify failure.

Same shape as bd-gqswx (in-memory commit_internal +
rollback_in_memory_commit) and bd-3ydm6 (is_reserved_inode
fail-closed): a critical reasoning mode applied without naming.

Acceptance: function-level doc blocks on `append_commit` and
`rollback_failed_append` naming the **append-only with
strict-monotonic sequence check + atomic-rollback** mode, listing
the three state pieces the rollback covers, and explicitly calling
out the two-rollback-paths invariant (the inline verify-failure
rollback is sufficient because the sync counter has not been
incremented yet; any new pre-sync state added between verify and
sync MUST be reset on verify failure too). NO behavioural change.
notes: Shipped: function-level doc blocks on WalWriter::append_commit and rollback_failed_append in crates/ffs-mvcc/src/wal_writer.rs naming the append-only + strict-monotonic + atomic-rollback reasoning mode. Documents the three state pieces rollback_failed_append covers (write_pos, file length, appends_since_sync) and explicitly calls out the two-rollback-paths invariant: (1) verify-failure inline rollback only resets write_pos and file length because the sync counter has NOT been incremented yet; (2) post-counter sync-failure delegates to rollback_failed_append. Any new failure path or reordering that puts the increment before verify MUST update both rollback paths to keep the WAL invariant. Pure documentation diff — no behavioural change. Pairs with bd-gqswx (in-memory commit_internal atomic-or-rollback) and bd-3ydm6 (fail-closed reasoning). Verified via rch exec -- cargo check -p ffs-mvcc --lib (Finished in 33.27s).

title: Source-scoped tracker hygiene for FrankenFS agent triage
description:
## Background
FrankenFS agent triage currently sees open `br-r37-c1-*` and `franken_networkx-*` rows in `.beads/issues.jsonl`. Those rows do not describe FrankenFS code, but `br ready --no-db` and `bv --robot-triage` still surface them as actionable work. That misroutes agents, hides the true state of the FrankenFS queue, and makes stalled/open-count audits unreliable.

## Idea-wizard phase summary
Phase 2 generated 30 improvement ideas for making FrankenFS more robust for massive multi-agent work. The top five after rubric scoring were: source-scoped tracker hygiene, permissioned-run readiness packets, proof-bundle lane freshness hardening, adaptive runtime evidence dashboards, and non-mutating foreign-row reconciliation. Phase 3 added ten complementary ideas: source-prefix triage wrappers, JSONL quarantine reports, stale-agent row audits, tracker import health probes, cross-project contamination fixtures, mail-to-bead handoff packets, no-db recovery playbooks, source-aware bv recipes, deterministic open-count reports, and cleanup authorization ledgers. Phase 4 overlap checks found related closed tracker-source diagnostics and dotted-ID work, but no open bead for foreign-row pollution in the current FrankenFS tracker.

## Goal
Create a non-destructive tracker hygiene lane that detects, reports, and eventually quarantines cross-project rows without deleting data or obscuring audit history.

## Non-goals
Do not delete foreign rows, rewrite history, or mutate rows that may belong to another project without an explicit reconciliation plan. Do not change Beads itself inside this repo.

## Success
Future agents can distinguish true FrankenFS ready work from foreign tracker pollution using checked-in reports, a documented playbook, and tests that prevent the issue from silently recurring.
close_reason: Completed: all source-scoped tracker hygiene children are closed with non-destructive reports, fixtures, source-aware ready-work wrapper, reconciliation playbook, and foreign group owner summaries.

title: perf(btrfs): bulk durable write fails with EINVAL on fsync — the whole workload is UNRUNNABLE on btrfs, same class as bd-ftev0
description:
Measured 2026-08-05 (SapphireBirch). ffs-mounted-kernel-bench --workload bulk-durable-write --filesystem btrfs dies 12 seconds in, before any timed measurement:

  mounted_kernel_gate,error=fsync bulk durable workload /tmp/frankenfs-mounted-kernel-mounts/run_1785978261_4159855/btrfs/fuse_a/bulk-durable.bin: Invalid argument (os error 22)

Reproduce exactly:
  ffs-mounted-kernel-bench --ffs-cli <PGO+v3 ffs-cli> --workload bulk-durable-write --filesystem btrfs --operations 64 --observation-repeats 1 --image-size-mib 1024 --pairs 512 --harness-builder <host> --candidate-builder <host>
Candidate ELF bcf2bc80f02154aa16681b87c64e1beddab996b20cc0bb5ec911b5743133c9d1, kernel 6.17.0-41-generic. The ext4 arm of the identical invocation runs fine (it reaches a full 512-pair measurement), so this is btrfs-path specific, not harness-specific.

The workload is: preallocate one file, overwrite it with 64 sequential 1 MiB positioned writes, then ONE fsync on the file. EINVAL on that fsync (or on the write that precedes it) is the same shape of defect as bd-ftev0, where btrfs mount seeded block-group used_bytes from the chunk map and any image-resident extent free underflowed to EIO on the first positioned write. bd-ftev0 is CLOSED, so this is either a second, distinct accounting/validation path or a regression on the same one — determine which BEFORE proposing a fix.

WHY IT MATTERS: it blocks an entire scorecard row. bd-bulk-durable-write-unscored-orfck wants a banked row per filesystem; ext4 can produce one (it needs ~2048 pairs because the durability boundary is the variance source) and btrfs currently cannot produce one at all.

ACCEPTANCE: either (a) fix the EINVAL, with a regression test at the layer that returns it, and then produce the banked btrfs row; or (b) prove it is a genuine unsupported-operation answer rather than a bug, in which case the scorecard records btrfs bulk durable write as UNRUNNABLE with this error text, the way the btrfs fsync row was recorded. Do not paper over it by dropping the fsync from the workload — the fsync IS the workload.
close_reason: Fixed in 839eb708: growing-replace split + delete-rebalance byte guard. Mounted 32 MiB and full 64 MiB write->fsync->unmount->remount all pass byte-identical; 5 new tests with a negative control proving the gate bites; ffs-btrfs 381 pass; clippy/fmt at or better than clean-HEAD baseline.

comments.author: SapphireBirch
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND REPRODUCED DETERMINISTICALLY. Not fixed — this is the diagnosis, with the boundary measured and a regression-test target.

IT IS NOT FSYNC, AND NOT BTRFS-WRITE-IN-GENERAL. The daemon's own record, with tracing raised:

  WARN ffs_fuse: FUSE op failed op="fsync" ino=257 errno=22
       error=invalid on-disk format: btrfs mutation: invalid config: node overflow: data

Every pwrite returns success; the failure lands on fsync because the writes are buffered and the durable commit is what actually serializes them. The error comes from the leaf serializer in crates/ffs-btrfs/src/lib.rs:3153 — "node overflow: data" — which correctly refuses to write items past the end of one node. The DEFECT IS ITS CALLER: OpenFs::btrfs_full_transaction_commit builds a single leaf per tree and never splits it, so a commit whose item set exceeds one 16 KiB node cannot be written at all.

MEASURED BOUNDARY (fresh 1 GiB image and mount per point, 1 MiB positioned writes into a 64 MiB preallocated file, then one fsync):

   1 MiB  fsync OK        17 MiB  fsync OK
   2 MiB  fsync OK        18 MiB  fsync OK        <-- last passing
   4 MiB  fsync OK        20 MiB  fsync FAILED errno=22   <-- first failing
   8 MiB  fsync OK        22 MiB  fsync FAILED errno=22
  16 MiB  fsync OK        24/32/48/64 MiB  FAILED errno=22

So the ceiling is between 18 and 20 MiB of dirty data in a single transaction. That is consistent with the mechanism: btrfs caps a data extent at 128 KiB, so each 1 MiB overwrite produces 8 FILE_EXTENT_ITEMs; a 16 KiB leaf minus its 101-byte header holds roughly 200 items at 25 bytes of descriptor plus 53 bytes of payload each, and ~19 MiB x 8 items/MiB lands right at that ceiling alongside the inode and directory items sharing the leaf.

THE ext4 ARM OF THE SAME PROBE PASSES at every size, which is why the comparator sees ext4 complete and btrfs die.

SECOND SYMPTOM, SAME CAUSE: the failure is not confined to the fsync reply. On unmount the daemon also logs
  btrfs_destroy_commit_rejected ... error_class="destroy_commit_failed"
  flush_on_destroy failed during FUSE destroy: invalid on-disk format: btrfs mutation: invalid config: node overflow: data
so the dirty data is never persisted at all — a silent durability hole for any workload that writes more than ~18 MiB between commits, not merely a failed syscall.

REPRODUCTION (no comparator needed, ~40 s):
  1. 64 MiB file of 0xB7 in a seed dir; mkfs.btrfs -f -q -r <seed> <1 GiB image>
  2. ffs-cli mount --rw <image> <mountpoint under /tmp>   (fusermount3 refuses /data/tmp)
  3. open O_RDWR, 20 x os.pwrite of 1 MiB at i*1MiB, then os.fsync -> errno 22
  Script kept at /data/tmp/claude-1000/-data-projects-frankenfs/7dbaf32b-1ce3-4b43-8573-01adfa71e48e/scratchpad/repro_cjqhh2.sh and bisect_cjqhh.sh.

ACCEPTANCE, UNCHANGED IN SPIRIT BUT NOW SPECIFIC: the fix is leaf splitting in the durable commit path, so a transaction whose items exceed one node writes multiple leaves and an internal node above them. crates/ffs-btrfs already has COW leaf-split machinery ("btrfs_cow_leaf_split" at lib.rs:4490, with adversarial allocator-failure tests at 12553/12589); the durable-commit path does not use it. The regression test writes >18 MiB in one transaction and asserts fsync succeeds AND the data is readable after remount — the second half matters because of the destroy-path symptom above.

DO NOT "fix" this by capping the workload or by dropping the fsync: the comparator's bulk durable write job is 64 MiB by design and the ext4 arm completes it, so shrinking the job would hide a real durability limit rather than measure it.

SCOPE NOTE: this bounds every btrfs write workload, not just this row. bd-btrfs-parallel-meta-1p93x and bd-btrfs-create-delete-storm-2p36x pass today only because their per-transaction footprints stay under the ceiling.

comments.author: PlumRiver
comments.text:
FIXED AND LANDED in 839eb708. Acceptance path (a): EINVAL fixed, regression tests at the layer
that returned it, and the workload now completes.

ROOT CAUSE WAS TWO DEFECTS, and the diagnosis on this bead named only the first. Both are in the
COW tree, both reached by the same overwrite workload:

1. A replace that GROWS an item never split (this bead's diagnosis, correct as far as it went).
   `insert_into_leaf`'s replace branch returned `split: None` unconditionally.

2. THE ONE THAT ACTUALLY FIRED: delete-rebalance merged two byte-full leaves. `EXTENT_CSUM` items
   are ~1 KiB and up (a max-size one is 16,281 bytes against the 16,283-byte budget), so csum
   leaves sit permanently below `min_items` and every delete looked like an underflow.
   `rebalance_child` merged neighbours on ITEM COUNT alone. Overwriting a file frees its old
   extents -> deletes their checksums -> merged two full csum leaves into a 17,833-byte leaf that
   could not be serialized.

The bead's proposed fix — "use the existing btrfs_cow_leaf_split machinery in the durable commit
path" — was not what was needed. The commit path was fine and the split machinery was already
wired; the tree was building unserializable leaves before the commit ever ran, via the delete
path. Fixing only defect 1 left fsync still failing, which I measured rather than assumed.

EVIDENCE, MOUNTED, REAL FUSE, WRITE -> FSYNC -> UNMOUNT -> REMOUNT -> READ BACK:
  32 MiB: fsync OK, no destroy-path rejection, all 32 chunks byte-identical after remount
  64 MiB (the full comparator job shape): fsync OK, all 64 chunks byte-identical after remount
Intermediate state with only defect 1 fixed: same 32 MiB run still failed, with the new
structured error naming the tree — "tree owner 7 level 0 has 17 items needing 17934 bytes in a
16384-byte node". Owner 7 is the csum tree; that is what redirected the investigation.

Baseline for comparison, from this bead: 18 MiB passed, 20 MiB failed.

GATES: 5 new unit tests in ffs-btrfs (381 passed, was 376). NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: with the two
rebalance predicates neutralised, `delete_does_not_merge_leaves_past_the_byte_budget_bd_cjqhh`
fails with the same overflow class, so the gate bites rather than merely passing. clippy at the
exact clean-HEAD baseline (20 sites, none in changed regions); fmt --check now 0 where clean HEAD
was 1.

SCOPE NOTE FROM THIS BEAD IS DISCHARGED: "this bounds every btrfs write workload, not just this
row." It did, and the bound is gone for all of them, not just bulk-durable-write.

TWO THINGS THIS TURNED UP THAT ARE NOT THIS BEAD:
- bd-72tn8 (new, P1): `btrfs_reflink_random_matches_reference_model` finds a REAL data divergence
  (122 bytes wrong at offset 184198) reproducible byte-for-byte on CLEAN HEAD at
  PROPTEST_CASES=512. It fails ~never at default cases, which is why it reads as flaky. Also:
  crates/ffs-core/proptest-regressions/ is UNTRACKED, so every counterexample proptest has ever
  found in that crate has been thrown away.
- The remaining ffs-core failure, `fast_commit_del_range_apply_punches_and_frees_passes_e2fsck`,
  also fails on clean HEAD and is unrelated to this work.

STILL OPEN, DELIBERATELY NOT DONE HERE: the banked btrfs bulk-durable-write scorecard row. The
workload now runs, so the row is producible, but a comparator run needs a quiet window and a
v3+PGO build; it is measurement, not this fix. bd-2i2ez is the sibling ext4 row.

comments.author: PlumRiver
comments.text:
THIRD ACCEPTANCE ARM: the scorecard text is corrected (1ea814fa); the ROW itself is still not
produced, and I am not claiming it.

The file still read "Btrfs bulk durable write: UNRUNNABLE ... by a DEFECT" because it was last
touched before this bead was fixed. That is now corrected to UNMEASURED, with the distinction
stated explicitly: the defect is gone, the capability is proven (a mounted 64 MiB run — the full
comparator job shape — completes with fsync OK and every chunk byte-identical across unmount and
remount), and what is missing is a measurement, not a capability.

WHAT IS STILL OWED: the banked btrfs bulk-durable-write ratio. It needs a quiet window and a
v3+PGO build, and per the header now on both scorecards it must be taken on a CURRENT ELF — every
existing row predates HEAD, and this bead's own fix plus 241093de/9d64f4a1/7fac4779 all sit in the
btrfs write path. Measuring it against the old frozen candidate would produce a number that
describes a binary that no longer exists.

Reopening is not warranted — the fix and its regression gates are landed and verified — but the
scorecard row remains outstanding work under the perf umbrella and should not be assumed done
because this bead is closed.

5. **Scenarios 13 (CLI ergonomics) and 14 (structured logging traceability) have no evidence.**

## Required deliverables

### A. The script (`scripts/e2e/ffs_v12_program_gate_e2e.sh`)

- [ ] Author the script under `scripts/e2e/`, sourcing `lib.sh` and following project conventions used by the existing `ffs_program_gate_e2e.sh` (V1.1 13-scenario gate, P0 reference).

title: Harden block alignment normalization against overflow
description: AlignedVec alignment normalization rounds non-power-of-two requests with usize::next_power_of_two(). Extreme requested alignments above the largest representable power of two can overflow/panic before the block layer can handle the request. Clamp to the largest representable power-of-two alignment and add a regression test that covers oversized requests without allocating.
close_reason: Completed: block alignment normalization now uses checked rounding and clamps oversized requests to the largest representable power-of-two alignment, with regression coverage.

title: Add GitHub Actions CI workflow for fmt/check/clippy/test gates
description:
## What
Create .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs all quality gates on every push to main and on PRs.

## Why
Currently all gates (cargo fmt --check, cargo check --workspace --all-targets, cargo clippy
--workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace) run manually. Regressions
can be committed undetected. CI automation is the single highest-leverage improvement.

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1: Create .github/workflows/ci.yml
- Trigger: push to main, pull_request to main
- OS: ubuntu-latest (FUSE-dependent; no macOS/Windows)
- Rust: install via dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly (per rust-toolchain.toml)
- System deps: apt-get install libfuse3-dev fuse3 (for fuser crate)
- Cache: actions/cache for ~/.cargo/registry, ~/.cargo/git, target/

### Step 2: Define CI jobs
Job 1 — fmt-check:
  cargo fmt --check

Job 2 — check-clippy:
  cargo check --workspace --all-targets
  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

Job 3 — test:
  cargo test --workspace
  cargo test --workspace --all-features (separate step, catches feature-gated issues)

Job 4 — test-e2e (optional, needs privileged):
  Only if /dev/fuse available
  cargo test -p ffs-harness --test fuse_e2e -- --test-threads=1

### Step 3: Add CI status badge to README.md
Replace or add alongside existing badges:
  [![CI](https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankenfs/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](...)

### Step 4: Verify CI works
- Create a test branch, push it, verify Actions run
- Intentionally break something (add a clippy warning), verify CI catches it
- Fix and verify green

## Considerations
- rust-toolchain.toml pins nightly — CI must respect this (dtolnay/rust-toolchain reads it)
- E2E FUSE tests skip gracefully when /dev/fuse unavailable (tested: fuse_e2e.rs line 225)
- Build time estimate: ~2min check+clippy, ~1min tests (from rch timings)
- asupersync has no special CI requirements (pure Rust, no system deps beyond FUSE)
- Cargo.lock should be committed for reproducible CI builds
- Consider: actions/cache key should include rust-toolchain.toml hash for cache invalidation

## Test Plan
- Push to a test branch and verify all 4 jobs run
- Verify FUSE E2E tests either run (if privileged) or skip (if not) without failing
- Verify cache hits on second push reduce build time
- Verify intentional failure (e.g., add unused variable) is caught by clippy job

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] .github/workflows/ci.yml exists and is valid YAML
- [ ] CI runs on every push to main and on PRs
- [ ] All 4 gates (fmt, check, clippy, test) are separate jobs
- [ ] README badge shows CI status
- [ ] E2E tests skip gracefully when FUSE unavailable
- [ ] Cache configured for cargo artifacts
- [ ] Verified: CI catches intentional failures

title: [parity][durability] btrfs metadata COW-commit is not wired to the production write path — RW metadata does not persist a kernel-readable image
description:
CONFIRMED at the code level (SlateRaven, 2026-06-04): the entire btrfs COW-commit machinery in ffs-btrfs — WriteDependencyDag, serialize_node, BtrfsTransaction::commit, stage_tree_root, patch_root_commit — has ZERO callers in ffs-core. Every reference is inside writeback.rs unit tests (grep: writeback.rs:1193+/1449 are #[cfg(test)]). The production write path (ffs-core btrfs_write_logical, lib.rs:5782) writes DATA blocks straight to the block device via block_dev.write_block, but the metadata-tree COW commit that would (a) re-serialize the modified fs_tree/extent_tree/etc. nodes, (b) update the ROOT_ITEMs, and (c) write a valid superblock with the new tree roots + generation is NEVER invoked by any flush/fsync/umount.

CONSEQUENCE: btrfs RW is a durability facade. Data blocks land on disk but the metadata that references them (and the superblock generation) is not committed through the real on-disk format, so a FrankenFS-written btrfs image is not a consistent, kernel-mountable result after RW mutations. This is the ROOT BLOCKER behind several deferred items:
- bd-x3fcu (csum tree): cannot populate/persist a csum tree because there is no production metadata-commit to insert it into or root it from. The NODATASUM interim is the correct stopgap until this is fixed.
- Any btrfs RW parity work (mutations, nlink, dir ops) is low production-value until metadata persists.

SCOPE (epic, multi-wake, corruption-adjacent — do deliberately):
1. Wire a production flush path that, on fsync/umount/explicit commit, drives the existing WriteDependencyDag from the dirtied in-memory trees.
2. Serialize the dirtied/COWed tree nodes via serialize_node to freshly-allocated metadata blocks (crc32c tree-block csum already correct at writeback.rs:1939).
3. Update each modified tree's ROOT_ITEM (patch_root_commit) and the superblock root pointers + generation; write the superblock(s) with correct csum.
4. Validate end-to-end: write a file via FrankenFS, then have the real kernel / btrfs check read the image clean. (mkfs/kernel validation likely needs a non-rch fixture.)

This bead exists to make the gap first-class and prioritizable; it was previously only a comment on bd-x3fcu. Relates to bd-64t15 (FEATURE_PARITY.md btrfs-rw-ephemeral claim) and the 'btrfs RW is a durability facade' reality-check finding.
close_reason: INVALID — premise is factually wrong. btrfs metadata COW-commit IS wired to the production fsync path: ffs-core btrfs_full_transaction_commit (lib.rs:15637, called at 15602 in durable-mode sync and 24088) builds a WriteDependencyDag from the in-memory fs_tree, allocates real metadata blocks, serializes nodes via DiskWritebackContext/WritebackExecutor, writes them chunk-mapped to physical disk, patches FS_TREE + EXTENT_TREE ROOT_ITEMs, and commits the superblock. Added by 9cbc524a (2026-05-22) for bd-jdo53, which is CLOSED (2026-05-23) with acceptance 'mutations -> sync flushes through writeback DAG + atomic root commit -> remount preserves them'. 34 ffs-btrfs writeback tests pass (disk round-trip + WB-I1/WB-I2 crash consistency). Real kernel/btrfs-check validation exists as the mounted_differential_oracle harness but is permission-gated in sandbox. My last-wake grep that reported 'zero ffs-core callers' was simply wrong (it missed lib.rs:15660 WriteDependencyDag::from_cow_tree). Residual real gap = csum tree only, tracked by bd-x3fcu (now unblocked).

title: perf(mvcc): eliminate redundant per-write block copies in commit (3 copies/block -> 1, ~2.2x write)
description: The MVCC write path memcpys each 4KB block THREE times: (A) MvccBlockDevice::write_block data.to_vec() [needed, borrowed slice]; (B) resolved_write_bytes does staged.to_vec() in the common no-conflict case [redundant - txn is owned by commit]; (C) compress_data does new_bytes.to_vec() for algo None [redundant - version_bytes already owned]. Post-compression-removal (bd-i5gwr) the write path is ~730ns/block and 3x 4KB memcpys dominate. Refactor apply_fcw_commit: std::mem::take(txn.writes) to MOVE staged bytes; resolve all into owned Vecs (no clone in the no-conflict case, merge case unchanged) BEFORE any push (preserve atomicity); push with VersionData::Full(version_bytes) move for algo None / dedup-not-identical (no to_vec). Eliminates B+C -> 1 copy. Target ~2.2x (write_batch bench default_none). Isomorphism: merge/conflict/SSI/COW/dedup tests + from_device write suites. Keep resolved_writes_for_commit (pub) for SSI callers.
close_reason: apply_fcw_commit now std::mem::takes staged writes and MOVES bytes through resolution + into VersionData::Full for the no-compression store (92cea0d1): drops copies B (resolved_write_bytes clone) and C (compress_data to_vec) -> 3 copies/block to 1. Atomic apply preserved (resolve-all-before-push); merge/conflict unchanged; is_identical_to_latest factored from maybe_dedup. write_batch default_none 186.7us->116.7us (~1.6x). Byte-identical: 457 mvcc + 1095 core tests green; clippy clean. NOTE: 1.6x not 2.2x (alloc A + BTreeMap + dedup-compare share the budget); dedup_identical default-off would add ~0.6x but is a separate behavioral tradeoff.

title: btrfs LZO decompression ignores inter-segment sector-boundary padding
description: OpenFs::btrfs_decompress_lzo (ffs-core) hand-rolls btrfs LZO segment framing but reads segments contiguously (pos=seg_end then read next header). Per kernel fs/btrfs/lzo.c, a segment header may NOT cross a sector boundary: the writer pads up to 3 zeros at a sector's end and the reader must skip them (sector_left = sectorsize - cur_in%sectorsize; if < LZO_LEN(4): cur_in += sector_left). Missing skip => any multi-segment compress=lzo extent (uncompressed > one sector) whose segment layout includes sector padding is misread -> Corruption error or wrong data. Less-exercised (LZO uncommon, and the existing btrfs_test_lzo_frame helper itself packs contiguously so never produced a padded frame). Verified format against torvalds/linux master fs/btrfs/lzo.c. FIX: added the sector-boundary skip + sector_size param (caller passes BTRFS_LZO_SECTOR_SIZE=4096; same value already assumed by the per-segment output cap) + round-trip test with a forced pad.
close_reason: Fixed in 22537c6a: btrfs_decompress_lzo now skips inter-segment sector-boundary padding (kernel fs/btrfs/lzo.c rule), via a sector_size param (caller passes BTRFS_LZO_SECTOR_SIZE=4096). New test btrfs_decompress_lzo_skips_inter_segment_sector_padding round-trips a kernel-valid padded frame; ffs-core 970/970. Same commit repaired the ffs-core FC test fixtures regressed by 7f4014e2.

title: btrfs FICLONE whole-file clone onto a non-empty dst leaves stale extents / errors KeyAlreadyExists
description: btrfs_clone_file_data (whole-file FICLONE, also the clone_file_range reduction for src_off==0 && dst_off==0 && len>=src_size) only INSERTED src's EXTENT_DATA into dst and copied src size/nbytes — it never dropped dst's pre-existing extents. On a NON-EMPTY destination this (a) collides on a same-offset EXTENT_DATA key -> InMemoryCowBtrfsTree::insert returns KeyAlreadyExists, aborting mid-loop with a half-cloned dst, or (b) leaves stale dst extents past the cloned i_size: extent-beyond-i_size + leaked EXTENT_DATA_REF + nbytes mismatch -> btrfs check failure. The range path btrfs_clone_file_range_data already drops its dest window first (btrfs_remove_overlapping_extent_data); the whole-file path was missing the equivalent. FIX: before grafting src's extents, clear dst refcount-aware via btrfs_extent_data_items + btrfs_delete_extent_data_items (shared extents lose only this inode's ref; sole extents freed with their EXTENT_CSUM items); early-return for src==dst (self-clone no-op, also avoids freeing src's own extents). Regression test btrfs_clone_file_data_over_nonempty_dst_replaces_content.
close_reason: Fixed in adb5a27e: btrfs_clone_file_data now clears dst refcount-aware (btrfs_extent_data_items + btrfs_delete_extent_data_items) before grafting src's extents + early-returns for src==dst. Regression test btrfs_clone_file_data_over_nonempty_dst_replaces_content green; clone suite 10/10; clippy clean.
