title: Resolve cross-project bead-store contamination (Pass 1 F1; worse in Pass 2)
description:
# Resolve cross-project bead-store contamination (Pass 1 F1; worse in Pass 2)

Discovered by FrankenFS beads compliance audit Pass 1 (2026-05-10T03-20-31Z, synthesis F1). Re-observed and quantified as worse in Pass 2 (2026-05-13T23-14-23Z).

## Problem

The FrankenFS `.beads/` store contains beads from multiple unrelated projects, all tagged `source_repo: "."`:

| Prefix | Pass 1 count | Pass 2 count | Origin |
|--------|------------:|-------------:|--------|
| `bd-*` (genuine FrankenFS) | 1,924 closed | 2,242 closed | this project |
| `franken_networkx-*` | ~1,225 | ~1,223 | NetworkX-Rust port |
| `br-r3*/r4*-*` | ~360 | ~362 | NetworkX-Rust review batches |
| `frankenscipy-*` | 0 | **~1,200** | **NEW** — entire scipy-port project landed since Pass 1 |
| **TOTAL POLLUTION** | **1,585 (45%)** | **2,785 (55%)** | pollution now dominates the universe |

## Impact on FrankenFS workflow

1. `br ready`, `br list`, `br stats` mix FrankenFS work with unrelated projects.
2. `bv` graph metrics (PageRank, betweenness, critical path) are computed over a graph that conflates architecturally unrelated projects — outputs are meaningless for FrankenFS triage.
3. Audit metrics are inflated 2.2x (Pass 2: 5,038 total beads vs 2,253 real FrankenFS beads).
4. Cross-project beads will fail any evidence check by construction — their referenced code doesn't exist in this repo.
5. `.beads/beads.db` corruption events (18 preserved `*.bad_*` snapshots in `.beads/.br_recovery/`) may be exacerbated by the larger working set.

## Acceptance criteria

Pick ONE of two resolutions and implement it:

### Option A: Separate `.beads/` stores per project (recommended)

- [ ] Move `franken_networkx-*` beads to a NetworkX-port project's own `.beads/` store
- [ ] Move `br-r3*/r4*-*` beads similarly (they appear to be NetworkX review-batch beads)
- [ ] Move `frankenscipy-*` beads to a scipy-port project's own `.beads/` store
- [ ] FrankenFS `.beads/` retains only `bd-*` beads (2,242 closed + 40 open as of Pass 2)
- [ ] After the move, verify: `jq -r '.id' /data/projects/frankenfs/.beads/issues.jsonl | grep -vc '^bd-'` returns 0
- [ ] `br doctor --json` exits clean post-cleanup
- [ ] `bv --robot-insights` produces coherent FrankenFS-scoped graph metrics

### Option B: Add `project:` discriminator field

- [ ] Extend bead JSONL schema with a `project: <name>` field (default: "frankenfs")
- [ ] Backfill the field for all 5,038 existing beads using the ID-prefix heuristic
- [ ] Teach `br ready`, `br list`, `br stats` to filter by project (default: current project from `.beads/` config)
- [ ] Teach `bv` to scope graph metrics by project
- [ ] Coordinate the schema change with the upstream `beads_rust` repo
- [ ] Audit-policy.yaml gains a `project:` field

Option A is simpler and lower-coordination. Option B is more flexible if shared `.beads/` stores are a deliberate design choice elsewhere.

## Tests

FrankenFS currently has no constant, FUSE dispatch, or FsOps hook, so callers fall through to ENOTTY instead of a btrfs-aware response. Add the ioctl constant and input validation, return EROFS on read-only mounts, route writable requests through an explicit FsOps method under an IoctlWrite request scope, return EOPNOTSUPP for ext4/current unsupported btrfs device-add state, and add focused dispatcher tests.
close_reason: Implemented BTRFS_IOC_ADD_DEV constant, 4096-byte vol_args validation, read-only EROFS guard, FUSE dispatch, FsOps/OpenFs support, and focused dispatcher tests; rch test/check/clippy passed.

title: Determinism MR for parse_send_stream
description: parse_send_stream parses btrfs send streams (subvolume send/receive workflow). It dispatches CRC32C verification, command type recognition, and attribute parsing — significant surface area for non-determinism. No existing determinism MR. SendStreamCommand and SendStreamParseResult lack PartialEq derives, blocking direct prop_assert_eq comparison. Add PartialEq+Eq derives to the two types, then add proptest_parse_send_stream_raw_bytes_determinism that calls parse_send_stream twice on arbitrary 0..=256 byte buffers and prop_assert_eq the results. Catches non-determinism on both Ok and Err paths. Sister parsers (parse_root_item, parse_xattr_items, parse_inode_refs, parse_root_ref, parse_dir_items, parse_inode_item, parse_extent_data via bd-whybk) all have raw-bytes determinism MRs.

title: btrfs write/truncate-extend/fallocate do not enforce max file size (MAX_LFS_FILESIZE) -> no EFBIG, silent oversized i_size
description: Sibling-asymmetry follow-on to bd-3pa5m (ext4 EFBIG). btrfs_setattr's truncate-EXTEND branch sets inode.size = size with NO max-file-size check, so ftruncate to e.g. 2^63 (or u64::MAX) is silently accepted, leaving an i_size past the btrfs maximum. btrfs_write computes end = offset+len and btrfs_fallocate computes new_end with only a u64-overflow guard, never the file-size limit. The kernel sets sb->s_maxbytes = MAX_LFS_FILESIZE = i64::MAX (2^63-1) in btrfs_fill_super; the VFS (inode_newsize_ok for truncate, generic_write_checks for write/fallocate) returns EFBIG before the fs when a request exceeds it. FIX: add btrfs_max_file_size() = i64::MAX as u64 and a btrfs_reject_oversized_file(end) -> EFBIG helper, mirroring ext4_reject_oversized_file, called at btrfs_write (after end computed), btrfs_fallocate (after new_end), and the btrfs_setattr size block (closes the silent-extend gap). Same audit-both-boundaries class as bd-3pa5m/h909s/1qiqs/lowbz. Pin with btrfs tests analogous to the ext4 EFBIG tests; verify they fail pre-fix (extend silently accepted).
close_reason: Fixed in ce5cd4a1: btrfs_max_file_size()=i64::MAX + btrfs_reject_oversized_file()->EFBIG wired at write/fallocate/setattr-extend. Sibling of ext4 bd-3pa5m.

title: perf(fuse): A/B the record_memoized counter cost — bdd0fd1b adds two contended CAS loops on the hottest path (one per path-based metadata op)
description:
Risk introduced by my own instrument fix, filed so it is measured rather than argued.

bdd0fd1b added AtomicMetrics::record_memoized() so memoized xattr answers appear in requests_total. It calls saturating_add TWICE (requests_total, requests_ok), and saturating_add is a try_update CAS RETRY LOOP, not a single fetch_add.

Why that lands on the hottest possible path: bd-warm-stat-is-the-fuse-floor-4wxw9 established that Linux issues ONE uncached getxattr(security.capability) probe per path-based metadata operation, and the read-only memo answers every one of them. So on readdir-stat-8t that is two contended CAS loops on the SAME two shared counters, x32768 operations, x8 concurrent FUSE worker threads. CacheLinePadded prevents FALSE sharing between different counters; it does nothing about TRUE sharing of one counter across eight threads.

OBSERVATION THAT PROMPTED THIS (not attribution): the admitted 2026-08-04 readdir-stat-8t row measured 5.015699x [4.996497, 5.027581] where the bank has 4.967448x [4.946319, 4.989285] — non-overlapping CIs, about 1 percent worse. TWO confounds move the same way and this run controls NEITHER: (a) kernel drift, bank on 6.17.0-35-generic vs this host now on 6.17.0-41-generic, and (b) this counter. No causal claim is made either way.

ACCEPTANCE: make the counter path a PER-STORE field (not a compile-time cfg) so BOTH arms run from ONE ELF, then run readdir-stat-8t with the kernel incumbent live in the same invocation, both A/A nulls reported, actual observed thread count, executing-ELF SHA-256 self-reported in-process, median-CI decision. Use --pairs 32; --pairs 12 is the documented minimum and its bootstrap CI is too wide to decide this row (measured: FUSE A/A spread 1.028819 at 12 pairs vs 1.005674 at 32, same two ELFs).

IF THE COST IS REAL, DO NOT DROP THE INSTRUMENT. Route the counts through the existing per-core metrics in crates/ffs-fuse/src/per_core.rs instead. An uncounted daemon is exactly how the security.capability mechanism stayed invisible (a read-only mount serving 6001 path stats reported 22 requests). Cheaper intermediate option worth measuring in the same A/B: a plain fetch_add, since u64 saturation is unreachable at any real request rate.

IF THE COST IS INSIDE THE NULL MARGIN, close with the negative-evidence row and keep the counter as-is.
close_reason: NULL result, measured not argued. Same-ELF A/B (38eece54..., flag symbol verified present in the ELF, fail-closed guard) on ext4 readdir-stat-8t, operations=32768, --pairs 32, client-threads 8, kernel incumbent live in the same invocation, both arms ADMITTED with all four A/A nulls clear: counter off 5.219658x [5.217375,5.268615], counter on 5.231748x [5.162397,5.335599]. Delta 0.23%, and the on-arm CI contains the off-arm median. The adjacent ledger row measures this workload's cross-window spread on a byte-identical ELF at 4.71%, so the effect is ~20x below the instrument's resolution. DISPOSITION: keep the counter as-is at default-on; explicitly NOT doing the per-core refactor or the fetch_add swap, both of which were contingencies for a cost that does not exist at this scale. This also positively refutes my own earlier suspicion that bdd0fd1b caused the ~1% gap vs the bank. Implementation a7192121 (4 tests pass incl. both negative cases); evidence rows in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md; reports under /data/tmp/lilac-d9378b-20260804/{off,on}/report.json.

comments.text:
Implementation landed in a7192121 (pushed to main). Note for the audit trail: I wrote the change and its tests, but a concurrent agent in this shared checkout committed my working tree under that SHA before I got to it — the diff is my work (helper + both new tests present), so I am citing it rather than re-committing.

WHAT LANDED
- FuseInner gains `count_memoized_requests: bool`, a PER-STORE field (not a cfg) so both A/B arms
  run from ONE ELF and the ISA/PGO provenance cancels between them.
- `count_memoized_requests_from_env()` reads FFS_D9378_COUNT_MEMOIZED, delegating to a pure
  `count_memoized_requests_from_value(Option<&str>)` so the opt-out spelling is testable without
  mutating process-global env from a test thread (matches the existing *_from_env(...as_deref())
  pattern in this crate).
- Default is ON. Only the exact strings 0/false/off/no (case-insensitive, trimmed) disable it, so a
  typo cannot silently un-instrument a production mount.
- All three memo early-returns are guarded (2 in getxattr_value, 1 in listxattr).

TESTS (4 passed / 0 failed, strict remote RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1, targeted run)
- memoized_request_counting_defaults_on_and_only_exact_opt_outs_disable_it — pins the default-on
  behaviour AND the negative case a typo'd parser would fail: "offf", "no thanks", "disable" must
  NOT be read as opt-outs.
- memoized_request_counting_flag_gates_the_counter_in_both_arms — pins BOTH arms, because a flag
  that is wired inverted or ignored would make the A/B measure two identical arms and silently
  report "no cost". Default arm (1 format-layer call, 4 counted requests) vs opt-out arm (1 format
  call, 1 counted request). The difference of exactly 3 is the memo hits, which is what the A/B
  prices. NOTE the opt-out arm is 1 and not 0: the FIRST probe misses the memo and goes through the
  real request path, so it is counted in both arms. My initial expectation of 0 was wrong and the
  test caught it.
- The two pre-existing memo tests still pass unchanged.
ubs on the changed file: zero findings in any of my edited line ranges.

A/B NOW RUNNING: same ELF, readdir-stat-8t, ext4, operations=32768, --pairs 32 (NOT 12 — see the
readdir bead: 12 is the documented minimum and its bootstrap CI is too wide to decide this row),
client-threads 8, image 1024 MiB, both arms in one window so sbh cannot reclaim the binaries between
them. Artifacts under /data/tmp/lilac-d9378-20260804/{on,off}/report.json.

comments.text:
### 2026-08-04 (LilacRaven) — INVALID A/B, and the free cross-window A/A it accidentally produced: the SAME ELF admits at `5.015699x` and at `5.251849x` with non-overlapping CIs

**First, the error, because it invalidates a run.** The first bd-d9378 A/B was INVALID and its numbers
must not be used. The driver script reused an existing `release-perf` binary when one was present
(`if [ ! -x ... ]`), and that binary was built at 20:08 — an hour BEFORE the flag landed in `a7192121`
at 21:09. `strings -a` on the ELF under test returns **zero** occurrences of
`FFS_D9378_COUNT_MEMOIZED`, so the env var was ignored and BOTH "arms" were the identical pre-flag
binary. The rerun always rebuilds and now **fails closed** unless the flag symbol is present in the
ELF, which is the guard that should have been there from the start.

**What it accidentally bought: a rigorous, free A/A of one ELF across three separate windows.** All
three runs are `ffs-mounted-kernel-bench`, ext4, `readdir-stat-8t`, `operations=32768`, `--pairs 32`,
`client-threads 8`, image 1024 MiB, host `thinkstation1`, candidate ELF
`be5137009ecd125c8ccd74844c7803f2cd8f87205946cad2be7486b448974a4a` (self-reported in-process,
identical in all three), incumbent kernel live in the same invocation, decision by bootstrap median
CI over 20 000 resamples:

| window | `fuse_over_kernel` median | bootstrap median CI | kernel A/A spread | FUSE A/A spread | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | `5.015699x` | [4.996497, 5.027581] | 1.013222 | 1.006240 | **admitted** |
| B | `5.379904x` | [5.101723, 7.089810] | 1.039115 | 1.026092 | BLOCKED_NULL |
| C | `5.251849x` | [5.239011, 5.278118] | 1.015468 | 1.013080 | **admitted** |

Same invocation four-arm crossover throughout; A/A null control kernel 0.997811 and A/A null control
FUSE 0.996844 in window C, both inside the 2% median limit with bootstrap median CI [0.990085,
1.005399] and [0.986699, 0.999605] respectively.

⭐ **The result: two ADMITTED runs of a byte-identical binary differ by 4.71% and their CIs do not
overlap.** Window A says `5.015699x` [4.9965, 5.0276]; window C says `5.251849x` [5.2390, 5.2781].
Both cleared every gate the harness has. An admitted row's CI is therefore an **intra-run** interval,
not a reproducibility interval, and on this row it understates cross-window spread by roughly 5x.

**Three consequences, and one retraction of my own.**

1. 🛑 **Retracting my own suspicion from the row above.** I flagged that `bdd0fd1b`'s two CAS-loop
   increments might have caused the ~1% gap between `5.015699x` and the banked `4.967448x`. That
   gap is **well inside** the 4.71% cross-window spread now measured on the identical ELF, so the
   evidence does not support the suspicion. The counter may still cost something — bd-d9378 exists
   to measure it — but nothing observed so far is attributable to it, and the earlier row's
   non-overlapping-CI argument was simply not a valid inference.
2. **Do not difference admitted medians across runs on this row at the few-percent level.** That
   includes comparing any new run to the banked `4.967448x`. Cross-run deltas below ~5% on
   `readdir-stat-8t` are indistinguishable from window effects.
3. **A lever on this row must be measured as a SAME-WINDOW A/B from one ELF**, which is exactly what
   bd-d9378's per-store flag is for, or it must clear ~5%. A lever worth 1–2% is not measurable here
   with the current instrument, and claiming one would be reading noise.

**Retry predicate for the instrument itself:** if a future change wants to make few-percent effects
decidable on this row, the fix is more crossover blocks / pairs *interleaved within one window*, or
an in-process paired estimator — not more repeats of the same shape, since windows A and C each
already passed every null gate while disagreeing by 4.71%.

comments.text:
### 2026-08-04 (LilacRaven) — bd-d9378 RESOLVED NULL: the `record_memoized` counter costs nothing measurable on `readdir-stat-8t`; same-ELF A/B, `0.23%` against a `4.71%` instrument floor

Closes the suspicion I raised two rows above, this time by measurement rather than by inference.

**Design.** The counter path is a PER-STORE field (`FuseInner::count_memoized_requests`, landed
`a7192121`), not a `cfg`, so both arms run from **ONE ELF** and the ISA/PGO provenance cancels
between them. ELF under test
`38eece541053bbe1da63098d0b85ad37c9cb92b09f1ba80ada5897f6ed3bcd7e`, PGO profile
`5c6530a0261f658ed0ace2a9d8bef7c6c63b6f94b4b955e4f7ccba038e011e96`, `compile_avx2=true`
`runtime_avx2=true`. The driver **fails closed** unless `FFS_D9378_COUNT_MEMOIZED` is actually
present in the ELF, so the earlier invalid-arm failure mode cannot recur. Both arms:
`ffs-mounted-kernel-bench`, ext4, `readdir-stat-8t`, `operations=32768`, `--pairs 32`,
`client-threads 8`, image 1024 MiB, incumbent kernel live in the same invocation, decision by
bootstrap median CI over 20 000 resamples, `cv_used=false`.

| arm | `fuse_over_kernel` median | bootstrap median CI | kernel A/A | FUSE A/A | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| counter **off** (`=0`) | `5.219658x` | [5.217375, 5.268615] | 0.997201 clear | 0.999385 clear | admitted |
| counter **on** (default) | `5.231748x` | [5.162397, 5.335599] | 1.000097 clear | 0.993359 clear | admitted |

Same invocation four-arm crossover in both arms; A/A null control kernel 0.997201 and A/A null
control FUSE 0.999385 in the off arm, both within the 2% median limit with bootstrap median CI
[0.990712, 1.005930] and [0.996483, 1.009383].

**Result: NULL — no cost detected, and the row could not have seen one this small anyway.**
on/off = `5.231748 / 5.219658` = **1.00232**, i.e. **0.23%**, and the on-arm CI [5.1624, 5.3356]
comfortably contains the off-arm median 5.2197. For scale, the row immediately above measures the
cross-window spread of a byte-identical ELF on this same workload at **4.71%**, and this run's own
`twice_null_margin_ratio` is 1.041202. The observed delta is roughly **20x below the instrument's
resolution**. Two contended `saturating_add` CAS loops per path-based metadata op are simply not
visible against a ~5.2x FUSE-vs-kernel wall-time gap.

**Disposition: KEEP THE COUNTER AS IS, at its default-on setting.** This is the bead's own stated
acceptance branch ("if the cost is inside the null margin, close with the negative-evidence row and
keep the counter"). Explicitly NOT doing the per-core refactor of `requests_total`, and explicitly
NOT swapping `saturating_add` for `fetch_add`: both were contingency plans for a cost that does not
exist at this scale, and either would be an unmeasured change to a shared metrics path. The
instrument is what made the `security.capability` mechanism visible at all — a read-only mount
serving 6 001 path stats reported 22 requests before `bdd0fd1b` — and it is now shown to be free.

**Retry predicate.** Re-open only if the counter path is measured on a workload where per-request
overhead is a much larger fraction of the total than it is here, e.g. a hypothetical row whose FUSE
arm is within ~1.2x of the kernel arm, or if `requests_total` acquires additional per-request work
beyond these two increments. Do NOT re-run this A/B on `readdir-stat-8t`: the effect is below the
floor and re-running it is reading noise.

**Method note worth carrying.** The `FFS_D9378_COUNT_MEMOIZED` opt-out is an instrumentation seam
for this measurement, not a supported tuning knob; it defaults on and only the exact spellings
`0/false/off/no` disable it, pinned by
`memoized_request_counting_defaults_on_and_only_exact_opt_outs_disable_it` (which asserts `offf`,
`no thanks` and `disable` do NOT disable) and
`memoized_request_counting_flag_gates_the_counter_in_both_arms` (which pins both arms, because a
flag wired inverted or ignored would make an A/B compare two identical arms and silently report
"no cost" — exactly the failure the first attempt at this A/B actually hit).

title: Kernel-conformance pin for BTRFS_MAGIC and BTRFS_SUPER_INFO layout constants
description: Found via /porting-to-rust audit. ffs_types::BTRFS_MAGIC (lib.rs:26) = 0x4D5F_5366_5248_425F per fs/btrfs/btrfs_tree.h '_BHRfS_M' in BE display, stored LE on disk. ffs_types::BTRFS_SUPER_INFO_OFFSET (lib.rs:24) = 64*1024 = 0x10000 and BTRFS_SUPER_INFO_SIZE (lib.rs:25) = 4096 per fs/btrfs/disk-io.h. None of these have a kernel-conformance pin test — bd-jbilz pins EXT4_SUPER_MAGIC and EXT4_EXTENT_MAGIC, bd-xhswi (per the ext4 doc) pins btrfs CSUM_TYPE_*, and bd-khzn4 pins tree objectids, but BTRFS_MAGIC itself and the superblock layout constants are unpinned. A regression that swapped any of these would silently mis-read every btrfs filesystem on mount. Fix: add btrfs_super_info_constants_match_kernel_header that pins BTRFS_MAGIC=0x4D5F_5366_5248_425F, BTRFS_SUPER_INFO_OFFSET=0x10000, BTRFS_SUPER_INFO_SIZE=4096, plus the ASCII identity check that BTRFS_MAGIC.to_le_bytes() == b'_BHRfS_M' (the on-disk byte sequence). Bead size: <50 min.
close_reason: duplicate of bd-63e4e (constants already pinned at ffs-types/src/lib.rs:2607-2624 including the ASCII byte-decomposition cross-check)

title: perf(read): cap the parallel-read fan-out — rayon default (nproc=64) over-parallelizes reads, causing kernel page-cache xa_lock contention (cold 1.24-1.44x, warm 1.48x)
description:
EVIDENCE (BlackThrush/cc_ffs 2026-07-10, profile of the prebuilt release-perf ffs-cli; full ranked
frame table in docs/progress/perf-negative-results.md).

MECHANISM. `ffs-cli read` fans a large read across the GLOBAL rayon pool (nproc = 64 on this box).
Every worker preads the SAME inode, so all 64 threads serialize inserting folios into that one
address_space xarray. perf -g resolves it exactly:
  File::read_exact_at -> __libc_pread -> __x64_sys_pread64 -> vfs_read -> ext4_file_read_iter
    -> generic_file_read_iter -> filemap_read -> filemap_get_pages (32.71%)
       -> page_cache_sync_ra (31.62%) -> page_cache_ra_unbounded -> filemap_add_folio
          -> __filemap_add_folio (28.34%)   [xa_lock]
`native_queued_spin_lock_slowpath` is 39.07% of self-time at the default 64 threads.
Cold read converts I/O parallelism into kernel lock contention.

RULED OUT (do not re-investigate):
  * per-block syscall overhead -- only 1,034 pread64 calls for 128 MiB (~128 KiB each).
  * extent-tree walks -- tax is uncorrelated with extent count (1.35x @2 extents, 1.15x @9, 1.36x @14);
    no extent/indirect frame reaches 0.1% self-time.
  * copy tax -- _copy_to_iter 5.69% + clear_page_erms 5.21% ~= 11%, real but not dominant.
  * readahead/fadvise tuning and cold chunk-size sweeps -- already refuted (bd-5v3mh, bd-q6k00).

MEASURED LEVER (prebuilt binary, RAYON_NUM_THREADS, byte-identical sha256, no rebuild):
  cold 128 MiB, min-of-5, read ms: T=1 86.2 | 2 63.3 | 4 40.4 | 8 32.0 | 16 30.1 | 32 32.9 | 64 37.0
  contention: T=64 spinlock 42.27%, steal 5.42%, sys 0.446s  ->  T=16 spinlock 10.96%, steal 1.26%, sys 0.158s
  paired interleaved A/B 7 reps: T=16 faster 7/7, p=0.0156, 1.24x
  generalizes: indirect 1.44x faster, fragmented 1.19x faster at T=16
  kernel gap (vs dio-loop kernel best): extent 1.37x -> 1.11x; indirect 1.45x -> 1.09x; fragmented 1.31x -> 1.09x
  WARM wants the same cap (no regression risk): T=4/8/16/32/64 read = 15.5/9.0/8.5/10.0/12.6 ms

PROPOSED CHANGE. Cap read fan-out at a bounded width instead of inheriting the global pool.
Fan-out sites: crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:10108 (`jobs.into_par_iter().map(exec_job)`),
:12677 (same), :12819 (`specs.into_par_iter().map(read_run)`). Options:
  (a) a dedicated rayon ThreadPool for reads with num_threads = min(available_parallelism, 16), or
  (b) chunk the job list so at most N jobs are in flight.
Add an env override (FFS_READ_PARALLELISM) alongside the existing FFS_READ_CHUNK_BLOCKS.
16 is the measured optimum on a 64-core box; the right default is probably a fraction of nproc
(e.g. nproc/4 clamped to [4,16]) -- MEASURE on a second machine before hardcoding.

CAUTION / OPEN QUESTIONS.
  * The optimum is contention-dependent and may shift with device speed and core count. Do not
    hardcode 16 without a second-box measurement.
  * Interacts with bd-kdmu4 (OWNER-GATED, mmap/io_uring zero-copy): O_DIRECT would eliminate
    filemap_add_folio entirely and make the fan-out cap moot. This bead is the cheap,
    forbid-unsafe-compatible subset -- it does NOT require io_uring or mmap.
  * Other rayon consumers (scrub, walk, repair) share the global pool; a dedicated read pool avoids
    perturbing them. Do not simply set a global RAYON_NUM_THREADS.
  * Gates required: byte-identity (sha256) per fixture, cold + warm A/B, conformance 100/0/2.

OPERATIONAL MITIGATION AVAILABLE TODAY, ZERO CODE: run with RAYON_NUM_THREADS=16.
notes: LANDED 2026-07-10 in 7a6091a2: dedicated ext4 data-read pool. CLOSED 2026-07-27 by GreenSpring after an actual-binary topology audit corrected the default from (nproc/4).clamp(4,16) to min(nproc,16). The original 64-thread profile remains valid and scoped: 64 to 16 reduced native_queued_spin_lock_slowpath self-time 42.27% to 9.32% and improved cold wall about 1.21x. A self-hashing v3 whole-binary run on pinned ovh-a then proved the old rule over-corrected a 16-thread worker: default4 / explicit16 = 0.793266x, bootstrap median CI [0.772379,0.808476], with A/A CI [0.961861,1.022792]. Corrected policy run ELF 8f7039d78a42e5ca7aa79cf7fa0e5c80415b61971469465d0ca5e9d881003082 owned 31 alternating A/A+B pairs in one invocation: A/A 0.993140x CI [0.986304,1.002085], null floor 1.013887x, twice-null 1.027966x; corrected16 / old4 1.248257x CI [1.226142,1.279943]. Parent and child ELF SHAs matched; AVX2+FMA true; exact 33554432-byte stream SHA edeadec8f638055689d5be63b4bcf2654fb64bf91fb6651e9a924f052a9c7db0. Gate was bootstrap median wall CI, never CV/instructions. This is v3 non-PGO offline evidence; no mounted/kernel ratio was rescaled. Two noisy runs and one fixture-capacity failure were excluded, not pooled. Focused strict-remote tests and CLI check passed; ledger preflight self-test/audit passed with VOID numerator fixed at 205. Full evidence and retry predicate: tests/artifacts/perf/2026-07-10_bd-ddryj_read_fanout_cap.md and docs/progress/perf-negative-results.md.
close_reason: Actual-binary gate closed the disclosed gap; retain 16-thread ceiling, correct default to min(nproc,16), and restate ratio as v3 non-PGO offline evidence.

title: perf(core): cap btrfs decompress concurrency to fix pool over-subscription
description: btrfs_read_file fans every per-extent decompress (zstd/lzo) job across the FULL rayon pool. Decompression is CPU- and cache-bound (not I/O-overlap-bound like the uncompressed memcpy path), so on a many-core box spreading ~270 short jobs across 64 threads OVER-subscribes and thrashes L2/L3. Measured (perf stat, 34 MiB zstd file, walk --read-data) at 64 vs 8 threads: 4.5x task-clock (293M vs 64M), 4.2x cache-misses (6.6M vs 1.6M), 8x context-switches => whole read 1.6x slower warm (18.0 vs 11.4ms) AND 1.46x slower cold (20.9 vs 14.3ms) at the default pool size; both warm+cold peak at ~8 threads. FIX: cap the decompress-job concurrency to ~16 tasks via IndexedParallelIterator::with_min_len(jobs.len()/16) when the read is decompress-dominated (decompress_jobs>16 && >=50% of jobs); pure-uncompressed reads keep full parallelism so the bd-vffrx 32-block chunking win is preserved. with_min_len only coarsens task granularity -> collect preserves job order -> byte-identical output, lowest-idx error still wins. Sibling of bd-vffrx (both: wrong parallelism for the core count, opposite directions).
close_reason: Measured reject/no code kept: dedicated decompression pool regressed on RCH (global 9.0318ms vs dedicated 15.322ms; multi-file 52.085ms vs gated 59.538ms), larger walk windows all regressed (4/8/16/64MiB), and direct btrfs-kernel comparator remains a loss (walk 40.282ms vs kernel 8.006ms). Evidence in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md and docs/progress/perf-bd-defgb-cod-a.md.

title: Clarify generated ext4 golden image artifact contract
description:
Discovery from `$testing-conformance-harnesses` while source-aware ready work was empty and RCH capacity was blocked.

Current evidence:
- `tests/source-scope-manifest/source_scope_manifest.json` includes `conformance/golden/*.ext4` in the active `conformance_fixture_artifacts` source family.
- `crates/ffs-harness/src/open_ended_inventory.rs` hard-codes `conformance/golden/*.ext4` in `CONFORMANCE_FIXTURE_ARTIFACT_GLOBS`, and its source-scope validation test fails if that glob is removed.
- `conformance/PROVENANCE.md` says binary `.ext4` images produced by capture scripts are regenerated locally and ignored by `conformance/golden/.gitignore`, with committed checksum manifests covering only JSON and text golden artifacts.
- `scripts/verify_golden.sh` writes and verifies conformance golden checksums only for `*.json` and `*.txt`; `golden_checksum_manifest_is_complete` also validates only JSON/TXT extensions.
- `git ls-files conformance/golden` confirms no `.ext4` images are tracked, while local ignored files such as `conformance/golden/ext4_8mb_reference.ext4` and `conformance/golden/ext4_dir_index_reference.ext4` may exist and mask clean-clone behavior.

Problem: the source-scope and open-ended-inventory surfaces treat generated `.ext4` images like active conformance artifacts, while provenance/checksum gates deliberately treat them as local regenerated artifacts. Future agents can read the manifest as requiring committed `.ext4` proof even though the canonical integrity gate excludes them.

Scope: make the contract explicit and machine-checked. Either split generated `.ext4` images into a distinct generated-artifact source family with non-applicability/freshness semantics, or add explicit report fields/tests that distinguish tracked JSON/TXT goldens from ignored regenerated binary images. Do not commit large binary images. Keep `scripts/verify_golden.sh` checksum behavior intentional, but make the source-scope report and docs explain why `.ext4` is not checksum-listed and how to regenerate it.

Acceptance:
1. Source-scope/open-ended inventory output clearly distinguishes tracked conformance goldens from generated ignored `.ext4` images.
2. A focused unit test fails if `conformance/golden/*.ext4` is presented as a checksum-covered tracked artifact, and passes only when it is represented as generated/regenerated-local evidence.
3. `conformance/PROVENANCE.md`, `scripts/verify_golden.sh --self-check` expectations, and any affected source-scope manifest rows agree on JSON/TXT checksum coverage versus `.ext4` regeneration.
4. Validation includes `jq empty .beads/issues.jsonl`, `git diff --check`, focused RCH cargo tests for open-ended inventory/source-scope validation and verify-golden self-check, `br dep cycles --no-db --no-auto-import --json`, and source-aware hygiene. If RCH remains blocked, keep this bead blocked on `bd-oowwx` and do not use local cargo as proof.
close_reason: Split generated ext4 golden images out of tracked conformance fixture artifacts. Source-scope now keeps committed JSON/TXT goldens and checksums in conformance_fixture_artifacts, tracks conformance/golden/*.ext4 under conformance_generated_image_artifacts with regenerated-local non-applicability semantics, rejects attempts to present .ext4 images as checksum-covered tracked artifacts, and documents the provenance/checksum contract. Validation: scripts/verify_golden.sh --self-check, jq empty tracker/manifest JSON, git diff --check, br dep cycles count=0, rch remote ts2 cargo test -p ffs-harness source_scope -- --nocapture, rch remote ts2 cargo check -p ffs-harness --all-targets, rch remote ts2 cargo clippy -p ffs-harness --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo fmt -p ffs-harness --check.

title: btrfs send: generate_send_stream emits subvol-name-prefixed (and '..'-escaping) command paths -> unreceivable by btrfs receive
description: generate_send_stream's build_path (ffs-btrfs lib.rs ~6706) unconditionally prepended subvol_name to EVERY inode command path, so MKFILE/MKDIR/WRITE/CHMOD/CHOWN/UTIMES targeted 'subvol/<path>' instead of '<path>'. btrfs send command paths are RELATIVE to the received subvol root (no subvol-name prefix, no leading slash) — the receiver creates entries inside the freshly-created subvol. title: [bug] e2compr multi-cluster write panics: unchecked existing_end - cluster_file_offset underflow
description: FOUND via new test. In ext4_write_compressed (ffs-core lib.rs ~12446), cluster_data_len was computed as usize::try_from(existing_end - cluster_file_offset). existing_end = inode.size.min(cluster_end_offset). When a new/short file is written across MORE THAN ONE e2compr cluster, the 2nd+ cluster has existing_end (<= small inode.size) < cluster_file_offset, so the u64 subtraction UNDERFLOWS -> panic in debug builds (in release it wraps to a huge value, accidentally masked by the trailing .min(cluster_bytes), but still semantically wrong: compresses the whole cluster incl. trailing zeros instead of just write_end_in_cluster). The read-existing block just above is correctly guarded by 'if existing_end > cluster_file_offset' but this line was not. Existing compressed-write test only wrote 1 block (logical 0, direct ptr) so never hit a 2nd cluster.
close_reason: Fixed (commit pending): changed existing_end - cluster_file_offset to existing_end.saturating_sub(cluster_file_offset) at ffs-core lib.rs ~12446, so the pre-existing-data-in-cluster length floors at 0 instead of underflowing. When there is no existing data in the cluster, cluster_data_len now correctly = write_end_in_cluster.min(cluster_bytes). Isomorphic for the already-working single-cluster case (existing_end - 0). Regression test added: tests::compressed_write_spanning_indirect_blocks_roundtrips_ext4 (128 KiB compressed write spanning logical blocks 0..31 via the single-indirect write path; was panicking at 12446, now byte-identical roundtrip). ffs-core --lib 884/884 green, no warnings.

title: setxattr XATTR_REPLACE on a missing attribute returns ENOENT instead of ENODATA (core/library API)
description: ext4_setxattr and btrfs_setxattr return FfsError::NotFound (->ENOENT, errno 2) when XattrSetMode::Replace is requested for an attribute that does not exist. Linux setxattr(2) mandates ENODATA (61): 'The named attribute does not exist and XATTR_REPLACE was specified in flags.' The project already uses ENODATA for the missing-xattr case everywhere else (getxattr returns Ok(None) -> FUSE missing_xattr_errno()==ENODATA; removexattr Ok(false)->ENODATA). The FUSE setxattr handler papers over this with a getattr() heuristic that remaps Replace+NotFound+inode-exists -> ENODATA, so the mounted path is correct — but the public library API (OpenFs::setxattr, used by CLI/ffs-ops and any non-FUSE consumer) surfaces the raw ENOENT, and the core is internally inconsistent with getxattr/removexattr. FIX: return FfsError::Io(from_raw_os_error(libc::ENODATA)) for the Replace-on-missing case in both setxattr paths (the code knows unambiguously it is the xattr that is missing). The FUSE getattr-heuristic workaround then becomes redundant. Update the write_setxattr_modes test assertion (currently ENOENT) to ENODATA with a setxattr(2) citation.
close_reason: Fixed in 5f77395e: ext4_setxattr + btrfs_setxattr now return ENODATA (not NotFound/ENOENT) for XATTR_REPLACE on a missing attribute, matching setxattr(2) and the project's getxattr/removexattr missing-attribute errno. title: fuzz: no dedicated fuzz target for ext4_chksum (CRC32c) algebraic-laws contract
description:
Finding (via /testing-fuzzing skill, NEW target): fuzz/fuzz_targets has 50 targets and ext4_chksum is referenced in 2 (fuzz_ext4_checksums.rs, fuzz_ext4_htree_mmp.rs) but ONLY as a helper to validate other parsers. There is NO dedicated libfuzzer target that pumps random (seed, data) pairs through ext4_chksum and asserts the algebraic-law contract.

ext4_chksum is the CRC32c-based checksum function used by every metadata block (group desc, inode, extent block, dir block, MMP, fast-commit). The proptest layer pins:
  * ext4_proptest_chksum_deterministic — same input → same output
  * ext4_proptest_chksum_empty_data_varies — chksum(seed, &[]) == seed
  * ext4_proptest_chksum_collision_resistance — different inputs yield different outputs (with high probability)
  * ext4_proptest_chksum_incremental — seed-then-append equals direct compute

A libfuzzer target lifts these algebraic laws to >1M iterations/session with corpus learning across input lengths, byte-pattern boundaries, and sign-bit transitions. A regression to a slower-but-correct implementation would slip past unit tests; a regression to a wrong-polynomial CRC variant would fail the algebraic law immediately.

Acceptance: new fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_ext4_chksum.rs that, for an arbitrary (seed, data) split from libfuzzer input, asserts:
  * MR-1 — Determinism: chksum(s, d) called twice gives same result
  * MR-2 — Empty-data identity: chksum(s, &[]) == s
  * MR-3 — Incremental composition: chksum(chksum(s, &d[..k]), &d[k..]) == chksum(s, &d) for all valid k
  * MR-4 — Never panics: implicit
Plus a [[bin]] entry in fuzz/Cargo.toml.
close_reason: done

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Shipped fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_ext4_chksum.rs + Cargo.toml [[bin]] entry. Asserts 4 algebraic laws on arbitrary (seed: u32, data: bytes) input split from libfuzzer: MR-1 determinism, MR-2 empty-data identity (chksum(s, &[]) == s), MR-3 incremental composition at 4 split points (chksum(chksum(s, left), right) == chksum(s, full)), MR-4 never-panics. Pairs with the existing ext4_proptest_chksum_* layer to lift the algebraic laws to libfuzzer scale (>1M iter / session). title: btrfs BTRFS_IOC_SCRUB ioctl family support
description:
## Summary

Implement btrfs scrub ioctls for filesystem verification via CLI.

- `BTRFS_IOC_SCRUB`: Start/continue scrub operation
- `BTRFS_IOC_SCRUB_CANCEL`: Cancel running scrub
- `BTRFS_IOC_SCRUB_PROGRESS`: Query scrub progress

- `BTRFS_IOC_SCRUB_PROGRESS` = `_IOWR(0x94, 29, ...)`

1. Add ioctl constants and dispatch in ffs-fuse
2. Add trait methods in ffs-core/vfs.rs
3. Integrate with existing scrub/repair infrastructure in ffs-repair

title: Refine mounted write matrix with namespace atomicity and fsyncdir durability proofs
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-rchk0.3.2.1. The mounted write matrix covers operation classes and no-partial-mutation cases, but users also need namespace durability evidence: create, rename, link, unlink, rmdir, symlink, and xattr updates must survive reopen according to explicit fsync/fsyncdir boundaries, and rejected operations must not leave split-brain parent/child state.

Scope: define namespace atomicity and directory durability scenarios for ext4 and btrfs mounted paths. The scenarios should distinguish data fsync, parent directory fsync, file close, unmount, forced reopen, unsupported operation rejection, and host capability skips. They should check both visible namespace state and underlying image/reopen state.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/schema tests reject mounted write scenarios missing parent directory id, child inode/path id, namespace operation kind, fsync/fsyncdir boundary, expected survivor set, expected link count, reopen expectation, and no-partial-mutation checks.
2. Unit tests cover rename overwrite, rename no-overwrite, cross-directory rename, link count update, symlink target persistence, unlink after open handle, rmdir non-empty rejection, xattr namespace update, and unsupported fallocate no-op/refusal classification.
3. E2E mounted smoke covers at least one ext4 and one btrfs namespace scenario in the permissioned lane, plus a dry-run or fixture lane for missing capability.
4. Logs include scenario id, filesystem flavor, mount options, operation sequence, fsync/fsyncdir calls, pre/post directory entries, link counts, xattr keys, image hashes, reopen observations, cleanup status, artifact paths, and reproduction command.
5. Readiness gates cannot count mounted rw namespace coverage if only status-code checks ran without reopen and parent-directory durability proof.

title: perf(core/mvcc): parallel RANDOM read is ~88x slower than kernel (NEGATIVE scaling) — per-read MvccStore RwLock contention in with_latest_scope
description: MEASURED (CrimsonFox cc/opus 2026-06-21, 64-core, warm, new ffs-cli rand-read harness fa8108d8, 200MiB ext4 /big.bin, 100k x 4KiB random reads). FIRST random-read head-to-head in the campaign. SERIAL random read: frankenfs 237.9ms / 420k IOPS / 1642 MiB/s vs kernel C pread loop 236.6ms / 423k IOPS / 1651 MiB/s = PARITY (1.0x). Frankenfs single-threaded random read MATCHES the kernel — the per-read overhead is fine. PARALLEL random read: frankenfs --parallel 1070ms / 93k IOPS / 364 MiB/s = **4.5x SLOWER than its own serial (NEGATIVE scaling!)** vs kernel 64-thread 12.1ms / 8.26M IOPS / 32284 MiB/s = **~88x slower than kernel**; kernel 16-thread 16.3ms / 6.14M IOPS. Kernel scales ~20x with threads; frankenfs DE-scales. ROOT CAUSE (perf --no-children + call graph): dominated by parking_lot RwLock contention — lock_shared_slow 2.42% + WordLock::lock_slow 3.65% + lock_exclusive_slow 0.96% + futex syscalls (the [k] unknowns ~10%+). Caller: OpenFs::with_latest_scope (crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:27499) does 'self.mvcc_store.read().current_snapshot()' on EVERY read_into call — a shared acquire of the Arc> (lib.rs:887). current_snapshot() (ffs-mvcc lib.rs:1809) just reads next_commit.saturating_sub(1), a single u64. 64 threads x 100k reads = ~6.4M acquisitions of ONE lock word => the lock-state cache line ping-pongs across cores. Serial pays it uncontended (=> kernel parity); parallel collapses. (can_cache_ext4_read_only_block returns early on !is_writable so it is NOT the lock for RO images; the unconditional with_latest_scope acquire is.) FIX (lock-free snapshot publication; ffs-mvcc is CLEAN/ownable, the caller is the 1-line ffs-core part): publish next_commit as a sibling Arc on MvccStore, bumped wherever next_commit changes (ffs-mvcc lib.rs:2547 next_commit_seq, :2881 recovery, :1575 init). Add pub fn published_commit_handle(&self)->Arc. OpenFs caches the cloned handle at construction (mvcc_published: Arc field) and with_latest_scope reads Snapshot{high:CommitSeq(published.load(Acquire).saturating_sub(1))} with NO RwLock. Semantically equivalent: the old code only held the read lock to read one u64; an atomic read gives the same latest-committed snapshot. For RO images next_commit never changes => byte-identical; for mixed RW it acquires the same current snapshot. Eviction/visibility paths unchanged. Reproduce: ffs-cli rand-read /big.bin --count 100000 --size 4096 --parallel (vs the C krandread baseline in /tmp/krandread.c). Likely also helps parallel many-small-file reads (each opens with_latest_scope). ffs-core construction is currently cod-b WIP-dirty — coordinate the OpenFs field add; the ffs-mvcc half can land independently. Supersedes the bd-7f6yr extent-cache hypothesis: the dominant lock is the MVCC snapshot acquire, not the extent-cache hit counter (extent cache was secondary).
notes: 2ND WIN (CrimsonFox): the 9376f4d6 fix is workload-agnostic — it also gives the REAL multi-file parallel read (walk --read-data --parallel, the grep -r/tar/build-read pattern) 64t 145ms->33ms (4.4x), 16t knee flattened (66->22ms), and even SERIAL 170->110ms (1.5x, proving the per-file register/release OVERHEAD mattered, not just contention). This WIDENS the existing many-files-read kernel domination (was 14-24x). It also CORRECTS my earlier ledger row e4e45c53 which mis-attributed the walk knee to rayon coordination rather than the MVCC register/release lock. Conformance 100/0/2. So bd-eflng's fix benefits every read-only parallel read workload, not just synthetic random read.
close_reason: FIXED + SHIPPED 9376f4d6 (CrimsonFox). The 88x negative-scaling pathology is RESOLVED: per-read snapshot register/release (store write lock) for read-only adapters eliminated via MvccBlockDevice::new_unregistered (used in block_device_adapter when !is_writable). MEASURED parallel random read 64t 949ms->170ms (5.6x), collapse->scaling-to-16t, vs-kernel gap 88x->3.3x; also +4.4x on the grep/tar multi-file workload (flipped a default-config kernel loss to a 1.4x win); cold random read dominates ~14x. Byte-identical, conformance 100/0/2, no sequential/metadata regression. RESIDUAL 3.3x warm (distributed: ShardedCache shard-Mutex on hot inode block + per-read overlay store.read() + inode re-parse + harness alloc artifact) is a diminishing follow-up documented in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md — NOT the catastrophic gap this P1 tracked. title: [MAINT] FuseInodeLocks.table grows unboundedly — every accessed inode allocates a FuseInodeLock that is never evicted
description:
# Maintainability / resource finding from modes-of-reasoning pass

## Finding

`FuseInodeLocks` at crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:703-737 stores a `Mutex<BTreeMap<InodeNumber, Arc<FuseInodeLock>>>`. Every FUSE mutation operation (create/mkdir/unlink/rmdir/rename/setattr) calls `acquire()`, which does `table.entry(ino).or_insert_with(...)` — inserting a new entry on first encounter and never evicting.

For a long-running FUSE mount that touches many inodes, the table grows monotonically. With ~80 bytes per entry (key + Arc + FuseInodeLock fields), a mount that accesses a million inodes parks ~80 MB of never-freed locks.

## Evidence

- Storage: crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:705 `table: Mutex<BTreeMap<InodeNumber, Arc<FuseInodeLock>>>`
- Insertion: line 727 `table.entry(ino).or_insert_with(|| Arc::new(FuseInodeLock::default()))`
- No `remove` call anywhere — confirmed via `rg 'table\.\(remove\|clear\|retain\)' crates/ffs-fuse/`
- No TTL, no LRU eviction, no drop-on-last-guard hook

## Why this wasn't caught earlier

Not a deadlock (inspected in /deadlock-finder pass, out of that skill's scope). Not a correctness bug. Pure resource accumulation that only matters for long-running mounts. Relevant as soon as FrankenFS targets real production workloads.

## Fix directions

1. **Drop-on-last-guard cleanup.** When `FuseInodeGuard::drop` runs, check if the `Arc<FuseInodeLock>` strong_count is 1 (we hold the last ref). If so, remove the entry from the table. Race-safe because `acquire()` holds the table mutex during insert, so we can hold it during the last-guard removal check.
2. **Epoch-based GC.** Periodically scan the table and evict entries whose `Arc` strong_count is 1 (no active guard) AND that haven't been acquired in N seconds.
3. **Cap-based eviction.** Soft cap the table size; evict idle entries LRU when the cap is exceeded.

Option 1 is cleanest and matches the natural lifecycle (entries exist only when a guard is live).

## Acceptance

- A stress test creating/unlinking 100K inodes shows FuseInodeLocks.table stays bounded (approximately proportional to concurrent guards, not to total inodes-ever-accessed).
- No regression in the sorted-ino total-order guarantee (the crate's only concurrency invariant). /deadlock-finder sweep remains CLEAN.
- Unit test: acquire+drop a single inode's guard, assert the table is empty afterward.

## Severity rationale

P3 (low) — not exploitable, not correctness, not currently a production concern (FrankenFS mounts are short-lived in V1.x). But it is a real resource leak that will matter when V2+ targets longer-running deployments. Worth tracking so it doesn't get lost.
close_reason: Reconciled stale JSONL row: FuseInodeLocks leak fix already implemented and closure is present in commit 776fe07.

title: ffs-mvcc: wal_throughput benches missing checkpoint + truncate_wal latency floors
description:
Finding (via /profiling-software-performance skill, fifth visit,
different target): the wal_throughput criterion bench file

benches covering commit throughput, SSI overhead, EBR memory,
RCU/RwLock/Mutex read scaling, write amplification, MVCC contention,
sharded MVCC, pruning, coalesced append. But TWO operations on the
PersistentMvccStore persistence path have NO bench coverage:

  1. `PersistentMvccStore::checkpoint(path)` — writes a snapshot
     of the version chains to disk via temp-file + atomic rename.
     Cost scales with version count and version-chain length.

  2. `PersistentMvccStore::truncate_wal()` — rewrites the WAL header
     and truncates the file to header_size after a successful
     checkpoint. Cost is dominated by the file_set_len + sync_all.

Both are on the operator-facing maintenance path. A regression that
made checkpoint quadratic in version count, or truncate_wal slower
because of an extra fsync, would silently degrade the maintenance
window cost without tripping any existing bench gate.

crates/ffs-mvcc/benches/wal_throughput.rs registered in the
existing `wal_benches` criterion_group!, each priming the store
with a deterministic workload before invoking the operation under
test. Verified via `rch exec -- cargo check -p ffs-mvcc --benches`.

title: btrfs fiemap omits FIEMAP_EXTENT_DATA_INLINE/NOT_ALIGNED for inline and ENCODED for compressed extents
description: btrfs_fiemap reported an inline extent with only FIEMAP_EXTENT_LAST and never set FIEMAP_EXTENT_ENCODED for compressed extents. Linux btrfs extent_fiemap sets FIEMAP_EXTENT_DATA_INLINE|FIEMAP_EXTENT_NOT_ALIGNED for inline extents (data mixed with metadata at a non-block offset) and FIEMAP_EXTENT_ENCODED for compressed extents (cannot be read raw while unmounted). filefrag -v and other tools rely on these flags to label inline/compressed extents; FrankenFS misreported them as plain extents. FIX: add the three flag constants (DATA_INLINE=0x200, NOT_ALIGNED=0x100, ENCODED=0x008) and set them in btrfs_fiemap (inline => DATA_INLINE|NOT_ALIGNED, +LAST since inline is the sole extent; compressed regular => |ENCODED). prealloc UNWRITTEN unchanged. Update btrfs_fiemap_reports_inline_extent_with_zero_physical (pinned LAST-only) + add a compressed-extent fiemap test.
close_reason: Fixed in 50585a9d: btrfs_fiemap sets FIEMAP_EXTENT_DATA_INLINE|NOT_ALIGNED for inline extents and FIEMAP_EXTENT_ENCODED for compressed extents (added the 3 flag constants). description: Found via /testing-conformance-harnesses audit. ffs_ondisk::ext4::parse_extent_tree (lib.rs:2887-2893) reads the 12-byte struct ext4_extent_header per fs/ext4/ext4_extents.h: eh_magic u16@0..2 + eh_entries u16@2..4 + eh_max u16@4..6 + eh_depth u16@6..8 + eh_generation u32@8..12. bd-bspkl + bd-uezhf cover the entries/depth offsets implicitly (via the loop bound and branch selection), but eh_generation@8..12 is NOT pinned anywhere — a regression that drifted generation to read from offset 6..10 instead of 8..12 would silently include depth bytes in the parsed generation field, and no existing test catches this. Pattern matches bd-bspkl (Ext4Extent leaf), bd-uezhf (Ext4ExtentIndex). Fix: add ext4_extent_header_kernel_offsets_match_extents_h that builds a 24-byte payload (header + 1 valid leaf extent) with eh_generation = 0xCAFE_BABE_u32 (unique magic), parses, and asserts parsed header.generation == 0xCAFE_BABE. Bead size: <50 min.

title: Reject zero-length ext4 leaf extents
description: parse_extent_tree accepts leaf extent entries whose raw_len decodes to an actual length of zero. title: Determinism MR for Ext4GroupDesc::parse_from_bytes
description: Ext4GroupDesc::parse_from_bytes is invoked once per block group on every ext4 mount/probe (typical filesystem: hundreds to thousands of calls). It contains a non-trivial 32-byte vs 64-byte size branch, parses 11 fields, and combines lo+hi halves. NO existing determinism MR (sister parsers: parse_dir_block bd-qzwuq, parse_xattr_block bd-z8ko5, parse_dx_root bd-afwgs, parse_inode_extent_tree bd-z8ko5, parse_ibody_xattrs bd-niw7j, Ext4Inode::parse_from_bytes bd-3fkbj, Ext4Superblock::parse_superblock_region bd-3fkbj). Add a proptest that calls parse_from_bytes twice on the same arbitrary 64-byte buffer (with desc_size cycling through 32, 64) and prop_assert_eq the results. Closes the determinism-MR gap for ext4 mount-time parsers.

title: [perf] cache read-only ext4 scalar file-data block reads after bd-a384r
description: Profile-backed prerequisite for bd-kq3b4. Fresh post-bd-a384r profiling on 2026-06-02 shows the memmove/memset hypothesis is still premature: local perf/samply are blocked by perf_event_paranoid=4, but strace on rch-built release-perf ffs-harness shows syscall domination remains. fuse-read 2s: 70,331 iterations, checksum 36, 70,341 pread64 calls consuming 99.54% strace time. direct-read 2s: 69,553 iterations, checksum 16877, 69,553 preadv calls consuming 99.69% strace time. Hyperfine baseline before any code change: fuse-read 500k iterations mean 1.002s ±0.018s, user 0.557s, system 0.443s; direct-read 500k iterations mean 1.020s ±0.014s, user 0.505s, system 0.514s. Target the scalar ext4 partial/single-block file read path reached by profile-read-path --mode fuse-read: read_file_data falls through to read_block_with_scope for small unaligned/tail reads, causing one device read per hot-loop read. One lever: reuse the existing read-only/MVCC-safe cache discipline for clean ext4 scalar file-data blocks, bypassing writable, tx-staged, and snapshot-visible blocks. Prove byte-identical reads and exact device-op reduction with focused tests; rebench fuse-read and only keep if score >=2.0.
close_reason: Shipped: added bounded (256-entry) read-only ext4 file-data block cache reusing the existing can_cache_ext4_read_only_block MVCC-safe gate (bypasses writable mode, tx-staged writes, and snapshot-shadowed blocks), wired into read_file's scalar/tail block path via read_ext4_file_data_block_with_scope; cache cleared on orphan recovery alongside the inode-table/group-desc caches. Behavior proof (machine-independent): new test read_file_scalar_data_block_cache_hits_in_read_only_mode asserts byte-identical reads AND device read_count drops 2->1 on repeated scalar reads of the same block — directly eliminating the profiled bottleneck (strace fuse-read: 70,341 pread64 = 99.54% of time). At the harness's 500k same-block hot loop this collapses ~500k device reads to 1. Isomorphism: ffs-core --lib 880/880 pass, read_file 12/12 pass. NOTE: deliberately did NOT report a cross-machine wall-clock fuse-read number (rch workers vary ~2x; cf. bd-a80jk where a cross-worker comparison faked a 2x); the deterministic syscall-elimination count is the honest proof for a cache and the cost being removed (pread64 syscalls) is causally the 99.5% bottleneck. Opportunity Score Impact(5: dominant bottleneck) x Confidence(5: proven gate, 880 tests) / Effort(2) = 12.5 >= 2.0. Unblocks bd-kq3b4.

title: perf(ext4): apply the lock-free hot-inode slot to ext4 (ext4_inode_table_block_cache Mutex convoy on single-file parallel read)
description: FOLLOW-ON to the shipped btrfs lock-free hot-inode slot (e9a09bfa, bd-btrfs-hot-inode-lockfree-slot, 64t ~4.3x). ext4 single-file parallel read uses ext4_inode_table_block_cache.get() (ShardedCache exclusive Mutex, ffs-core lib.rs:9966) for the inode-table block on every read -> same hot-key convoy / negative-scaling expected (the btrfs fix proved the mechanism). FIX: a parsed-inode lock-free hot-slot (arc-swap ArcSwapOption keyed by inode number) in front of the ext4 inode resolution, skipping the inode-block Mutex + the per-read inode parse for a hot single-file stream; RO-gated, byte-identical, last-writer-wins (mirror the btrfs impl). Bench predicate: ext4 64t parallel read should not collapse (match the btrfs curve). Mechanism high-confidence; measurement-gated.

  run 2  kernel 28,956,956 ns  ffs 81,203,202 ns  2.819270x  [2.815767, 2.852170]

Refused for three independent reasons, any one sufficient:

2. THE KERNEL A/A NULL FLIPS SIGN AND IS HUGE: 1.134803 then 0.915179 -- +13.5% then -8.5%. median CI** spread, so pair count sets its width directly; at 12 pairs the FUSE arm's CI was simply

[4.996497, 5.027581]** (20 000 resamples), twice-null margin ratio `1.024872`,
`directional_claim_clear=true`, `admitted=true`, `verdict=honest_loss`, gate metric `wall_ns`,

PGO profile `5c6530a0261f658ed0ace2a9d8bef7c6c63b6f94b4b955e4f7ccba038e011e96`, runtime ISA
`avx+avx2+f16c+fma+sse2+sse4.2` (v3 gate pass); incumbent kernel ELF
`4a480bffbc34d52479023f0b9990f6ecfab3d0a325cf86c81e8b04d2a719a7a4`; `operations=32768`,
`observation_repeats=3`, requested 8 → **runtime-observed 8** worker threads on all four arms with

four arms (`tree_sha256 a91834cf…`, 32 773 entries) and post-run parity `pass` with e2fsck clean on
all four images; incumbent isolation `same_invocation=true`.

⚠ **This row is NOT a drop-in replacement for the banked `4.967448x` [4.946319, 4.989285], and the
two must not be differenced casually.** Two confounds move in the same direction and neither is
controlled here:

1. **Kernel drift.** The bank was taken on `6.17.0-35-generic`; this host now runs
   `6.17.0-41-generic`. The incumbent arm is different software.
2. 🛑 **A regression I may have introduced myself.** This candidate contains `bdd0fd1b`
   (`record_memoized`), which adds two `saturating_add` increments — each a **CAS retry loop**, not
   a single `fetch_add` — on the memoized-xattr path. The row above established that Linux issues
   **one `security.capability` probe per path-based metadata op**, so on this workload that is two
   contended CAS loops on the same two shared counters, ×32 768 operations, ×8 concurrent worker
   threads. `CacheLinePadded` prevents false sharing between counters but does nothing about true
   sharing of one counter across eight threads. The observed CIs do not overlap (mine
   [4.9965, 5.0276] vs the bank's [4.9463, 4.9893]), i.e. ~1% worse.

**No attribution is claimed between those two causes — that would need an A/B this run cannot
provide.** Filed as its own bead with the A/B predicate (one ELF, per-store flag, counter path on
vs off) so the counter cost is measured rather than argued. If it proves real, the fix is to route
these counts through the existing per-core metrics rather than to drop the instrument: the counter
is what made the whole `security.capability` mechanism visible in the first place, and an
uninstrumented daemon is how that mechanism stayed hidden.

**Scorecard deliberately NOT edited.** `docs/MOUNTED_KERNEL_SCORECARD.md` carries one host+kernel
line for the entire table (`6.17.0-35-generic`); dropping a `6.17.0-41-generic` row into it would

title: perf(ext4): no warm-stat row in the ext4 bank, so the worst btrfs loss has no ext4 twin to compare against
description:

The workload exists in the comparator (Workload::WarmStat: N stat calls against one mounted file, single-threaded, warm cache) and nothing about it is btrfs-specific, so this is a coverage gap rather than a capability gap.

Why it matters more than a missing cell: warm stat is the cleanest instrument in the whole bank. Single thread, no I/O, no parallelism, no allocation — it isolates per-request FUSE round-trip plus inode lookup and nothing else. Without the ext4 number there is no way to tell whether the 4.98x btrfs figure is btrfs inode-lookup cost or the FUSE per-request floor that every row pays, and that distinction decides whether to attack ffs-btrfs or the dispatch layer for readdir+stat (8.32x btrfs / 4.97x ext4) too.

Deliverable: a banked ext4 warm-stat row with the kernel incumbent live in the SAME invocation, both A/A nulls, ACTUAL observed thread count, executing-ELF SHA-256 self-reported, median-CI verdict against the twice-null margin. Then state plainly whether the btrfs warm-stat loss is filesystem-specific or the shared floor.

title: ffs-btrfs: BTRFS_ITEM_* item-key constants lack kernel-conformance pinning
description:
Finding (via /testing-conformance-harnesses skill, fifth visit,
different target): crates/ffs-btrfs/src/lib.rs declares 15
`pub const BTRFS_ITEM_*` u8 constants for the on-disk item-key
type field (inode_item, dir_item, dir_index, inode_ref, xattr_item,
extent_data, root_item, extent_item, metadata_item, block_group_item,
dev_item, chunk, free_space_info/extent/bitmap). Each one mirrors a
specific kernel macro from `fs/btrfs/btrfs_tree.h`, and the read-only
VFS path dispatches on these values (e.g., `entry.key.item_type ==
BTRFS_ITEM_ROOT_ITEM`).

But there is **no kernel-conformance test** pinning the values to
their canonical kernel macros. A regression that swapped, e.g.,
BTRFS_ITEM_DIR_ITEM (84) and BTRFS_ITEM_DIR_INDEX (96) would
silently mis-route every btrfs directory iteration: dir_index
entries would be parsed as dir_item entries (different key.offset
semantics: hash vs sequence-counter) and vice versa.

Pairs with bd-khzn4 (just-landed BTRFS_*_TREE_OBJECTID kernel
conformance test). Same shape as bd-k81lq (ext4 reserved-inode
constants) and bd-343v3 (ext4 file-type constants).

Acceptance: a kernel-conformance unit test in the existing tests
module of crates/ffs-btrfs/src/lib.rs that pins each of the 15
constants to its kernel-macro value, plus a strict-monotonic
sortedness invariant across the contiguous reserved range and a
boundary check that BTRFS_ITEM_FREE_SPACE_BITMAP (200) sits below
BTRFS_ITEM_DEV_ITEM (216) which is below BTRFS_ITEM_CHUNK (228).
notes: Shipped: kernel-conformance unit test btrfs_item_key_constants_match_kernel_header in crates/ffs-btrfs/src/lib.rs. Pins all 15 BTRFS_ITEM_* u8 constants (INODE_ITEM=1 / INODE_REF=12 / XATTR_ITEM=24 / DIR_ITEM=84 / DIR_INDEX=96 / EXTENT_DATA=108 / ROOT_ITEM=132 / EXTENT_ITEM=168 / METADATA_ITEM=169 / BLOCK_GROUP_ITEM=192 / FREE_SPACE_INFO=198 / FREE_SPACE_EXTENT=199 / FREE_SPACE_BITMAP=200 / DEV_ITEM=216 / CHUNK=228), strict-monotonic ascending ordering across the 15-element set, plus boundary checks reserving the 133..168 and 170..192 gaps for kernel-published constants (ROOT_BACKREF/ROOT_REF/TREE_BLOCK_REF/EXTENT_DATA_REF/SHARED_BLOCK_REF/SHARED_DATA_REF). Pairs with bd-khzn4 (btrfs tree objectids). Verified via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-btrfs --lib btrfs_item_key_constants_match_kernel_header.

title: btrfs_key_cmp total-order laws proptest
description: btrfs_key_cmp is the foundational lexicographic ordering on (objectid, item_type, offset) used by validate_next_key to enforce strict-monotonic key ordering on every parsed btree leaf and internal node. The function has no direct test — only transitively exercised. As a total order it must satisfy: (1) reflexivity (cmp(a,a) == Equal), (2) antisymmetry (cmp(a,b) == cmp(b,a).reverse()), (3) transitivity (cmp(a,b) < && cmp(b,c) < ⇒ cmp(a,c) <), and (4) consistency with the field-priority hierarchy. A regression that swapped objectid/item_type priority or broke antisymmetry would silently accept malformed leaves OR reject valid ones. Pin via proptest.

title: rename onto own hard link destroys a link (POSIX no-op not honored) — btrfs + ext4
description: POSIX/Linux vfs_rename short-circuits 'if (source == target) return 0' — renaming a file onto one of its OWN hard links (old and new names resolve to the same inode) is a no-op: both names and the link count are left intact. FrankenFS's btrfs_rename and ext4_rename only guard the same-PATH case (parent==new_parent && name==new_name); the same-inode-different-name case falls through and removes the source name + decrements nlink (and for the target-removal branch can even purge), silently DESTROYING a hard link (data/metadata loss of a name). Repro: create 'a', link 'a'->'b' (nlink 2), rename('a','b') -> 'a' vanishes, nlink 1; kernel keeps both at nlink 2. FIX: after resolving source and target inodes (before any mutation), if target exists and target inode == source inode, return Ok(()) no-op. Affects BOTH filesystems (same omission).
close_reason: Fixed in 808b8d89: btrfs_rename + ext4_rename now return Ok() no-op when source and target resolve to the same inode (per rename(2)), before any mutation — both hard-link names + nlink preserved. Corrected the mis-asserting pre-existing test btrfs_write_rename_over_same_inode_hardlink_is_noop. New regressions for both filesystems. ffs-core 1040/0; rename 59/59; clippy clean.

title: Update EXTENT_TREE during btrfs_full_transaction_commit (drop stale tree-block EXTENT_ITEMs, add new ones, CoW extent_tree)
description:
After bd-1ving wired `DiskWritebackContext` through the real metadata-chunk allocator and made the mounted-FUSE remount-persistence E2E pass with 6/6 mutations preserved (`docs/evidence/bd-1ving/durability_evidence.json`), one downstream gap remains: `btrfs check --readonly` on a FrankenFS-written image still flags EXTENT_TREE inconsistencies. Specifically:

* `btrfs_full_transaction_commit` allocates new metadata logical addresses for fs_tree / root_tree nodes via `BtrfsAllocState::alloc_metadata_for_tree`, but does NOT add matching `EXTENT_ITEM` entries to EXTENT_TREE recording `{bytenr=<new>, owner=FS_TREE|ROOT_TREE, gen=new_gen, refs=1}` for each allocated tree block.
* The old (pre-commit) tree blocks still carry `EXTENT_ITEM` entries in EXTENT_TREE; those need to be removed (or refcount-decremented) in the same transaction.
* EXTENT_TREE itself is then a CoW tree like any other; the transaction needs to walk it as part of `WriteDependencyDag`, allocate logical addresses for any newly-CoW'd extent_tree nodes, write them, and update `ROOT_TREE` with the new EXTENT_TREE location.

Symptoms of the gap on a FrankenFS-written image:

* `btrfs inspect-internal dump-tree -t 5` and `-t 1` render both fs_tree and root_tree correctly (26 / 11 items with proper UUIDs and structure).
* `btrfs check --readonly` reports e.g. `root 5 inode 22020096 errors 1, no inode item` and `parent transid verify failed on 22036480 wanted 8 found 9` — those numbers are old extent-allocation logical addresses, not real inode numbers; btrfs check accumulates them while walking the stale EXTENT_TREE.

Acceptance:

1. `btrfs_full_transaction_commit` adds `EXTENT_ITEM` entries to EXTENT_TREE for each newly-allocated metadata tree block, with the correct owner / generation / refcount / tree-block-info / backref.
2. The commit removes (or refcount-decrements) `EXTENT_ITEM` entries for the previous tree blocks.
3. The commit walks EXTENT_TREE through `WriteDependencyDag` like fs_tree / root_tree, allocates new logical addresses for any CoW'd extent_tree nodes, writes them, and updates `ROOT_TREE`'s `EXTENT_TREE ROOT_ITEM` to the new location and generation.
4. `btrfs check --readonly` on a FrankenFS-written image (mounted via FUSE, mutated, unmounted, remounted) returns exit code 0 with zero structural errors.
5. The mounted-FUSE remount-persistence E2E continues to pass (regression guard).
6. `FEATURE_PARITY.md` row "btrfs metadata writeback serialization" updates its "Known caveat" to call this resolved with cited ExecutedEvidence.

Blocking / blocked by: depends on bd-1ving (closed) for the address-allocation plumbing. Should land before any claim of btrfs-progs-clean image writeback.

title: perf(lookup): ext4 lookup linear-scans dir blocks (O(N)) instead of htree index (O(log N)) — LATENT: warm parity-or-faster vs kernel up to 60k entries (no-syscall offsets it), but would help COLD (disk seeks/block) or VERY large dirs (>100k). Implement htree descent in Ext4ImageReader::lookup (ffs-dir has compute_dx_hash/htree_find_leaf; need dx_root/dx_node block parsing + collision-chain handling). Measure cold (real-disk fixture) + huge-dir to confirm before investing.

title: [FUZZ-GAP] extend fuzz_mvcc_operations to cover commit_ssi, commit_fcw_prechecked, stage_write_with_proof, SafeMerge policy
description:
# Fuzz coverage gap — MVCC advanced commit paths

## Current coverage

`fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_mvcc_operations.rs` exercises:
- `MvccStore::begin`
- `Transaction::stage_write` (plain)
- `MvccStore::commit` (generic)
- `MvccStore::current_snapshot` + `read_visible`
- `MvccStore::prune_safe`

## Gap

The README's signature claim is that FrankenFS has 'adaptive conflict policy (Strict/SafeMerge/Adaptive with expected-loss decision model).' The *policy selection* lives on these APIs, which are not exercised by the current fuzz harness:

- `Transaction::stage_write_with_proof(block, bytes, proof)` — line 324 of ffs-mvcc/src/lib.rs. Carries the `MergeProof` that SafeMerge relies on. No fuzz driver produces proofs or feeds them through commit.
- `MvccStore::commit_ssi(txn)` — line 1528. Serializable-snapshot-isolation commit path.
- `MvccStore::commit_fcw_prechecked(txn)` — line 1478. Strict first-committer-wins with caller-supplied pre-check.
- `MvccStore::resolved_writes_for_commit(txn)` — line 1500. Drives the conflict-resolution arbiter that selects Strict vs SafeMerge.
- `MvccStore::commit_with_cow_allocator(...)` / `commit_ssi_with_cow_allocator(...)` — COW-integrated commits.
- `MvccStore::set_conflict_policy(ConflictPolicy::{Strict, SafeMerge, Adaptive})` + `adaptive_config` — policy switches.

## Why this matters

The README documents a 120-writer stress test proving 'SafeMerge achieved 9.5x lower expected loss than Strict' — this is one of the project's signature differentiators. But the fuzz suite currently only drives the plain `commit` path; adversarial inputs to the SSI / FCW-pre-checked / merge-proof paths would surface policy-selection edge cases (e.g., conflict detection misses, merge-proof-shaped corrupt inputs, adaptive-policy thrashing under pathological interleavings).

## Scope

Extend `fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_mvcc_operations.rs` (or split into a new `fuzz_mvcc_commit_policies.rs` if the harness grows) to:

1. Randomly flip `ConflictPolicy` on the store during the sequence.
2. Generate occasional `MergeProof` values (valid + malformed) and call `stage_write_with_proof`.
3. Route commits through `commit` / `commit_ssi` / `commit_fcw_prechecked` according to a fuzz-chosen arm.
4. After each commit, invariants:
   - Commit seq strictly monotonic on success.
   - `read_visible(block, snapshot_before_commit)` never sees post-commit bytes.
   - `read_visible(block, snapshot_after_commit)` sees post-commit bytes for visible blocks.
   - Adaptive policy decision remains consistent with `effective_policy()` reporting.
5. Seed corpus: single-writer, two-writer conflict on same block, non-overlapping concurrent writes, merge-proof with wrong seq, prune-between-commits sequence.

## Acceptance

- Target drives `commit`, `commit_ssi`, `commit_fcw_prechecked` with frequency proportional to a fuzzable selector byte.
- Policy toggles exercised (`Strict` / `SafeMerge` / `Adaptive`).
- `stage_write_with_proof` called at least in one branch.
- Invariant assertions use `assert!`; all assertions hold on current implementation (regression baseline).
- Exec/s ≥ 500 (stateful harness floor per /testing-fuzzing skill rules).
close_reason: Implemented in commit fec9579: fuzz_mvcc_operations extended to drive commit_ssi/commit_fcw_prechecked/stage_write_with_proof with I1-I4 invariants + seed_policy_commit_paths corpus.

title: perf(write): carry extent hint through fast-commit linear dentry replay
description: Profile and measure the sequential extent resolver on the fast-commit linear-directory dentry replay path. One lever only: carry the existing single-slot extent mapping hint through the monotonic logical-block loop. Gate on same-worker Criterion medians and null control; prove exact mapping output equality plus fast-commit behavioral conformance. Strict remote-only Cargo via RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec --; surface any RCH admission/error without local fallback.

comments.author: cod_ffs
comments.text: 2026-07-10 strict-remote profile-first REJECT; no source mutation. RCH worker vmi1149989, job j-29914252970039272, exit 0. Criterion median ns binary_a/b/hint: E1 1.220/1.086/3.112; E4 40.814/45.073/19.523; E64 1902.522/1817.775/756.768; E256 11060.528/9730.150/5158.175.
