title: Fix btrfs INODE_REF metadata loss for same-parent hard links
description: Btrfs INODE_REF items are keyed by (child,parent) but current insert/remove logic treats the payload as a singleton. Same-parent hard links to the same inode overwrite sibling backrefs on insert and drop all backrefs on removal. Track helper refactor, regression coverage, and verification.
close_reason: Fixed btrfs INODE_REF payload handling for same-parent hard links. Insert/remove now merge and surgically delete individual backref names instead of overwriting/deleting the whole (child,parent) item. Added regression btrfs_write_hard_links_same_parent_preserve_all_inode_refs. Verified with cargo fmt and focused rch test; lib clippy also passed.

title: fuse opendir rejects non-directory and missing inodes
description:
Phase B mock-code-finder finding: crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs has opendir return reply.opened(0, 0) after a no-op request scope, and releasedir documents that opendir returns dummy handles. That means FUSE opendir can succeed for missing inodes or regular files; the first real error is deferred until readdir/fsyncdir, which is not kernel-compatible and weakens FUSE boundary validation.

Fix: route opendir through a small validation path that calls FsOps::getattr for the requested inode, returns NotDirectory unless the attr kind is Directory, and only then replies success. Keep the existing handle value/open flags unless the adapter has a real directory-handle table. Update the releasedir comment so it no longer claims dummy opendir behavior.

Tests: add ffs-fuse unit coverage for the validation helper: directory attr succeeds; regular-file attr returns ENOTDIR/FfsError::NotDirectory; missing inode preserves the FsOps NotFound error.

Validation: cargo fmt -p ffs-fuse --check; rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-fuse opendir -- --nocapture; rch exec -- cargo check -p ffs-fuse --all-targets; rch exec -- cargo clippy -p ffs-fuse --all-targets -- -D warnings; br dep cycles --json.
close_reason: Implemented opendir getattr/type validation with focused ffs-fuse tests

title: btrfs original-mode check: total extent tree bytes 0 / chunk not found in block group
description: After lowmem btrfs check passes fully (41cc5ea6), the ORIGINAL-mode 'btrfs check' (no --mode lowmem) still fails on a FrankenFS-created+committed image: 'total extent tree bytes: 0', 'Chunk[256,228,X]: ... is not found in block group' for ALL block groups, and the 'ref mismatch ... extent item 0, found 1' cascade. lowmem [3/8] checking extents PASSES, so the on-disk extent tree + block groups are structurally valid; original-mode uses a different extent-tree load/accounting path (builds a full in-memory extent-record cache via the block-group/free-space path) that reports the extent tree as empty. Likely a block-group-cache or extent-tree-walk detail original mode is stricter about. Diagnose via btrfs_dump_tree_bd_myrgc_diag (dumps both modes). Last btrfs-check gap for bd-x36qn. Found by AmberOtter.
close_reason: Fixed in f31ce06b: tree-block header flags were written as 0; real btrfs sets WRITTEN|(MIXED_BACKREF_REV<<56). With flags=0 btrfs check read EXTENT_ITEMs in the OLD separate-backref format, ignored FrankenFS's inline TREE_BLOCK_REFs, and reported 'total extent tree bytes: 0' + 'extent item 0 / no backref' in original mode. Set BTRFS_HEADER_FLAGS_COMMITTED in DiskWritebackContext::params_for_block. VALIDATED with real btrfs-progs v6.16: FrankenFS-created+committed file now passes 'btrfs check' in BOTH original and lowmem mode ('no error found', total extent tree bytes: 16384). Last btrfs-check gap closed.

title: [bug] FileByteDevice vectored read accepts empty buffers
description: FileByteDevice::read_vectored_exact_at calls preadv even when the total vectored length is zero; preadv returns 0 for that no-op and the implementation reports UnexpectedEof. Exact zero-byte reads should be a successful no-op, matching scalar/default ByteDevice behavior and ByteBlockDevice empty contiguous reads. Add an early return plus regression coverage.
close_reason: VERIFIED (cc): read_vectored_exact_at total_len==0 no-op before preadv/bounds (lib.rs:581); test file_byte_device_empty_vectored_read_is_noop (7543). cargo test: ok.

title: test(ffs-block): pin FileByteDevice u64 range overflow guards
description: FileByteDevice has scalar read, vectored read, and write offset+length u64 overflow checks separate from ordinary out-of-bounds validation. Existing file-backed tests cover empty I/O, mixed zero-length iovecs, and end>len bounds errors, but not the arithmetic overflow branches. Add a no-mock tempfile-backed regression that asserts each overflow returns the specific Format branch before mutating read buffers or file contents.
close_reason: VERIFIED (cc): file_byte_device_rejects_u64_range_overflow_before_io (ffs-block:7741). cargo test: ok.

title: fix(ffs-error): map filesystem io::ErrorKind values to POSIX errno
description: FfsError::to_errno preserves raw OS errno but synthetic io::Error values fall back to an ErrorKind table. The table covered older generic kinds but newer stable filesystem/network kinds such as StorageFull, ReadOnlyFilesystem, DirectoryNotEmpty, FileTooLarge, QuotaExceeded, CrossesDevices, and NotSeekable fell through to EIO. Map the stable POSIX-equivalent ErrorKind variants to their precise errno values and add table coverage so FUSE/userspace sees ENOSPC, EROFS, ENOTEMPTY, and related errors instead of generic EIO.
close_reason: VERIFIED (cc): errno_mapping_covers_io_error_kinds + io_error_kind_mapping_without_raw_errno (ffs-error:370/731) map io::ErrorKind->POSIX errno. cargo test: ok.

title: ffs-inode does not compile on main: stale free_inode_persist arity and Vec/SmallVec inode extent_bytes
description:
HEAD does not build. crates/ffs-inode/src/lib.rs is two API revisions behind its dependencies:

1. line 786 calls ffs_alloc::free_inode_persist with 6 arguments; the function has taken a 7th (is_dir: bool) since the bd-0y7jp used_dirs maintenance landed in ffs-alloc (E0061).
2. line 378 initialises Ext4Inode::extent_bytes with a Vec<u8>; ffs-ondisk changed that field to Ext4InodeBlockBytes = SmallVec<[u8; 64]> (E0308).

Both errors are in the LIBRARY target, so every crate that depends on ffs-inode fails to build — the whole workspace, including the harness and the mounted comparator. Found while trying to run a conformance test for bd-ftev0.

Correctness note for the first one: the is_dir argument must be computed BEFORE delete_inode zeroes inode.mode, or the group's bg_used_dirs_count decrement is silently lost.

ffs-inode's own test and bench targets carry further drift (GroupStats missing three fields, serialize_inode_into no longer exported, ~20 more type mismatches); those are filed separately if they are not cleaned up alongside.
close_reason: cargo check -p ffs-inode --all-targets finishes clean (1m17s) on a clean HEAD baseline with no overlay — lib, tests and benches, so the further test/bench drift the description flagged is gone too. Both original errors are resolved: the file was one of seven rolled back by the bulk-revert incident, and d81af6bb restored it from 3b48b7b6^, whose version already passes is_dir to free_inode_persist and already types extent_bytes as the SmallVec. The interim adaptation in 159dae7c is therefore subsumed rather than kept.

title: main does not build: merge 8da28cb3 dropped the ffs-mvcc merge-proof/version-resolve API that sharded.rs calls
description:
The workspace cannot be compiled at HEAD, so no crate downstream of ffs-mvcc (ffs-btrfs, ffs-block, ffs-core, ffs-harness, ffs-cli — effectively everything) can be built or tested by any agent.

Symptoms (cargo check, clean baseline, no working-tree overlay):
  error[E0432]: unresolved import `crate::resolve_version_bytes_cow_at_or_before`   (crates/ffs-mvcc/src/sharded.rs:15)
  error[E0599]: no method named `staged_base` found for reference `&Transaction`
  error[E0599]: no method named `merge_valid` found for enum `MergeProof`

Forensics. Merge 8da28cb3 has parents cd4c8432 (local) and 19532525 (remote), merge-base 48629432. For crates/ffs-mvcc the merge took the REMOTE side of src/lib.rs (HEAD differs from 19532525 by 2 lines, and from cd4c8432 by 270+/1752-). The callers in src/sharded.rs — lines 15, 935, 937, 942, 944, 1073, 1074, 1079 — survived, but their definitions did not:

  - resolve_version_bytes_cow_at_or_before: defined at cd4c8432:crates/ffs-mvcc/src/lib.rs:460, absent at HEAD
  - resolve_version_bytes_at_or_before, append_only_merge_valid, merge_non_overlapping_ranges_valid, MergeProof::merge_valid: same, absent at HEAD
  - Transaction::staged_base: absent at HEAD and not in cd4c8432's lib.rs either, so it lives in a third file the merge also dropped

This is NOT a small patch: HEAD's ffs-mvcc/src/lib.rs is 1752 lines SHORTER than the local parent's, so a substantial body of MVCC merge-proof work is missing, and restoring it means choosing between two divergent versions of the engine. That is a decision for whoever owns the sharded/merge-proof lane, not a mechanical fix — which is why this is filed rather than repaired unilaterally.

Two sibling breaks from the same merge are already handled: bd-k1t70 (workspace.dependencies lost `xattr`; fixed in 0821d10c) and bd-ffs-inode-head-build-break-ua2k9 (ffs-inode two API revisions behind ffs-alloc/ffs-ondisk). Both were found the same way. It is worth assuming more of this merge is unsound until the workspace builds end to end.

Probe to close on: RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec --clean-overlay --base HEAD --no-overlay -- cargo check --workspace --all-targets exits 0.
close_reason: Named probe passes: rch exec --clean-overlay --base HEAD --no-overlay -- cargo check --workspace finished in 4m49s with zero errors on a clean baseline with no working-tree overlay. The ffs-mvcc half was fixed by restoring lib.rs from 921831b7^ in f4e77542 — that crate went from E0432/E0599/E0308/E0277 to clean in 1m28s. The rest of the chain the compiler then exposed is recorded and closed on bd-bulk-revert-incident-24k-lines-w5hkf.

The existing bench fixtures `ext4_group_desc_32byte.json` and
`ext4_group_desc_64byte.json` already provide deterministic input
bytes; we can parse them once and reuse the resulting Ext4GroupDesc
for the encode bench.

`bench_ext4_group_desc_write_64` to ondisk_parse.rs, register them in

title: btrfs BTRFS_IOC_INO_PATHS and BTRFS_IOC_LOGICAL_INO ioctls
description:
## Summary

Implement reverse-mapping ioctls for btrfs error tracing and path discovery.

- `BTRFS_IOC_INO_PATHS`: Given an inode, find all paths that reference it
- `BTRFS_IOC_LOGICAL_INO`: Given a logical address, find inodes that reference it

These are used by `btrfs check` and scrub to trace filesystem errors back to affected files.

## Kernel reference

- `fs/btrfs/ioctl.c: btrfs_ioctl_ino_to_path()`, `btrfs_ioctl_logical_to_ino()`
- `BTRFS_IOC_INO_PATHS` = `_IOWR(0x94, 35, ...)` = 0xD000_9423
- `BTRFS_IOC_LOGICAL_INO` = `_IOWR(0x94, 36, ...)` = 0xD000_9424

## Implementation scope

1. Add ioctl constants and dispatch in ffs-fuse
2. Add trait methods in ffs-core/vfs.rs
3. Walk backref tree to resolve paths/inodes in ffs-core/lib.rs

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit tests for argument validation
- Integration test with known inode → path mapping
- EOPNOTSUPP returned for ext4 backend

title: fuzz: no dedicated fuzz target for ext4 *_extra timestamp bit-pack contract
description:
Finding (via /testing-fuzzing skill, NEW target): fuzz/fuzz_targets has 49 targets but NONE dedicated to the Ext4Inode::extra_nsec / extra_epoch bit-pack contract. The newly-shipped bd-834zk proptest (32 cases) pins the [nsec:30][epoch:2] u32 layout; a libfuzzer target lifts that to >1M iterations/session with corpus learning across mask-edge u32 values, sign-bit boundaries, and pathological bit patterns.

The bit-pack helpers are on the hot path for every inode timestamp read on ext4 v6+ filesystems. A regression that swapped the masks (epoch ⇔ nsec) would silently corrupt every timestamp on every ext4 image — invisible to substring tests.

Acceptance: new fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_ext4_extra_bit_pack.rs that, for arbitrary u32 input, asserts:
  * MR1 — Bit-pack inverse: (extra_nsec(x) << 2) | extra_epoch(x) == x
  * MR2 — Epoch bound: extra_epoch(x) ≤ 3
  * MR3 — Nsec bound: extra_nsec(x) ≤ 0x3FFFFFFF
  * MR4 — Disjoint encoding: extra_nsec(epoch_only) == 0 and extra_epoch(nsec_only) == 0
  * MR5 — Never panics on any u32
Plus a [[bin]] entry in fuzz/Cargo.toml.

title: Profile fsync and journal commit latency gap vs kernel ext4
description: Evidence correction 2026-07-10. The old ovh-a row (FrankenFS 71.744 us vs host syscall 23.654 us, nominally 3.033x slower; CV 44.94% / 97.22%) is routing evidence only, not a current-source or keep-gate ratio. The arms are API/durability asymmetric: direct OpenFs write+fsync versus host syscalls; the host backing filesystem was not proven ext4/JBD2; FrankenFS performs duplicate sync work; there was no warmup/interleaving; and final e2fsck does not prove per-fsync durability. The refined hz2 attempts never reached the workload executable or e2fsck; they were interrupted during cold fat-LTO compile/link, so the earlier executable-phase attribution is withdrawn. Next work: build a same-boundary persistent harness, verify the kernel arm is ext4, match durability semantics, run at least 30 interleaved same-worker release-perf batches with cv_pct < 5, validate bytes and durability outside timing, then profile only if a gap survives. title: FrankenFS returns EIO on positioned writes to a btrfs mount
description:
Deterministic 6/6: the mounted comparator's fsync-journal-commit workload (8 x 4KiB positioned writes to one file, fsync after each) fails on a FrankenFS-mounted btrfs image with:

  positioned write .../btrfs/fuse_a/fsync.bin: Input/output error (os error 5)

Reproduce: ffs-mounted-kernel-bench --filesystem btrfs --workload fsync-journal-commit --operations 8 --pairs 128 --observation-repeats 1 --image-size-mib 512

Scope: the identical workload succeeds on FrankenFS ext4 (banked 0.997098x neutral row), and the btrfs KERNEL arms are unaffected, so this is specific to the FrankenFS btrfs write path. Failure is at the first positioned write, before any timing.

Impact: btrfs fsync/journal-commit is the one workload of six that cannot be scored at all, so the btrfs scorecard is 1 win / 4 losses / 1 UNRUNNABLE. A capability gap outranks a slow ratio.

Evidence: docs/MOUNTED_BTRFS_SCORECARD.md; driver 4b0f0889..., candidate f44b3dc4... (x86-64-v3 + PGO 6a22cfcf).
close_reason: Both named probes pass on the live tree: btrfs_positioned_write_over_mkfs_populated_file_conforms (ffs-harness conformance — the 8x4KiB positioned-write + fsync reproduction of the failing workload) and reconciled_block_group_accounting_makes_a_preexisting_extent_freeable_bd_ftev0 (ffs-btrfs, including its negative case). Root cause: block-group used_bytes seeded synthetically from the chunk map before the on-disk extent tree was walked, so the first free of an image-resident extent underflowed the tally and surfaced as EIO. Fix calls the existing sync_block_group_accounting() at load, guarded on extent_tree_items_loaded > 0. Full evidence in the closing comment. The scorecard ROW remains unscored — that needs a four-arm mounted run and is filed separately.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Fix + tests landed in 32dd093f (pushed to main):

- crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs calls sync_block_group_accounting() at load, immediately
  after the on-disk extent tree is walked, guarded on extent_tree_items_loaded > 0.
- Hermetic pin in ffs-btrfs:
  reconciled_block_group_accounting_makes_a_preexisting_extent_freeable_bd_ftev0.
  It builds the exact mount-time state and includes the negative case a naive fix would
  fail: unreconciled, the free must STILL fail closed with
  BrokenInvariant("block group used bytes underflow"). This is the test
  docs/MOUNTED_BTRFS_SCORECARD.md already cites by name but that was never written.
- End-to-end regression in ffs-harness conformance:
  btrfs_positioned_write_over_mkfs_populated_file_conforms. It mirrors the failing
  workload — an image populated by the btrfs format tool with --rootdir carrying a
  4096-byte fsync.bin, then 8 x 4 KiB positioned writes at offset 0, each followed by
  fsync, readback equality, and a size assertion.

Root cause (confirmed by code forensics; matches the diagnosis already pinned in
docs/MOUNTED_BTRFS_SCORECARD.md, which prescribed this exact fix but had not implemented
it): block groups are registered from the chunk map with a synthetic used_bytes (zero, or
a 128 KiB reserved prefix for a chunk at logical 0) BEFORE the on-disk extent tree is
walked. Every extent the image already carried is therefore invisible to the allocator's
accounting, so the first free of an image-resident extent underflows the tally at
crates/ffs-btrfs/src/lib.rs:5006 -> BrokenInvariant -> FfsError::Corruption -> EIO.
Writes to FrankenFS-created files pass because their extents were allocated in-session,
incrementing the tally first; ext4 is unaffected because it allocates against real
on-disk bitmaps read at mount.

The guard on extent_tree_items_loaded > 0 is deliberate. It avoids the regression the
scorecard predicted for btrfs_largest_contiguous_free_run_uses_allocator_gaps: that
test's fixture (build_btrfs_fsops_image) carries no extent tree at all, so there is
nothing to reconcile from and its existing tally legitimately stands. The underflow guard
itself is NOT weakened — it simply stops being reachable from a correctly loaded
filesystem.

STATUS: NEITHER PROBE HAS RUN YET. Both are blocked by
bd-ffs-mvcc-merge-dropped-merge-proof-api-y1ch7: the workspace does not compile at HEAD,
so ffs-btrfs (through its ffs-mvcc dependency) and ffs-harness cannot be built. Three
clean-baseline runs on three different workers (vmi1293453, vmi1264463, hz1) all died
inside ffs-mvcc. This bead stays open until both named tests are observed passing.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Both named probes observed passing on the live tree.

1. ffs-harness conformance, the end-to-end reproduction of the failing workload:
     test btrfs_positioned_write_over_mkfs_populated_file_conforms ... ok
     test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 102 filtered out; finished in 0.12s
   It builds an image with the btrfs format tool's --rootdir carrying a 4096-byte
   fsync.bin, asserts the pre-write content differs from every payload, then performs
   eight 4 KiB positioned writes at offset 0 — each followed by fsync, a readback
   equality check against that iteration's own bytes, and a size assertion. That is the
   mounted comparator's fsync-journal-commit shape, which failed 6/6 at the first write.

2. ffs-btrfs unit pin:
     test tests::reconciled_block_group_accounting_makes_a_preexisting_extent_freeable_bd_ftev0 ... ok
     test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 375 filtered out
   It builds the exact mount-time state and carries the negative case: unreconciled, the
   free must STILL fail closed with BrokenInvariant("block group used bytes underflow").
   An implementation that "fixed" this by softening the underflow guard instead of
   correcting the tally passes every other assertion and fails that one.

Fix: crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs calls sync_block_group_accounting() at load, immediately
after the on-disk extent tree is walked, guarded on extent_tree_items_loaded > 0.
Block groups are seeded from the chunk map with a synthetic used_bytes before that walk,
so every extent the image already carried was invisible to the allocator's accounting and
the first free of one underflowed at ffs-btrfs/src/lib.rs:5006 -> BrokenInvariant ->
FfsError::Corruption -> EIO. Writes to FrankenFS-created files passed because their
extents were allocated in-session; ext4 was unaffected because it allocates against real
on-disk bitmaps.

The guard is load-bearing, not incidental: the scorecard predicted this fix would regress
btrfs_largest_contiguous_free_run_uses_allocator_gaps, whose fixture asserts 64 free
blocks against the un-reconciled tally. That fixture (build_btrfs_fsops_image) carries no
extent tree, so there is nothing to reconcile from and its tally legitimately stands. No
gate, golden or expectation was weakened to land this.

Landed across: 32dd093f (original fix + both tests), then re-applied onto the restored
ffs-core in d81af6bb after the bulk-revert incident, with the pin restored in 353eab39.

NOT claimed here: this is the capability fix, not a scored row. The btrfs
fsync/journal-commit row in docs/MOUNTED_BTRFS_SCORECARD.md remains unscored — scoring it
needs a four-arm mounted comparator run with the kernel incumbent live in the same
invocation, which needs root for the kernel arms and a quiet window. Filed separately.

title: btrfs QUOTA_CTL ioctl parity
description: Upstream btrfs exposes BTRFS_IOC_QUOTA_CTL (_IOWR(0x94, 40, struct btrfs_ioctl_quota_ctl_args), 16 bytes) in linux/btrfs.h so callers can enable, disable, or enable simple quotas. FrankenFS currently has no constant, FUSE dispatch, or FsOps hook, so callers fall through to ENOTTY instead of a btrfs-aware response. Add the ioctl constant and input/output validation, return EROFS on read-only mounts, route writable requests through an explicit FsOps method under an IoctlWrite request scope, return EOPNOTSUPP for ext4/current unsupported btrfs qgroup state, and add focused dispatcher tests.

title: perf(fuse): per-core mount constructs an inert dispatcher and never routes a request through it
description: Static trace: mount_with_per_core_fuse constructs PerCoreDispatcher, uses it only to choose worker_threads and zero-valued aggregate telemetry, then calls mount_managed without providing dispatcher state to the FUSE request path. The advertised per-core runtime therefore has no request-routing effect. Fix must make runtime selection truthful and cover it with a parent-red CLI-level test; any actual thread-per-core routing remains separately measurable.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FOLLOW-UP HARDENING, not the fix (AzureBay, 2026-08-15).

THE BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE IS ALREADY MET, by a peer, in 2ba60eaa 'fix(cli): fail closed when
--runtime-mode per-core cannot route FUSE requests'. MountRuntimeConfig::validate() now rejects
PerCore with '--runtime-mode per-core runtime is unavailable: its dispatcher does not route FUSE
requests', and mount_cmd rejects it before opening the image, covered by two CLI-level tests
(mount_per_core_config_rejects_inert_dispatcher,
mount_cmd_per_core_mode_rejects_inert_dispatcher_before_opening_image). That is 'runtime selection
made truthful' plus a parent-red CLI-level test, i.e. exactly what this bead asked for. I did not
close it -- not my bead to close.

WHAT WAS STILL WRONG, and is now fixed: failing closed made mount_with_per_core_fuse UNREACHABLE,
but left the falsehood inside it intact. That function still built a per-core observation from a
dispatcher that never routes, and the specific danger is imbalance_ratio(): it returns 1.0 when max
and min are both zero, so an inert dispatcher published PERFECT per-core load balance. The moment
someone wires up routing and re-enables the mode -- which this bead explicitly leaves as separate
work -- that fabricated telemetry comes straight back.

CHANGE: build_mount_per_core_shutdown_observation and emit_per_core_mount_console now publish a
per-core block ONLY when per_core_routing_observed(aggregate) is true (non-zero total OR any
non-zero per-core row, so a partial wiring cannot report a total with no distribution). The debug
log no longer prints an imbalance ratio derived from an inert dispatcher. This is a runtime check on
the counters, not a hardcoded None, so real distributions publish themselves the day routing lands.

TESTS (3 new, ffs-cli):
  per_core_observation_is_omitted_when_the_dispatcher_routed_nothing  -- PARENT-RED, verified
    empirically: with the pre-fix body restored it FAILS on rch worker vmi1227854 with 'a mount

--bin ffs-cli). rustfmt clean (pinned nightly-2026-07-20). ubs: 17 criticals in this 10k-line file,
NONE in my edited ranges -- all pre-existing.

title: [parity] ext4 external xattr blocks written with h_checksum=0 — e2fsck-corrupt on metadata_csum images
description: FrankenFS never stamps the ext4 xattr block checksum (struct ext4_xattr_header.h_checksum at offset 16). build_external_block (crates/ffs-xattr/src/lib.rs:225) zero-fills the block and writes magic/refcount/blocks/h_hash but leaves h_checksum=0; no stamp_xattr_block_checksum / verify_xattr_block_checksum function exists anywhere (ffs-ondisk/ffs-xattr/ffs-core), and the read path does not verify it. On a filesystem with RO_COMPAT_METADATA_CSUM (the default for the modern ext4 format tool — confirmed on conformance/golden/ext4_8mb_reference.ext4: features include metadata_csum + crc32c + ext_attr), the kernel/e2fsck compute ext4_xattr_block_csum = crc32c(s_csum_seed, block_nr as le64) then crc32c over the whole block with the h_checksum field zeroed. So after ANY FrankenFS setxattr/removexattr that creates or modifies an EXTERNAL xattr block (file_acl != 0; triggered when xattrs spill out of the inode ibody), the block carries h_checksum=0 and e2fsck reports 'extended attribute block checksum does not match' = corruption. Same class as bd-vdi91 (FrankenFS must keep metadata_csum images e2fsck-clean) but for xattr blocks. Affected write sites in ffs-core/src/lib.rs: ext4_setxattr new-block write (~13414) and COW block (~13399); apply_ext4_xattr_post_inode_actions UpdateRefcount (~13486, pokes h_refcount then writes - also invalidates csum) and WriteBlock (~13507); ext4_removexattr COW (~13609). FIX PLAN: (1) add ext4_xattr_block_csum + stamp_xattr_block_checksum to ffs-ondisk, validating the formula against an e2fsprogs-written block (debugfs ea_set + e2fsck as oracle); (2) stamp the block when has_metadata_csum, immediately before every block_dev.write_block of an xattr block in the 5 sites above; (3) optionally verify on read. PROOF: e2fsck-clean round-trip on a generated metadata_csum image after a FrankenFS large-xattr setxattr (RED before, GREEN after). RISK: a wrong formula writes corrupt checksums - validate against e2fsprogs first.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: FIXED (commit pending). Wired ffs_ondisk::stamp_xattr_block_checksum into all 5 ext4 external-xattr-block write sites in ffs-core via a new helper stamp_ext4_xattr_block_csum (gated on sb.has_metadata_csum(), keyed on the physical block number + sb.csum_seed()): ext4_setxattr new-block + COW-block writes; apply_ext4_xattr_post_inode_actions UpdateRefcount (restamp after the h_refcount poke) + WriteBlock; ext4_removexattr COW-block. PROOF CHAIN (e2fsck-clean without needing an in-test e2fsck subprocess): (1) ffs-ondisk oracle test xattr_block_csum_matches_e2fsprogs_oracle — ext4_xattr_block_csum reproduces e2fsprogs h_checksum 0x4763fce2 EXACTLY on a real external xattr block written by debugfs ea_set on a metadata_csum image and verified clean by e2fsck -fn (non-circular: both block bytes and expected value come from e2fsprogs); (2) ffs-core write-path test setxattr_external_block_is_metadata_csum_clean_bd_fwph3 — a setxattr spilling a 2000-byte value into an external block yields h_checksum != 0 that verify_xattr_block_checksum accepts, AND stays valid after a removexattr in-place rewrite. Since the formula == e2fsprogs (oracle) and the write path stamps with the correct block_nr+seed, e2fsck WILL accept FrankenFS-written xattr blocks. ffs-core 896 lib tests pass; clippy -D warnings clean; #![forbid(unsafe_code)] intact. Read-side verification of xattr block checksums is deliberately NOT added here (would risk rejecting pre-existing images on any formula edge; write-side stamping is the parity fix) — could be a separate hardening bead.

title: Harden ffs-dir test coverage with property-based and boundary tests
description:
## What
Expand ffs-dir from 49 tests to 70+ with property-based tests (proptest) and additional
boundary/corruption tests.

## Why
ffs-dir has the lowest test count (49) of any non-trivial crate. Directory operations are
safety-critical: a bug in add_entry/remove_entry can corrupt the entire directory structure.
The crate has proptest as a dev-dependency but no property-based tests yet.

## Current Coverage (49 tests)
- init_dir_block: 5 tests (basic, tail, sizes, inode numbers)
- add_entry: 10 tests (split, reuse, enospc, reject, max name, types)
- remove_entry: 7 tests (coalesce, first entry, nonexistent, overlap)
- htree: 8 tests (insert, find, remove, edge cases)
- compute_dx_hash: 3 tests (deterministic, seeds, names)
- Multi-operation: 3 tests (fill, cycle, alternating)
- Corruption detection: 3 tests (rec_len zero, misaligned, exceeds block)

## Gaps to Fill
1. Property-based tests (proptest):
   - proptest_add_remove_roundtrip: random names (1..255 bytes), random inodes,
     add then remove → block parseable, entry gone
   - proptest_add_never_exceeds_block: random sequence of adds → never writes past limit
   - proptest_init_parse_roundtrip: random self_ino, parent_ino, reserved_tail →
     init_dir_block → parse_dir_block → exactly . and .. with correct inodes
   - proptest_htree_insert_always_sorted: random hash sequence → entries always sorted

2. Boundary tests:
   - add_entry with exactly 0 bytes of slack (entry fits perfectly, no split needed)
   - remove_entry of last entry in block (rec_len extends to block end)
   - init_dir_block with reserved_tail = block_size - 24 (minimum viable)
   - add_entry with name at every alignment boundary (1,2,3,4,5,8,12,16 bytes)

3. Corruption resilience:
   - add_entry with rec_len pointing past block boundary
   - remove_entry with circular rec_len chain (entry points back to itself)
   - add_entry to block of all zeros (no valid first entry)

4. Stress tests:
   - Fill 4096-byte block completely, verify parse_dir_block recovers all entries
   - Add 100 entries, remove 50, add 50 more, verify final state

## Implementation Plan
Add to the existing #[cfg(test)] module in crates/ffs-dir/src/lib.rs.
proptest is already a dev-dependency of ffs-dir.

## Test Plan
- cargo test -p ffs-dir --lib → all pass, count >= 70
- proptest cases: 128 per property test
- No flakes in 3 consecutive runs

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 4+ property-based tests added
- [ ] 5+ boundary tests added
- [ ] 3+ corruption resilience tests added
- [ ] 2+ stress tests added
- [ ] Total test count >= 70
- [ ] Zero test flakes
close_reason: Completed

title: perf(repair): parallelize capture_expected_current_blocks serial device reads (I/O-overlap)
description: RecoverySession::capture_expected_current_blocks (ffs-repair recovery.rs:429) reads each corrupt block's scrub-time bytes SERIALLY: for index in corrupt_indices { cx.checkpoint; self.device.read_block(cx, block)?.to_vec() }. The reads are independent; on real storage each pays an access latency (seek/queue/network round trip) so a recovery touching N corrupt blocks serializes N read latencies. LEVER (I/O-overlap, bd-307e4/bd-tyym4/bd-yg6tk family): plan the BlockNumbers serially (cheap, keeps cx.checkpoint cancellation), then read them via blocks.into_par_iter().map(|b| Ok((b, device.read_block(cx,b)?.to_vec()))).collect::<Vec<Result>>() consumed in index order with ? — a blocking read parks its rayon worker so latencies overlap up to pool size (bounded by pool not core count => >2x). BlockDevice: Send+Sync (ffs-block lib.rs:636), Cx: Sync (W152), rayon already a src dep (scrub.rs). Iso: indexed collect preserves block order; serial ?-consume preserves first-error-in-index-order = identical to the serial early-return. Bench target: recovery_capture_io_overlap with a LatencyBlockDevice (250us/read, blocks prebuilt) serial vs parallel, assert_eq verdict. cc filed from ffs-repair quiet-crate frontier (sibling of just-shipped bd-avqg1).
close_reason: VERIFIED bench recovery_capture_io_overlap: serial vs parallel_rayon 7.10x(16)/7.38x(64)/7.68x(256) I/O-overlap. KEEP.

title: btrfs fiemap does not set FIEMAP_EXTENT_SHARED for reflinked/shared extents
description: btrfs_fiemap never sets FIEMAP_EXTENT_SHARED (0x2000). Linux btrfs extent_fiemap sets it for a data extent referenced by more than one inode (reflink via FICLONE/FICLONERANGE, or snapshots) — i.e. EXTENT_ITEM refcount > 1. FrankenFS supports reflink (btrfs_clone_file_data, bd-vh8p9) which bumps the extent refcount via add_data_extent_ref, and tracks it in extent_alloc.extent_item_refs(disk_bytenr, disk_num_bytes), but fiemap ignores it, so filefrag -v / cp --reflink tooling cannot see that an extent is shared. FIX: in btrfs_fiemap, for a regular extent with disk_bytenr != 0 on the writable path, query extent_item_refs and set FIEMAP_EXTENT_SHARED when refs > 1. Read-only images would need an on-disk extent-tree backref walk (separate follow-up). Add the constant + a reflink->fiemap test asserting SHARED on both src and dst and absence on an unshared file.
close_reason: Fixed in 4ac96c55: btrfs_fiemap sets FIEMAP_EXTENT_SHARED for a regular extent with refs>1 (extent_alloc.extent_item_refs) on the writable path. Regression btrfs_fiemap_marks_reflinked_extent_shared_bd_g704k (reflink -> SHARED on src+dst, absent on unshared). Read-only extent-tree backref walk is a follow-up. ffs-core 1048/0; clippy --no-deps clean.

title: Bitmap CRC: remove or deprecate the wrong compute_bitmap_checksum (XOR-based)
description:
ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs has two bitmap checksum functions:
1. ext4_bitmap_checksum (line ~1255): Correct — chains group_number as LE data bytes.

(b) Fix compute_bitmap_checksum to use the correct algorithm (chain, not XOR).
(c) At minimum, add a comment explaining the bug and deprecate.

title: btrfs_send_crc32c associativity + empty-suffix proptest MR
description: btrfs_send_crc32c is the in-house CRC32C primitive (polynomial 0x82F6_3B78 = bit-reversed Castagnoli) used by send_stream_command_crc32c. The command-header CRC computation depends on associativity: btrfs_send_crc32c(crc, &command[10..]) is applied on top of an already-seeded CRC over command[..6] || zeros — which only works if btrfs_send_crc32c(seed, a||b) == btrfs_send_crc32c(btrfs_send_crc32c(seed, a), b). No direct test exists; only transitively exercised through parse_send_stream. Sister bd-8pbjm pins the laws for ext4_chksum, bd-oviw2 for crc32c_append, bd-0djme for ext4_gdt_crc16. Add btrfs_send_crc32c_proptest_empty_suffix_is_seed_identity + btrfs_send_crc32c_proptest_associative_across_appends + three-way variant.

title: [perf][parity][no-gaps] ext4 runtime directory ops are linear O(n), not htree O(log n)
close_reason: Completed read-half: runtime ext4 htree/DX lookup with linear fallback. Baseline linear scaling via rch vmi1167313: N=200 70.323us, N=800 197.634us, N=3200 661.18us. Final same-binary rch A/B vmi1149989: old linear 18.761us vs htree 4.973us = 3.77x. Behavior proof rch vmi1264463 ext4_runtime_htree_lookup_matches_linear_scan_reference passed; clippy rch vmi1293453 passed; golden sha256 manifests passed. Write-side htree maintenance remains separate.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: GAP (code-read, not yet profiled): the runtime ext4 directory paths ignore the htree/dir_index (EXT4_INDEX_FL) index. lookup_name_with_scope (ffs-core lib.rs ~7517) does a LINEAR scan `for lb in 0..num_blocks` reading every directory block and scanning it for the name — O(num_blocks) per lookup. ext4_add_dir_entry appends linearly and does NOT maintain an htree. So: large-directory lookup is O(n) vs upstream htree O(log n), and populating a directory of N entries is O(N^2) (each create does a duplicate-check lookup over the growing dir). CURRENT BEHAVIOR IS CORRECT, just slow: a linear scan over an htree directory still finds all real entries in the leaf blocks and correctly skips dx_root/dx_node index blocks (they present as a single filler dirent with a large rec_len); linear write + linear read both consistently ignore the index. MACHINERY ALREADY EXISTS but is unused at runtime: ffs-ondisk has parse_dx_root / parse_dx_root_with_large_dir + the dirhash (ext4.rs ~4561,4874,4882); ffs-dir has htree_find_leaf / htree_find_leaf_idx / htree_insert / htree_remove / HtreeEntry. NONE are referenced from ffs-core lib.rs (grep: 0 hits). IMPLEMENTATION is ALL-OR-NOTHING (coupled, corruption-risk if partial): wiring htree READ into lookup without also maintaining the index on add/remove/leaf-split would make htree lookups MISS entries that ext4_add_dir_entry added linearly -> correctness bug. So a real fix needs: (1) lookup: if EXT4_INDEX_FL, parse dx_root, hash the name (half-MD4/tea per s_def_hash_version), htree_find_leaf -> scan only that leaf (+ collision continuation); (2) add/remove: maintain dx_root/dx_node entries, split leaves + grow index levels when a leaf fills, and CREATE the index when a linear dir grows past one block (dx_root conversion). Isomorphism: htree lookup must return the same entry as the linear scan for a consistent index. PERF payoff: lookup O(n)->O(log n); dir population O(n^2)->O(n log n) — significant for workloads with large directories (mail spools, object stores, build trees). RISK: high (directory on-disk format + write path); a dedicated multi-step effort with a large-directory benchmark + a real-ext4 htree fixture for read-parity. Same risk class as bd-y6h03 (defer-not-rush). Suggested first step: a criterion bench populating + looking up in a 5k-entry directory to quantify the O(n^2)/O(n) scaling and make this profile-backed.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: PROFILE EVIDENCE (now profile-backed). Ran the scaling profiler profile_linear_directory_scaling_bd_gauub (ffs-core, in-memory generated image, release): N=200 lookup=39.4us, N=800 lookup=78.9us, N=3200 lookup=245.6us — per-lookup scales ~linearly with directory size (4x N -> ~2-3x lookup), confirming the O(n) linear scan in lookup_name_with_scope. populate: 34.3ms / 168ms / 1.137s for N=200/800/3200 (super-linear; per_create grows 171->355us as the dup-check scan lengthens -> O(N^2) population). At 3200 entries a single lookup is already 245us; a 50k-entry dir would be ~ms vs ~us for htree. Artifact: tests/artifacts/perf/2026-06-03_bd-gauub_dir_scaling/scaling.txt. Committed an #[ignore]d profiling tool to reproduce. Confirms bd-gauub is a real, measurable scaling gap (not just theoretical).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: DE-RISKED + SCOPED (correction to the earlier all-or-nothing framing). The READ side can be closed SAFELY and INCREMENTALLY without the risky write-maintenance, via htree-read-with-LINEAR-FALLBACK: in lookup_name_with_scope, if dir_inode.has_htree_index(), navigate the dx index to the candidate leaf and scan it; if found return it; on ANY miss/parse-error/uncertainty, FALL THROUGH to the existing linear scan. Correctness-safe by construction: (a) directory names are unique per dir, so an htree-found entry (scanned from a real leaf block) is always THE correct entry — no false positives; (b) any navigation bug, stale index (FrankenFS adds entries linearly without maintaining htree), or unsupported case just yields a miss -> linear fallback -> correct (only slower). So a porting bug CANNOT cause incorrectness, only loss of speedup. TEMPLATE EXISTS: ffs-ondisk Ext4ImageReader::htree_lookup (ext4.rs ~4543) is complete (dx_root parse, dx_hash, dx_find_leaf_idx, indirect levels, collision-chain continuation, linear fallback) — port it to the runtime using read_block_with_scope + self.resolve_extent(cx,scope,dir_inode,lb) (already used by the linear scan at lib.rs ~7518) and the pub primitives parse_dx_root_with_large_dir / dx_hash / dx_find_leaf_idx / parse_dx_entries / parse_dir_block / dx_hash_extends_collision_chain / effective_dirhash_version / sb.hash_seed. A simpler first cut (single candidate leaf, indirect_levels==0 only, no collision continuation) is also safe (fallback covers the rest). TEST/BENCH FIXTURE: replicate create_dir_index_reference_image (ffs-harness kernel_reference.rs — the ext4 format tool with dir_index + debugfs populating a large directory to force a real htree), open via OpenFs::from_device, then (1) assert htree lookup == linear scan for every entry (isomorphism) and (2) same-binary A/B htree-path vs linear-path on the large htree dir for the measured win. Write-maintenance (htree build/split on add/remove) stays the separate, risky, all-or-nothing piece and can be deferred — the read fallback keeps correctness while FrankenFS-modified htree dirs degrade gracefully to linear. RECOMMENDATION: implement read-with-fallback next (low risk); defer write-maintenance.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: STEP 1 DONE (commit ca8b1937): extracted the htree/DX navigation into a reusable pub htree_find_entry (ffs-ondisk), closure-based (reads logical dir blocks via FnMut; effective-hash-version via closure), returning HtreeFindResult { Found / NotFoundInIndex / IndexInvalid } so each caller picks its not-found policy. Ext4ImageReader::htree_lookup now delegates to it, behavior-preserved (ffs-ondisk 592 lib tests pass incl htree_lookup_stops_before_noncollision_successor_leaf which pins the trust-the-index semantics). Re-exported htree_find_entry + HtreeFindResult from ffs_ondisk. clippy -D warnings clean; ffs-ext4/ffs-harness build. NEXT (STEP 2, runtime wiring): in lookup_name_with_scope, if dir_inode.has_htree_index(), call ffs_ondisk::htree_find_entry with block_size + sb.hash_seed + sb.has_large_dir() + a closure |lb| self.resolve_extent(cx,scope,dir_inode,lb) -> Some((phys,false)) -> read_block_with_scope(phys).to_vec() (map unwritten/None/err to None) + |v| sb.effective_dirhash_version(v); on Found -> return it; on NotFoundInIndex OR IndexInvalid -> fall through to the existing linear scan (the runtime index may be stale: FrankenFS ext4_add_dir_entry appends linearly without maintaining the htree, so unlike the static reader the runtime MUST linear-fall-back on not-found). STEP 3 (test/bench): ffs-harness integration test that builds an htree fixture (reuse create_dir_index_reference_image) then opens via OpenFs::open_with_options and asserts runtime lookup_name == every entry (isomorphism) + a same-binary A/B htree vs linear for the win. Risk stays LOW (read-only + fallback: a navigation bug only loses the speedup, never correctness).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: READ-HALF LANDED (commit 47edae34). Runtime lookup_name_with_scope now uses the htree/DX index via the shared ffs_ondisk::htree_find_entry (scope-based reads), with a linear fallback on NotFoundInIndex/IndexInvalid/casefold/error — correctness-safe by construction (htree-found = real leaf entry, unique names => no false positives; any staleness/failure => authoritative linear scan). Verified: ext4_runtime_htree_lookup_matches_linear_scan_reference (uses the committed conformance/golden/ext4_dir_index_reference.ext4, or generates the htree image in-test) asserts the index is actually exercised (htree_lookup_name_with_scope locates each present entry directly) AND equals the linear reference; A/B (committed golden, 256-entry dir): linear ~17.6us vs htree ~10.5us = 1.67x (gap widens with dir size; cf. the earlier scaling profiler showing lookup 39->246us for 200->3200 entries linearly). ffs-core 891 tests pass; clippy -D warnings clean. REMAINING (write-half, deferred): FrankenFS ext4_add_dir_entry still appends linearly without building/splitting the htree, so (a) directory POPULATION is still O(n^2) and (b) FrankenFS-created large dirs never materialize a DX index (so they read via the linear path). The read fallback keeps modified htree dirs correct meanwhile. Write-side htree maintenance (build dx_root on overflow, leaf splits, index updates on add/remove) is the separate, risky, all-or-nothing piece — recommend a dedicated effort + a population A/B.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: PROFILE-BACKED (criterion bench landed, 35559550): ffs-harness ext4_runtime_htree_lookup_ab — old_linear_scan vs htree_with_linear_fallback on a real dir_index directory (committed golden ext4_dir_index_reference.ext4, or generated). old_linear_scan 30.08us vs htree_with_linear_fallback 13.81us = 2.18x, CIs cleanly non-overlapping, with an isomorphism assert (both paths agree on the target). Reproducible same-binary A/B confirming the read-half win (the #[ignore]d in-test profiler showed the same ~1.7-2.2x direction); the O(n)->O(log n) gap widens with directory size. Read-half is now landed + profile-backed. Remaining: write-half (htree maintenance for O(n^2)->O(n log n) population), deferred.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: WRITE-HALF STEP 1 (foundational, safe, committed): added ffs_ondisk::write_dx_root + dx_root_entry_limit — the exact inverse of parse_dx_root, the on-disk DX-root serializer the htree build/split path needs. Pinned byte-for-byte against the kernel layout (write_dx_root_round_trips_with_parse reproduces the same bytes the parse_dx_root_kernel_offsets_match_ext4_h offset test hand-builds, then parse round-trips entries/version/levels exactly) + dx_root_entry_limit matches the (block_size-0x20)/8 slot math with the metadata_csum dx_tail reservation. PURE function, no write-path wiring yet -> ZERO corruption risk; foundation for the risky pieces. REMAINING write-half steps: (2) leaf-split (rehash + redistribute a full leaf block into two, choosing the split hash; emit the new dx entry); (3) linear->htree conversion (when a linear dir grows past 1 block, move entries into a leaf, build dx_root in block 0, set EXT4_INDEX_FL); (4) wire (2)+(3) into ext4_add_dir_entry with metadata_csum dx_tail stamping; (5) PROOF: e2fsck-clean a FrankenFS-built large dir + isomorphism (read-back finds all entries; matches a kernel-built dir of the same set). Target: dir population O(n^2)->O(n log n), lookup O(n)->O(log n) on FrankenFS-created dirs (read-half already gives O(log n) on kernel-built htree dirs). Immune to the bd-416sl SIMD-codegen blocker (pure complexity-class win).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: WRITE-HALF STEP 2 (committed): added ffs_ondisk::choose_htree_leaf_split — the leaf-split decision for directory htree growth. Given a full leaf as (name_hash, on_disk_rec_len) in hash order, returns (split_index, split_hash) balancing the byte split ~50/50 while ONLY splitting on a clean hash boundary (entries[i].hash != entries[i-1].hash), so no equal-hash run is straddled across two leaves (dx_find_leaf_idx routes hash<=target, so a straddled run would be missed in the left leaf). Returns None when no clean boundary exists (single distinct hash) — caller falls back (collision-continuation deferred; linear leaf stays correct). PURE fn, property-tested (partition invariants: lower<split_hash<=upper, clean boundary, no entry lost; equal-hash run never split inside; byte-balance tie-break). No write-path wiring -> zero corruption risk. STEPS DONE: (1) write_dx_root serializer, (2) choose_htree_leaf_split. REMAINING: (3) pack sorted entries into leaf block bytes (rec_len = round_up(8+name_len,4), dx_tail csum on metadata_csum) + linear->htree conversion orchestration; (4) wire into ext4_add_dir_entry (set EXT4_INDEX_FL on overflow); (5) e2fsck-clean + isomorphism proof vs a kernel-built dir.

comments.author: ubuntu

title: correctness(btrfs): image becomes UNMOUNTABLE after ~32k creates through a mount — FS_TREE ROOT_ITEM missing on next open
description:
A btrfs image becomes UNMOUNTABLE after creating 32,768 files through a FrankenFS mount and
unmounting cleanly. The next open fails outright:

  error: failed to open filesystem image: .../btrfs.img:
         not found: btrfs ROOT_ITEM for default_root `default` (objectid 5)

The FS_TREE ROOT_ITEM is gone, so nothing on the filesystem is reachable. Every file created in
that session is lost, and so is anything that was on the image before it.

SEVERITY: same class as bd-cjqhh and bd-72tn8 — a write workload that reports success and then
loses the filesystem. Worse in one respect: those two lost data within a live filesystem, this
loses the ability to mount at all.

REPRODUCTION (found while doing perf work on bd-3zx2x, not while looking for this):
  1. fallocate -l 8G img && mkfs.btrfs -f -q -r <seed-with-one-empty-dir> img
  2. ffs-cli mount --rw img /tmp/mnt
  3. create 32,768 empty files in /tmp/mnt/large-directory, one open()+close() each
  4. fusermount3 -u /tmp/mnt        (clean unmount, no error reported)
  5. ffs-cli mount --rw img /tmp/mnt2   -> fails with the error above
Script: scratchpad/zx2x_fair.sh (arg 2 = entry count), binary = release-perf ffs-cli at
HEAD 7fa34f79 plus the bd-3zx2x readdir-bench commits.

SCALE-DEPENDENT, which is the useful part of the report:
  8,000 entries  -> seeds, unmounts, REMOUNTS FINE, sweep completes (measured 298 ms)
  32,768 entries -> seeds (all 32,768 confirmed present before unmount), unmounts clean,
                    then the image will not open
So it is not a general "creates are broken" defect; something crosses a threshold between 8k and
32k creates in one mount session. The seed count was verified in-mount before unmounting, so the
files WERE created and visible — the loss happens at or after commit/unmount.

The ext4 arm of the same script at the same entry count is unaffected: it seeds, unmounts, remounts
and sweeps (1,127 ms). So this is btrfs-specific.

FIRST THINGS TO CHECK, cheapest first:
  1. Does the durable commit succeed at 32,768 entries, or does it fail and get swallowed on the
     destroy path? bd-cjqhh was exactly that shape — flush_on_destroy failing while unmount looked
     clean — and its fix (839eb708) was leaf splitting in the durable commit. This may be the same
     ceiling reached via directory items rather than file data.
  2. Bisect the entry count between 8,000 and 32,768 to find the threshold, then check whether it
     lands near a node/leaf boundary for the fs tree or the root tree.
  3. Check whether the ROOT_ITEM is merely unreachable (tree written but root_tree not repointed)
     or actually absent — `btrfs check` and a raw dump of the root tree will separate those, and
     they imply different fixes.
  4. Confirm on a clean HEAD build, since the binary used here carries my bd-3zx2x CLI additions
     (readdir-bench only — it does not touch the write path, but rule it out).

NOT INVESTIGATED HERE: I found this at the end of a perf turn and am filing rather than diagnosing,
so the report stays what was actually observed. No fix attempted, no mechanism claimed.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RESOLUTION

Check 1 from the report was the right one, and it was the same SHAPE as bd-cjqhh but a
different node kind.

ROOT CAUSE (measured, not inferred): the in-memory COW b-tree split INTERNAL nodes on the
LEAF slot count. A leaf slot is `BTRFS_ITEM_SIZE` = 25 bytes, a key-pointer is
`BTRFS_KEY_PTR_SIZE` = 33, so a 16 KiB node fits 651 items but only 493 children. The fs
tree was allowed to build internal nodes with up to 652 children, and writeback could not
serialize them.

The reproduction, driven through the public API (mkfs image -> OpenFs -> N creates ->
`FsOps::flush_on_destroy` -> reopen), failed at the unmount commit with the exact
arithmetic:

    node overflow: tree owner 5 level 1 has 603 items needing 20000 bytes
    in a 16384-byte node (largest item 33 bytes)

That failure lands in the MIDDLE of `btrfs_full_transaction_commit`, after fs-tree nodes are
already on the device, so the superblock is never updated and still addresses blocks the
partial writeback overwrote — which answers check 3: the ROOT_ITEM is not absent, `sb.root`
resolves to a structurally valid btrfs node of this filesystem that simply contains no
`(objectid=5, ROOT_ITEM)`. That second half is a separate, still-live defect: filed as
bd-mqb9t (commit atomicity / pinned extents), P0.

THE FIX (crates/ffs-btrfs/src/lib.rs)
1. `InMemoryCowBtrfsTree` gains `max_children`, the internal-node key-pointer capacity.
   `with_leaf_byte_budget` -> `with_node_byte_budget` now derives it as
   `budget / BTRFS_KEY_PTR_SIZE` (floor 3) alongside the existing leaf byte budget, so one
   node-size fact bounds both node kinds. Default is `max_items + 1`, which is exactly the
   old bound, so count-only trees are byte-identical.
2. Internal split bounds on `children.len() <= max_children` instead of
   `keys.len() <= max_items`.
3. Underflow is per node kind: `node_min_keys` returns `min_items` for leaves and
   `min_internal_keys()` = `(max_children - 1) / 2` for internal nodes. Without the kind
   split, a freshly split internal node looks underfull the moment it is created. Equals
   `min_items` exactly for count-only trees.
4. `merged_leaf_fits` -> `merged_node_fits` also gates INTERNAL merges on `max_children` —
   the delete-side twin of the leaf merge overflow fixed in bd-cjqhh.
5. Fixed a real latent bug this uncovered: the merge-RIGHT branch of `rebalance_child` never
   refreshed `keys[child_idx - 1]`. The merged node inherits the minimum of the child that
   was just deleted from, so that separator can be stale. It stayed latent because
   merge-right with `child_idx > 0` is only reachable when merge-left is DECLINED, which
   only a byte-budgeted tree does (bd-cjqhh opened that path for leaves; this bead opened it
   for internal nodes, where it surfaced as `BrokenInvariant("internal separator mismatch")`
   on a mass delete). Proven specific to the decline path by a control test on an unbudgeted
   tree, which passes both before and after.
6. `validate_node` now also rejects an over-wide internal node, so the failure is caught
   while the transaction is still purely in memory.

`with_leaf_byte_budget` -> `with_node_byte_budget` renamed at all 11 call sites
(6 in crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs, 5 in ffs-btrfs tests).

EVIDENCE
- crates/ffs-core/tests/btrfs_large_dir_mount_cycle.rs (new): the bead's workload end to end.
  `btrfs_32k_create_batch_remounts_bd_giw9n` FAILED before the fix with the node-overflow
  above and PASSES after; `btrfs_8k_create_batch_remounts_bd_giw9n` is the known-good control
  from the report and passes throughout. Both assert every entry is visible in-mount before
  the unmount AND resolvable after the remount, so a failure cannot be blamed on the create
  path. A parameterized `--ignored` probe (`FFS_GIW9N_COUNT` / `FFS_GIW9N_SIZE_MB`) is left
  in place for bisecting the threshold, and a failed reopen preserves the corrupt image.
- crates/ffs-btrfs/src/lib.rs (new unit tests):
  `internal_nodes_split_on_key_pointer_capacity_bd_giw9n` (asserts no node exceeds capacity,
  that the tree really split past one internal node, that every node serializes, and that no
  item was lost); `delete_does_not_merge_internal_nodes_past_capacity_bd_giw9n` (FAILED
  before the separator fix with "internal separator mismatch");
  `mass_delete_keeps_separators_consistent_in_a_deep_tree_bd_giw9n` (the unbudgeted control
  that establishes the separator bug is confined to the merge-decline path).
- `cargo test -p ffs-btrfs --lib`: 384 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.
- `cargo test -p ffs-core --lib`: 1195 passed, 1 failed, 21 ignored. The single failure is
  `fast_commit_del_range_apply_punches_and_frees_passes_e2fsck`, an ext4 test, PROVEN
  pre-existing by rerunning it in a clean detached worktree at HEAD 879a42f5 (same two
  counter values, 0 passed / 1 failed). Filed as bd-age6i.
- `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p ffs-btrfs --all-targets` reports nothing in the
  changed files. (`-D warnings` cannot run workspace-wide: ffs-types has two pre-existing
  `chunks_exact` clippy errors and is unmodified in the working tree.)

NOT DONE HERE
- The exact create-count threshold between 8k and 32k was not bisected. It became moot once
  the mechanism was arithmetic rather than empirical: the overflow is reached whenever one
  internal node accumulates more than `(nodesize - 101) / 33` children. The probe test is
  left parameterized in case a future regression needs the empirical number.
- The image was never inspected with `btrfs check` / a raw root-tree dump (check 3). The
  in-process reproduction gave the mechanism directly, so it was not needed.

FOLLOW-UPS FILED
- bd-mqb9t (P0): commit atomicity — the commit frees the live trees' extent items into its
  own allocator, so any mid-commit failure can overwrite the image the superblock still
  points at. This is what converted the overflow above into an unmountable image.
- bd-age6i (P1): the pre-existing ext4 fast-commit e2fsck failure.

Verified: ffs-btrfs --lib 384/0; 32k create+unmount+remount round-trips (failed pre-fix with the node-overflow quoted in the description).

title: ffs-ondisk: EXT4_BG_INODE_UNINIT/BG_BLOCK_UNINIT/BG_INODE_ZEROED group desc flags lack public constants + kernel-conformance pin
description:
Finding (via /testing-conformance-harnesses skill, NEW target): Ext4GroupDesc.flags is a u16 bit-field but ffs-ondisk does NOT define public constants for the 3 kernel-defined bits (per fs/ext4/ext4.h):

  EXT4_BG_INODE_UNINIT = 0x0001  (inode table never initialized)
  EXT4_BG_BLOCK_UNINIT = 0x0002  (block bitmap never initialized)
  EXT4_BG_INODE_ZEROED = 0x0004  (inode table has been zeroed)

ffs-cli/src/main.rs:2774-2776 redefines them privately as fn-local consts and tests them against a 'known' mask, but:
  1. There is NO kernel-conformance test pinning the values
  2. The constants are duplicated across the codebase; any future user has to re-derive them
  3. There is no structural invariant test (power-of-2, no shared bits)

A regression that swapped EXT4_BG_INODE_UNINIT (0x0001) and EXT4_BG_BLOCK_UNINIT (0x0002) would silently mis-classify every group descriptor and either skip valid inode tables or read uninitialized memory.

Acceptance:
  1. Add 3 pub const u16 in crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs near the existing EXT4_VALID_FS / EXT4_ERROR_FS / EXT4_ORPHAN_FS state flags
  2. Re-export from crates/ffs-ondisk/src/lib.rs
  3. Add ext4_block_group_flag_constants_match_kernel_header conformance test pinning all 3 values + structural invariants (power-of-2, pairwise no-shared-bits)
  4. Update crates/ffs-cli/src/main.rs to use the new public constants instead of fn-local privates

Pairs with bd-jbilz (state flags + magic), bd-bevt2 (40 feature flags), bd-tyeic (27 inode flags).
close_reason: done

title: ffs-mvcc: commit_internal + rollback_in_memory_commit have implicit atomic-or-rollback contract
description:
Finding (via /modes-of-reasoning-project-analysis skill, second
visit, different target): `PersistentMvccStore::commit_internal`
(crates/ffs-mvcc/src/persist.rs:426) and the partner helper
`rollback_in_memory_commit` (l. 671) implement a critical
**atomic-or-rollback** contract:

  1. The in-memory MvccStore commits FIRST (advancing next_commit
     and inserting the new BlockVersion onto every block's chain).
  2. The WAL append happens SECOND.
  3. If the WAL append fails, `rollback_in_memory_commit` REVERSES
     the in-memory commit — pops the just-inserted version, removes
     the empty entry if no others remain, drops the SSI log entry,
     and rolls back next_commit so the slot can be reused.

If this rollback is incomplete, the on-disk state diverges from
in-memory state in an unrecoverable way: a reader at the latest
snapshot would see data that never reached the WAL. Existing tests
(`wal_append_failure_rolls_back_commit_state`,
`wal_append_failure_rolls_back_ssi_log_and_commit_seq`,
`wal_sync_failure_multi_block_rollback`) verify the behaviour, but
the **reasoning mode itself is not documented on either function**.

A future contributor adding a new failure path between the
in-memory commit and the WAL append (e.g., a sync barrier check, a
pre-flight quota check, anything that can return an error after
line 449) would NOT see the contract spelled out and might:
  * forget to call rollback_in_memory_commit
  * forget to roll back next_commit on the new failure path
  * forget to handle SSI log + cow_blocks in the rollback set

This is the same shape as bd-3ydm6 (fail-closed reasoning mode for
is_reserved_inode) and bd-7zd94/bd-bky2f/bd-pfv55 (lock-ordering
invariants): a critical reasoning mode applied without naming.

Acceptance: doc blocks on both `commit_internal` and
`rollback_in_memory_commit` naming the **atomic-or-rollback**
reasoning mode, listing the five state pieces the rollback must
cover (write_blocks chain head + cow_blocks chain head + SSI log
entry + next_commit + next_txn invariant), explicitly noting that
any new failure path after the in-memory commit MUST call
`rollback_in_memory_commit` before returning Err. NO behavioural
change.
notes: Shipped: doc blocks on PersistentMvccStore::commit_internal and rollback_in_memory_commit in crates/ffs-mvcc/src/persist.rs naming the atomic-or-rollback reasoning mode and listing the FIVE state pieces the rollback covers (write_blocks chain head, cow_blocks chain head, SSI log entry, next_commit advance, next_txn reservation). Explicitly notes that any new failure path inserted after the in-memory commit MUST call rollback_in_memory_commit before returning Err, otherwise the store wedges with on-disk-vs-in-memory divergence. Pure documentation — no behavioural change. Existing rollback tests (wal_append_failure_rolls_back_commit_state / wal_append_failure_rolls_back_ssi_log_and_commit_seq) still pass via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-mvcc --lib wal_append_failure_rolls_back. Pairs with bd-3ydm6 (fail-closed reasoning mode for is_reserved_inode) and bd-7zd94/bd-bky2f/bd-pfv55 (lock-ordering invariants).

title: add ffs-core fuzz target for ext4 crash-state and journal-replay mount boundary
description:
Apply /testing-fuzzing to the ext4 crash-state and journal-replay mount boundary in `ffs-core`.

## Target surface
- `OpenFs::from_device(...)` / `open_with_options(...)`
- `detect_and_recover_crash()` at `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:2755`
- ext4 journal replay integration around mount open (`maybe_replay_ext4_journal`, `ext4_journal_replay`, `crash_recovery`)
- external-journal / replay-mode combinations that decide whether mount proceeds, degrades, or errors

## Why this matters
The repo already fuzzes lower-level JBD2 replay, but not the `ffs-core` integration boundary where superblock state bits, replay policy, journal outcome, and recovery-report exposure interact. This is exactly where mount-time recovery regressions hide.

## Scope
- Add a fuzz target that mutates minimally-valid ext4 images plus replay-mode / external-journal knobs and opens through `ffs-core`.
- Seed from current clean/dirty/error/orphan state fixtures and journal replay tests.
- Assert:
  - no panic / no hang
  - `crash_recovery()` and `ext4_journal_replay()` remain deterministic for the same input
  - recovery reports never claim replay counts larger than available journal metadata
  - skip-validation mode never triggers unintended mount-time recovery work
  - malformed external-journal combinations fail gracefully with stable errno/error class

## Acceptance
- New fuzz target registered in `fuzz/Cargo.toml`
- Seed corpus added from existing ext4 recovery fixtures
- Crashers minimized and promoted to regression coverage

title: Add indirect block pointer write support for e2compr beyond direct range
description:
BACKGROUND: The e2compr compressed write path (write_ext4_compressed_cluster, write_ext4_uncompressed_cluster) uses set_indirect_block_ptr to write block pointers in the inode's i_block array. This function currently rejects logical_block >= 12 because entries 12-14 are the single/double/triple indirect pointers, and overwriting them with data block pointers would corrupt the indirect addressing table.

CURRENT LIMITATION: With the smallest cluster size (4 blocks, shift=2) and 4K block size, only clusters at logical blocks 0-3, 4-7, and 8-11 can be written — files up to 48KB. Cluster shift 3 (8 blocks) limits to 32KB. Larger files cannot be compressed at all.

THE READ PATH ALREADY WORKS: resolve_indirect_block handles single/double/triple indirect lookups for reading. The write side needs the inverse operation.

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN:
1. Add write_indirect_block_ptr(cx, scope, inode, alloc, logical_block, phys) that mirrors resolve_indirect_block but writes:
   - For logical_block < 12: direct write to inode.extent_bytes (existing code).
   - For 12 <= logical_block < 12 + ptrs_per_block: allocate or read the single-indirect block (i_block[12]), write the pointer at the correct offset within it.
   - For double-indirect range: allocate/read i_block[13] -> intermediate block -> write pointer.
   - For triple-indirect range: three-level allocation/read.
2. Intermediate blocks must be allocated on first use (when i_block[12/13/14] is 0).
3. Allocated intermediate blocks must be freed when the last pointer in them becomes 0 (during cluster freeing).
4. Update set_indirect_block_ptr callers to use the new function.
5. Add tests for files that span into the indirect range.

COMPLEXITY: Medium-high. The read path is ~120 lines; the write path will be ~200 lines due to allocation of intermediate blocks. Must correctly handle:
- First write to a new indirect level (allocate the intermediate block).
- Overwrite of existing pointers (read-modify-write the intermediate block).
- Freeing of intermediate blocks when all their pointers become 0.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Compressed write works for files up to at least 1MB (requires single-indirect support).
- Compressed read/write roundtrip test for a file spanning into indirect block range.
- set_indirect_block_ptr error at lb >= 12 is removed.
- No block leaks: freed clusters also free their intermediate block pointers if they become empty.
close_reason: All subtasks complete: single-indirect (bd-z15u, commit 18cd3d7) and double/triple indirect (bd-pv9l, commit 06a4288). e2compr can now compress files of any size.

title: perf(btrfs/send): memoize parent-chain path/depth in generate_send_stream (O(N*D)->O(N))
description: Phase-B (cc W155 Explore). generate_send_stream (ffs-btrfs/src/lib.rs:7717) builds command paths by walking the inode_parents chain per inode: build_path closure (7768) is called once per emitted inode (7865) and per hardlink parent (8010), each O(D); dir_depth closure (7827) is called once per directory inode in the sort key (7842), each O(D). Total O(N*D). LEVER: memoize both into a HashMap<u64,Vec<u8>> path cache + HashMap<u64,usize> depth cache so each inode's path = cached(parent) + '/' + name (computed once) -> O(N) amortized. PROOF: generate_send_stream returns Vec<u8>; golden sha256 of the stream must be byte-identical before/after (strong parity). Directly benchable: call with synthetic deep-tree  (model on tests at 19725+) + trivial read_extent closure; bench whole-stream gen. CAVEATS: (1) win only materializes on DEEP dir trees (D large); realistic D is small -> may be sub-2.0 on flat trees, bench a 10-12 level hierarchy. (2) memoization is SUBTLE: current build_path is ITERATIVE with break conditions (parent==self or parent==ROOT) and stops when a node is absent from inode_parents; a naive recursive cache can diverge (esp. self-loop -> current infinite-loops, recursion stack-overflows). Must match join semantics: result = base.is_empty()? name : base+'/'+name. Verify isomorphism via golden sha256 across flat/deep/renamed-child/hardlink fixtures. REJECTED SIBLINGS (don't re-hunt): csum per-sector lookup_data_block_csum batching (ffs-btrfs:399) is sub-2.0 — reverse-scan is O(1) in the common pure-csum list and crc32c verification (~0.4us/4KB sector) dominates the ~tens-of-ns partition_point. ext4_rename2_exchange ancestry double-walk (ffs-core:26429) is 2.0-2.5x but RENAME_EXCHANGE is a rare path.
close_reason: Kept btrfs send-stream path/depth memoization: vmi1227854 Criterion btrfs_send_stream_deep_paths/generate_send_stream mean 30.754 ms -> 24.530 ms (1.25x, conservative 1.19x). Raw send-stream SHA-256 goldens preserved for flat/deep/renamed-parent/hardlink/missing-parent/root-self/non-root-self fixtures; generate_send_stream tests, cargo check, clippy, fmt passed.

title: EPIC: V1.1 Post-Parity Hardening and Operationalization
description:
# EPIC: V1.1 Post-Parity Hardening and Operationalization

## Context
Tracked V1 parity is complete (75/75), but FrankenFS is explicitly still early-stage and experimental for mount/write operations. The project now needs a rigorous post-parity program focused on production-grade correctness confidence, failure containment, observability, and predictable performance under stress.

This epic converts that post-parity intent into an executable dependency graph that is:
- granular enough for independent agent execution,
- explicit about acceptance gates,
- self-contained (no need to reopen planning docs during execution).

## Why this exists
Parity completion proves breadth of implemented behavior, not necessarily depth of operational hardening. Remaining risk lives in:
- durability under crash/fault scenarios,
- clarity of experimental behavior (especially btrfs RW path),
- incomplete operational wiring (CLI mount path for managed backpressure/per-core hooks),
- benchmark/regression signal fidelity,
- unresolved spec open questions that can cause architecture drift if left ambiguous.

## Scope
This epic is fulfilled when all child epics below are complete:
1. Durable MVCC version-store implementation and replay hardening.
2. CLI mount wiring for managed backpressure/per-core scheduling.
3. btrfs experimental RW hardening and explicit compatibility contracts.
4. Fuzzing and adversarial test-depth expansion.
5. Benchmark fidelity and regression-guard upgrades.
6. Closure of formal open questions (with accepted decisions integrated into docs/tests/code).

## Non-goals
- Reopening excluded V1 scope items (multi-device btrfs, fscrypt, inline_data, etc.) unless explicitly approved in a separate scope-change epic.
- Marketing/docs polish without technical acceptance deltas.

## Definition of Done
- Child epics closed with evidence-backed acceptance criteria.
- FEATURE_PARITY.md, spec docs, and harness signals remain internally consistent.
- New work items include explicit test and observability requirements, not implementation-only checklists.
close_reason: V1.1 Post-Parity Hardening and Operationalization COMPLETE. All 9 child epics closed (1: MVCC replay, 2: mount modes, 3: btrfs RW, 4: fuzzing, 5: benchmarks, 6: OQ decisions, 7: operator tooling, 8: program gate, 9: verification toolchain). 296 beads total, all closed. 3,594+ workspace tests pass. Program gate bd-h6nz.8: 13/13 PASS. RELEASE RECOMMENDATION: PROCEED.

title: EPIC: Durable MVCC Version Store and Crash Replay
description:
# EPIC: Durable MVCC Version Store and Crash Replay

## Problem Statement
MVCC currently provides strong in-memory isolation and conflict semantics, but the long-term architecture calls for a durable version-store path with restart replay guarantees. This is explicitly documented as planned in the spec and is a key reliability boundary between "experimental" and "operationally trustworthy" write paths.

## Why this matters
Without a durable MVCC version-store:
- commit visibility across process restart is less explicit,
- crash-time reconstruction relies on narrower recovery channels,
- validation of full write-path durability semantics remains incomplete.

## Scope
Implement and harden a persistent MVCC version-store workflow including:
1. append protocol and on-disk record format,
2. replay engine and corruption handling,
3. mount/open integration + observability,
4. deterministic crash matrix coverage.

## Required Evidence
- deterministic replay tests proving latest committed state reconstruction,
- corrupted/truncated log handling tests with explicit outcomes,
- metrics and CLI visibility for replay/apply/skip decisions.

## Done Criteria
- Child tasks completed with green gates and replay evidence.
- Spec/architecture docs updated from "planned" to implemented behavior.
- No silent recovery ambiguity (each replay path emits a reasoned outcome).
close_reason: All child beads and verification gate closed. Program gate bd-h6nz.8 passed.

Treat this epic as a correctness program, not a feature program. Every step should produce replay-oracle evidence. If a design choice cannot be tested deterministically under crash schedules, it is not ready to ship.

title: Define durable MVCC version-store record format and invariants
description:
## Objective
Turn the planned durable MVCC record model into an implementable contract with no ambiguity around ordering, checksums, atomicity boundaries, and forward compatibility.

## Background
Spec section 5.9 defines high-level goals. This task crystallizes the concrete wire/storage format and invariant ledger required before implementation.

## Deliverables
1. Record schema for version-store entries (header + payload + integrity fields).
2. Explicit ordering model (commit_seq monotonicity, tie-breaking, duplicate handling).
3. Crash consistency points (what is guaranteed after power loss at each append stage).
4. Corruption semantics (truncate vs reject vs quarantine behavior).
5. Compatibility/versioning strategy for future schema evolution.

## Required Artifacts
- Spec updates in COMPREHENSIVE_SPEC_FOR_FRANKENFS_V1.md + PROPOSED_ARCHITECTURE.md.
- Invariant checklist suitable for test oracles.
- Example binary layout snippets and decode walkthrough.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No undecided fields in the record layout.
- Replay behavior is fully deterministic for all malformed/torn cases.
- At least 5 explicit invariants are documented and test-mappable.
## Mandatory Test & Logging Contract
1. Unit Tests (required)
- Add or extend crate-local tests for happy path, boundary/edge cases, and explicit error paths.
- Include at least one invariant-focused negative test proving failure handling is intentional.

2. Deterministic E2E Scripts (required)
- Add or extend deterministic E2E coverage (prefer `scripts/e2e/` or existing harness E2E path) with explicit setup/teardown.
- Every scenario must emit machine-parseable pass/fail markers plus stable `scenario_id` values.

3. Structured Logging (required)
- Emit structured logs at key state transitions and failure boundaries.
- Critical events must include `operation_id`, `scenario_id`, and outcome/error classification fields.
- Add test assertions (unit/integration/E2E) validating critical log markers for both success and failure paths.

4. Validation Evidence (required)
- Closure must include artifact paths and concise evidence summary for tests + logs.
- CPU-intensive gates must be run via `rch exec -- ...` when invoking cargo builds/checks/tests/benches.

title: Integrate durable MVCC store into OpenFs lifecycle and mount options
description:
## Objective
Wire durable MVCC persistence and replay into `OpenFs::open` / mount lifecycle with explicit mode controls and safe defaults.

## Scope
1. Open-time replay invocation and replay summary capture.
2. Mode flags for strict vs tolerant replay handling.
3. Read-only fallback behavior when replay policy requires it.
4. Integration with existing journal/recovery reporting surfaces.

## Constraints
- No hidden behavior changes for default read-only mount semantics.
- Replay failure modes must map to actionable CLI errors.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Mount/open path clearly reports replay decisions.
- Recovery + replay ordering is deterministic and documented.
- Integration tests cover clean start, crash restart, and replay-failure paths.
## Mandatory Test & Logging Contract
1. Unit Tests (required)

title: EPIC: CLI Mount Path Wiring for Managed Backpressure and Per-Core Scheduling
description:
# EPIC: CLI Mount Path Wiring for Managed Backpressure and Per-Core Scheduling

## Problem Statement
README explicitly documents that default `ffs-cli mount` does not wire optional backpressure/per-core scheduling hooks. This leaves high-value runtime controls available in code but not reliably exposed in the primary operator entrypoint.

## Why this matters
- Operators may believe pressure controls are active when they are not.
- Performance/latency investigations become noisy due to hidden runtime-mode differences.
- Hardening efforts in `ffs-fuse` and `ffs-core` are underutilized operationally.

## Scope
1. Expose runtime-mode controls in CLI in a clear and safe way.
2. Wire mount codepaths to managed/per-core execution when selected.
3. Ensure default mode remains conservative and predictable.
4. Add explicit runtime telemetry and tests for mode behavior.

## Done Criteria
- CLI supports explicit mode selection with documented defaults.
- Mount runtime reports active mode in logs/metrics.
- Integration tests verify behavior for standard vs managed modes.

title: EPIC: btrfs Experimental RW Hardening and Compatibility Contracts
description:
# EPIC: btrfs Experimental RW Hardening and Compatibility Contracts

## Problem Statement
btrfs mount/write support exists in experimental form with intentionally limited feature coverage. The remaining risk is not just missing features, but ambiguity around what is guaranteed, what is best-effort, and how failures are surfaced.

## Why this matters
- Experimental modes require tighter guardrails, not looser ones.
- Clear unsupported-op semantics prevent silent corruption and operator confusion.
- Recovery/scrub pathways must be validated under write churn, not only static metadata scenarios.

## Scope
1. Formalize current supported operation matrix and strict unsupported behavior.
2. Harden runtime checks so unsupported paths fail deterministically and safely.
3. Expand crash/recovery/scrub tests for btrfs write scenarios.
4. Keep alignment between docs, harness, and runtime behavior.

## Done Criteria
- Capability matrix and runtime behavior match exactly.
- Unsupported cases return stable errno + explicit logs.
- btrfs experimental write path has adversarial test evidence, not just happy-path coverage.

# EPIC: Benchmark Fidelity and Regression Guard Strengthening

## Problem Statement
Benchmark scaffolding and baselines exist, but post-parity evolution needs stronger anti-flake methodology, host-profile awareness, and explicit treatment of degraded/runtime-mode performance envelopes.

## Why this matters
Without disciplined benchmark governance, teams either miss regressions or chase noise. We need actionable signals that survive machine variance and evolving workloads.

## Scope
1. Expand benchmark taxonomy beyond current hot paths.
2. Add robust comparison methodology (effect sizes, noise thresholds, guardrails).
3. Validate performance under pressure/degradation modes.
4. Document operator workflow for interpreting and acting on regressions.

## Done Criteria
- Bench suite covers critical latency/throughput/write-amplification surfaces.
- Regression guard emits high-signal failures with clear next steps.
- Performance gates are reproducible across supported host profiles.
