title: Implement asupersync-based symbol exchange transport
description:
## Purpose

Implement the transport layer for exchanging repair symbols between hosts using asupersync structured concurrency.

## Scope

1. **Protocol framing** — Simple length-prefixed message framing over TCP using `std::net::TcpStream` wrapped in asupersync regions (`asupersync::region()` for cancel-correct lifecycle).

2. **Request types** — `GetSymbols(group_id, generation)`, `PutSymbols(group_id, generation, symbols[])`. Serde-serialized message envelope with version tag for forward compatibility.

3. **Server** — TCP listener using `std::net::TcpListener` with asupersync-managed accept loop. Each connection handled in its own asupersync region for structured cancellation.

4. **Client** — TCP client (`std::net::TcpStream`) for requesting symbols from remote hosts. Connection managed within asupersync region for timeout/cancellation.

5. **Timeout and retry** — Configurable connection timeout (default 5s) and retry policy (exponential backoff, max 3 retries). Timeouts enforced via asupersync deadline propagation through `Cx`.

## Transport implementation note
asupersync does not provide its own TCP primitives. Use `std::net::TcpStream`/`TcpListener` with blocking I/O inside asupersync regions. The region boundary provides the cancellation/timeout contract. If asupersync gains native async TCP before implementation, prefer that.

## Acceptance criteria
- Symbol exchange working over TCP with length-prefixed framing
- Uses asupersync regions exclusively for lifecycle management (no tokio)
- Timeout and retry handling via Cx deadline propagation
- Unit tests for framing, protocol serialization, and retry logic
- E2E script: two processes exchanging symbols over loopback

title: Implement end-to-end distributed repair pipeline
description:

End-to-end multi-host repair: detect corruption → acquire ownership → retrieve remote symbols → decode → verify → apply.

2. **Ownership check** — Check if local host owns the group. If not, acquire or request from owner.
3. **Remote retrieval** — If symbols not available locally, request from remote host via exchange protocol.
4. **Decode and verify** — Use retrieved symbols to reconstruct corrupted blocks. Verify integrity.
5. **Apply** — Write repaired blocks to local storage. Update repair generation.

## Acceptance criteria

2. **Chunk→stripe resolution** — For each chunk, resolve the stripe layout:

title: Implement btrfs snapshot navigation (read-only)
description:
## Purpose

Navigate btrfs snapshots for read-only access. List snapshots, mount specific snapshot, compare two snapshots.

## Scope

1. **Snapshot enumeration** — Identify snapshots (subvolumes with parent UUID set) and their creation time/generation from ROOT_BACKREF items.

2. **Snapshot mounting** — Mount a specific snapshot read-only. Same mechanism as subvolume mounting but keyed by snapshot name or UUID.

3. **Snapshot diff (generation-based)** — Compare two snapshots: enumerate files changed between two generations using btree item comparison. This is a *simplified* diff that compares inode metadata and extent data items by generation number — NOT a full send/receive stream implementation. title: Implement lightweight runtime metrics framework (counters, gauges, histograms)
description:
## Purpose

Lightweight metrics collection framework using atomics. No external deps. Lives in `ffs-harness` crate (alongside existing benchmark/perf infrastructure) with a public API re-exported through `ffs-core` for production use.

## Scope

1. **Metric types** — Counter (monotonic u64), Gauge (i64), Histogram (fixed-bucket latency distribution). All types in `ffs-harness::metrics` module.
2. **Registration** — Static metric registry using `parking_lot::RwLock<HashMap<&'static str, MetricHandle>>`. Thread-safe lazy initialization.
3. **Collection** — AtomicU64/AtomicI64 for zero-contention updates on hot paths. `MetricHandle` is a thin wrapper around atomic ops.
4. **Aggregation** — Per-second snapshots. Rolling window (configurable, default 60s). Snapshot computation is O(metrics_count), not O(events).
5. **Export** — `MetricsSnapshot` struct → JSON serialization via serde. Structured log emission at configurable interval via tracing.
6. **Zero overhead when unused** — Metrics disabled by default, enabled via `--metrics` CLI flag. When disabled, metric recording functions are no-ops (compiled-out via cfg or checked at registration time).
7. **Integration surface** — `ffs-core` re-exports `ffs_harness::metrics::{Counter, Gauge, Histogram, MetricsRegistry}` so that other crates (`ffs-repair`, `ffs-mvcc`, `ffs-block`) can record metrics without depending on ffs-harness directly.

## Acceptance criteria
- Counter, Gauge, Histogram types implemented in ffs-harness::metrics
- Zero-contention atomic updates verified under concurrent load
- Per-second aggregation working with configurable window
- JSON export functional via MetricsSnapshot
- <1% overhead when enabled, 0% when disabled (benchmark proof)
- Unit tests for each metric type (increment, decrement, histogram bucket distribution)
- E2E script: enable metrics, generate load, verify JSON emission in structured logs
close_reason: Completed: Implemented ffs-harness::metrics module with Counter (monotonic u64), Gauge (i64), and Histogram (fixed-bucket) types. Zero-contention atomic updates. Thread-safe MetricsRegistry with parking_lot::RwLock. JSON export via MetricsSnapshot. Enable/disable toggle with zero overhead when disabled. Rolling window snapshots. 14 unit tests pass including concurrent load verification (8 threads x 1000 ops). noop_handle for optional metrics paths.

title: Kernel-conformance pin for BTRFS_ITEM_* leaf-key type constants
description: Found via /porting-to-rust audit. crates/ffs-btrfs/src/lib.rs declares 17 BTRFS_ITEM_* key-type constants (lines 29-45 + 266-268) used by every leaf walk to dispatch to the right parser (parse_inode_item, parse_dir_items, parse_inode_refs, parse_xattr_items, parse_extent_data, parse_root_item, parse_root_ref, etc.). These are kernel discriminants from include/uapi/linux/btrfs_tree.h: INODE_ITEM=1, INODE_REF=12, XATTR_ITEM=24, DIR_ITEM=84, DIR_INDEX=96, EXTENT_DATA=108, ROOT_ITEM=132, ROOT_BACKREF=144, ROOT_REF=156, EXTENT_ITEM=168, METADATA_ITEM=169, BLOCK_GROUP_ITEM=192, FREE_SPACE_INFO=198, FREE_SPACE_EXTENT=199, FREE_SPACE_BITMAP=200, DEV_ITEM=216, CHUNK_ITEM=228. None has a kernel-pin test despite siblings (chunk_type_flags, file_extent_type, compression, tree objectids, BTRFS_FT_*) all being pinned. A regression that swapped any two values would silently route the wrong parser at every leaf walk but pass functional tests using INODE_ITEM only. Fix: add btrfs_leaf_item_type_constants_match_kernel_header pinning all 17 values + uniqueness invariant.
close_reason: completed

title: perf(core/btrfs): parallel decompression of compressed extents in a multi-extent read (parallelization primitive)
description: DEEP SWING (alien primitive: a different parallelization model). btrfs compressed reads (compress=zstd/lzo, common) decompress each compressed extent SERIALLY in the read assembly loop. zstd decompress is ~1GB/s and CPU-bound, so for a multi-MB read spanning K compressed extents the decompression is the bottleneck (not I/O once cached). Decompress the K extents in PARALLEL via the asupersync runtime (spawn one decompress task per extent into a pre-sized output, join), turning the per-read decompression from O(total_bytes/1GBps) serial into ~O(/Ncores). Target ~Ncores (3-6x) on decompression-bound multi-extent compressed reads. Isomorphism: each extent decompresses into its own disjoint [file_offset, file_offset+len) output slice independently; order-independent; same bytes. PROOF OBLIGATIONS: bounded task fan-out (cap at Ncores), no shared mutable state across tasks (disjoint output slices), error propagation (any task error fails the read). CAVEATS: btrfs unmeasurable on this worker (no btrfs format tool) -- measure via a unit harness that decompresses K synthetic zstd extents serial-vs-parallel; the win needs the asupersync within-request task API (verify it exists + is safe-Rust). Sibling idea: parallel csum verify is NOT worth it (crc32c ~10GB/s, sub-2.0 e2e).
close_reason: Shipped 00dea404: parallel-decompress multi-extent btrfs reads via rayon into_par_iter over the pure Self::btrfs_decompress, gathering compressed blobs in extent order (I/O ordering preserved) and consuming results in order. Component A/B 2.72x (760.98us->279.44us, N=16x128KiB zstd). 1104 ffs-core tests pass (322 btrfs). Completed by cc; NavyPelican (cod) idle.

title: Bound ioctl trace writer teardown on blocking trace paths
description:
Discovery from `$deadlock-finder-and-fixer` while source-aware ready work was empty and RCH remained blocked by `bd-oowwx`.

Evidence:
- `crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:1408-1414` spawns the `ffs-ioctl-trace` worker and does the trace-path `OpenOptions::open()` inside that worker.
- `crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:1479-1488` drops the sender and then joins the worker without a timeout.
- `crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:1504-1526` drains the channel if `open()` returns an error, but a blocking open never reaches that drain path.
- Existing closed `bd-adke` moved per-ioctl writes off the FUSE dispatcher and added `flush_sync()` coverage, but I did not find an open row covering teardown liveness for blocking special trace paths.

Problem:
A user or harness can set `MountOptions.ioctl_trace_path` to a blocking special file such as a FIFO with no reader. The worker can park in `OpenOptions::open(path)`, and dropping `FrankenFuse` / `FuseInner` / `IoctlTraceProbe` will then block forever in `worker.join()`. The dispatcher hot path remains non-blocking, but teardown is not bounded and a test using this path would hang instead of failing with a controlled diagnostic.

Scope:
Make ioctl trace startup/teardown fail closed for blocking or unsupported trace targets. Prefer validating that the target is a regular file path or opening with Unix `O_NONBLOCK` where applicable, then disabling trace with a warning if the path would block. Preserve the current non-blocking `record()` behavior and the test-only happens-before `flush_sync()` contract for ordinary files.

Acceptance:
1. `IoctlTraceProbe::new` / worker startup cannot block teardown forever on FIFO or other blocking special-file trace targets.
2. `Drop for IoctlTraceProbe` remains bounded; if a worker cannot be joined promptly, the implementation emits a structured warning and avoids hanging the caller.
3. A focused regression constructs a blocking trace-path fixture (for example a FIFO on Unix) and proves probe creation/drop returns within a named timeout without requiring a reader.
4. Existing ordinary-file trace tests still prove records are appended and `flush_sync()` is a happens-before barrier for concurrent recorders.
5. Validation uses RCH for focused `ffs-fuse` tests/check/clippy/fmt, plus `jq empty .beads/issues.jsonl`, `git diff --check`, `br dep cycles --no-db --no-auto-import --json`, and source-aware hygiene. If RCH still has no admissible workers, keep this blocked on `bd-oowwx` and do not use local cargo as proof.
close_reason: Completed: ioctl trace setup now rejects existing non-regular trace targets before spawning a writer and uses O_NONBLOCK for the final append open, with focused regressions proving special/directory paths disable without a joinable writer while ordinary trace flush coverage still passes. Validated focused RCH ioctl_trace tests, RCH check, RCH clippy, fmt, JSONL, diff, and dependency cycles.

title: [CRITICAL] FS_IOC_GET_ENCRYPTION_POLICY_EX ignores caller out_size for v2 replies
description:
# Review finding

Recent fscrypt `_EX` parity work still leaves a dangerous output-size hole in the FUSE ioctl handler.

## Problem
In `crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:1658-1679`, `FS_IOC_GET_ENCRYPTION_POLICY_EX` only rejects buffers smaller than `header + v1_policy_size`. After that check, it always allocates and returns `header + actual_policy_size` bytes.

That means a caller can advertise an `out_size` large enough for a v1 policy but still too small for a v2 policy, and the handler will return the full v2 payload anyway.

## Evidence
- Handler: `crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:1658-1679`
- Existing negative test only covers `out_size < header + v1_policy_size`: `crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:5165-5180`
- Existing v2 positive test only covers the full-size happy path: `crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:5117-5162`

## Why this is critical
This is an ioctl boundary contract violation. The handler is supposed to respect the caller-advertised output capacity, but the current logic can emit more bytes than requested for v2 policies. Even if the kernel/FUSE layer truncates or rejects later, FrankenFS is still violating the protocol boundary in its userspace reply construction.

## Expected fix direction
- Reject or clamp when `out_size < header + actual_policy_size`
- Add a regression test for a v2 policy with `out_size` between the v1 and v2 minimums
- Confirm expected errno/behavior against the intended fscrypt `_EX` contract
close_reason: Already resolved. Handler in crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:1866-1907 computes required_size=header+policy.len() post-backend-call and returns ERANGE when out_size<required_size (lines 1887-1892). Regression test dispatch_ioctl_get_encryption_policy_ex_v2_rejects_v1_sized_buffer at crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:5434-5472 exercises the exact advertised-v1/return-v2 scenario. All 5 dispatch_ioctl_get_encryption_policy_ex tests pass on workspace via rch.

title: Route e2e_mount away from direct local cargo run
description:
Discovery while source-aware ready work was empty, mock-code/policy scans were clean for code placeholders, and RCH remained blocked by critical_pressure=7.

Current evidence:
- `scripts/e2e/lib.sh:e2e_mount` launches `cargo run -p ffs-cli --release -- mount "$img_path" "$mnt_point" &` directly.
- The same shared E2E library already has RCH-aware capture helpers, and adjacent E2E scripts route cargo-bearing validator lanes through `e2e_rch_capture` / `run_rch_capture` or prebuilt harness paths.
- FUSE mounting must happen on the local host, but building/selecting the `ffs-cli` binary should not silently invoke a local release cargo build in remote-only validation mode.
- No existing open bead matched `e2e_mount`, `cargo run -p ffs-cli --release -- mount`, or a prebuilt FUSE mount helper.

Problem: any E2E script that calls `e2e_mount` can trigger a heavy local `cargo run --release` before the mount probe, bypassing the repo practice that cargo-based validation/build work uses RCH or explicit prebuilt artifacts. Under RCH pressure this can turn a FUSE capability probe into an untracked local build and muddle validation evidence.

Scope: teach `e2e_mount` to use an explicit prebuilt `ffs-cli` path (for example `FFS_CLI_BIN` or a helper that resolves an RCH-built binary/artifact) and fail with a clear blocked message when no binary is available in remote-only mode. Keep the actual FUSE mount local. Do not add local cargo fallback unless it is behind an explicit opt-in/debug flag and recorded in the E2E log.

Acceptance:
1. `e2e_mount` no longer invokes bare `cargo run -p ffs-cli --release -- mount` by default.
2. E2E logs clearly distinguish local mount execution from cargo build/proof execution.
3. A shell self-check or focused E2E fixture fails if `e2e_mount` reintroduces default local cargo build fallback.
4. Validation includes `bash -n scripts/e2e/lib.sh`, any focused E2E self-check added for the helper, `git diff --check`, `jq empty .beads/issues.jsonl`, `br dep cycles --no-db --no-auto-import --json`, source-aware hygiene, and RCH cargo proof once `bd-oowwx` is resolved. If RCH remains blocked, keep this bead blocked on `bd-oowwx` and do not use local cargo as proof.
close_reason: Completed: e2e_mount now requires explicit prebuilt FFS_CLI_BIN, logs prebuilt-cli and local mount execution markers, and verification runner fails if ffs-cli cargo fallback returns; validated with bash -n, verification runner PASS, remote RCH cargo unit-test proof on ts2, diff check, JSONL parse, no dependency cycles, and source-aware hygiene.

title: Replace flat FEATURE_PARITY percentages with tiered support-state accounting
description:
Fresh plan-space gap found during the 2026-05-02 bv/br review after restoring follow-ups for deferred btrfs multidevice, btrfs send/receive, and ext4 casefold work. Historical tracker and docs language repeatedly closed broad parity beads with flat count claims such as FEATURE_PARITY 86/86, 90/90, or 100 percent V1 parity. Those counts are useful as implementation inventory, but they are unsafe as user-facing readiness claims because they collapse very different states: parse-only support, basic fixture coverage, single-device-only support, experimental mounted writes, disabled writeback-cache, detection-only scrub, opt-in mutating repair, unsupported/deferred scope, and fully validated behavior.

Root cause: the current planning model lacks a dedicated support-state accounting layer between raw feature existence and public readiness. Without that layer, future agents can close inventory beads and accidentally allow README, FEATURE_PARITY, release gates, or proof bundles to imply more capability than the evidence supports. This is especially risky for mount/write paths and automatic repair, where a false-green parity claim can put user data at risk.

Scope: define a tiered parity/support-state accounting model that separates implementation breadth from validation depth and operational readiness. The model must preserve every feature and historical parity row, but add explicit state, evidence, artifact freshness, docs wording, gate impact, and follow-up ownership. It should become the source that README and FEATURE_PARITY wording can be generated or checked against, rather than another prose-only checklist.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/schema tests cover feature rows with feature id, domain, legacy count bucket, support state, evidence lane, artifact freshness, gate consumer, docs wording id, unsupported or deferred rationale, and owner bead.
2. Migration tests ingest fixtures representing historical 86/86, 90/90, and 100 percent claims and classify parse-only send/receive, single-device-only multidevice, basic casefold, experimental mount/write, detection-only scrub, disabled writeback-cache, rw repair blocked, and validated read-only inspection.
3. E2E or dry-run validator emits both JSON and human reports, rejects unscoped 100 percent parity wording, and explains which state dimension is safe to claim.
4. Structured logs include feature id, old count claim, new support state, controlling bead or artifact, downgrade or upgrade reason, docs target, release-gate effect, and reproduction command.
5. Public docs cannot collapse implementation-count parity and readiness parity into one percentage. Any unsupported, experimental, detection-only, parse-only, or deferred state must link to an active follow-up bead or an explicit non-goal rationale.
6. The design explicitly composes with bd-rchk0.5.6.1 so the fail-closed release evaluator consumes this accounting data instead of re-deriving feature states from prose.

User impact: users should be able to tell what is implemented, what is validated, what is experimental, what is detection-only, and what must not be trusted for data mutation yet. Future agents should be able to update one machine-checkable accounting surface instead of editing README and FEATURE_PARITY claims by hand.

title: correctness(btrfs): a transaction commit is not atomic — it frees the LIVE trees' extents into its own allocator, so any mid-commit failure overwrites the image the superblock still points at
description:
Found while fixing bd-giw9n. NOT the defect that fired in that report (that was an
internal-node split bound, now fixed) — this is the reason that defect DESTROYED the
image instead of merely failing the unmount.

THE DEFECT
`btrfs_full_transaction_commit` (crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs) opens every transaction with:

    alloc.extent_alloc.remove_metadata_items_owned_by_roots(&[
        BTRFS_ROOT_TREE_OBJECTID, BTRFS_EXTENT_TREE_OBJECTID,
        BTRFS_FS_TREE_OBJECTID,  BTRFS_CSUM_TREE_OBJECTID])

That deletes the extent items describing the trees CURRENTLY REFERENCED BY THE ON-DISK
SUPERBLOCK, and calls `invalidate_tail_cursors()`. The allocator's gap search
(`alloc_extent`, crates/ffs-btrfs/src/lib.rs) derives free space *purely* from extent-tree
items, so those addresses become allocatable within the SAME transaction — while the live
superblock still points at them. Node writes then go straight to the device
(`executor.execute(...) -> write_all_at`) LONG before the new superblock is written.

Consequence: a commit that fails at any point after its first device write can have already
overwritten the live root tree / fs tree. `sb.root` is unchanged, so it now addresses a
block that is a structurally valid btrfs node of this filesystem carrying someone else's
items. The next mount walks it, finds no `(objectid=5, ROOT_ITEM)`, and reports
`not found: btrfs ROOT_ITEM for default_root 'default' (objectid 5)` — which is exactly the
bd-giw9n symptom, including why the block passed csum/fsid validation.

Compounding: `alloc_metadata_for_root_tree` and `alloc_metadata_for_extent_tree` pass
`skip_extent_item = true`, so those blocks are invisible to the gap search as well.

WHY IT IS STILL LIVE AFTER bd-giw9n
bd-giw9n removed one trigger. Any other mid-commit failure has the same effect. `NoSpace` is
reachable today because FrankenFS never allocates a new metadata chunk: mkfs sizes the
metadata block group once (51.2 MiB on a 1 GiB image, 256 MiB on 8 GiB, both DUP) and the
commit rewrites every tree wholesale, so a large enough fs tree exhausts it.

PROPOSED FIX (btrfs's own pinned-extent semantics)
Keep the removal where it is — the serialized extent tree must not carry stale items — but
record the removed (bytenr, len) pairs, and every `skip_extent_item` allocation, in an
in-memory PINNED set on `BtrfsExtentAllocator` that the gap search excludes. Clear it at the
start of the next transaction, when those blocks are genuinely free. This preserves COW: the
committed on-disk state survives untouched until the superblock write linearizes the new one,
so a failed commit is an honest error rather than a destroyed filesystem.

Cost: old + new metadata coexist for the duration of a transaction, which raises the metadata
high-water mark and will make `NoSpace` reachable sooner. That is the correct trade (an
honest ENOSPC beats an unmountable image) but argues for a companion bead on metadata chunk
growth.

ACCEPTANCE
A test that forces a commit failure after writes have begun (fault injection on the device,
or a metadata block group sized to run out mid-fs-tree) and asserts the image still mounts
and still contains the pre-transaction contents.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RESOLUTION

Landed across 4c02142e, ab967a75, f2881abd and completed by **279a77e4** (main, mirrored to
master). The first three were captured mid-edit from the shared worktree and did not build;
279a77e4 carries the compile fix, the unit tests, and the gate evidence.

REPRODUCED, then fixed, both measured — the acceptance criterion above, by device fault
injection. crates/ffs-core/tests/btrfs_commit_crash_window.rs builds an image with 64 durably
committed files, starts a second transaction, and fails the k-th device write for every k,
asserting the image still mounts and still holds all 64.

  - Control at 5b9ee888 (bd-giw9n landed, this fix absent): cutting the device after just
    TWO writes already destroys the previous transaction —
        crash after 2 writes: committed file base00000.dat lost: not found: btrfs inode 256
    The fs-tree ROOT DIRECTORY itself had been overwritten. Not a corner case: two writes in.
  - With the fix: every crash point from 0 to past the end of the commit leaves a mountable
    image holding all 64 committed files.

THE FIX — pinned extents, two generations deep. The transaction's linearization point is the
superblock write; until it lands, every block the committed superblock references must still
hold its committed bytes.

  1. `remove_metadata_items_owned_by_roots` now PINS each block before deleting its extent
     item. The delete still happens (the serialized extent tree must describe only live
     blocks) but the space no longer reads as free.
  2. `skip_extent_item` allocations (the extent tree's and root tree's own nodes, bd-4nz82)
     pin themselves — by design nothing else ever records them.
  3. Mount pins the live root/extent tree blocks, walked via a new
     `OpenFs::btrfs_tree_node_addresses`. An image FrankenFS wrote carries nothing in the
     extent tree describing those two trees, so without this the FIRST commit after mount
     could allocate over the root tree the superblock is pointing at.
  4. The gap finder unions pinned ranges into its allocated-range list; `coalesce_ranges`
     keeps that list sorted and disjoint, which `first_gap_at_or_after`'s `partition_point`
     predicate requires.
  5. `release_pinned_after_superblock_commit` rotates one generation and runs ONLY after the
     superblock write+sync. It is deliberately absent from every error path: on a failed
     commit the old trees are still the filesystem.

The `live_after_commit` flag on each pin is what makes it exactly two generations: blocks
being replaced die when this transaction's superblock lands; blocks this transaction
allocated without extent items become the protected set for the next one.

TESTS
- crates/ffs-core/tests/btrfs_commit_crash_window.rs (new): the crash-window sweep above.
- crates/ffs-btrfs/src/lib.rs (new unit tests):
  `freed_live_tree_blocks_are_not_reallocated_in_the_same_transaction_bd_mqb9t`,
  `pinned_blocks_are_released_after_the_superblock_commits_bd_mqb9t` (the pin is a delay,
  not a leak), `skip_extent_item_allocations_are_pinned_for_two_generations_bd_mqb9t`
  (a just-published root/extent tree stays protected through the NEXT transaction),
  `coalesce_ranges_merges_overlaps_and_duplicates_bd_mqb9t`.

GATES
- cargo test -p ffs-btrfs --lib: 389 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.
- cargo test -p ffs-core --tests --no-fail-fast: btrfs_commit_crash_window 1/1,
  btrfs_large_dir_mount_cycle 2/2 (bd-giw9n's 32k case still fits despite the extra pin
  pressure), cross_crate_integration 27/27, metamorphic 11/11, htree_leaf_split_gate 1/1,
  repro_create 3/3, bd_bhh0i_lock_decomposition_model 7/7.
- cargo test -p ffs-core --lib: 1195 passed, 1 failed — the pre-existing ext4
  fast_commit_del_range e2fsck failure (bd-age6i), unchanged by this work.
- cargo fmt --check clean. cargo clippy -p ffs-btrfs --all-targets: nothing in the changed
  files. Workspace clippy still cannot run: ffs-types (2x chunks_exact) and ffs-dir (8
  errors) have pre-existing failures and are unmodified locally.

SCOPE NOT COVERED (deliberate; filed separately if it matters)
- DATA extents freed mid-transaction (overwrite/truncate) are not pinned. They are not
  reachable from the superblock's tree walk, so they cannot make an image unmountable, but
  reallocating one inside the same transaction would corrupt the contents of the snapshot
  that is still committed.
- The metadata block group is still never grown. Pinning makes old + new coexist for the
  duration of a transaction, so the metadata high-water mark is now higher and `NoSpace` is
  reachable sooner. That is the correct trade — an honest ENOSPC that leaves the filesystem
  intact beats a destroyed image — but chunk growth is the real ceiling fix.

title: exchange server accepts zero accept poll interval busy-spin
description: Phase B deadlock-finder finding in crates/ffs-repair/src/exchange.rs. Server::from_listener accepts Config without validating accept_poll_interval. Because the listener is nonblocking, serve_until_cancelled calls accept(); when no client is pending and accept_poll_interval is zero, sleep_with_budget returns immediately and the accept loop retries WouldBlock without sleeping. With a cancellation-capable but no-deadline Cx, this becomes an unbounded CPU spin until external cancellation. Fix by validating transport Config at construction time and rejecting zero accept_poll_interval; also reject zero connect/io timeout and zero max_frame_bytes at the same boundary because those create equivalent fail-fast/spin transport behavior rather than usable I/O. Add focused tests for rejection plus preserve default config construction. Validate with rch crate-scoped ffs-repair test/check/clippy and fmt.

This prevents zero accept poll interval from turning serve_until_cancelled into an unbounded WouldBlock busy-spin while preserving default transport behavior. Added focused constructor validation tests and default acceptance coverage. title: btrfs commit: extent_tree/root_tree self-allocated nodes carry no EXTENT_ITEM (bd-x36qn lever A)
description: On a real-image commit, btrfs check reports 'tree extent[X] parent X has no backref item in extent tree' + 'ref mismatch on [X 16384] extent item 0, found 1' for the metadata blocks that hold the EXTENT_TREE and ROOT_TREE themselves. Cause: those trees' own nodes are allocated during commit via alloc_metadata_for_extent_tree / alloc_metadata_for_root_tree with skip_extent_item=true (the bd-4nz82 recursion break), so NO EXTENT_ITEM/METADATA_ITEM is inserted for them. btrfs check then finds the block referenced by a parent but with no extent item (refs 0) -> errors. These are the 'parent X' entries where X is in FrankenFS's metadata alloc range (~30M). Real btrfs resolves this with a delayed-ref / fixpoint pass: allocate the tree nodes, then insert their EXTENT_ITEMs (which may grow the tree, iterate until stable). FIX DIRECTION: after serializing extent_tree+root_tree, run a bounded second pass that inserts EXTENT_ITEM+inline TREE_BLOCK_REF for each just-allocated extent_tree/root_tree node and re-serializes the affected extent-tree leaves to a fixpoint (1-2 iterations expected for a small fs). Validate via btrfs_created_file_passes_btrfs_check_bd_x3fcu harness on rch: the 'parent X' no-backref errors should clear. Sibling lever: bd-x36qn lever B (loaded-extent backref preservation).
notes: MAJOR PROGRESS (b21739e1, AmberOtter): the extent-backref class was NOT missing items — dump-tree confirms every metadata self-node HAS an EXTENT_ITEM with refs 1 + inline TREE_BLOCK_REF (correct). The actual bug was a GENERATION MISMATCH: BtrfsExtentAllocator stamped EXTENT_ITEMs with self.generation (load-time N-1) while the tree blocks were rewritten at new_gen N. btrfs check --mode lowmem pinpointed it ('backref generation mismatch wanted 9 have 8' for FS_TREE+CSUM_TREE nodes). FIX: set_generation(new_gen) on the allocator at commit start. VERIFIED: lowmem [3/8] checking extents + [5/8] checking fs roots now CLEAN. Diagnostic tool added: btrfs_dump_tree_bd_myrgc_diag (dumps extent/root tree + both check modes). REMAINING: lowmem [4/8] free space tree ('no free space entry for 30490624-30523392', 'cache appears valid but isnt 30408704') — FrankenFS doesnt update the FREE_SPACE_TREE for its commit-time allocations. The ORIGINAL-mode check still reports 'total extent tree bytes: 0' + 'Chunk not found in block group' which is LIKELY downstream of the free-space-tree gap (original mode builds its block-group picture differently). NEXT: fix free-space-tree maintenance (new bead) — that should clear both lowmem [4/8] and the original-mode cascade.
close_reason: STALE / fully resolved across the btrfs-check campaign — verified by its own validation harness now passing. The self-allocated extent_tree/root_tree nodes DO carry EXTENT_ITEM + inline TREE_BLOCK_REF (insert_self_metadata_item in btrfs_full_transaction_commit); the generation-mismatch (the real bug, b21739e1 set_generation), the free-space-tree gap (bd-qxo5x, 41cc5ea6), and the original-mode 'total extent tree bytes 0' cascade (bd-fdwuh, f31ce06b) are all fixed. title: btrfs read-only ops do O(N) full-tree-walk per call; add O(log N) targeted descent
description:
Read-only btrfs metadata ops (getattr/lookup/readdir/read) each call walk_btrfs_fs_tree, which fully traverses the fs tree from disk per operation (O(N) node reads, uncached). A reader workload of M ops over an N-item tree is O(N*M). The writable path already uses targeted alloc.fs_tree.range(); the read-only on-disk path lacked an equivalent.

INCREMENT 1 (this commit): landed walk_tree_range in ffs-btrfs - targeted b-tree descent that prunes internal-node children whose key span cannot overlap [lo,hi), reading only O(log N) covering-path nodes. Isomorphism + read-count pruning proven by unit test on a 2-level/8-leaf tree (results identical to filtered full walk; strictly fewer node reads whenever the range excludes any leaf). walk_tree (range=None) byte-identical, 320+38 ffs-btrfs tests green.

FOLLOW-ON: rewire ffs-core read-only btrfs ops (the ~12 walk_btrfs_fs_tree callers) to descend by inode-keyed range [(ino,0,0),(ino+1,0,0)) instead of full-walk+filter; same-binary criterion A/B on a large synthetic tree to prove Score>=2.0.

title: perf(btrfs): single-file RANDOM read does a full B-tree extent descent per read (no cross-read cache) — 75x heavier than ext4, serial 17.9s/100k
description: MEASURED (CrimsonFox cc/opus 2026-06-21, ffs-cli rand-read harness fa8108d8, /data/tmp/btrc_1268087.img:/c.bin 150MB, 100k x 4KiB random, warm). btrfs single-file random read: SERIAL 17.9s = 5589 IOPS / 21 MiB/s = ~180us per 4KiB read, vs ext4 serial 2.4us/read = **75x heavier per read**. Parallel HELPS (4t 3.1s, 64t 458ms/853 MiB/s) because it is COMPUTE-bound (the opposite of ext4's lock-contended parallel collapse, bd-eflng). Root: each read_into on btrfs resolves the file extent via a full extent-tree DESCENT with no cross-read caching of the resolved path/extent map — random access re-walks from the root every read. This is the bd-xmh5g.421 per-descent pathology surfacing in the SINGLE-FILE random case (.421's prewarmed BtrfsReadPlanIndex covers the multi-file walk, not single-file random read_into). FIX direction: cache/memoize the per-inode btrfs extent map across reads (like ext4's resolve_extent extent cache) so a random read is an in-memory lookup + one pread, not a tree descent. ffs-core btrfs_read_file_into / read_into btrfs arm + ffs-btrfs tree walk. Reproduce: ffs-cli rand-read <btrfs-img> /c.bin --count 100000 --size 4096 [--parallel]. Distinct from bd-eflng (ext4 MVCC lock). Related: bd-xmh5g.421.
notes: PRECISELY SCOPED (CrimsonFox): btrfs_read_file_into (ffs-core:8632) has 3 extent-fetch branches: (1) writable COW tree (alloc_state); (2) 'else if btrfs_cached_read_plan_index()' = FAST in-memory lookup but the index is WHOLE-FS and only built/prewarmed by the multi-file walk path (bd-xmh5g.421); (3) 'else' = on-disk per-read B-tree descent (walk_btrfs_fs_tree_range bounded to the read window) = the ~180us/read cost. Single-file RO random read (rand-read) hits branch 3 because the whole-fs index is never built for it → re-descends the on-disk tree EVERY read_into. FIX = a per-inode extent-list cache: on first read of an inode (RO), fetch ALL its EXTENT_DATA items once, cache (OpenFs ShardedCache<inode, Arc<(BtrfsInodeItem, Vec<(u64,BtrfsExtentData)>)>>), and per-read do an in-memory range filter (the same filter branch 2 already does) instead of a fresh tree descent. RO-safe (immutable, no COW); gate on !is_writable like bd-eflng. Distinct from branch 2's whole-fs index (that amortizes over MANY files in a walk; this amortizes over MANY reads of ONE inode). Moderate core-path change. Confirmed bd-eflng's lock fix did NOT help here (descent-bound, not lock-bound). Reproduce: ffs-cli rand-read <btrfs-img> /c.bin --count 100000 --size 4096 --parallel.
close_reason: FIXED + SHIPPED b4b9f331 (CrimsonFox). Per-inode read-only btrfs extent cache: btrfs_read_file_into now resolves the inode's FULL extent list once (btrfs_load_inode_all_extents) into a ShardedCache keyed by inode objectid, then filters the read window in-memory per read — eliminating the ~57us/read on-disk tree descent. Gated on read-only (past the COW branch) + no pending tree log (on-disk tree is the complete immutable source); writable path unchanged. MEASURED: uncompressed btrfs random read ~2.1us/read serial = ~ext4 PARITY (derived ~28x, tree descent ~57us/read eliminated); compressed c.bin serial 17.9s->12.2s (1.47x, decompression-bound there not descent). Byte-identical (sha=kernel both compressed+uncompressed), conformance 100/0/2. Landed via git apply --cached (cod-b e2compr untouched). The descent-per-read pathology is RESOLVED; compressed random read residual is per-read decompression (decompress 128KB extent per 4KB read), a separate workload-specific cost.

title: Refine repair writeback routing with single mutation authority and rollback coupling
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-rchk0.1.2. Routing repair writeback through the mounted mutation path is the right direction, but implementation needs a single mutation authority and rollback coupling so repair, client writes, MVCC, journal, cache, and evidence ledger cannot diverge after partial failure.

Scope: define implementation proof requirements for a single authority that owns mutating writes, repair writeback, ledger state transitions, symbol refresh, rollback/abort, cancellation, and durable acceptance. Direct block writes should be impossible in rw repair mode unless explicitly classified as read-only/detection-only or offline repair.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit tests prove repair writeback cannot bypass the mounted mutation authority, MVCC epoch checks, journal/transaction boundary, cache invalidation, ledger state transition, or symbol-refresh gate.
2. Unit tests cover successful repair writeback, rejected state, writeback failure, journal abort, ledger write failure, symbol refresh failure, cancellation, stale snapshot, stale lease, rollback after partial write, and retry idempotence.
3. E2E/scenario smoke records visible data before/after repair, image hashes, ledger rows, transaction ids, symbol generation, rollback or abort outcome, and cleanup status.
4. Logs include operation id, authority id, epoch id, transaction id, ledger row ids, repair plan id, block range, mutation result, rollback result, symbol refresh result, artifact paths, and reproduction command.
5. Read-write automatic repair enablement must fail closed if any mutating repair path still writes outside the single authority or lacks rollback/evidence coupling.
close_reason: Completed duplicate repair writeback target fail-closed guard with ffs-core tests and e2e route artifact coverage.

title: Kernel-conformance pin for parse_dev_item 98-byte field offsets
description: Found via /testing-conformance-harnesses audit. ffs_ondisk::btrfs::parse_dev_item (lib.rs:1074) reads 13 fields from a 98-byte struct btrfs_dev_item per fs/btrfs/btrfs_tree.h: devid u64@0..8, total_bytes u64@8..16, bytes_used u64@16..24, io_align u32@24..28, io_width u32@28..32, sector_size u32@32..36, dev_type u64@36..44, generation u64@44..52, start_offset u64@52..60, dev_group u32@60..64, seek_speed u8@64, bandwidth u8@65, uuid [u8;16]@66..82, fsid [u8;16]@82..98. Existing parse_dev_item_valid (lib.rs:5037) only verifies devid/total_bytes/bytes_used/sector_size — 9 of 13 fields (io_align, io_width, dev_type, generation, start_offset, dev_group, seek_speed, bandwidth, uuid, fsid) aren't pinned at their offsets. A regression that drifted any of those would silently corrupt every DEV_ITEM read on btrfs mount. Fix: add parse_dev_item_kernel_offsets_match_btrfs_tree_h that stamps each addressable field with a unique non-zero magic and asserts every parsed field round-trips. Pattern matches bd-qwo4a (parse_dir_items kernel offsets), bd-9rup3 (parse_xattr_items), bd-kelr0 (parse_inode_refs), bd-bspkl (Ext4Extent leaf), bd-uezhf (Ext4ExtentIndex), bd-tpgp7 (Ext4MmpBlock). Bead size: <50 min.

title: Restore btrfs send-receive export apply parity beyond parse-only
description:
Fresh review follow-up from the closed bd-nzv3.14, bd-nzv3.15, and bd-nzv3.25 lane. Historical close reasons say the protocol model was extracted, send stream parsing exists, and full export was deferred or parse-only in V1. That is a valid scoped state only if the tracker, docs, proof bundle, and release gates keep it explicit. It is not 100% feature/functionality parity for btrfs send/receive.

Scope: restore the missing send/receive export/apply parity work as explicit implementation and conformance planning. Define deterministic send stream export, receive-side apply, incremental parent assumptions, unsupported-record refusal, metadata/xattr/link/rename ordering, stream corpus provenance, and roundtrip oracle outputs. The bead should preserve parse-only as an explicit supported subset until export/apply evidence exists.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit tests cover stream record schema, deterministic serialization, parser/export roundtrip, receive apply state machine, incremental parent validation, unsupported record rejection, path/name normalization, xattr metadata, clone/rename/link ordering, checksum/hash validation, and diagnostic rendering.
2. Unit/schema tests reject corpus rows missing source snapshot provenance, parent snapshot id where needed, expected stream hash, expected receive filesystem state, unsupported-record class, capability requirement, cleanup policy, and artifact requirements.
3. E2E or integration smoke runs at least one full export-then-receive roundtrip on deterministic fixtures, one incremental-parent mismatch refusal, and one unsupported-record refusal, emitting pass/fail/skip/error artifacts with raw logs.
4. Logs include stream id, source snapshot hash, parent snapshot hash, record count, stream hash, receive target hash, unsupported record id where relevant, expected state, observed state, remediation id, artifact paths, cleanup status, and reproduction command.
5. README, FEATURE_PARITY, release gates, and proof bundles must distinguish parse-only, export-only, receive-only, roundtrip-supported, and unsupported states; no public claim may imply full send/receive parity until roundtrip corpus evidence is fresh.

title: ext4 writable PUNCH_HOLE + flush_mvcc_to_device leaves superblock free counts unsynced (e2fsck count mismatch)
description: Found while adding an e2fsck check for unaligned punch (bd-xnel9). A writable ext4 PUNCH_HOLE followed by flush_mvcc_to_device produces a device snapshot e2fsck flags with 'Free blocks count wrong' AND 'Free inodes count wrong' (sb over-counts free vs the bitmaps). REPRODUCES WITH AN ALIGNED PUNCH TOO, so it is pre-existing and NOT specific to the unaligned change (which is data-correct: byte-exact + the ext4_write_fallocate_random gauntlet pass). Contrast: a create+write+flush (no punch) IS e2fsck-clean (see fast_commit_inode_update_on_regular_file_passes_e2fsck), so the write path syncs sb counts but the writable punch path does not. The free_inodes-by-1 discrepancy is odd for a block punch — suggests flush_mvcc_to_device or the punch alloc-state path does not persist the updated superblock s_free_blocks_count/s_free_inodes_count after a fallocate-free, while the recovery punch path (load_ext4_alloc_state, used by FC DEL_RANGE) IS e2fsck-clean. INVESTIGATE: whether flush_mvcc_to_device should also persist the superblock free counters (or whether fs.sync/unmount does and the test just needs that call). Likely a missing superblock-counter flush in the writable fallocate/flush path. Low severity (counts are e2fsck-repairable; in-memory state is correct) but a real on-disk-consistency gap for a snapshot taken after a writable punch.
close_reason: done

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ⭐CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE (my W25 'punch-specific' conclusion was WRONG — disproved by a size-controlled probe): the bug is BROAD, not punch-specific. A bare create+write(5 blocks)+flush_mvcc_to_device+e2fsck is ALSO dirty ('Free blocks count wrong 6526 counted=6519' + 'Free inodes count wrong 2036 counted=2035'). The 6526/2036 are the PRISTINE post-mke2fs superblock free counts → the writable ext4 path NEVER updates the superblock totals s_free_blocks_count_lo/hi and s_free_inodes_count; only the GROUP DESCRIPTOR free counts + bitmaps are persisted (via PersistCtx/alloc_blocks_persist/free_blocks_persist). flush_mvcc_to_device only flushes MVCC data blocks. So EVERY writable-fs device snapshot is e2fsck-dirty on the sb free totals (repairable, not corruption). (My earlier 'baseline clean' at 3 blocks was a vacuous run_e2fsck=None skip.) This is why fallocate/punch e2fsck tests can't validate cleanly. DE-RISKED FIX: on the durability boundary (flush_mvcc_to_device, gated alloc_state.is_some()+ext4), recompute totals = sum of alloc.groups free_blocks/free_inodes (or compute_ext4_free_space_summary @lib.rs:8700), write into the sb block: s_free_blocks_count_lo @sb+0x0C, s_free_inodes_count @sb+0x10, s_free_blocks_count_hi @sb+0x158 (64bit feat), then re-stamp the sb csum if has_metadata_csum: ext4_chksum(!0u32, &sb[sb_off..sb_off+EXT4_SB_CHECKSUM_OFFSET]) written at sb_off+EXT4_SB_CHECKSUM_OFFSET (ext4_chksum is pub in ffs-ondisk; validate_checksum @ext4.rs:1258 is the formula). sb_block=1024/block_size, sb_off=1024%block_size. ⚠️SUPERBLOCK WRITE = corruption-sensitive: VALIDATE with e2fsck on BOTH open_ext4_mke2fs(with_csum=true AND false) + a from_device reopen (sb must parse+csum-verify) + FULL ffs-core suite (blast radius: flush_mvcc_to_device has many callers; any test asserting stale sb free-count bytes would need updating). Bumped to P2 (affects all writable e2fsck snapshots).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ⚠️CRITICAL IMPL GOTCHA: do NOT copy clear_ext4_orphan_state's sb-write pattern verbatim — it hardcodes sb_block=BlockNumber(0) + block_data[sb_off=1024..], which is OUT OF BOUNDS for a 1024-byte-block fs (direct_block_device_adapter uses self.block_size(), so read_block(0) returns only 1024 bytes; the sb is in block 1). open_ext4_mke2fs uses -b 1024, so the e2fsck test WILL hit this. Compute: bs=self.block_size(); sb_block=BlockNumber(1024/bs); sb_off_in_block=(1024%bs) as usize; read that block, edit s_free_blocks_count_lo @sb_off+0x0C / s_free_inodes_count @sb_off+0x10 / hi @sb_off+0x158 (gate on sb.is_64bit()), re-stamp csum over [sb_off..sb_off+EXT4_SB_CHECKSUM_OFFSET] writing at sb_off+EXT4_SB_CHECKSUM_OFFSET. (clear_ext4_orphan_state itself may have a latent 1024-block bug — separate, low-pri.) Validate the fix with the W5 probe (create+write5+flush+e2fsck CLEAN) on BOTH open_ext4_mke2fs(with_csum true/false).

So the bd-nd61w fix = ext4_superblock_location() + write free-count fields at sb_off+0x0C/0x10/0x158 + restamp csum, on flush_mvcc_to_device.

comments.text: ⭐ROOT CAUSE FOUND (3rd correction) + the 'sb free count sync' fix abandoned. Disproved 'writable path never syncs sb totals' (W26): a 3-block write+flush+e2fsck is CLEAN without any fix — data-block alloc DOES keep sb/GD/bitmap consistent. The free-count (AND i_blocks) errors appear ONLY for >4-block writes, because those fragment into >4 single-block extents (no coalescing) -> tree grows -> metadata leaf block uncounted. So bd-nd61w is a SYMPTOM of the missing extent coalescing -> filed bd-bdro7 (the real fix). My 'recompute sb free counts on flush' approach was a zero-value band-aid (it never makes any file e2fsck-clean: <=4-block already clean; >4-block still fails on i_blocks) — NOT shipped. Recommend: fix bd-bdro7 (scoped write-path coalescing) which makes contiguous writes e2fsck-clean; then bd-nd61w's residual = i_blocks for genuinely-fragmented files' tree-growth metadata (also noted on bd-bdro7). Suggest closing bd-nd61w in favor of bd-bdro7 + the residual note, OR keeping for the residual. ext4_superblock_location() (from bd-icebl) remains available if a real sb-total resync is ever needed.

comments.text: ROOT CAUSE FIXED via bd-bdro7 (4056b657): contiguous writes now coalesce -> no premature tree growth -> e2fsck-clean. The 'sb free count' symptom is resolved for the common (contiguous) case. RESIDUAL: a genuinely-fragmented file (>4 physically-NON-contiguous extents) still grows the extent tree, and that metadata leaf block is not counted in i_blocks (nor the free total) -> e2fsck dirty for such files only. Re-scoping bd-nd61w to THAT residual: fix the extent-tree-growth path (ffs_btree grow_root_leaf/grow_root_index allocate metadata blocks via the tree allocator) to bump the inode i_blocks (+ the alloc accounting) for metadata blocks. Lower priority (rare: needs >4 non-contiguous extents). My W26 'sb free count sync on flush' band-aid is NOT the fix (abandoned).

comments.text: BROADENED + bumped P3->P2. The namespace-churn fuzz (e9f1b206) confirms this is a GENERAL writable-path on-disk-accounting-totals gap, not just sb free blocks: after create/mkdir/unlink/rmdir/rename churn, e2fsck reports (1) 'Free blocks count wrong', (2) 'Free inodes count wrong', AND (3) NEW: 'Directories count wrong for group #N' = group descriptor bg_used_dirs_count not maintained when dirs are created/removed/renamed. So the writable path keeps bitmaps + per-op state consistent (readdir/lookup/model all correct) but does NOT maintain the on-disk TOTALS: sb s_free_blocks_count (0x0C/0x158), sb s_free_inodes_count (0x10), and gd bg_used_dirs_count. This blocks e2fsck validation of the ENTIRE writable path (every snapshot is dirty on these totals), which is why the namespace fuzz + the punch/fallocate e2fsck checks can't run clean. FIX (the right one, now that the coalescing i_blocks bug is fixed via bd-bdro7): on the durability boundary (flush_mvcc_to_device / a sync path), recompute + write the totals from the in-memory alloc state — sb free_blocks = sum(groups.free_blocks), sb free_inodes = sum(groups.free_inodes), and bg_used_dirs_count per group (either maintained incrementally in alloc_inode_persist/free_inode_persist with an is_dir flag, or recomputed). Use ext4_superblock_location() (bd-icebl) for the sb block; restamp sb csum; restamp gd csums. VALIDATE: namespace-churn fuzz + punch/fallocate fuzz e2fsck-clean on BOTH metadata_csum modes + reopen. Once landed, re-enable the deferred e2fsck passes in those fuzzes (they'll then also cover ../link-count invariants).

title: perf(readdir): inode-table prefetch rayon coordination dominates htree-dir readdir (~60% self-time, load-independent profile)
description: prefetch_ext4_readdir_inode_table_blocks fires per readdir page (lib.rs:30329/30354) unconditionally; htree dirs return hash-ordered entries so a 512-entry page touches up to 512 scattered inode-table blocks -> exceeds serial threshold -> rayon fan-out -> StackJob 31% + sched_yield 30% + steal 18% + thread-spawn dwarf the reads. Wasted entirely for readdir-only (ls -f). Fix: (a) skip for no-stat consumers (needs stat-intent flag); (b) nested-rayon guard like 3e94e916; (c) raise serial threshold. MEASURE under low load (box was 45-97 from peers, timing dead). See NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md 2026-06-22 entry.
close_reason: RESOLVED across 3 commits: no-stat skip 62f77460 (~2.25x default), FFS_NO_READDIR_PREFETCH knob 79878ff5/c0d51dde (~1.4x warm opt-in), serialize-prefetch default 18239fdc (~1.2x with-stat, byte-identical, no cold risk). frankenfs large-htree-dir readdir was slower than kernel ls -f (44ms fan-out), now faster (~54ms with-stat / 20ms no-stat). ffs-core green.

title: btrfs add_data_extent_ref cannot merge a duplicate EXTENT_DATA_REF (fail-stop vs kernel increment)
description: ffs-btrfs add_data_extent_ref (src/lib.rs ~4302) always insert()s a keyed EXTENT_DATA_REF with count:1 at hash_extent_data_ref(root,objectid,offset). If the same (root,objectid,offset) is added twice it returns KeyAlreadyExists (ffs-btrfs ~2688) instead of incrementing the existing ref's count, which is what the kernel does (shared refs on one extent from one inode at one offset). Currently HARD to reach (clone paths clear the dst window first; distinct dst offsets hash differently) and it FAILS CLOSED (error, not corruption). Parity gap, low severity. Found in the same btrfs mutation audit as bd-5svhs/bd-iv5uy. Fix: on KeyAlreadyExists, read+parse the existing EXTENT_DATA_REF, increment its count, update() in place.
close_reason: done

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: FIXED in 4645aade: add_data_extent_ref now merges a duplicate EXTENT_DATA_REF for the same (root,objectid,offset) by incrementing the existing keyed item's count + update() in place (kernel behavior), instead of insert()->KeyAlreadyExists. Merge only fires when the stored triple matches, so a genuine hash collision with a DIFFERENT triple still falls through to insert() (preserves prior fail-closed behavior, no regression). Test add_data_extent_ref_merges_duplicate_backref_bd_ngt1y: two refs for (5,257,0) over a refs==1 inline extent -> total EXTENT_ITEM refs==3 + exactly one keyed ref count==2; the 2nd add no longer errors. 334 ffs-btrfs green, clippy clean. Closing.

title: Refine crash replay proof artifacts with survivor-set verification
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-rchk0.5.5.1. The crash replay lab already requires schedule minimization and dual-lane coverage; this bead makes the proof artifact itself a contract so failures are reproducible, reviewable, and hard to misclassify. It exists because crash tests without a stable survivor-set model can still produce impressive logs while leaving users unsure whether data loss was expected, detected, repaired, or missed.

Scope: define and validate a versioned crash replay artifact schema, including operation trace, schedule identity, crash point, expected survivor set, observed survivor set, repair/replay actions, oracle verdict, minimization status, lane capability state, and reproduction command. The artifact must be consumable by the proof bundle, release gates, and follow-up bead creation flow without re-reading implementation logs manually.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/schema tests reject artifacts missing schedule id, seed, lane type, crash taxonomy value, pre-crash image hash, post-replay image hash, expected survivors, observed survivors, oracle verdict, minimization status, raw-log path, and reproduction command.
2. Unit tests cover survivor-set comparison for exact match, allowed repaired divergence, missing file, unexpected extra file, metadata-only mismatch, unsupported host skip, replay failure, and inconclusive oracle.
3. E2E smoke emits at least one core/LabRuntime artifact and one mounted-lane artifact or explicit capability skip using the same schema.
4. Detailed logs include every command, image path/hash, schedule seed, crash point, replay step, repair step, cleanup status, minimization decision, and follow-up bead id or reason no follow-up is needed.
5. The proof bundle and release-gate evaluator can ingest the artifact and fail closed on stale schema versions, missing survivor fields, or inconclusive product-failure classifications.

title: ffs-fuzz: no stamp/verify round-trip fuzz target for ext4 dir-block / extent-block checksums
description:
Finding (via /testing-fuzzing skill, third visit, different target):
ext4 has stamp/verify pairs for several checksum families
(dir_block, extent_block, group_desc, inode, MMP). The existing
fuzz target fuzz_ext4_checksums.rs hits every verify_*_checksum
function with arbitrary bytes (no-panic) but does NOT exercise the
stamp/verify round-trip — i.e. "stamp a random block, then verify
the stamp". The fixed-input round-trip tests
(`stamp_dir_block_checksum_round_trips_with_verify`,
`stamp_extent_block_checksum_round_trips_with_verify`) cover one
input each; the proptest layer is sparse.

Concrete missing coverage:

  MR-1 — dir_block stamp/verify round-trip: for any dir_block
         payload with a valid 12-byte tail
         (inode=0, rec_len=12, name_len=0, file_type=EXT4_FT_DIR_CSUM)
         and any (csum_seed, ino, generation) triple,
         stamp_dir_block_checksum(buf, ...) followed by
         verify_dir_block_checksum(buf, ...) MUST return Ok.

  MR-2 — extent_block stamp/verify round-trip: for any extent_block
         buffer of length >= 12 + 12*eh_max + 4 with eh_max in
         the valid range, stamp followed by verify must succeed.

A regression that drifted the stamp coverage range or the seed
formula would silently make every newly-mutated dir/extent block
fail verification on read — but the existing no-panic fuzz target
would not detect it (it only checks "did parser panic?", not
"did the freshly-stamped checksum verify?").

Acceptance: a new fuzz target
fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_ext4_stamp_verify_roundtrip.rs that uses a
ByteCursor pattern (same as bd-38xrn fuzz_ext4_group_desc_roundtrip
and bd-rivds fuzz_btrfs_devitem_roundtrip) to synthesise structured
inputs, stamps via the public stamp_*_checksum functions, and
asserts verify_*_checksum returns Ok. Companion `[[bin]]` entry in
fuzz/Cargo.toml. Verifies build via
`rch exec -- cd fuzz && cargo check --bin fuzz_ext4_stamp_verify_roundtrip`.
notes: Shipped: fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_ext4_stamp_verify_roundtrip.rs + [[bin]] entry in fuzz/Cargo.toml. ByteCursor-driven structured input synthesises a dir_block (with valid 12-byte tail per ext4_dir_entry_tail layout) and an extent_block (with valid eh_max in [1, 200) so the tail offset fits), stamps via stamp_dir_block_checksum / stamp_extent_block_checksum, then asserts verify_*_checksum returns Ok. Also fixed missing pub-use re-exports in crates/ffs-ondisk/src/lib.rs for the bd-k81lq / bd-3ydm6 / bd-343v3 constants and is_reserved_inode predicate (they were defined in the ext4 submodule but not re-exported from the crate root). Verified via rch exec -- cd fuzz && cargo check --bin fuzz_ext4_stamp_verify_roundtrip (Finished in 4.82s).

title: ext4 extent-tree index/leaf child blocks read uncached during descent; route through the RO block cache
description: walk_extent_tree (resolve_extent) and collect_extents_with_scope descend depth>0 extent trees by reading each child index/leaf block via read_block_with_scope, which consults no block cache. After bd-r7enr a single file's sequential scan descends once, but a large/fragmented file has many extents under SHARED index blocks: resolving extents in different leaves (random/strided access, or extent_cache misses) re-descends through the SAME index block every time, re-reading it from the device. Route both Index-branch child reads through read_ext4_file_data_block_with_scope (gated by can_cache_ext4_read_only_block; identical scope/MVCC semantics via read_block_arc_with_scope incl. bd-bw90c) so extent-tree internal blocks are cached on read-only mounts. Writable mounts unchanged. Completes bd-r7enr; mirrors bd-di429/bd-jgx7u. Isomorphic on read-only. PROOF: CountingDevice on a shared index block, resolve extents in 2 leaves, index block read once vs twice, Score>=2.0.
close_reason: done

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: DONE (6639b918). Routed both extent-tree Index-branch child reads (walk_extent_tree + collect_extents_with_scope) from uncached read_block_with_scope to read_ext4_file_data_block_with_scope (gated can_cache_ext4_read_only_block; writable unchanged). Completes bd-r7enr; mirrors bd-di429/bd-jgx7u. PROOF (test ext4_extent_index_block_cache_hits_in_read_only_mode_bd_nlggu, depth-1 tree + 2 leaves, CountingDevice on leaf): after extent_cache.invalidate_all() a re-descent serves the leaf block from the block cache (0 device reads) vs re-reading it → 2 descents read the leaf once not twice → Score 2.0. title: btrfs FICLONERANGE does not enforce max file size (EFBIG) on the destination

title: [parity] ext4 external extent-tree block CRC32C not stamped on write — e2fsck-dirty on metadata_csum
description: Same class as bd-x4icj (dir-block csum), bd-fwph3 (xattr block csum), bd-vdi91 (bitmap csum): a stamping helper exists but is never wired into the write path. ffs_ondisk::ext4::stamp_extent_block_checksum (crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs:2388) has ZERO production callers — only ffs-ondisk/ffs-harness TESTS reference it. Meanwhile ffs-btree (crates/ffs-btree/src/lib.rs) writes EXTERNAL extent-tree nodes (index + leaf blocks, depth>=1) via dev.write_block at ~12 sites (642,660,664,701,718,721,738,769,778,835,844,1048,1107) WITHOUT ever stamping the 4-byte CRC32C tail at offset 12+12*eh_max. ffs_btree::insert (and the GroupBlockAllocator that feeds it) never receive the inode number or i_generation, which the extent-block checksum is keyed on (csum_seed -> ino -> i_generation -> block[0..tail_off], per verify_extent_block_checksum at ext4.rs:2337). So whenever a FrankenFS ext4 file's extent tree spills out of the inode (>4 extents -> grow_root_leaf/grow_root_index -> depth>=1) on a metadata_csum image, the external extent blocks carry a zero/stale checksum -> e2fsck reports 'extent block passes checks, but checksum does not match extent block' -> dirty. Reachable from 4 file-write insert sites in ffs-core (lib.rs:10846,11118,19710,19723). FIX: thread (csum_seed, ino, i_generation, has_metadata_csum) into ffs-btree node writes (e.g. add a finalize_node stamp hook to the BlockAllocator trait + carry ino/generation on GroupBlockAllocator), stamp every external node before write_block; root writes (write_leaf_root/write_index_root into i_block) are covered by the INODE checksum and must NOT be extent-stamped. PROOF: build a depth>=1 extent tree on a generated metadata_csum image, verify every external extent block via verify_extent_block_checksum (RED before, GREEN after); ideally an e2fsck round-trip.
close_reason: Fixed in 7cce2a66. Wired stamp_extent_block_checksum into the write path via a BlockAllocator::finalize_node hook routed through ffs-btree's new write_node() (covers all 13 external index/leaf node writes in insert/grow/split/delete). GroupBlockAllocator stamps with fs csum seed + owning inode ino+i_generation, carried by a new ExtentOwner threaded through the 7 ffs-extent mutation fns + all ffs-core/ffs-inode callers (write, fallocate, setattr, move_ext, delete_inode). RED->GREEN proof external_extent_blocks_carry_valid_crc32c_bd_o3wif forces a depth>=1 tree on a metadata_csum image and verifies every external block via verify_extent_block_checksum. ffs-core 899/899 pass; clippy/fmt clean. Inode-root i_block writes unaffected (covered by inode checksum).

title: [HIGH] build_btrfs_image fixture omits default-root ROOT_ITEM for OpenOptions::default()
description:
# Review finding

`cargo test --workspace --all-targets` is still red in the basic btrfs smoke suite even after checksum stamping landed. The remaining failure shape is no longer CRC mismatch; it is `NotFound("btrfs ROOT_ITEM for default_root `default` (objectid 5)")` from `OpenFs::from_device(..., OpenOptions::default())`.

## Failed tests
- `tests::open_fs_from_btrfs_image`
- `tests::open_fs_btrfs_debug_format`
- `tests::open_fs_btrfs_superblock_accessor`
- `tests::open_fs_btrfs_walk_root_tree`

## Evidence
- Fixture builder: `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:22119-22204`
- It currently emits a single synthetic root-tree leaf entry with `objectid=256`, `item_type=ROOT_ITEM`, and 8 bytes of dummy payload.
- Current selection logic resolves `BtrfsMountSelection::DefaultRoot` to `BTRFS_FS_TREE_OBJECTID` (`objectid 5`) and requires a matching `ROOT_ITEM` before it can fall back to the superblock `root_dir_objectid`: `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:2395-2428`.
- Workspace repro still fails these four tests with the `NotFound` error after the checksum-only fix.

## Why this is high severity
This keeps the full workspace test gate red in the most basic btrfs `OpenFs` smoke path. It is a separate regression from the already-filed readdir checksum family.

## Repro
`rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_frankenfs_cod cargo test --workspace --all-targets`

## Expected fix direction
Make `build_btrfs_image()` model the current default-root mount contract: include a `ROOT_ITEM` for `BTRFS_FS_TREE_OBJECTID` (objectid 5) with parseable enough payload for default-root resolution, or explicitly adjust the smoke tests to open a non-default root selection if that is the intended contract. Verify the four basic open/root-tree tests independently once fixed.

title: ffs-harness: no conformance test that re-encodes ext4 group desc fixtures
description:
Finding (via /testing-conformance-harnesses skill): the conformance
suite under crates/ffs-harness/tests/conformance.rs parses the
canonical ext4 group descriptor fixtures (32-byte and 64-byte) and
asserts the parsed field values, but **no conformance test re-encodes
the parsed Ext4GroupDesc back through `write_to_bytes` and confirms
the produced bytes match the fixture byte-for-byte**.

This is a distinct contract from the bd-ov7zr proptest MRs:

  * proptest MR1 — parse(write(gd, ds), ds) == gd
    (encoder/decoder are mutually consistent)
  * conformance — write_to_bytes(gd_from_fixture, ds) == fixture_bytes
    (encoder produces KERNEL-SHAPED bytes)

The proptest MR can pass while the conformance MR fails: e.g. if the
encoder mis-computes an offset and the decoder mis-parses it from the
SAME wrong offset, the round-trip is internally consistent but the
bytes our writer produces are NOT what the kernel writes — every
ext4 image we mutate would silently drift from the on-disk format.

The conformance fixtures already encode the kernel-shaped byte layout:
  * conformance/fixtures/ext4_group_desc_32byte.json
  * conformance/fixtures/ext4_group_desc_64byte.json

These are the canonical reference for "what bytes does the kernel
write for a group descriptor with these field values". A re-encode
test pins our writer to match.

Acceptance: 2 new tests in crates/ffs-harness/tests/conformance.rs
that load each fixture, parse it, re-encode the parsed Ext4GroupDesc
into a fresh buffer via write_to_bytes, and assert the produced bytes
equal the original fixture bytes. The 32-byte test exercises the lo-
half-only path; the 64-byte test exercises the full lo+hi split.
notes: Shipped: 2 new conformance tests in crates/ffs-harness/tests/conformance.rs that re-encode parsed Ext4GroupDesc through write_to_bytes and assert byte-equality with the original fixture (32-byte and 64-byte paths). Distinct from bd-ov7zr proptest MRs — those pin encoder/decoder mutual consistency; these pin encoder fidelity to the kernel-shaped on-disk layout. Both pass via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-harness --test conformance ext4_group_desc.

title: [bug] ext4 slow-symlink creation always fails (cannot write to a symlink)

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: FOUND+FIXED. Creating any ext4 symlink whose target exceeds EXT4_FAST_SYMLINK_MAX (60 bytes) always failed with Format("cannot write to a symlink"). Root cause: slow-symlink creation writes the target into data blocks via self.ext4_write(ino,0,target) (lib.rs ~11555), but ext4_write had an UNCONDITIONAL guard `if inode.is_symlink() { return Err("cannot write to a symlink") }` (~12191) — and the inode it just created is S_IFLNK. So the write the creation path itself issues was rejected. Broken on ALL images; never caught because the only tests gate on open_writable_ext4, which skips when the fixture is absent (= everywhere incl rch; bd-cc6ua). FIX: added a reject_symlink:bool param to ext4_write (zero cost — it already reads the inode); the public write path (FsOps::write ext4 branch ~20378) passes true (external writes to a symlink still rejected), the slow-symlink creation path passes false. Regression test write_symlink_slow_target_create_and_public_write_guard_ext4 uses open_writable_ext4_mkfs(64) so it RUNS on rch: asserts slow symlink creates + readlink round-trips + is NOT a fast symlink + public write to the symlink is still rejected. Was RED (cannot write to a symlink) before, GREEN after. Full ffs-core suite 895 pass; clippy -D warnings clean; #![forbid(unsafe_code)] intact.

title: perf(btrfs): find what 8 concurrent fs-tree descents contend on — 1.53x of the memo's benefit is concurrency pressure, invisible to every per-op counter
description:
HALF THE MEMO'S BENEFIT WAS CONCURRENCY PRESSURE, NOT WORK — and nobody has looked at
what 8 concurrent fs-tree descents actually contend on.

MEASURED (bd-btrfs-readdir-stat-8x-8y7vp, 2026-08-16, commit f9dc4ab0):

  dispatch counters   —          ~1.12x
  1 client thread                1.359036x  CI [1.162220, 1.405694], null 1.002902x
  8 client threads (comparator)  2.078x-2.095x

2.078 / 1.359 = 1.529x of the memo's measured effect is ABSENT at one thread. The memo
buys ~1.36x of genuine per-op saving; the rest appears only when 8 threads descend
simultaneously. That component is invisible to every per-op counter this daemon has,
which is why dispatch metrics under-explain the readdir+stat row by ~8x.

THE QUESTION: what do concurrent fs-tree descents contend on? Candidates, none measured:
  - the parsed-node cache (ShardedCache) — lock or shard skew on hot interior nodes
  - the btrfs floor-leaf memo's Mutex, which every descent takes (bd-5vis3 fixed it being
    held ACROSS floor_in_leaf, but it is still taken)
  - allocator pressure from per-descent temporaries
  - memory bandwidth / LLC from re-reading the same interior nodes 8 ways

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS ROW: the capability probe is ~99% of warm stat and is one
round trip per path-based op regardless of filesystem, depth, privilege or xattr
presence (five nulls, bd-z0rb8). Nothing daemon-side can remove the SEND. But the
DESCENT behind a probe is entirely ours, and this measurement says descent concurrency
costs more than descent work at 8 threads. That is a daemon-side lever on a row where we
had concluded there was none.

ACCEPTANCE:
  - identify the contended resource by measurement, not inspection — a thread sweep
    (1/2/4/8) on the SAME fixture at 4096 slots is the cheapest discriminator: if the
    per-entry cost degrades superlinearly with threads, it is contention; if it is flat,
    the 1.53x is something else and this bead is wrong
  - a counted or profiled mechanism naming the resource
  - any fix measured at 1 AND 8 threads, because a lever that only helps at 8 is a
    contention fix and must be described as one

DO NOT start by optimising a descent. bd-btrfs-readdir-stat-8x's attribution already shows
per-descent work is the smaller half, and the dispatch counters undercount even that.

METHOD NOTE: --runtime-mode managed exposes the dispatch counters that the comparator's
standard runtime discards (bd-viil0). The thread sweep can be done with the mounted
comparator's --client-threads directly, which is the instrument that will have to admit
any resulting claim.
close_reason: REFUTED (commit 263e70c8). Filed on the claim that 1.53x of the memo's 2.08x is concurrency pressure, derived from differencing my 1-thread harness against the comparator's 8-thread run. At MATCHED concurrency my harness measures 1.200033x where the comparator measures 2.063608x, so that subtraction compared two clients, not two thread counts. Separately, --client-threads is silently discarded for ReaddirStat8 (harness line 183), so the thread sweep this bead specified as its discriminator ran at 8 threads in every cell and was not executable as written. The ~12% dispatch-counter gap remains real and now has no explanation; it is carried on bd-btrfs-readdir-stat-8x-8y7vp rather than here.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
REFUTED — THIS BEAD'S PREMISE IS FALSE (AzureBay, 2026-08-16, commit 263e70c8).

I filed this on the claim that 1.53x of the memo's 2.08x is concurrency pressure, derived from comparing my single-threaded harness (1.359x) against the comparator's 8-thread run (2.078x). That comparison was invalid.

The check I should have run before filing — does my harness reproduce the comparator's ratio at the SAME thread count?

  my harness   1 thread   4096 20723.9 ns/entry  65536 15387.0  ratio 1.346845
  my harness   8 threads  4096  7980.7 ns/entry  65536  6650.4  ratio 1.200033
  comparator   8 threads  4096  6669.2 ns/entry  65536  3231.8  ratio 2.063608

At matched concurrency my harness measures 1.20x where the comparator measures 2.06x. It does not reproduce the instrument I was differencing against, so 1-vs-8 measured the difference between two CLIENTS, not the effect of threads. 2.078 / 1.359 = 1.529x was arithmetic on incomparable numbers.

The absolutes show the mechanism: my 65,536 arm costs 6650 ns/entry against the comparator's 3232 (~3400 ns of client overhead) while my 4096 arm costs 7981 against 6669 (only ~1310 more). Overhead large relative to the fast arm and small relative to the slow one compresses every ratio it measures. My harness's ratio also moves the WRONG way with threads (1.347 -> 1.200), the signature of dilution rather than a thread effect.

A SECOND INDEPENDENT REASON THE DISCRIMINATOR COULD NOT HAVE WORKED: --client-threads is silently discarded for this workload. Workload::client_threads (ffs_mounted_kernel_bench.rs:183) returns DEFAULT_PARALLEL_THREADS unconditionally for ReaddirStat8, ParallelRead8 and ParallelRead8ColdCache; only ParallelMetadataWrite honours it. Every cell of my 1/2/4/8 sweep ran at 8 threads. The report is honest — it prints requested_client_threads=8, actual_observed_worker_threads=8 whatever you pass — which is exactly why the effective value belongs in the report and not only in the flag. So the acceptance criterion I wrote into this bead ("a thread sweep 1/2/4/8 on the same fixture is the cheapest discriminator") was not executable as written.

CLOSING AS REFUTED. Nothing here says concurrency is irrelevant to readdir+stat — it says I never measured it and the number I quoted was an artifact. Anyone reopening this needs a client that reproduces the comparator at matched threads first, or a way to vary concurrency inside the comparator itself (which today means editing Workload::client_threads or using ParallelMetadataWrite, a different workload).

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND UNEXPLAINED: the dispatch counters account for only ~12% of the comparator's 2.06x. That gap is real. The contention hypothesis was its explanation and is now withdrawn, so it should be carried as unexplained rather than as evidence for anything. It belongs on bd-btrfs-readdir-stat-8x-8y7vp, not on a bead named for a mechanism nobody has shown.

USEFUL BYPRODUCT: five completed cells of the invalid sweep were all 8-thread runs on one fixture, so they serve as replication — 4096 arm 215935808/224072610/218535580 (3.8% spread), 65536 arm 108894048/101942138/105899775 (6.8% spread), medians 2.063608x. Five more samples agreeing with the banked 2.078x-2.095x.

title: Reject reserved dot path components in filesystem writes
description:
Reviewer finding [HIGH]: ffs-core accepts reserved path components "." and ".." as user-supplied directory entry names in mutating filesystem operations.

Evidence:
- crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:14500 validate_single_path_component only rejects empty names, embedded slash, and names longer than 255 bytes. It returns Ok for b"." and b"..".
- The validator feeds ext4 create/mknod/link/rename/unlink paths and btrfs create/mkdir/link/symlink/rename/unlink paths before directory mutation. For example, btrfs_create validates at crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:13207 and then inserts the provided name into the directory index; btrfs_link validates at 13586 and later stores new_name in a BtrfsDirItem.
- fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_path_component_validation.rs models only Empty, ContainsSlash, TooLong, and Valid. Its oracle treats "." and ".." as Valid, so the existing fuzz target cannot catch the reserved-component bug.

Why this matters:
"." and ".." are reserved namespace entries. Accepting them for create/mkdir/link/symlink/rename can shadow or conflict with synthesized parent/current-directory semantics and can corrupt lookup/readdir/link-count behavior.

Expected behavior:
Reject b"." and b".." with a format/invalid-name error before allocating inodes or mutating directory entries, across ext4 and btrfs create, mkdir, mknod, link, symlink, unlink/rmdir as applicable, and rename old/new components.

Reproduction direction:
Add regression tests that attempt create/link/symlink/rename using "." and ".." under both ext4 and btrfs test filesystems. Assert the operation fails and pre-existing source/directory state remains unchanged.
close_reason: Completed: central path-component validator rejects reserved dot names; ext4/btrfs mutation regressions and fuzz oracle updated

title: ffs-harness benches: BtrfsRaidProfile::from_chunk_type lacks Criterion benchmark
description:
Finding (via /profiling-software-performance skill, NEW target): crates/ffs-harness/benches/ondisk_parse.rs has 26 Criterion benchmarks but NONE measure BtrfsRaidProfile::from_chunk_type throughput. The classifier is on every read path on a multi-device btrfs filesystem (lookup_in_dir_block_casefold and friends choose a stripe based on profile classification).

The classifier has a 9-arm if/else cascade over RAID_MASK bits. Performance is interesting because:
  1. Single (no RAID bits set) — 9 short-circuit checks, all false
  2. Raid0 (first arm) — 1 check, succeeds
  3. Dup (second-to-last arm) — 8 checks before success
  4. Multi-bit pathological inputs — full cascade walked

Without a bench, a regression that swapped the order of arms (e.g., putting Single first via an early-return on raid_bits == 0) would silently slow the common Raid1/RAID10 cases. Pairs with bd-kansf (proptest MR), bd-luedn (libfuzzer >1M iter), and bd-rx88y (casefold benches) — same hot-path correctness/perf trio applied to RAID classification.

Acceptance: 4 Criterion benches in crates/ffs-harness/benches/ondisk_parse.rs:
  * bench_btrfs_raid_profile_single — Single (default, no RAID bits)
  * bench_btrfs_raid_profile_raid0 — Raid0 (first cascade arm)
  * bench_btrfs_raid_profile_dup — Dup (last cascade arm)
  * bench_btrfs_raid_profile_mixed — realistic mix across all 9 profiles

Each iterates over a small workload of representative chunk_type u64s with black_box on inputs.

title: Document FuseInner subsystem lock-ordering invariants

Pattern matches the existing struct-level lock-ordering docs on FuseInodeLocks (bd-pfv55), DegradationFsm (bd-2rxal), SnapshotRegistry (bd-7esyh), ShardedMvccStore (bd-bky2f), and PersistentMvccStore. Fix: add a struct-level doc comment to FuseInner that enumerates each subsystem lock, classifies each as leaf (kernel_notifier, access_predictor, readahead) or rank-0 (inode_locks), and asserts the no-cross-subsystem-nesting rule with a caller-method matrix matching the bd-pfv55 pattern.
