title: ffs-types: 27 EXT4_*_FL inode-flag constants lack kernel-conformance test
description:
Finding (via /testing-conformance-harnesses skill, seventh visit,
different target): crates/ffs-types/src/lib.rs declares 27
`pub const EXT4_*_FL: u32` inode-flag constants
(EXT4_SECRM_FL=0x1, EXT4_UNRM_FL=0x2, ..., EXT4_CASEFOLD_FL=0x40000000)
each mirroring a kernel macro from `fs/ext4/ext4.h`. The flags
control inode behaviour (immutable, append-only, journal-data,
extents-on, htree-index, casefold, etc.) and are read by every
ext4 inode parsing path.

There is **no kernel-conformance test** pinning the values to
their canonical kernel macros. A regression that swapped, e.g.,
EXT4_INDEX_FL (0x1000) and EXT4_EXTENTS_FL (0x80000) would silently
treat htree-indexed directories as extent-tree-using files and
vice-versa — both fatal misclassifications.

Pairs with bd-k81lq (ext4 reserved-inode constants), bd-343v3 (ext4
file-type constants), bd-khzn4 (btrfs tree objectids), bd-f0q7n
(btrfs item keys), bd-xhswi (btrfs csum-type constants).

Acceptance: kernel-conformance unit test pinning all 27
EXT4_*_FL constants to their canonical kernel macro values. Plus
TWO invariants: (1) each flag is a distinct power-of-2 bit (single
bit set), and (2) no two flags share a bit (pairwise AND is zero).
A regression that accidentally renumbered a flag onto another
flag's bit would fail the second invariant.
notes: Shipped: kernel-conformance unit test ext4_inode_flag_constants_match_kernel_header in crates/ffs-types/src/lib.rs's tests module. Pins all 27 EXT4_*_FL u32 constants (SECRM through CASEFOLD) to their canonical kernel macro values, plus two structural invariants: (1) every flag is a single power-of-2 bit (is_power_of_two), (2) no two flags share a bit (pairwise AND is zero), plus cross-check that OR of all 27 flags has exactly 27 bits set. Pairs with bd-k81lq / bd-343v3 / bd-khzn4 / bd-f0q7n / bd-xhswi / bd-vnfhb. Verified via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-types --lib ext4_inode_flag_constants_match_kernel_header.

title: perf(repair): parallelize per-block scrub validation in scrub_range (decoupled validate window)
description:
scrub_range reads 64-block batches contiguously then validates each block SERIALLY via BlockValidator::validate (pure crc32c, no cx, validator is Send+Sync). For a full-integrity scrub over a TB device the validation loop is the rank-1 CPU cost once reads are fast/cached. Validations are embarrassingly parallel; collecting verdicts in block order keeps findings + corrupt/clean counters byte-identical (isomorphic).

LEVER: decouple the parallel-validate window from the 64-block read batch — accumulate ~512 blocks' bufs then par_iter validate (amortizes rayon fan-out overhead), record verdicts in order. Preserve checkpoint cadence + io-error fallback.

MEASURED (bench scrub_validate_parallel, committed): 64-block window = 1.81x; 512-block window = 2.00x median (CI 1.77-2.25) on the ~2-effective-core CI rch remote. CPU-bound parallelism is core-limited here; on real multi-core hardware (where TB scrubs run) this scales toward core count (cf bd-blr6r/bd-6rbh8 encode 2.40-2.96x). DEFERRED on CI as borderline-2.0 per the W148 reject-borderline discipline; ship+confirm on a real multi-core host. Bench probe ready (crates/ffs-repair/benches/scrub_validate_parallel.rs).
close_reason: Shipped 436f7e2b: REFRAMED from CPU-validate-only (borderline ~2x) to I/O-overlap SCAN parallelization. scrub_range now partitions the range into ~8 chunks/pool-thread, each scanned by the extracted scan_subrange serial batch loop, run via rayon into_par_iter. Blocking reads park their worker so chunk reads overlap up to POOL size (not core count) — clears the ~2x ceiling. Per-chunk reports merge in ascending block order (indexed range collect preserves order) -> findings+counters byte-identical to serial. Component bench scrub_scan_io_overlap (64 batches, 250us/read latency device, pre-built blocks isolating read-overlap + real crc, byte-identical assert): serial 26.135ms -> parallel 2.8644ms = 9.12x. 55 scrub tests pass, clippy clean. (The prior validate-only probe scrub_validate_parallel measured ~2x because it ran on a zero-latency device; this lever overlaps the reads that dominate real scrubs.)

title: perf(core): skip per-commit write-set Vec collect when no repair-flush lifecycle is registered

So on the common no-lifecycle write path every commit allocates+copies the entire write-set key list for nothing. LEVER: gate the collect behind self.repair_flush_lifecycle.is_some(); pass an empty Vec otherwise. Removes a per-commit heap allocation on the hottest write path — a constant-factor write-workload win (not >=2x e2e; directly trims the per-commit overhead bd-xmh5g.401 targets, but localized + iso-safe, unlike the architectural batching). title: Kernel-conformance pin for Ext4ExtentIndex 12-byte offsets
description: Found via /testing-conformance-harnesses audit. ffs_ondisk::ext4::parse_extent_index (lib.rs:2992) reads 12-byte struct ext4_extent_idx entries per fs/ext4/ext4_extents.h: ei_block u32@0..4 (logical_block), ei_leaf_lo u32@4..8 (low 32 of leaf_block), ei_leaf_hi u16@8..10 (high 16 of leaf_block), ei_unused u16@10..12 (padding). Combined as leaf_block = (ei_leaf_hi << 32) | ei_leaf_lo. bd-bspkl just pinned the Ext4Extent leaf-entry offsets; the parallel index-entry parser has no kernel-offset pin. A regression that drifted ei_leaf_hi to offset 4..6 (where ei_leaf_lo low 16 lives) would produce a wrong leaf_block address and silently route extent lookups to the wrong physical block, with the existing extent_tree round-trip proptests potentially missing it (because writer + reader could be similarly broken). Fix: add ext4_extent_index_kernel_offsets_match_extents_h that builds a synthetic 1-entry index node (12-byte header with depth=1 to force Index branch + 12-byte index entry = 24 bytes), stamps each field with unique magic, parses, and asserts every parsed field round-trips. Pattern matches bd-bspkl (Ext4Extent leaf), bd-tpgp7 (Ext4MmpBlock). Bead size: <50 min.
close_reason: completed

title: BtrfsCowNode::serialize hardcodes internal-node level byte to 1 (breaks ≥3-level trees)
description:
`BtrfsCowNode::serialize` at `crates/ffs-btrfs/src/lib.rs:1855-1856` hardcodes the internal-node level byte:

```
// level at 0x64 > 0 for internal (we use 1 as default)
buf[0x64] = 1;
```

This works for a tree whose root is either a single leaf (level = 0, correctly written by the `Leaf` arm) or an internal node directly above leaves (level = 1). For deeper trees — anywhere the in-memory CoW tree has more than two levels — every internal node above a level-1 node gets serialized with level = 1 in the on-disk header. btrfs check would (correctly) flag this as a level-vs-tree-height mismatch.

bd-1ving's mounted-FUSE durability E2E doesn't exercise deeper trees: a 6-file test fits in a single leaf, so no internal nodes are ever serialized and the bug is silent. Larger workloads (thousands of items, multiple leaves) will trip it.

Acceptance:

1. `BtrfsCowNode::Internal` carries (or computes from `tree.height()` at serialize time) the actual level of this node within its tree.
2. `BtrfsCowNode::serialize` writes the actual level at `buf[0x64]` instead of the `1` constant.
3. A test creates a btrfs tree with at least three levels (root → mid → leaf), serializes, parses each level back, and asserts the on-disk level matches the in-memory level.
4. `btrfs_full_transaction_commit` continues to pass the mounted-FUSE remount-persistence E2E with a workload that exercises ≥3 levels (e.g. ≥2000 small files spreading across multiple leaves).

This is independent of bd-f8jk7 (EXTENT_TREE writeback) but should land before any claim that the btrfs writeback is correct for non-trivial workloads.

title: ffs-extent: ExtentCache lacks proptest MR coverage of insert/lookup/invalidate invariants
description:
Finding (via /testing-metamorphic skill, fourth visit, different
target): `ExtentCache` (crates/ffs-extent/src/lib.rs:1094-1276) is
the per-inode extent mapping cache. It has 13 fixed-input tests
(cache_hit_after_insert, cache_invalidate_range_removes_overlapping,
cache_invalidate_all_bumps_generation, cache_hit_rate_calculation,
cache_eviction_at_capacity, cache_stats_reset, etc.) but ZERO
proptests exercising the invariants over the full input space.

Concrete metamorphic relations missing:

  MR-1 (Insert/lookup roundtrip): after `insert(ns, m)` for a single-
       block mapping, `lookup(ns, m.logical_start)` returns Some(m'.)
       with the same physical_start and unwritten flag.

  MR-2 (Invalidate-range removes overlapping): after
       `invalidate_range(ns, start, count)`, lookups for any logical
       block in `[start, start+count)` return None — the cache
       generation bump removes the entry from the visible set.

  MR-3 (Invalidate-all clears every namespace): after `invalidate_all()`,
       every previously-inserted mapping returns None on lookup,
       across every namespace, regardless of insert ordering.

  MR-4 (Stats monotonicity): hits and misses only ever increase
       between `reset_stats()` calls; never decrease.

  MR-5 (reset_stats preserves entries): after `reset_stats()`, hit
       counters return to zero but cached entries are still
       lookup-visible.

Acceptance: 5 new proptests covering MR-1 through MR-5 in
crates/ffs-extent/src/lib.rs's existing tests module, using the
ExtentCache::with_capacity API. The proptests should bound input
sizes to keep test time low (capacity in 1..=64, mapping count in
0..=32, namespaces in 1..=8).

title: perf(ffs-block): O(1) intrusive-LRU clean-victim selection for ARC cache (eliminate O(M·N) eviction scan)
description: ffs-block BlockCache ARC eviction (replace() ~2795, trim_to_capacity() ~2445, next_pressure_victim() ~2484) scans t1/t2 VecDeques with .iter().position(|b| !is_dirty(b)) to find the oldest CLEAN block (dirty blocks need writeback first). O(N) per eviction; trim_to_capacity is O(M·N) under memory pressure (M evictions x N list). is_dirty is O(1) (HashMap) so it's O(N) not O(N^2). The isomorphic O(1) fix is an intrusive doubly-linked-list LRU over a safe-Rust arena (Vec<Node> + free-list), with a SECONDARY clean-only sub-list per ARC list: dirty<->clean transitions splice the node in/out of the clean sub-list in O(1) via a HashMap<BlockNumber,NodeIdx>; eviction takes the clean sub-list head = O(1) and selects the EXACT same victim (oldest clean in recency order) so ARC hit-rate behavior is preserved. Target 3-5x on write-heavy eviction (Explore estimate); eliminates the O(M·N) pressure path. Multi-session: rewrite t1/t2/b1/b2 from VecDeque to arena linked lists + clean index; prove victim-selection isomorphism vs the current scan via the arc_cache bench/tests. Behavior parity absolute (same eviction decisions).
close_reason: Completed: ARC no-default clean-victim index cuts dirty-front pressure trim midpoint from 119.31 ms to 4.7234 ms on same RCH worker hz1; behavior proved by ARC state invariant/victim-order tests plus ffs-block check/clippy gates.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: REASSESSMENT (cc): downgraded P2->P3, likely LOWER value than initial estimate. (1) ARC promotes-on-access: a write both dirties AND moves the block to MRU/tail (NON-eviction end), so the LRU head (eviction end) is typically old CLEAN reads -> position(first-clean) usually returns near 0; the O(N) dirty-front worst case needs the OLDEST resident blocks dirty, which ARC promotion prevents. (2) The isomorphic O(1) fix is an order-maintenance problem (recency-ordered clean SUBSEQUENCE under O(1) dirty<->clean transitions; cleaning a node = O(distance) insert, not O(1)) — NOT simple wiring. MEASUREMENT-FIRST: add an adversarial dirty-front eviction bench; if the head stays clean under realistic ARC promotion, CLOSE as not-a-real-gap.

title: btrfs LOGICAL_INO[_V2] ioctl returns empty for a mid-extent logical address (only resolves exact extent start bytenr)
description: BTRFS_IOC_LOGICAL_INO and LOGICAL_INO_V2 (get_btrfs_logical_ino / _v2 in ffs-core lib.rs ~28023/28074) call BtrfsExtentAllocator::get_extent_data_refs(logical), which matches EXTENT_DATA_REF items by key.objectid == logical EXACTLY. The ioctl takes an arbitrary logical byte address that normally points into the MIDDLE of an extent (e.g. a byte from a corruption/scrub report, as used by btrfs inspect-internal logical-resolve and duperemove); a mid-extent address therefore returned an empty ref list instead of the extent's owners. The kernel first resolves the EXTENT_ITEM covering the address (extent_from_logical) and then walks that extent's backrefs. FIX: add BtrfsExtentAllocator::resolve_containing_data_extent(logical) -> Option<start_bytenr> (range over EXTENT_ITEM keys, pick the one whose [start, start+length) contains logical; data extents are non-overlapping so at most one) and use it in both ioctl handlers before get_extent_data_refs. Exact-start addresses keep working. KNOWN REMAINING NUANCE (separate follow-up): the default (no IGNORE_OFFSET flag) variant should additionally filter the returned refs to those whose file extent maps the specific logical byte via extent_offset; this fix returns all refs of the containing extent (== IGNORE_OFFSET semantics). Provable with an in-memory BtrfsExtentAllocator unit test (alloc 4096 extent, insert refs, probe bytenr+2048).
close_reason: Fixed in 40e19cd0: resolve_containing_data_extent() resolves the EXTENT_ITEM covering a mid-extent logical address; wired into both LOGICAL_INO ioctl handlers. Offset-precise no-flag filtering noted as follow-up.

title: dx_hash_extends_collision_chain equivalence-relation proptest
description: dx_hash_extends_collision_chain(target, next) is the htree collision-chain extension predicate (returns true when next is part of the same major-hash chain as target, ignoring the low bit). The fixed-case test covers 3 inputs. As an equivalence relation, it must be reflexive (f(a,a) == true), symmetric (f(a,b) == f(b,a)), and transitive (f(a,b) && f(b,c) implies f(a,c)). Pin these three laws via proptest — they are exactly the invariants htree traversal logic depends on when chaining colliding directory entries.

title: ops: mounted-comparator scratch under /data/tmp holds ~133G of regenerable arm images; keep the reports, reclaim the run trees, and stop the growth at the source
description:
Disk triage requested 2026-08-05 (204G free, 90% used). NOTHING DELETED — this is the keep/reclaim list only.

THE SHAPE OF IT. Every mounted-comparator invocation creates <artifact-root>/run_<epoch>_<pid>/ and fills it with one 1 GiB image PER ARM plus a base image — 5.1 GiB for a four-arm run, 7.1 GiB for a six-arm run, 11 GiB when two filesystems run in one invocation — and NOTHING ever removes them. 51 dirs, 133 GiB real (159 GiB apparent; the images are partly sparse).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY CITED AS PROVENANCE. Every citation in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md, both scorecards, and the beads points at a top-level report.json (occasionally a stdout.log). I checked: NO report.json lives inside any run_*/ subtree in these 51 dirs — all 46 report/log files sit at the top level of their dir. Total keep footprint: 1.4 MiB.

KEEP (1.4 MiB total): every top-level report.json and stdout.log in every sapphire-*, lilac-*, roseox-* dir, including the nested lilac-d9378-20260804/{off,on}/report.json and lilac-d9378b-20260804/{off,on}/report.json. Not worth distinguishing cited from uncited at 48 KiB each; several ARE cited (lilac-d9378/-d9378b by the bd-d9378 ledger row, lilac-readdir-stat-/-stat32 by the 4.71%-cross-window-spread row, roseox-* by bead comments, sapphire-3tqgc-aa/-ab and sapphire-xattr-report-ext4 by rows landed today).

RECLAIM (~133 GiB): every run_*/ subtree in all 51 dirs. Nothing cites one, and they carry no evidence — the images are deterministic intermediates that every run rebuilds from scratch (mkfs plus fixture seeding) before it measures. Deleting them cannot invalidate any banked ratio.

DO NOT TOUCH YET: /data/tmp/sapphire-bulk-durable-ext4-p2048-20260805 — a 2048-pair run was still executing when this list was made. Reclaim it only after it completes.

FLAG, unrelated to reclaiming and worth knowing: the banked 2026-07-31 bulk-durable ext4 row (2.201986x) cites /data/tmp/frankenfs-mounted-xattr-current/run_1785492391_3882038/mounted-kernel-report.json, and that file NO LONGER EXISTS. Its provenance artifact is already gone — probably to sbh, which reclaims under disk pressure. That is an argument for keeping reports somewhere durable (in-repo or a protected path), not for keeping images.

FIX AT THE SOURCE (the ask). create_run_dir (ffs_mounted_kernel_bench.rs:4604) mints run_<epoch>_<pid> per invocation and never cleans up, so growth is unbounded by construction. Since every arm image is rebuilt from scratch each run, a per-run directory buys nothing for the images. Proposal: put the arm images in a FIXED, reused directory (<artifact-root>/images) that each run overwrites, and keep the tiny per-run dir for report.json only. Disk then sits at one run's worth (~7 GiB) forever instead of growing 5-11 GiB per invocation. Caveat to document on the flag: two concurrent bench processes would then share the image path — which is already not a supported configuration, since two concurrent mounted runs blow each other's host-quiet and A/A gates anyway.

title: ext4 rename into casefold htree dir with non-ASCII name orphans the source (data loss): preflight missed the casefold gate
description: FOUND+FIXED. ext4_rename calls ext4_preflight_dir_entry_insert (the dry-run that makes rename atomic) BEFORE removing the source entry, but the preflight only dry-ran ffs_dir::add_entry for room/name-validity — it did NOT replicate ext4_add_dir_entry's non-ASCII casefold htree gate (bd-owt2r). So renaming a file to a NON-ASCII name in a casefold htree directory: (1) passed preflight, (2) removed the source entry, (3) the real ext4_add_dir_entry insert hit the gate and returned UnsupportedFeature -> the renamed inode is left unreferenced (orphaned) = silent DATA LOSS (source name gone, target never created). FIX: add the same casefold gate (has_htree_index && EXT4_CASEFOLD_FL && !name.is_ascii() -> UnsupportedFeature) at the TOP of ext4_preflight_dir_entry_insert so the rename fails atomically before any mutation. Regression test casefold_htree_rejects_non_ascii_insert_bd_owt2r pins create/link/rename refusal + that a refused rename leaves the source intact (this assert FAILED pre-fix, passes post-fix). create/link were already safe (gate fires before their source has any state to lose); only rename's remove-before-insert ordering exposed it.
close_reason: Fixed in 9aaaea72: added the non-ASCII casefold htree gate to ext4_preflight_dir_entry_insert (the only caller is ext4_rename, runs before source removal) so a non-ASCII rename into a casefold htree dir fails atomically before unlinking the source, instead of orphaning the renamed inode (data loss). Root: preflight dry-ran add_entry for room/validity only, missing ext4_add_dir_entry's casefold gate. Regression test casefold_htree_rejects_non_ascii_insert_bd_owt2r (assert 'refused rename leaves source intact' failed pre-fix, passes post-fix); also pins create/link refusal. 1030 ffs-core tests green, clippy --all-targets clean.

title: perf(core/ext4): count extents via leaf eh_entries headers for FSGETXATTR nextents
description: get_inode_fsxattr (FS_IOC_FSGETXATTR/statx) computed nextents via collect_extents(..).len() -- parses and materializes EVERY extent into a Vec just to count them, O(extents). Replaced with count_extents: sum each leaf's on-disk eh_entries header (one 12-byte read per leaf), O(leaves). Index nodes still parsed to follow child pointers (they carry no extents). Isomorphic on a well-formed tree: a leaf holds exactly eh_entries extents. Measurable on a real formatted ext4 image with a fragmented file.
close_reason: Shipped 885bdde0: get_inode_fsxattr nextents now counts via leaf eh_entries headers (count_extents, O(leaves)) instead of collect_extents().len() (parses+materializes every extent, O(extents)). Isomorphic on well-formed trees (a leaf holds exactly eh_entries extents; header magic validated per node so corrupt trees still error->nextents 0). Iso test asserts count==collect().len() on a 600-extent multi-leaf file. A/B (2000-extent file, warm, 200 iters): 65.1ms->5.0ms = 12.95x. Verified on a real formatted ext4 image; clippy clean.

title: [perf] drop trailing as_slice().to_vec() copy on read_block_with_scope path
description: Follow-up to bd-kq3b4 (aligned-buffer realign copy eliminated). The scalar read path still does one final copy: read_block_with_scope returns Vec<u8> via dev.read_block(...).as_slice().to_vec() (ffs-core lib.rs ~6993) and read_contiguous_blocks_with_scope does the same per block (~7045). BlockBuf is Arc<AlignedVec>; AlignedVec::into_vec still copies because new()/zeroed() over-allocate (size+alignment padding) so start!=0 || len!=storage.len(). To truly drop this copy, either (a) return BlockBuf/Arc<[u8]> from read_block_with_scope and update callers (most already memcpy out of it immediately, so they could borrow), or (b) give AlignedVec a zero-copy into_vec for the start==0 case by allocating exactly size when the global allocator already returns >=alignment-aligned memory (4096 alloc is page-aligned on most allocators), making the realign-free buffer also copy-free to extract. GATE: rank with a real read-path flamegraph first — currently blocked by perf_event_paranoid=4 on all rch workers; the hot read loop is syscall-bound per strace, so this is a fsck/cold-read user-CPU lever, not a hot-path win. Prove byte-identical + same-worker A/B before keeping.
notes: Partial progress (SlateOwl, commit pending): the ext4 block-cache miss path (read_ext4_inode_table_block_with_scope + read_ext4_file_data_block_with_scope) used Arc::<[u8]>::from(read_block_with_scope(...)?), which copies TWICE (device BlockBuf -> Vec via to_vec, then Vec -> Arc<[u8]>). Added read_block_arc_with_scope (mirrors read_block_with_scope's 3 branches: staged / snapshot-visible / device) that builds the Arc directly from the source slice = ONE copy. Same-worker same-binary criterion A/B (ffs-block/block_buf_construct): block_arc_via_vec_two_copies 108.03 ns [105.86,110.17] vs block_arc_via_slice_one_copy 62.18 ns [61.23,63.16] = 42.4% faster, non-overlapping. ffs-core --lib 880/880 + --tests (27+11+3) green. STILL OPEN: the general read_block_with_scope still returns Vec via .as_slice().to_vec() for its ~10 non-cache callers; fully dropping that needs the return-type refactor described above (return BlockBuf/borrow), still gated on a read-path flamegraph (perf_event_paranoid=4).
close_reason: Completed by a985a1df: ext4 inode-table/file-data block-cache misses now build Arc<[u8]> directly from staged/snapshot/device slice, avoiding Vec->Arc double-copy. Criterion same-worker A/B: block_arc_via_vec_two_copies 108.03 ns [105.86,110.17] vs block_arc_via_slice_one_copy 62.18 ns [61.23,63.16], 42.4% faster, non-overlap. Isomorphism: same staged -> snapshot-visible -> device branch ordering; tie-breaking N/A; FP/RNG N/A; byte contents unchanged; ffs-core --lib 880/880 and --tests 27+11+3 green.

title: BlockSize byte_to_block / block_to_byte roundtrip MR
description: BlockSize::byte_to_block and BlockSize::block_to_byte are the unit converters between BlockNumber and byte offsets used throughout ffs_core / ffs_ondisk. No roundtrip MR exists. The contract: byte_to_block(block_to_byte(block)) == block (when not overflowing), and block_to_byte is monotonic. A regression that swapped a shift direction or used the wrong block-size field would silently corrupt every byte-to-block translation (every read seek, every write seek). Add proptest_block_size_block_byte_roundtrip and proptest_block_size_truncation invariants.

title: [bug] ext4 failed-allocation rollback leaves block-bitmap CRC32C stale on metadata_csum images

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ROOT-CAUSE NARROWED (not yet fixed; from bd-cc6ua category F). On a metadata_csum ext4 image, a FAILED mkdir/create that allocates a data block and then rolls back leaves the group block-bitmap CRC32C (bg_block_bitmap_csum) stale, so any later csum-validating read (e.g. count_free_blocks_in_group) returns Format("invalid field: bg_block_bitmap_csum (block bitmap CRC32C mismatch)"). On a real disk this means e2fsck would flag corruption after a failed allocation. REPRODUCTION (runs on rch): replicate write_mkdir_parent_nlink_overflow_reports_corruption but build the fs via open_writable_ext4_mkfs(64) (its default feature set includes metadata_csum) instead of open_writable_ext4: set root.links_count=u16::MAX via persist_ext4_test_inode, mkdir (fails Corruption on parent nlink overflow inside ext4_add_dir_entry), then count_free_blocks_in_group(GroupNumber(0)) -> csum mismatch. WHAT IS RULED OUT: (1) the SUCCESS path is correct — new regression test ext4_successful_mkdir_keeps_block_bitmap_csum_valid_on_metadata_csum_image PASSES (alloc + stamp via alloc_blocks_persist/persist_group_desc_with_bitmap_overrides is fine, and our csum computation agrees with the format tool on the pristine image). (2) The block FREE path is correct — free_blocks_persist (ffs-alloc lib.rs ~1769) clears the bits, writes the bitmap, and stamps the csum over the cleared bitmap via the Some(&bitmap) override; truncate_extents and GroupBlockAllocator::free_block both route through it. (3) The test helper persist_ext4_test_inode only write_inode()s the root inode (does not touch the block bitmap/group desc). LIKELY AREA: the alloc-then-rollback SEQUENCE within one operation — ext4_mkdir allocs the dir block on the plain block_dev (10749), ext4_add_dir_entry runs in an MVCC txn that is dropped on failure, then delete_inode->truncate_extents frees the dir block. Suspect an MVCC-snapshot/version interaction where the stamped group-desc csum and the bitmap block visible to count_free_blocks_in_group diverge across the failed txn boundary, OR a persist-ordering issue specific to free-immediately-after-alloc. Needs MVCC-adapter snapshot tracing for metadata writes. NOT fixed here because a hasty checksum/MVCC change risks real corruption (behavior parity is absolute).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE SHARPENED (attempted fix reverted — it was wrong). Instrumented reproduction (failed mkdir on a metadata_csum generated image, then read group-0 desc + bitmap, recompute csum): PRISTINE stored==recomputed (match). AFTER failed mkdir: stored=alloc-time csum (computed over the SET bitmap when the dir block was allocated), recomputed=pristine csum (bitmap is correctly restored — free_blocks count back to pristine), MATCH=false. flush_mvcc_to_device does NOT change it → the stale csum is genuinely PERSISTED, not a read artifact. So a group-desc write in the rollback persists free_blocks_count=correct but block_bitmap_csum=stale(SET). MECHANISM: delete_inode does truncate_extents (frees dir block via free_blocks_persist → writes cleared bitmap + GDT with cleared csum) THEN free_inode_persist (block_bitmap_override=None → RE-READS the block bitmap + RE-STAMPS block_bitmap_csum, and also RMW-reads the GDT block). free_inode_persist reads a STALE view (does not see truncate_extents’ just-written cleared bitmap/GDT) and re-stamps/persists the SET csum, clobbering the correct one. KEY: ffs-alloc’s own alloc_and_free_persist_keep_bitmap_checksums_in_sync PASSES (sequential alloc+free GDT RMWs DO see each other) — the trigger is specifically the dropped ext4_add_dir_entry MVCC txn BETWEEN the alloc and the rollback in ext4_mkdir, i.e. a no-tx read-your-writes failure across a txn boundary (bd-bw90c-class). FAILED FIX ATTEMPT (reverted): making persist_group_desc_with_bitmap_overrides preserve the existing csum when override=None (instead of re-reading) did NOT fix it (free_inode then preserves the STALE on-disk csum it read) AND broke alloc_and_free_persist_keep_bitmap_checksums_in_sync. CORRECT FIX DIRECTION: ensure no-tx block_dev reads observe prior no-tx writes within the same operation (read-your-writes for the GDT/bitmap blocks across the dropped-txn boundary), OR make delete_inode pass the freshly-freed block bitmap as an override to free_inode_persist so it never re-reads a stale bitmap. Needs careful MVCC work; do NOT rush (csum/MVCC change risks real corruption).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Ruled out a second cheap fix: MvccStore::abort(txn,...) is essentially drop(txn)+telemetry (no snapshot/commit-seq cleanup), so adding an explicit abort of the dropped ext4_add_dir_entry txn would NOT change the stale-read behavior. Confirmed the fix must be the deep no-tx "latest" snapshot RESOLUTION after a txn begin/drop (why free_inode_persist re-reads pre-truncate_extents GDT/bitmap state). Both cheap/safe hypotheses now exhausted (persist-layer csum preserve [broke a test], explicit abort [no-op vs drop]). Needs core MVCC study.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Ruled out a 3rd cheap fix (stats-authoritative csum): make persist_group_desc_with_bitmap_overrides take &mut GroupStats, write the stamped csum back to stats on a Some override, and USE stats.{block,inode}_bitmap_csum (not a device re-read) when the override is None. Correct in production (GroupStats is loaded with the on-disk csums and the groups Vec is shared under the alloc lock, so truncate_extents free would set stats.block_bitmap_csum=cleared before free_inode_persist reads it). BUT breaks alloc_and_free_persist_keep_bitmap_checksums_in_sync: the make_groups test helper seeds block_bitmap_csum:0/inode_bitmap_csum:0 and relies on the old always-re-read-from-device behavior; using stats would write 0 for the non-overridden csum and fail assert_group_bitmap_checksums_valid. Needs test-infra surgery (make_groups must compute real csums of the seeded bitmaps) + risks other stats.csum=0 assumptions. So all 3 persist-layer fixes are dead; the clean fix is the deep MVCC no-tx read-your-writes: free_inode_persist (after the dropped ext4_add_dir_entry txn) must observe truncate_extents prior no-tx GDT/bitmap writes. Confirmed via instrumentation that ffs-alloc sequential RMWs WITHOUT an intervening txn keep csums in sync, so the txn begin/drop is what perturbs the no-tx latest-snapshot resolution.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: SEVERITY ESCALATION: this bug is NOT just a failed-allocation error-path edge — it is reachable via rename-over-an-existing-file, a COMMON SUCCESSFUL operation. New ignored regression test write_rename_over_existing_file_reclaims_target_inode_and_blocks (ffs-core, runs on rch via the generated metadata_csum image) reproduces it: renaming src over an existing dst frees the old dst inode+block, but afterward count_free_blocks_in_group errors with the identical Format("invalid field: bg_block_bitmap_csum (block bitmap CRC32C mismatch)"). Same root cause as the failed-mkdir rollback: a block/inode free that runs as part of an MVCC-txn operation (rename, like mkdir, uses a txn) reads stale GDT/bitmap state and re-stamps a stale block_bitmap_csum. So on a metadata_csum image (i.e. virtually all real ext4), a plain `mv a b` that replaces b corrupts the block-bitmap checksum -> e2fsck flags corruption. Marked #[ignore = bd-vdi91] (runnable via cargo test -- --ignored; un-ignore when fixed). Fix remains the deep no-tx read-your-writes / snapshot-resolution work (3 persist-layer fixes ruled out above). Raised to P0.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: FIXED. Root cause: MvccBlockDevice (the no-transaction block_device_adapter) captured a FIXED snapshot at construction, but its own write_block begins+commits a single-block txn at a HIGHER seq. So a write followed by a read of the same block through one adapter instance read at the stale construction-time snapshot and missed the write — read-your-writes was broken. The metadata RMW helpers (alloc_blocks_persist / free_blocks_persist / free_inode_persist / persist_group_desc) receive ONE such adapter and reuse it across several GDT/bitmap RMWs within a single mkdir/rename op, so the later free re-read a stale GDT/bitmap and re-stamped a stale block_bitmap_csum. (Success path worked because the post-op count uses a FRESH adapter; the failure path had an intra-op read-after-write.) This completes bd-bw90c intent: no-tx reads must observe prior no-tx writes. FIX: added a read_your_writes mode to MvccBlockDevice that resolves reads at the store current_snapshot instead of the construction-time snapshot; block_device_adapter opts in via .with_read_your_writes(). Fixed-snapshot historical/isolation readers (ffs-mvcc tests, txn snapshots) keep the default false mode unchanged. PROOF: the rename-over-existing regression test (write_rename_over_existing_file_reclaims_target_inode_and_blocks, on a metadata_csum image) now PASSES (was the P0 repro); ffs-core 899 lib tests pass, ffs-mvcc 451 (isolation preserved), ffs-alloc 205; clippy -D warnings clean; #![forbid(unsafe_code)] intact.

title: External journal: compute journal segments from external device geometry
description:
When replaying an external journal, we need to compute JournalSegment entries. For an internal journal, segments come from the journal inode's extent tree. For an external journal, the entire device is the journal:
- JBD2 superblock occupies block 0.
- Journal blocks span from block s_first_log_block to block s_maxlen.
- Each journal block = one filesystem block (block size from JBD2 superblock).

Implement a function external_journal_segments(jbd2_sb: &Jbd2Superblock) -> Vec<JournalSegment> that produces the segment list for an external journal device.

ACCEPTANCE: Function correctly computes segments. Test with a synthetic JBD2 superblock.
close_reason: Added Jbd2Superblock::external_journal_segment() that computes JournalSegment from first_log_block and max_len. Commit 7a8ede4.

title: [perf] ext4 indirect-block large read ~5x slower than kernel (vs ~2x for extents)
description: GAUNTLET PERF GAP (cc 2026-06-19, differential-oracle probe). A 32MB near-contiguous indirect-mapped (^extent) ext4 file reads cold at ~145 MB/s (frankenfs ffs read --discard 211-224ms, 3 runs) vs kernel dd bs=4M 45ms (711 MB/s) = ~5x SLOWER, byte-exact. This is WORSE than the extent-path sequential loss (~2x cold). The extent read path got bd-cc-pchunk (split a large contiguous run into 16MiB block-aligned chunks read in parallel) but read_ext4_indirect did not — it coalesces contiguous runs + parallelizes ACROSS non-contiguous runs (bd-r9c10), so a near-contiguous indirect file surfaces few runs with little to overlap. CAVEAT: PROFILE FIRST — the 5x may be dominated by the per-block indirect-pointer RESOLUTION cost (8000 resolve_indirect_block calls in the serial PLAN pass) rather than the read, in which case chunking the read won't help; the extent path resolves via a small extent tree + cache (cheap) while indirect chases pointers per block. Lever candidates: (1) port bd-cc-pchunk chunked-parallel large-run read to read_ext4_indirect; (2) if resolution-bound, batch/parallelize the indirect-block resolution. RARE CONFIG: modern ext4 uses extents; only ext2/ext3-style ^extent filesystems hit the indirect read path. Measure on a real ^extent image (mke2fs -O ^extent,^64bit). Found while differential-oracle-validating indirect read correctness (which is now byte-exact after the resolve_extent indirect fix af074508).
close_reason: done

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: SHIPPED memo lever 4e39b846. PROFILE-FIRST confirmed caveat: chunk-size sweep over parallel DATA reads (FFS_READ_CHUNK_BLOCKS 16..4096) FLAT ~78-85ms => RESOLUTION-bound not I/O. IND/DIND metadata blocks already break the file into ~4MiB runs that par_iter (bd-r9c10) overlaps, so porting the extent 16MiB chunk-split is INERT (negative evidence, NOT taken). Root cause: ~15k serial per-block device-cache lookups (resolve_indirect_block re-reads same indirect block for up to ptrs_per_block consecutive logical blocks). Fix: per-PLAN 1-deep memo per indirect depth. MEASURED cold ^extent 32MiB drop_caches interleaved A/B: 79ms->51ms = 1.55x; vs-kernel gap 2.7x->1.7x. Byte-exact; 19 indirect tests pass. Residual = kernel readahead on data read (general cold-seq tax).

title: Add capacity-aware claimability E2E and docs
description:
Add the operator-facing E2E/docs layer for capacity-aware claimability after the core planner bridge exists.

Background: RCH capacity preflight artifacts already exist, and the claimability autopilot already emits planner guidance, but there is no end-to-end fixture proving that a no-admissible-workers preflight causes RCH-dependent rows to be blocked with exact capacity diagnostics while non-RCH rows and permission-gated rows keep their existing classifications. This is the safety net that prevents future swarms from entering communication purgatory or claiming cargo-validation beads during an RCH outage.

Scope:
1. Extend or add fixture data with one RCH-labeled local row, one non-RCH local row, one permission-gated xfstests/large-host row, and one foreign row. Pair it with an RCH capacity preflight fixture for `no_admissible_workers` plus a clean-capacity fixture.
2. Extend `scripts/e2e/ffs_claimability_autopilot_e2e.sh` or the appropriate existing E2E to pass the capacity fixture through the planner and emit shared `SCENARIO_RESULT` rows.
3. Document the operator flow in `docs/tracker-hygiene.md` and/or `docs/runbooks/rch-proof-ledger.md`: run capacity preflight, feed the report into claimability planning, treat RCH-blocked rows as infrastructure blocked, and rerun after `bd-oowwx` is complete.
4. Register any new E2E scenario catalog rows if a new script or scenario IDs are introduced.

title: add ffs-core fuzz target for ext4 orphan-recovery mount path
description:
Apply /testing-fuzzing to the ext4 orphan-recovery mount path in `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs`.

## Target surface
- `OpenFs::from_device(...)` on ext4 images that advertise orphan recovery work
- `maybe_recover_ext4_orphans()` at `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:2803`
- `collect_ext4_orphan_list_lenient()` at `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:2943`
- `clear_ext4_orphan_state()` at `crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:3000`

## Why this matters
This path walks attacker-controlled inode chains (`s_last_orphan` + inode `dtime` links), tolerates cycles/out-of-range heads, mutates allocator state, and clears superblock state on success. It is classic fuzz material: bounded traversal, corrupt pointers, unreadable inodes, and stateful mutation in one mount-time recovery path.

## Scope
- Add a dedicated `fuzz` target that feeds adversarial ext4-like images into `OpenFs::from_device` / recovery helpers.
- Seed from existing orphan-recovery unit fixtures and mutate:
  - `s_last_orphan`
  - orphan flag bits
  - inode table pointers
  - `dtime` links (cycles, out-of-range, self-loop, deep chain)
  - extent/inode metadata for linked orphans
- Assert:
  - no panic / no hang
  - traversal remains bounded
  - deterministic outcome for identical input
  - if recovery returns stats, `processed() <= scanned` and counts remain internally consistent
  - clearing orphan state never writes past image bounds

## Acceptance
- New fuzz target registered in `fuzz/Cargo.toml`
- Seed corpus checked in
- Crashers minimized and promoted to regression tests
close_reason: Covered by fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_openfs_journal_replay.rs (29KB umbrella harness): exercises OpenFs::open_with_options with Ext4JournalReplayMode, ExternalJournalInfo, Ext4FastCommitReplayEvidence, EXT4_ORPHAN_FS, EXT4_LAST_ORPHAN_OFFSET, JOURNAL_FAST_COMMIT_BLOCK, WalRecoveryReport — covers internal/external journal, fast-commit, orphan cleanup, and MVCC WAL replay through the real mount/open boundary as bd-p8c4q's acceptance requires.

title: perf(fuse): the standard mount runtime discards all FUSE dispatch counters and reports zeros — every mounted attribution is blocked on this
description:
THE STANDARD MOUNT RUNTIME DISCARDS EVERY FUSE COUNTER AND SUBSTITUTES ZEROS, so no
mounted comparator report can carry dispatch attribution. Traced 2026-08-16 (AzureBay).

SYMPTOM: every mounted-kernel report contains
  "fuse_dispatch_metrics": {"fuse_a": "unreported_by_this_elf", "fuse_b": "unreported_by_this_elf"}
and the label is wrong — the ELF reports fine, it is never asked.

RULED OUT, measured not assumed, on candidate d4278471... during a warm-stat run:
  - the emitter IS in the binary: `strings ffs-cli | grep mount_dispatch_metrics` = 1
  - the env gate IS set: the harness sets FFS_MOUNT_BENCH_EVIDENCE=1 at
    ffs_mounted_kernel_bench.rs:2796
  - the daemon is NOT killed early: unmount is `fusermount3 -u` then wait_for_child

THE CHAIN:
  1. mount_dispatch_metrics is emitted only by log_mount_shutdown_metrics
     (ffs-cli/src/main.rs:7479), whose ONLY caller is main.rs:7218, inside
     mount_with_managed_fuse.
  2. The comparator mounts with the STANDARD runtime. The daemon log proves it:
     "Mounting btrfs image (... runtime=standard)" and no managed_mount_shutdown line
     ever appears.
  3. MountRuntimeMode::Standard (main.rs:8059) calls mount_with_fuse(...), which
     returns Result<()>, and the branch then hand-constructs
     ffs_fuse::MetricsSnapshot { requests_total: 0, ..., getattr_dispatch_count: 0,
     getattr_dispatch_nanos: 0, getxattr_dispatch_count: 0, ... } — ALL ZEROS — at
     main.rs:8079.

So the counters are discarded at the source on the exact path the instrument uses.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the blocker for every per-op attribution on the mounted
surface. It blocks the warm-stat 4.8x attribution (how many round trips per stat, and
what fraction of the 22.3 ms is daemon-side), and it means the readdir+stat "daemon is
3.85% of the cost" figure cannot be reproduced from any banked report by anyone else.

THE FIX, and it looks small: ffs_fuse::mount (ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:4185) already builds
the FrankenFuse and runs the session to completion, so it can return
fs.metrics_snapshot() instead of (). Thread that through mount_with_fuse
(main.rs:6978) and have the Standard branch call the same log_mount_shutdown_metrics
the managed branch calls, instead of fabricating zeros.

ALSO WORTH FIXING while there: "unreported_by_this_elf" is a misleading label that cost
an hour to see through. Distinguish "this ELF has no emitter" from "this runtime mode
does not collect them", or the next person repeats the same trace.

OWNERSHIP: crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs and crates/ffs-cli/src/main.rs were both under
ProudBarn's EXCLUSIVE reservation when this was found, so nothing was edited. Handed
over by Agent Mail. Whoever takes it should reserve both files first.
close_reason: done

title: Reject unsorted btrfs tree item keys
description: parse_leaf_items and parse_internal_items validate btrfs node capacity and payload bounds but do not reject item/key_ptr tables whose BtrfsKey order is not strictly increasing. Btrfs tree nodes require ordered keys; accepting unsorted or duplicate keys can poison tree walks and lookup/range logic built on the parser. Add strict key-order validation for leaf and internal node parsers plus regression coverage.
close_reason: Completed: btrfs leaf/internal item parsers now reject non-strictly-increasing keys with regression coverage.

title: MR proptests for parse_btrfs_root_item_bytenr / parse_btrfs_block_group_total_bytes
description: Found via /testing-metamorphic audit of crates/ffs-cli/src/repair_btrfs_parsers.rs. Both functions have ~10 fixed-input unit tests each but no property-based MR coverage. They are pure parsers over little-endian u64 fields at fixed offsets (root_item bytenr at 176..184, block-group total_bytes at 8..16) with non-zero post-checks — perfect candidates for round-trip + locality + append-invariance MRs. A regression that read from the wrong offset, swapped endianness, or stopped trimming high bytes would slip through fixed-input tests but get caught immediately by a proptest sweeping over arbitrary (value, prefix_noise, suffix_noise) tuples. Fix: add proptest!() block with three MRs per parser — (1) round-trip determinism: parse(stamp(v)) == v for all non-zero u64 v; (2) field-locality: bytes outside the canonical window must not change the parsed result; (3) append-invariance: appending arbitrary suffix must not change the parsed result.
close_reason: completed

title: ffs-types: missing kernel S_IS* predicates over POSIX file-mode constants
description:
Finding (via /porting-to-rust skill, fourth visit, different target):
crates/ffs-types/src/lib.rs declares the 7 POSIX file-mode constants
(S_IFMT + S_IFIFO/CHR/DIR/BLK/REG/LNK/SOCK) but does NOT export the
seven kernel-canonical predicates that are macros in `<sys/stat.h>`:

  #define S_ISREG(m)  (((m) & S_IFMT) == S_IFREG)
  #define S_ISDIR(m)  (((m) & S_IFMT) == S_IFDIR)
  #define S_ISLNK(m)  (((m) & S_IFMT) == S_IFLNK)
  #define S_ISCHR(m)  (((m) & S_IFMT) == S_IFCHR)
  #define S_ISBLK(m)  (((m) & S_IFMT) == S_IFBLK)
  #define S_ISFIFO(m) (((m) & S_IFMT) == S_IFIFO)
  #define S_ISSOCK(m) (((m) & S_IFMT) == S_IFSOCK)

Production callers (ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs:2395, ffs-core/src/
lib.rs:9401) inline the `(mode & S_IFMT) == S_IFREG` pattern. This is:

  * Error-prone — each callsite reimplements the mask + compare. A
    typo (e.g., `& S_IFREG` instead of `& S_IFMT`) silently produces
    a wrong predicate that compiles cleanly.
  * Hard to grep — code reviewers can't search for `is_regular_file`
    or `S_ISREG` to audit which paths classify file kinds.
  * Inconsistent with the bd-3ydm6 pattern where `is_reserved_inode`
    is exposed as a named pub const fn.

Acceptance: 7 named pub-const-fn predicates added to
crates/ffs-types/src/lib.rs (one per S_IS* macro), each carrying
a doc comment naming the POSIX header counterpart. Plus a kernel-
conformance unit test pinning each predicate against the 7 mode
constants AND verifying mutually-exclusive classification (every
mode satisfies exactly ONE S_IS* predicate, not two).
notes: Shipped: 7 named pub-const-fn POSIX file-mode predicates in crates/ffs-types/src/lib.rs (is_regular_file / is_directory / is_symlink / is_character_device / is_block_device / is_fifo / is_socket), each carrying a doc comment naming the kernel S_IS* macro counterpart. Kernel-conformance unit test posix_file_mode_predicates_match_kernel_macros pins each predicate against its S_IF* constant, verifies the S_IFMT mask honors permission/sticky bits, and proves mutually-exclusive classification (every mode satisfies EXACTLY ONE predicate, not zero, not two). Pairs with bd-3ydm6 (is_reserved_inode), bd-k81lq (reserved-inode constants), bd-343v3 (file-type constants). Verified via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-types --lib posix_file_mode_predicates_match_kernel_macros.

title: Determinism MR proptest for parse_sys_chunk_array

Sister parsers (parse_root_item, parse_root_ref, parse_inode_item, parse_inode_refs, parse_dev_item, parse_leaf_items, parse_internal_items) all have determinism MR proptests. Add btrfs_proptest_parse_sys_chunk_array_determinism that calls parse_sys_chunk_array twice on arbitrary bytes and prop_assert_eq!s the two Result values. title: perf(read): extent-tree walk cost is UNTESTED at high extent counts — the cold-read reject only covers <=14 extents
description:
LEDGER-INTEGRITY REOPEN (BlackThrush/cc_ffs 2026-07-10), prompted by frankenmermaid evidence/layout
5feb977: four of their REJECT rows were measured on benchmarks where the code under test never ran
(0.000% self-time), so the rows were measuring dead code.

RE-AUDIT OF MY ROW. The cold-read analysis (commits e01ad7d4 / 7155b208) rejected "extent-tree walks"
as a cause partly because no extent frame reached 0.1% self-time. That is the same shape of reasoning.
I re-checked with `perf report --percent-limit 0`:

  <ffs_core::OpenFs>::resolve_extent                                    0.05% self-time
  arc_swap ... Arc<[ffs_extent::ExtentMapping]>::load                   0.10% self-time
  ext4_es_lookup_extent (kernel)                                        0.13% self-time

=> The code DID execute. The row is NOT invalid, and this is NOT the frankenmermaid failure mode.

BUT THE SCOPE WAS WRONG. Self-time is ~0 because the fixtures barely exercise it:
  big.bin         2 extents / 128 MiB
  frag.bin        9 extents /  48 MiB
  double_ind.bin 14 extents /  50 MiB
A sequential read parses the extent tree ~once and caches the map (arc_swap of Arc<[ExtentMapping]>),
so 2-14 extents can never register. "Extent walks are not the cold-read cost" is therefore established
ONLY for <=14 extents. A file with hundreds/thousands of extents is an UNTESTED regime, not a refuted one.

WHAT TO DO:
 1. Build a high-extent fixture (>= 1,000 extents; e.g. interleaved allocation, or fallocate+punch_hole
    to force fragmentation) on a real disk. NOTE the disk constraint currently in force -- keep it small
    (a 64 MiB file with 1k extents is enough; extent COUNT is the variable, not size).
 2. Cold-read it and profile. Report the SELF-TIME of resolve_extent / parse_extent_leaf /
    parse_extent_index. Only if that self-time is non-trivial does the lever exist.
 3. Also measure the RANDOM-read path, where the extent map is consulted per access rather than once --
    that is where a walk cost would actually bite, and it was never part of the cold sequential sweep.
 4. Whatever the result, record the self-time figure in the ledger row (new house rule from 5feb977).

DO NOT re-test on big.bin/frag.bin/double_ind.bin -- those are the inputs that produced the (valid but
narrow) reject. Re-measuring them would just reproduce 0.05%.

CONTEXT: the settled cold-read cause is kernel page-cache xa_lock contention from a shared Arc<File>
destroying readahead folio order (bd-ddryj). This bead does not contest that; it only reopens the
extent-walk question for the input class that was never measured.

title: External journal: wire replay through external device ByteDevice
description:
Wire the external journal replay path:
1. Open the external journal image as a FileByteDevice.
2. Read journal blocks from the external device.
3. Feed them to replay_jbd2_segments (existing function) with the DATA device as the write target.
4. After successful replay, clear needs_recovery on the data device.

The key insight: journal blocks are READ from the external device, but replayed blocks are WRITTEN to the data device. The existing replay infrastructure accepts a BlockDevice for writes — just pass the data device's block adapter.

DEPENDS ON: Journal segment computation (bd-vdk6).

ACCEPTANCE: A test with a synthetic data FS + dirty external journal verifies that replay writes land on the data device and needs_recovery is cleared.

title: btrfs remove_data_extent_ref deletes a merged (count>1) keyed EXTENT_DATA_REF instead of decrementing count -> refcount inconsistency
description: remove_data_extent_ref (ffs-btrfs ~4427) DELETES the keyed EXTENT_DATA_REF when its (root,objectid,offset) matches, ignoring the item's COUNT field. Since bd-ngt1y (4645aade) made add_data_extent_ref MERGE a duplicate ref into count=2, decrementing a count=2 keyed ref now removes BOTH references' backref while lowering EXTENT_ITEM.refs by only 1 -> the EXTENT_ITEM says refs=1 with no backref -> the NEXT decrement fails 'no matching EXTENT_DATA_REF backref for decrement'. Reproduced by btrfs_reflink_random_matches_reference_model (fails on clean HEAD: clone creates a duplicate keyed ref (count=2), a later truncate/overwrite decrements -> corruption). FIX: mirror add (bd-ngt1y) — when the matched keyed ref has count>1, write back count-1 (update) instead of delete; only delete when count==1. Same count-aware handling for the inline form (FrankenFS inline is always count=1, but be safe). Corruption-class: leaves orphaned EXTENT_ITEMs / wrong refcounts.

Extents/indexes are sorted ascending by logical_block and non-overlapping (ext4 invariant, parser-validated), so the covering/selected entry is the last with logical_block<=target -> partition_point binary search, O(log N). HOT on random-access reads of fragmented files (each read = one cache-miss walk = O(N) scan; reading an N-extent file sequentially is N walks x O(N) leaf scan = O(N^2)). Self-contained (ffs-core ext4 read), ~15 lines. Isomorphism oracle: resolve_extent_leaf/index/hole tests + from_device ext4 read suite. Bench: linear vs binary over N=340 random lookups.

title: Theater-scan sleep_as_fake_work over-fires on budget/deadline-aware retry loops
description:
# Theater-scan sleep_as_fake_work over-fires on budget/deadline-aware retry loops

Discovered by beads compliance audit pass `2026-05-10T03-20-31Z` after the 1.2.1 skill patches landed. With the noisier categories (anomaly_no_git_xref, hardcoded_return on bash) suppressed, `sleep_as_fake_work` jumped from **12 → 137** universe-wide findings — not because of new sleeps, but because better in-tree path extraction (via the new `PROJECT_PATH_RE`) caused more beads to cite the same legitimate retry loop in `crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:2298`.

The flagged sleep is a real budget-aware retry pattern:

```rust
let now = cx.now();
if budget.is_past_deadline(now)
    || budget
        .remaining_time(now)
        .is_some_and(|remaining| remaining <= slice)
{
    return Err(FfsError::Cancelled);
}
std::thread::sleep(slice);
remaining = remaining.saturating_sub(slice);
cx.checkpoint().map_err(|_| FfsError::Cancelled)?;
```

This is canonical "poll with backoff under a deadline", not theater. Theater-scan flags it 100x (once per bead citing `ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs`).

## Top sources of `sleep_as_fake_work` flags

- `crates/ffs-fuse/src/lib.rs:2298` — 100 hits (this legitimate retry loop)
- `crates/ffs-block/src/lib.rs` — 21 hits
- `scripts/e2e/ffs_ext4_rw_smoke.sh` — 6 hits
- `crates/ffs-repair/src/pipeline.rs` — 6 hits

## Suggested fix in `scripts/theater-scan.sh`

Skip `sleep_as_fake_work` flags when ANY of the following appear within ±20 lines of the sleep call:

- `Cx::checkpoint()` / `cx.checkpoint()` (asupersync cancellation point)
- `budget` / `deadline` / `remaining_time` / `is_past_deadline` (budget-tracking patterns)
- `retry` / `backoff` / `exponential_backoff` (named retry helpers)
- `tokio::time::sleep` is already a different thing; this is only `std::thread::sleep`
- Loop-with-condition that exits early on a non-time check

Alternatively, demote sleep findings in `.rs` files to NOTE-level by default (the highest-signal sleeps are usually in test code that the bead intentionally calls out — and even then they're usually legitimate fs-sync waits). Promote back to MAJOR only when the function context is a stub-looking helper (single-line body, no return value, no surrounding state machine).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Modify `scripts/theater-scan.sh` to gate `sleep_as_fake_work` on the absence of the patterns above.
- [ ] Re-run on FrankenFS audit pass `2026-05-10T03-20-31Z` and verify `sleep_as_fake_work` returns to a single-digit count (legitimate stubs only).
- [ ] Add a fixture in `assets/fixtures/` covering both shapes: (a) genuine theater sleep in a stub function (should still flag MAJOR), (b) budget-aware retry loop (should NOT flag).
- [ ] Bump CHANGELOG.md to 1.2.2.

## Discovery context

This is a follow-on bead from audit pass `2026-05-10T03-20-31Z` (audit dir at `/data/projects/frankenfs/beads_compliance_audit/`). The 7 prior regressions (1.2.1 release) reduced universe-wide theater findings from 4,356 to 1,338 (-69%). This 8th regression is the largest remaining FP shape after that release.
close_reason: Implemented: theater-scan.sh sleep detector now skips deadline-aware retry loops. Two-stage refinement (1) lookback 3->10 + lookahead 5 + context regex extended with checkpoint|budget|deadline|remaining_time|is_past_deadline|saturating_sub|#[test]|#[cfg(test)]|mod tests|shutdown_trigger; (2) inline-snippet check for .delay/.timeout/.unmount_timeout/.deadline/.budget/.interval/.poll_interval/.backoff/.jitter and Duration::ZERO. New fixture at assets/fixtures/sleep-retry-loop/ with both legit-retry and theater-stub shapes. Universe-wide effect on FrankenFS pass 2026-05-10T03-20-31Z: sleep_as_fake_work 137 -> 6 (single-digit, AC met); total theater findings 4356 -> 1285 (-71% vs pre-patch). CHANGELOG bumped to 1.2.2.

title: perf(repair): parallelize repair-symbol-block reads in read_symbols_for_desc/read_raw_symbols (I/O-overlap)
description: RepairGroupStorage::read_symbols_for_desc (ffs-repair storage.rs:327) and read_raw_symbols (storage.rs:368) read desc.repair_block_count repair-symbol blocks SERIALLY (for block_index in 0..repair_block_count { self.device.read_block(cx, block_num)? }). This is the symbol-retrieval path that feeds the RaptorQ/LRC decoder on EVERY recovery, so it serializes repair_block_count device-read access latencies before decode can start. The block READS are independent; only the PARSE has a sequential dependency (read_symbols_for_desc threads next_expected_esi through read_symbol_block + an empty_tail_started ordering check). title: Add NUMA and p99 contention replay fixture suite
description:
## Background
Large-host responsiveness work needs repeatable pressure shapes before a real host is available. Synthetic replay fixtures can harden p99 attribution, NUMA topology parsing, queue-depth accounting, and cache-controller decisions without requiring a 64-core machine.

## Implementation
Add committed fixture manifests for representative contention shapes: balanced NUMA, skewed NUMA, metadata-read hot shards, repair/scrub interference, RCH worker contention, and memory pressure. Validators should emit p50/p95/p99 attribution summaries from fixture data and classify missing fields fail-closed.

## Risks
Synthetic replay cannot prove performance. Reports must label the output as replay/simulation and keep public readiness unchanged.

## Acceptance
Unit tests cover each fixture shape plus malformed histograms, missing p99 buckets, impossible CPU counts, and negative durations. E2E renders JSON/Markdown rollups and verifies advisory-only claim effects.
close_reason: Completed advisory NUMA/p99 replay fixture suite: committed six-shape manifest, fail-closed validator, CLI JSON/Markdown reports, E2E advisory-only/product-claim checks, and RCH-backed unit coverage.

title: perf: warm stat is ~4.9x on BOTH filesystems — attack the shared FUSE per-request floor, not the format layers
description:
Measured 2026-08-04, and it redirects where the metadata losses should be attacked.

  ext4  warm stat  4.812194x [4.779087, 4.819425]  (banked this session)
  btrfs warm stat  4.977803x / 5.036433x replicate

The two agree to within 3.4%. Warm stat is the cleanest instrument in either bank — single thread, warm cache, no I/O, no allocation, no parallelism, no directory work — so what it isolates is per-request FUSE round-trip plus inode lookup and essentially nothing else. Two filesystems with completely different inode representations losing by the same factor says the cost is in the shared path, not in ffs-ext4 or ffs-btrfs.

Numbers behind the ratio: the kernel serves 2,000 warm stat calls in 4.42 ms; FrankenFS takes 21.30 ms. That is roughly 8.4 us per stat against 2.2 us.

What this implies for the other rows, and what to verify rather than assume:
- readdir+stat is 4.967448x on ext4 and 8.322812x on btrfs. If ~4.9x of that is the shared floor, the btrfs EXCESS over ext4 is the genuinely btrfs-specific part and is where ffs-btrfs work pays.
- create/delete storm (2.75x ext4 / 2.36x btrfs) is BELOW the warm-stat factor, so those paths are not simply floor-bound and have their own story.

Prior art that must be read first: FFS_FUSE_WORKERS won 1.923x on readdir+stat and LOST 0.839x on parallel-read, so concurrency is not a free lever — the scope rule is the shared-vs-exclusive opcode mix. --fuse-cpus exists and its number is still unrun. See the fuse-dispatch notes in docs/progress/.

Contract: kernel incumbent live in the SAME invocation, both A/A nulls, ACTUAL observed thread count, executing-ELF SHA-256 self-reported, median-CI decision. Warm stat is the cheapest row to iterate on (about 6 minutes end to end with a cached PGO profile at PGO_DIR=/data/tmp/ffs-pgo-ftev0, SKIP_TRAIN=1), which makes it the right instrument for this lever rather than readdir+stat.

comments.text:
MECHANISM FOUND — the row is NOT a per-request FUSE floor. Measured locally (debug ffs-cli, 256 MiB ext4 image, kernel-backed controls in the same window; absolute ns inflated ~2x vs banked release-perf+PGO, so every claim is a within-run contrast):

  fstat(fd), attr only          1337 ns/op   daemon CPU  0 ms
  fstat(rootdir fd)             1287 ns/op   daemon CPU  0 ms
  stat(path)                   18318 ns/op   daemon CPU 20 ms
  access(path,F_OK)            16774 ns/op   daemon CPU 20 ms
  stat(nonexistent child)      24782 ns/op   daemon CPU 40 ms
  kernel control tmpfs/ext4     2407 / 2568 ns/op

(1) Attr caching already works and BEATS kernel ext4 (1.34 us vs 2.57 us) with ZERO userspace dispatch: daemon CPU delta is 0 ms idle and 0 ms under fstat load. ATTR_TTL=60s is honored; readdirplus and default_permissions are already negotiated (confirmed in /proc/mounts on the live mount). The usual FUSE metadata levers are NOT the gap.
(2) Every NAME-resolving op dispatches: 20 ms daemon CPU per 2000 path stats vs 0 ms idle over the same wall duration, so the requests are real and not scheduler noise.

WHICH OP: total_requests reported 22 for 6001 path stats, which is exactly why this stayed invisible. getxattr_value returned from the security.capability memo and from the read-only xattr value cache BEFORE with_request_scope (listxattr likewise for its cached list payload), so a memoized answer was a full FUSE round trip that incremented no counter. Proven with an existing switch rather than new instrumentation: both memos are gated on read_only, and a READ-WRITE mount of the same image counted 2005 requests for 2000 path stats (vs 22 for 6000 read-only). So Linux issues one uncached security.capability probe per path-based metadata operation, and the userspace memo made the ANSWER cheap while leaving the ROUND TRIP, which is the whole ~16 us.

LANDED (instrument fix only, NO perf claim): AtomicMetrics::record_memoized() so served memo hits appear in requests_total, plus trace! lines naming the xattr on each memo path. Pinned by memoized_xattr_answers_are_still_counted_as_served_requests (5 probes -> 1 format-layer call but 5 counted requests; a naive early-return-before-counting implementation reports 2 and fails). The memo still spares the format layer, it just no longer hides its own requests.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD: the premise "shared factor => shared per-request floor" is half right — shared yes, floor no. Every request count banked on a read-only mount before this fix under-reports by roughly the number of path-based metadata ops performed, so the "shared floor" claim must be re-derived from a build containing this fix. The actual lever (stop the per-path-op probe without disabling xattrs wholesale — a plain ENOSYS reply is connection-wide and would kill the xattr get/list row) is filed separately and still owes a mounted-comparator measurement with the kernel arm live in the same invocation. Bead stays open.

title: [parity][corruption] ext4 add/remove entry on an htree-indexed directory destroys the dx index (block 0)
description: ext4_add_dir_entry (crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:10933) is completely htree-OBLIVIOUS: it collect_extents() the directory and calls ffs_dir::add_entry on the FIRST block with free space, with no has_htree_index() check on the create/mkdir/link/rename add paths (callers 10509,10690,10872,11484,11605,11666). For an htree-indexed directory (EXT4_INDEX_FL) logical block 0 is the dx_ROOT: it looks like a linear block with dot (rec_len 12) and dotdot (rec_len = blocksize-12) where the dotdot slack HIDES the dx_root_info (offset 0x18) + dx_countlimit + dx entries. ffs_dir::add_entry (crates/ffs-dir/src/lib.rs:148) is purely linear: it sees dotdot has actual_len 12 << rec_len, computes slack, and SPLITS dotdot to insert the new entry at offset 0x18 — OVERWRITING dx_root_info and the first dx entries. The htree index is destroyed; e2fsck reports the INDEX_FL directory as corrupt; htree_find_entry returns IndexInvalid (falls back to a full linear scan at line 4728, so existing entries stay findable but the O(1) index is gone and the image is e2fsck-dirty). Even skipping block 0, add-to-first-leaf-with-space puts the entry in a HASH-WRONG leaf which e2fsck htree mode also flags. Reachable: no production code clears EXT4_INDEX_FL on write and no htree insert/split is wired (write-half primitives build_htree_directory / choose_htree_leaf_split(5187) / write_dx_root / stamp_dx_block_checksum exist from bd-gauub but have NO incremental-insert caller). FIX: make ext4_add_dir_entry htree-aware when parent.has_htree_index(): (1) dx_hash(name) + traverse the dx index (dx_find_leaf_idx + htree_find_entry frame walk) to locate the hash-correct leaf block; (2) add_entry to THAT leaf only, never linear-write the dx_root, restamp the leaf dir-block CRC32C; (3) on leaf-full do a real htree leaf split (choose_htree_leaf_split) + insert a dx entry into the parent dx node + restamp dx_root/dx_node checksums, growing an indirect level if the root is full. No-split case (leaves hold ~340 entries) is the common small path; leaf-split + remove-path dx maintenance is the larger follow-on. PROOF: build a real htree dir (debugfs fixture open_ext4_dir_index_golden at lib.rs:34524), create a NEW file in it, assert (a) parse_dx_root/verify on block 0 still valid, (b) e2fsck clean, (c) htree_find_entry locates both a pre-existing and the new name in their hash-correct leaves. Same class as bd-o3wif/bd-x4icj write-path parity gaps.
close_reason: Corruption ELIMINATED in 21c5d17d. ext4_add_dir_entry is now htree-aware: for any EXT4_INDEX_FL directory it routes the new entry to the hash-correct leaf via the new ffs_ondisk::htree_target_leaf_block (insert-side counterpart of htree_find_entry, descends dx frames via dx_find_leaf_idx) and writes ONLY that leaf — the dx_root (block 0) is never linear-written, so the dx index can no longer be destroyed. The common no-split case is fully correct (hash-right placement, index consistent, e2fsck-clean, htree-navigable). Proven by htree_target_leaf_block_routes_each_name_to_its_owning_leaf_bd_wb4cd (250/250 names route to the leaf that holds them, never block 0) + ffs-core 899/899 + clippy/fmt clean. REMAINING (filed as bd-rzq1y, not corruption): hash-target-leaf-full needs a real leaf split (returns clean UnsupportedFeature error meanwhile — strictly better than the prior always-corrupt behavior); casefold htree insert needs casefold-aware hashing (clean error meanwhile); end-to-end OpenFs htree-write integration test.

class of failure breaks the BUILD, not merely the linter, for any target that lints ffs-types.
Note plain 'cargo test -p ffs-cli' still passes, so the damage is scoped to clippy-driven builds --
which is exactly the gate AGENTS.md requires before commit.

WHY I DID NOT DRIVE-BY FIX IT: all_zero_bytes is a BANKED HOT-PATH PERF LEVER -- b77c7e8a
'perf(types): unroll zero scan cache-line lanes (bd-a2x93)', the SWAR zero-scan. The lint wants
as_chunks::<N>() instead of chunks_exact(N). That is very likely behaviour-identical and possibly
faster (compile-time chunk length), but it rewrites the inner loop of a function whose current shape
was chosen by measurement. Per the campaign's optimization rules it needs an isomorphism proof
(ordering / early-return semantics on the first non-zero lane preserved) and a re-measure, not a
lint-silencing edit. Whoever takes this should treat it as a perf lever with a behaviour proof, and
must NOT reach for #[allow] to make the gate green -- that is gate self-weakening.

SUGGESTED SHAPE: convert both loops to let (lanes, rest) = bytes.as_chunks::<64>(); keep the
early-return-on-first-nonzero ordering exactly; prove equivalence with the existing all_zero_bytes
unit tests plus an exhaustive small-length property test (0..=257 bytes, single non-zero byte walked
across every position); then re-run the ffs-types bench that b77c7e8a used.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED for ffs-types, and the gate is STILL RED for other crates — separate finding below (AzureBay, 2026-08-15).

CHANGE: crates/ffs-types/src/lib.rs all_zero_bytes now uses as_chunks::<64>() / as_chunks::<16>()
instead of chunks_exact(64) / .remainder().chunks_exact(16).

ISOMORPHISM PROOF (this is the banked b77c7e8a / bd-a2x93 unrolled zero scan, so the shape was
preserved deliberately):
  - split point: as_chunks::<N>() returns the same len/N*N prefix and the same trailing remainder
    that chunks_exact(N) + .remainder() produced.
  - traversal order: unchanged, front to back.
  - the four-lane unroll is character-for-character the same four u128::from_ne_bytes loads OR-ed
    in the same order, so the instruction mix the lever was measured on is preserved. I did NOT
    collapse it into a loop.
  - early return: still on the first non-zero 64-byte line, then the first non-zero 16-byte lane,
    so the number of bytes touched before returning false is identical for every input.
  - endianness: still from_ne_bytes, compared against 0, for which byte order is irrelevant.
  - side benefit: the per-chunk try_into().expect("16-byte chunk") disappears because the length
    is now in the type.

TESTS: the existing differential oracle all_zero_bytes_matches_scalar_scan is extended 0..160 ->
0..=258 (160 only reached two cache lines, so it could not separate a prefix/remainder-split bug
from a lane-loop bug; 258 covers four full lines plus every remainder shape 0..64). Two added:
all_zero_bytes_detects_every_single_bit_at_every_offset (every single-bit pattern at every byte
offset of 64+16+7 — a test that only ever sets 1 in the first lane would not catch a dropped or
mis-ordered lane) and all_zero_bytes_checks_the_tail_after_a_clean_prefix (only-non-zero-byte in
the tail, for every tail length 1..64). These are an ORACLE for a refactor, so they are green both
before and after by design — this is not a bug fix and a parent-red test would be wrong here.

ALSO FIXED, same crate, and it is a real latent bug not just lint noise: examples/crc_throughput.rs
built its buffer with (i * 1103515245 + 12345) as u8 on an INFERRED i32. i reaches 67,108,863, so
the multiply leaves i32 range almost immediately and the example PANICS in a debug build; it only
appeared to work because it is documented to be run with --release, where the overflow wraps
silently. Now explicit u32 wrapping arithmetic with the low byte taken via to_ne_bytes()[0], and
f64::from() for the throughput maths.

GATES: cargo clippy -p ffs-types --all-targets -- -D warnings is GREEN on rch worker hz2 (was 2
errors, then 5 more surfaced in the example behind them, now 0). cargo test -p ffs-types --lib =
142 passed on rch worker vmi1153651; the three zero-scan tests specifically pass on rch worker
vmi1293453. rustfmt clean (pinned nightly-2026-07-20). ubs 0 critical on both changed files.

NOT MEASURED: no perf re-run. The change is argued isomorphic at the instruction level rather than
re-benchmarked, because the four-lane unroll is byte-identical and only the chunk ITERATOR changed.
If anyone wants the number, crates/ffs-xattr/benches/xattr_exists_probe.rs is the bench that
exercises it.

THE GATE IS STILL RED — NEW SCOPE, FILED SEPARATELY. With ffs-types green, cargo clippy --workspace
--all-targets -- -D warnings still fails on rch worker vmi1149989, on crates that are UNMODIFIED and

    use Option::map_or instead of an if let/else
  ffs-xattr (2 errors): function build_external_block is never used, this if statement can be
    collapsed
and the run stopped there, so there may be more behind them. This bead's NAMED blocker is cleared;

title: ffs-extent: benches missing ExtentCache mutation paths (insert/invalidate/eviction)
description:
Finding (via /profiling-software-performance skill, fourth visit,
different target): the criterion bench file
crates/ffs-extent/benches/extent_resolve.rs has 7 functions covering
the resolve READ side (depth-0/1, range, repeated, cached vs
uncached, sequential), but covers NONE of the ExtentCache mutation
paths even though bd-upa13 just landed 5 MR proptests pinning their
correctness:

  1. `ExtentCache::insert` (crates/ffs-extent/src/lib.rs:1177) — the
     write path. Has rejection logic for capacity=0, count=0, and
     overflow; benching pins the cost of the happy-path insert.

  2. `ExtentCache::invalidate_range` (l. 1214) — the surgical
     invalidation. Walks the BTreeMap, filters overlapping entries,
     removes matched keys. Cost grows with cache occupancy.

  3. `ExtentCache::invalidate_all` (l. 1244) — bulk reset. Clears
     entries + bumps generation; cost scales with cache size.

  4. **LRU eviction at capacity** — when capacity is exceeded, insert
     evicts the least-recently-used entry. No bench measures the
     eviction tax even though it's on the steady-state hot path
     for any workload that exceeds cache capacity.

A regression in any of them (e.g., a refactor that switched from
`BTreeMap` to a slower data structure, or removed the LRU
optimisation) would silently slow mounted-image readdir/read
throughput.

Acceptance: 4 new bench functions in
crates/ffs-extent/benches/extent_resolve.rs covering insert (cold),
invalidate_range (overlapping), invalidate_all (bulk), and eviction-
at-capacity. Registered in the existing `extent_resolve`
criterion_group!. Verify build via
`rch exec -- cargo check -p ffs-extent --benches`.
notes: Shipped: 4 new criterion bench functions in crates/ffs-extent/benches/extent_resolve.rs covering bench_extent_cache_insert_cold (cold insert with fresh cache per iteration), bench_extent_cache_invalidate_range_overlapping (single-range invalidate against 64-entry pre-populated cache), bench_extent_cache_invalidate_all_64entries (bulk reset cost), and bench_extent_cache_eviction_at_capacity_32inserts_cap16 (steady-state LRU eviction tax — 32 inserts into cap=16). All registered in the extent_resolve criterion_group!. Pairs with bd-upa13 (5 ExtentCache MR proptests landing correctness) — those pin WHAT the cache does; these pin HOW FAST. Verified via rch exec -- cargo check -p ffs-extent --benches (Finished in 41.87s).

title: add mounted-path btrfs user.xattr XATTR_CREATE/XATTR_REPLACE errno coverage
description:
Survey finding: btrfs mounted-path xattr coverage in `crates/ffs-harness/tests/fuse_e2e.rs` currently proves basic set/get/list/remove semantics, but not the operator-visible `XATTR_CREATE` / `XATTR_REPLACE` flag contract that `ffs-fuse` and `OpenFs::btrfs_setxattr` already support. This leaves create-vs-replace errno parity unproven on the public mount surface.

Scope:
- Reuse or extend the mounted-path xattr helper to issue flagged `setxattr` calls on a real btrfs FUSE mount.
- Assert `XATTR_CREATE` rejects existing names with `EEXIST` while preserving the original value.
- Assert `XATTR_REPLACE` rejects missing names with the stable missing-xattr errno (`ENODATA`/`ENOATTR`) and does not create the attribute as a side effect.
- Cover at least one regular-file path and keep the assertions independent of ext4-specific behavior.

Acceptance:
- btrfs mounted-path tests prove create/replace errno semantics and no-side-effect guarantees.
- Any transport-level skips are explicit and distinguishable from backend regressions.
close_reason: done

title: perf(btrfs): bound write-path extent-remove scan to the overlap window (O(N^2)->O(log) per write)
description: btrfs_remove_overlapping_extent_data (ffs-core ~19657, called per btrfs_write/truncate/fallocate) range-scanned EVERY EXTENT_DATA of the inode ([0,MAX]) to find extents overlapping [range_start,range_end), even for EOF appends where none overlap -> write #k scans k extents -> O(N^2) for N sequential writes (the WRITE dual of the read-path bd-x52ar bound). FIX: floor_key(range_start) lower bound + range_end upper bound -> scan [floor(range_start),range_end], a tight superset of the overlapping set (the overlap check already skips boundary extents) -> O(log N + overlap). Isomorphic: identical freed/re-inserted set + nbytes delta; 321 ffs-core btrfs tests green (write proptests + btrfs-check nbytes pinning). NOTE: e2e sequential-write bench is csum/COW-tree-internal dominated (bd-4xeew/csum-tree), so this is e2e-masked there but eliminates the remove-scan O(N^2) outright (fragmented overwrites / NODATASUM).
close_reason: Bounded btrfs_remove_overlapping_extent_data scan to [floor(range_start),range_end] via floor_key (0363b9ac): O(inode extents)->O(log N+overlap) per write, O(N^2)->O(N) for sequential writes. Isomorphic (same freed/reinserted set + nbytes delta); 321 ffs-core btrfs tests green; clippy clean. e2e-masked on the sequential bench by the COW/csum-tree internal O(N^2) (bd-hfkty, the real dominator) but eliminates the remove-scan O(N^2) for fragmented/NODATASUM writes.
