title: perf(inode): batch contiguous data-block frees in indirect delete/truncate (O(blocks)->O(runs) bitmap RMW)
description: free_indirect_chain (ffs-inode lib.rs:443, level==1) and free_indirect_blocks direct loop (lib.rs:485) free each data block of a legacy indirect-mapped inode INDIVIDUALLY via free_blocks_persist(child, 1) — one call per block (up to ppb=1024 per leaf indirect block, x indirect tree). free_blocks_persist(start,count) already splits the range across groups and does ONE bitmap-block read-modify-write per group per call (split_free_block_segments + single bitmap_buf read + clear bits + write). So freeing a contiguous run of L data blocks individually costs L bitmap RMWs (L block reads + L writes) vs ONE RMW when freed as a range. LEVER: gather each leaf's non-zero data-block pointers and free them in MAXIMAL CONTIGUOUS RUNS via a new free_data_blocks_in_runs helper (start=blocks[i]; extend while start.checked_add(len)==Some(blocks[i+len]); free_blocks_persist(start,len)) — O(blocks)->O(runs) bitmap RMW. ISO: free_blocks_persist(start,L) is the canonical range API == L individual frees (same bits cleared, same double-free/reserved validation, same group-stats); freeing is commutative so order-independent; on error both abort. Hot on rm/truncate of large sequentially-allocated files (runs collapse ppb frees to ~1). Applies to direct blocks + level==1 leaves; level>1 still recurses. Bench target: inode_free_runs (per-block vs run-batched free over a 1024-ptr leaf w/ latency-modeled bitmap RMW, contiguous vs fragmented), assert_eq freed set. Needs criterion dev-dep added to ffs-inode. cc filed, delete/truncate frontier (ffs-inode uncontested).
close_reason: VERIFIED bench inode_free_runs: per_block vs run_batched contiguous_1024 1008x (181646us->180us, O(blocks)->O(runs) bitmap RMW); fragmented_512 neutral 1.01x (correct: no runs to coalesce). KEEP.

title: touch_* version-bump dispatch invariant proptest
description: touch_atime, touch_mtime_ctime, and touch_ctime have a load-bearing NFS-coherence contract: atime updates MUST NOT bump i_version (atime is a lazy attr that shouldn't invalidate NFS caches), while mtime_ctime and ctime updates MUST bump i_version by exactly 1. The fixed-input touch_atime_does_not_modify_ctime_mtime test confirms timestamp isolation but NOT version isolation. A regression that started bumping version on atime would silently invalidate every NFS client cache and trigger spurious revalidation storms. Add ext4_proptest_touch_atime_does_not_bump_version + ext4_proptest_touch_mtime_ctime_bumps_version_by_one + ext4_proptest_touch_ctime_bumps_version_by_one.

title: flaky: btrfs_write_fsync_log_contract_success intermittently misses btrfs_sync_applied log in CI
description: ffs-core lib unit test (crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:~44877). Intermittently fails in GitHub Actions 'Lint & Test / Unit tests' with .expect('expected btrfs_sync_applied fsync log') — the captured JSON log buffer is missing the btrfs_sync_applied/btrfs_rw_fsync entry. Passes 878/878 consistently locally (isolation 5/5; full parallel suite 4/4) and passed in CI run for 5f286769 with identical ffs-core code, so it is flaky, not a code regression. Likely root cause: install_json_subscriber uses tracing::dispatcher::set_default (THREAD-LOCAL DefaultGuard); if the btrfs fsync path emits btrfs_sync_applied from a worker thread under CI scheduling, the thread-local subscriber misses it. log_contract_guard() only serializes the contract tests; it does not make capture cross-thread. Candidate fixes: (a) ensure the fsync log is emitted synchronously on the caller thread, or (b) capture via a process-global subscriber guarded by a single global mutex across all log-contract tests so cross-thread events are recorded. Blocks main CI going green alongside bd-g91se. Could not reproduce locally; needs CI-environment repro or code-path audit of where btrfs_sync_applied is emitted.
close_reason: Fixed via option (b): replaced thread-local set_default + global rebuild_interest_cache with a single process-global always-on INFO subscriber (set_global_default, installed once) routing to a swappable active-buffer slot keyed by installing ThreadId. Eliminates the global callsite-interest-cache race that intermittently cached ffs::btrfs::rw as 'never' and dropped btrfs_sync_applied in CI. Thread-keying prevents cross-test pollution. Verified: log_contract 10/10, full ffs-core lib green, clippy -D warnings clean. Commit 8bd586fa.

title: Raw-bytes determinism MR for parse_extent_data
description: parse_extent_data is invoked on every btrfs file read — heaviest-trafficked btrfs leaf-item parser. The existing proptest block (lib.rs:7402-7480) only covers encode→parse round-trips on VALID inputs (sparse Regular, uncompressed Inline, compressed Inline). It does NOT exercise parse_extent_data(arbitrary_bytes) twice on the Err paths. Sister parsers parse_root_item (bd-fs41s), parse_xattr_items (bd-fhznm), parse_inode_refs (bd-9f8ef), parse_root_ref (bd-x2320), parse_dir_items, parse_inode_item, parse_root_ref all have raw-bytes determinism MRs. title: test infra: latency-injecting BlockDevice + serial multi-extent read baseline bench (prereq for bd-307e4)
description:
Separable, low-risk prerequisite that unblocks MEASUREMENT for bd-307e4 (parallel multi-extent btrfs I/O). Today bd-307e4 is unmeasurable: the test harness BlockDevice is in-memory (read_block = memcpy, zero latency), so a parallel restructure of btrfs_read_file shows only rayon overhead, never the queue-overlap win it would deliver on real storage.

DELIVERABLE (test-only, no production change): a LatencyInjectingDevice<D: BlockDevice> decorator (in a bench/test module) wrapping any BlockDevice; on each read_block it spins/sleeps a configurable per-read latency (models real-disk/SSD-queue access time) before delegating. Then a criterion bench that drives a btrfs (or ext4 extent) read spanning N extents through the latency device, establishing the SERIAL baseline wall-clock. This is profile-first discipline: build the measurement before the optimization.

Once this lands, bd-307e4's parallel restructure (par_iter the per-extent btrfs_read_logical_into gather) becomes A/B-measurable against the serial baseline under injected latency, and the Cx:Sync gate can be verified concretely.

BlockDevice trait: crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs (fn read_block(&self,&Cx,BlockNumber)->Result<BlockBuf>). Note: rayon already in ffs-core. Does NOT itself ship a Score>=2.0 win (it's the measurement substrate); the win is bd-307e4 on top of it.

Filed by cc W152 after exhaustive frontier re-verification (ffs-block remove_from_list = non-default ARC path false lead; GF SIMD proven dead W118-120; bw_tree O(N^2) not production-reachable; journal recovery already BTreeSet; xattr scans small-N). No within-the-hour Score>=2.0 production lever remained; this is the concrete next forward step.
close_reason: Completed by existing HEAD implementation and verified via RCH: crates/ffs-core/benches/btrfs_read_io_overlap.rs provides the requested generic LatencyBlockDevice<D: BlockDevice> wrapper around a blob-backed BlockDevice plus serial_read_then_par_decompress vs par_read_and_decompress criterion arms. RCH cargo bench -p ffs-core --bench btrfs_read_io_overlap on vmi1293453 passed; serial [8.3999 ms,8.9612 ms,10.071 ms], parallel [2.3103 ms,2.4837 ms,2.7313 ms], 3.61x midpoint. The bench asserts byte-identical decompressed extents before measuring. This closes the measurement substrate; not a production optimization lever.

title: Refine mounted repair conformance with read-only mutation boundaries and rw refusal side effects
description:
Supplemental refinement for bd-rchk7.3. Mounted repair policy fixtures should prove the exact mutation boundary: default read-only scrub detects only, explicit read-only repair may mutate only the controlled image/ledger path when allowed, and read-write background repair must refuse without partial client-visible side effects until serialization is proven.

Scope: define mounted repair conformance scenarios that check image hashes, ledger rows, symbol refresh, mount options, CLI exit status, visible files, no host-path mutation, and reopen behavior for detection-only, read-only repair, read-write refusal, missing ledger, stale ledger, and host capability skip cases.

Required proof before close:
1. Unit/schema tests reject mounted repair fixture rows missing mount mode, background repair flag state, ledger path policy, expected mutation scope, image hash expectation, visible namespace expectation, ledger expectation, and cleanup policy.
2. Unit tests cover default detection-only, explicit read-only repair allowed, missing ledger refusal, stale ledger refusal, read-write repair refusal, unsupported flavor refusal, host capability skip, and cleanup failure classification.
3. Mounted E2E smoke uses the permissioned lane where available and proves read-write refusal leaves file size, directory entries, xattrs, ledger rows, and image hash in the expected state.
4. Logs include scenario id, CLI flags, mount options, image hash before/after, ledger rows before/after, repair classification, expected mutation scope, observed mutation scope, host paths touched, cleanup status, artifact paths, and reproduction command.
5. Release gates cannot promote mounted automatic repair readiness unless detection-only, read-only repair, and read-write refusal side-effect fixtures are all represented with fresh evidence.

title: Pin BTRFS_SEND_STREAM_MAGIC + BTRFS_SEND_STREAM_VERSION to fs/btrfs/send.h
description: BTRFS_SEND_STREAM_MAGIC (b'btrfs-stream\0') and BTRFS_SEND_STREAM_VERSION (1) are read by parse_send_stream at the head of every btrfs-send/receive stream. title: the campaign's only honest_win does not reproduce: btrfs parallel-read returns OPPOSITE verdicts on two admitted runs minutes apart, non-overlapping intervals, 6.09% spread
description:
The campaign's ONLY honest_win does not reproduce stably, and the row currently scores nothing.

MEASURED 2026-08-08, bd-c5210's re-measurement on the corrected fixture. Two admitted runs, same candidate ELF 913c36a4, same PGO b30de364, same kernel 6.17.0-41, same performance governor, same 128 pairs / 32 crossover blocks, taken MINUTES APART on one machine:

    run 1  1.019622x  [1.007602, 1.062585]  margin 1.034273  HONEST_NEUTRAL (we are slightly SLOWER)
    run 2  0.961107x  [0.958445, 0.971937]  margin 1.021503  HONEST_WIN     (we are 3.9% FASTER)

    kernel arm  3.887 -> 3.943 ms   (+1.45%)
    ffs arm     3.917 -> 3.787 ms   (-3.34%)

The intervals DO NOT OVERLAP and the verdicts DISAGREE. Spread 6.09% — the largest same-ELF spread the campaign has measured, larger than the 4.71% and 9.15% that motivated bd-4sull, and roughly 6x the CI width either run reports. Both runs passed every admission gate: both A/A nulls clear, four-arm parity pass, post-unmount validation clean, preflight verdict=clear.

For comparison the banked row (old fixture, ELF f44b3dc4) was 0.894290x and 0.830537x — and its own two runs already spread 7.7%, which the scorecard noted at the time and did not act on.

SO THE WIN IS NEITHER CONFIRMED NOR WITHDRAWN. It cannot be quoted as a win. It also must not be quoted as refuted. The btrfs scorecard now scores it UNRESOLVED and the file's score line reads 0 confirmed wins / 5 losses / 1 UNRESOLVED.

CANDIDATE EXPLANATIONS, none eliminated:

1. CO-TENANT LOAD. A peer's `pytest` (254% CPU) started 06:54:19 and ran through both runs. The PLACEMENT CPUs were quiet — max busy 0.020, mean 0.006 across 0-7/32-39, which is why the preflight legitimately cleared — but the load sat elsewhere on the same socket (CPUs 16, 19, 48, 51, 54 above 20%). Memory bandwidth, LLC capacity and boost budget are socket-wide. This is precisely what bd-4sull says the gate cannot see, and it is the leading candidate.
2. INTRINSIC ROW VARIANCE. The banked pair also spread 7.7% on a different fixture and ELF, so this row may simply be noisy at this precision regardless of load. If so, it needs far more pairs than 128 to decide, and possibly cannot be decided by this instrument at all.
3. BTRFS EXTENT LAYOUT UNDER THE NEW FIXTURE. bd-c5210 moved fixture creation from the mkfs `-r` seed to through-the-mount writes. For ext4 the layouts were PROVEN identical (scripts/cmp_extent_layout_probe.sh: one contiguous 64-block extent per file either way). For btrfs this is UNVERIFIED — debugfs is ext4-only and btrfs is COW with its own allocator. A layout difference would matter on a read benchmark and could plausibly move a ~4 ms batch.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT
1. A btrfs extent-layout probe analogous to the ext4 one (`btrfs inspect-internal dump-tree` / `filefrag` on both constructions). Cheap, no quiet window needed, and it eliminates or confirms cause 3 outright. DO THIS FIRST.
2. The pair re-run in a genuinely quiet window with no co-tenant process, verified by sampling load DURING the run rather than only before it. If the spread collapses, cause 1 is confirmed and the instrument needs a during-run quiescence check.
3. If the spread survives a quiet window: raise pairs until the CI is small relative to the spread, or accept that this row is undecidable by this instrument and say so in the scorecard rather than banking either verdict.
4. Record both arms' absolute medians every time (bd-4sull item 3, now enforced) so a future disagreement is decomposable. The banked wins are NOT decomposable, which is why nobody can say today whether they were ever our speed or the incumbent's slowness.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE ROW: a campaign that reports one win and five losses, whose single win evaporates on re-measurement, has a credibility problem that no individual row fixes. Better to carry it as UNRESOLVED and settle it than to keep quoting 0.894290x.
close_reason: RESOLVED: cause 1 (co-tenant load) confirmed. Re-run in a verified-quiet window with external CPU sampled every 3s throughout: 0.893282x and 0.927352x, both HONEST_WIN, both directional_claim_clear=true, spread 3.81%, verdicts agree 2/2. Quiet run 1 lands 0.11% from the banked 0.894290x on a DIFFERENT fixture construction, so two instruments and two fixtures converge. The win is CONFIRMED and the btrfs scorecard is restored to 1 win / 5 losses. The contended pair (1.019622x NEUTRAL / 0.961107x WIN, 6.09% spread, non-overlapping) is inadmissible and I was premature to bank it. TRANSFERABLE FINDING: the preflight was CORRECT to report verdict=clear - the peer's load never touched the placement CPUs (max busy 0.020) - but a start-of-run, placement-CPU-only gate cannot certify a window, because bandwidth/LLC/boost are socket-wide. bd-4sull argued this from drift; this row shows it flipping a verdict inside one session. The crossover itself held: kernel arm moved -12.6% between quiet runs while the ratio moved 3.81%. Follow-up filed for in-band during-run external-load sampling.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CAUSE 3 IS NOW MEASURED, NOT UNVERIFIED — and the answer splits in two. It does NOT explain the run-1-vs-run-2 disagreement, but it DOES disqualify the banked wins from comparison with the new numbers.

MEASURED (scripts/cmp_btrfs_layout_probe.sh, 8 x 256 KiB files, the harness's own names). Fragmentation is IDENTICAL — exactly one extent per file under both constructions, 8 total either way. The ORDERING is not:

    file             BAKED (-r seed)    SEEDED (through mount)
    read-000000            3584                3328
    read-000001            3328                3392
    read-000002            3456                3456
    read-000003            3712                3520
    read-000004            3520                3584
    read-000005            3776                3648
    read-000006            3648                3712
    read-000007            3392                3776

The seeded layout is PERFECTLY ASCENDING in name order. The baked layout is scrambled.

WHY THAT MATTERS FOR THIS SPECIFIC WORKLOAD: `parallel_read_batch` does `read_dir`, then SORTS the paths by name, then 8 workers pread them in that sorted order. So under the seeded fixture the read sequence walks the disk forwards; under the baked fixture it jumps around. For a read benchmark with kernel readahead in play, those are materially different jobs.

MECHANISM, verified rather than guessed: `mkfs.btrfs -r` copies the seed tree in HOST READDIR order, and the host directory here is ext4 with an htree, so readdir returns HASH order. Listing the seed tree with `ls -U` gives read-000001, read-000002, read-000000, read-000003 ... — scrambled exactly as the physical layout is. The btrfs image therefore inherits the host filesystem's hash order as its physical layout.

NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WITH EXT4, which is why the earlier ext4 probe did not predict this: `mke2fs -d` lays the same files out in ascending name order under BOTH constructions (2160-2223 then 2224-2287 baked; 32896-32959 then 32960-33023 seeded). The two mkfs tools differ, so the ext4 result genuinely did not transfer — as flagged.

CONSEQUENCES, split precisely:

1. FOR THE 6.09% RUN-1-vs-RUN-2 SPREAD: cause 3 is ELIMINATED. Both new runs used the seeded construction and therefore byte-identical images with identical layout. Layout cannot explain a disagreement between two runs that shared a fixture. That leaves cause 1 (co-tenant load) and cause 2 (intrinsic row variance), and cause 1 remains the leading candidate.

2. FOR THE BANKED WINS vs THE NEW NUMBERS: cause 3 is CONFIRMED as a disqualifying confound. The banked 0.894290x / 0.830537x were measured against a physically SCRAMBLED fixture; the new 1.019622x / 0.961107x against a SEQUENTIAL one. Those are not the same benchmark, so the movement from "win" to "unresolved" cannot be read as a change in FrankenFS at all. The old numbers should be treated as describing a workload the harness no longer runs.

WHICH CONSTRUCTION IS RIGHT? The seeded one, and this is not a close call — a real btrfs filesystem populated by writing files has them laid out in write order, not in some other filesystem's hash order. bd-c5210's fix made the fixture more realistic on btrfs as well as fixing ext4's index. But it means the btrfs parallel-read row must be re-baselined from scratch rather than compared to its predecessor.

STILL OPEN on bd-ws9dg: the quiet-window re-run (cause 1) and, if the spread survives it, the question of whether this row is decidable by this instrument at 128 pairs (cause 2).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
RESOLVED (2026-08-08). Cause 1 — co-tenant load — is CONFIRMED. The win is real; the instrument was the fragile part.

RE-RUN IN A VERIFIED-QUIET WINDOW, external CPU sampled every 3 s throughout rather than only at the gate (median 113.5% of a 6400% box, ~1.8% utilisation, no excursions):

    quiet run 1   0.893282x [0.891253, 0.896649]  margin 1.019037  HONEST_WIN
    quiet run 2   0.927352x [0.923351, 0.930643]  margin 1.016213  HONEST_WIN
    kernel arm 4.742 / 4.143 ms      ffs arm 4.311 / 3.820 ms
    spread 3.81%, verdicts AGREE 2/2, both directional_claim_clear=true

versus the contended pair that opened this bead:

    contended r1  1.019622x  HONEST_NEUTRAL
    contended r2  0.961107x  HONEST_WIN
    spread 6.09%, verdicts DISAGREE, intervals non-overlapping

⭐ AND QUIET RUN 1 LANDS 0.11% FROM THE BANKED 0.894290x — on a DIFFERENT fixture construction, months apart, different ELF, different kernel. That agreement is why the win is restored rather than merely un-withdrawn: two independent instruments and two fixtures converge on the same number.

WHAT I GOT WRONG EARLIER TODAY, stated plainly: I scored this row UNRESOLVED and wrote in the scorecard that "the win did not survive re-measurement". That was premature. The contended pair was INADMISSIBLE EVIDENCE and I should not have banked it — I disclosed the contention in the same commit, which was right, but I should have re-run before publishing a verdict rather than after. The scorecard section is rewritten and the score line restored to 1 win / 5 losses.

THE TRANSFERABLE FINDING, which is worth more than this row:

The preflight was not wrong. It reported verdict=clear and it was CORRECT to: the peer's pytest (254% CPU) never touched the placement CPUs — max busy 0.020, mean 0.006 across 0-7/32-39. The arms genuinely had idle cores. The load sat elsewhere on the same socket (CPUs 16, 19, 48, 51, 54 above 20%), and memory bandwidth, LLC capacity and boost budget are socket-wide, not per-core.

So: A START-OF-RUN, PLACEMENT-CPU-ONLY GATE CANNOT CERTIFY A MEASUREMENT WINDOW. bd-4sull argued this from cross-window drift. This row demonstrates it FLIPPING A VERDICT inside one session — a stronger and more alarming form of the same claim.

Note also what did NOT break: the crossover. Between the two quiet runs the kernel arm moved -12.6% (4.742 -> 4.143 ms) while the ratio moved only +3.81%. Common-mode effects cancel in the quotient exactly as designed. What contention does is hit the two arms ASYMMETRICALLY — plausibly because the FUSE arm has a daemon pinned to one private core while the kernel arm runs in the callers' context — and no amount of pairing removes that.

(Curiosity, untested and irrelevant to the ratio: both absolute arms are SLOWER in the quiet window than under load, consistent with deeper C-state residency on an idle box.)

WHAT SHOULD CHANGE IN THE HARNESS, filed separately rather than assumed here: sample host-wide external CPU DURING the run and fail the row if it exceeds a threshold, instead of sampling placement CPUs once before it. The sampler used here is 6 lines of shell; doing it in-band would have refused both contended runs automatically and this bead would never have been filed.

Cause 2 (intrinsic row variance) is not separately eliminated but is bounded: 3.81% in a quiet window, with a consistent verdict. Cause 3 (btrfs extent layout) was eliminated for the run-to-run spread earlier in this bead — both runs share a fixture — and confirmed only as a banked-vs-new confound.

title: ext4 same-parent directory rename inflates parent link count by 1
description:
ext4_rename: 'mv P/child P/child2' (same parent, child is a directory) leaves P's i_links_count too HIGH by 1 (confirmed via test: before=3, after=4). ext4_add_dir_entry increments the parent's links_count whenever the inserted entry is a directory (the new '..' backref). For a cross-parent dir move that +1 is compensated by a -1 on the OLD parent (the block gated on parent != new_parent). For a same-parent rename the '..' backref never moves, so the +1 is spurious and uncompensated -> parent leaks a link. e2fsck reports 'inode

ref count is N, should be N-1'; can also block rmdir of the parent. FIX: the dir-rename link-count fixup now decrements by 1 in BOTH branches (cross-parent: old parent loses backref; same-parent: undo the spurious add_dir_entry increment). Regression test write_rename_directory_within_same_parent_preserves_parent_link_count (fails before, passes after).
close_reason: Fixed in b68a6a36: same-parent directory rename now decrements parent links_count by 1 to undo ext4_add_dir_entry's spurious +1 (the moved dir's '..' backref never moved). Cross-parent path unchanged. Regression test write_rename_directory_within_same_parent_preserves_parent_link_count (before=3/after=4 -> equal). ffs-core 971/971, clippy clean.

title: Create non-permissioned readiness lab E2E orchestrator
description:
## Background
Each lab component needs a single non-destructive E2E proving that future agents can regenerate the full advisory evidence package and inspect detailed logs without relying on old transcripts.

## Implementation
Add a scripts/e2e orchestrator that builds synthetic inputs, runs the lab validators through direct RCH for cargo lanes, captures command transcripts, writes JSON and Markdown artifacts, and verifies no permissioned env ACK was consumed. Use the existing E2E helper conventions and fail-closed RCH capture pattern.

title: Add operator runtime console for managed and per-core mounts
description:
Idea-wizard result: FrankenFS already has managed/per-core mount runtime modes, BackpressureGate/PressureMonitor, per-core aggregate metrics, adaptive runtime summaries, and a MetricsRegistry, while README.md still says asupersync runtime introspection is library-only and future work will ship an `ffs mount --console` flag.

Goal: turn those existing signals into an operator-facing, non-magical runtime console surface for long-running managed/per-core mounts. The console must help operators and agent swarms understand pressure, request counts, per-core imbalance, throttled/shed requests, cache hit/miss shape, and shutdown evidence without promoting advisory data into public readiness claims.

Scope constraints:
- No ambient runtime creation and no tokio; stay within existing asupersync/Cx and FUSE lifecycle boundaries.
- Console output must be bounded, redacted, schema-pinned, and usable in artifacts.
- Do not claim swarm.responsiveness or adaptive_runtime proof-bundle acceptance from local console output; permissioned large-host lanes remain authoritative.
- Implementation children remain blocked on `bd-oowwx` while RCH has no admissible workers, because cargo check/test/clippy must run through RCH.

Success criteria: all child beads closed with CLI surface, metric snapshot contract, non-permissioned validator/E2E coverage, docs/runbook updates, and release-gate wording that keeps console output operational/advisory unless a separate permissioned evidence lane accepts it.

title: rename O(N^2): dir bloats (splits add leaves, removes never reclaim) -> collect_extents par_iter rayon-coordination per op
description: Profile of rename-bench: ~30% rayon coordination (steal/yield/epoch/wait) + ~25% parse_dir_block/to_vec/malloc. The dir bloats because every overflow appends a leaf but a removal never reclaims an emptied leaf, so collect_extents_recursive walks an ever-growing block set and fans out a par_iter per rename (past the 64-block metadata guard threshold). Fix: serialize the metadata par_iter for the warm rename/collect_extents path regardless of block count, and/or reclaim emptied leaves on removal. The htree leaf split (bd-8ch29) + removal fast-path are correct+e2fsck-clean but wall-neutral here (shelved) because this, not the htree maintenance, is the bottleneck.
close_reason: Closed as stale/refuted by fresh profile: no rayon/collect_extents bottleneck in current rename-bench; top current costs are memmove, lookup_in_dir_block, add_entry, MVCC commit, CRC, with preflight at 0.54%, and current release-perf 40k rename beats loop-mounted kernel ext4 in the measured phase.

title: fix(ffs-block): default vectored reads preserve buffers on scalar failure
description: Fallback quality work after br ready returned no rows and peer-owned graph picks were unavailable. The default ByteDevice::read_vectored_exact_at preflights bounds but reads directly into caller iovecs one scalar chunk at a time, so a later scalar read failure can leave earlier caller buffers replaced and the failing buffer partially dirty even though the operation returns Err. Stage scalar reads into scratch storage and copy into caller iovecs only after every scalar read succeeds, with a focused regression that preserves offsets, call lengths, and caller bytes on an injected second-read failure.
close_reason: VERIFIED (cc): the default ByteDevice::read_vectored_exact_at stages the whole vectored range into a scratch buffer and scatters into caller iovecs ONLY after every scalar read succeeds (lib.rs:354), so a later scalar-read failure leaves all earlier iovecs unreplaced and the failing buffer untouched while returning Err. Regression default_vectored_read_preserves_iovecs_when_later_scalar_read_fails (7851) — injected second-read failure, asserts offsets/lengths/caller bytes preserved — passes. (This is the unconditional preservation contract that correctly rejected a blind-shipped direct-vectored fast path earlier this campaign.) cargo test -p ffs-block green.

title: fix(ffs-block): FileByteDevice scalar reads preserve buffer on short read

FileByteDevice::read_exact_at validates against the open-time cached length but reads directly into the caller buffer, so a backing file truncated after open can partially overwrite caller bytes before returning UnexpectedEof. title: ffs-ondisk: Ext4DirEntry::actual_size and Ext4FileType::from_raw lack MR proptest coverage
description:
Finding (via /testing-metamorphic skill, fifth visit, different
target): two ext4 directory-entry helpers on the readdir hot path
have minimal proptest coverage even though they each have rich
metamorphic invariants:

  1. `Ext4DirEntry::actual_size` (crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs:3093):
     implements the kernel macro `EXT4_DIR_REC_LEN(name_len)` =
     `((name_len) + 8 + 3) & ~3`. Existing
     `ext4_proptest_dir_entry_actual_size_aligned` only pins the two
     weakest invariants (`>= 8` and `% 4 == 0`). NOT pinned:
       MR-A — kernel formula equivalence: actual_size(n) ==
              ((u32::from(n) + 11) & !3) as usize.
       MR-B — monotonicity: actual_size is non-decreasing in name_len.
       MR-C — step bounded: |actual_size(n+1) - actual_size(n)| ∈ {0, 4}.
       MR-D — 4-byte step every 4 names: every 4 increments of
              name_len produces exactly one +4 step in actual_size.
       MR-E — boundary values: actual_size(0) == 8 and actual_size(255) == 264.

  2. `Ext4FileType::from_raw` (crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs:3061):
     total mapping from u8 to enum. The bd-343v3 fixed-input test
     pins values 0-7 round-trip and >= EXT4_FT_MAX → Unknown.
     NOT pinned in the proptest layer:
       MR-F — variant roundtrip: for every variant v,
              from_raw(v as u8) == v.
       MR-G — boundary fallback: for every raw u8 not in [0, MAX),
              from_raw(raw) == Unknown.

Acceptance: 5 new proptests (MR-A through MR-E for actual_size,
plus a single combined MR-FG proptest for from_raw covering both
roundtrip and boundary fallback) added to the existing `proptest!`
block in crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs's tests module. All pass
under workspace pedantic+nursery clippy.
notes: Shipped: 5 new MR proptests in crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs. MR-A (kernel-formula equivalence — pins actual_size = (name_len+11)&~3), MR-B (monotonicity), MR-C (step bounded to 0 or 4), MR-D (4-byte cycle — actual_size grows by 4 per 4 name_len increments), MR-FG (Ext4FileType::from_raw is total + round-trips on [0, EXT4_FT_MAX) + falls back to Unknown elsewhere including 0xDE). Type fix during writing: prop_assert_eq! does not support {var} format args in the expansion context — switched to plain prop_assert_eq!(left, right). Verified via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-ondisk --lib ext4_proptest_dir_entry_actual_size_matches_kernel_macro and ext4_proptest_file_type_from_raw_total_and_round_trips.

title: ffs-ondisk: is_reserved_inode predicate lacks proptest MR coverage
description:
Finding (via /testing-metamorphic skill, sixth visit, different
target): `is_reserved_inode(first_ino, ino) -> bool`
(crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs:135) is the public fail-closed
predicate added by bd-3ydm6 that mirrors the kernel
`ext4_is_reserved_inode` helper. It currently has ONE fixed-input
test (`is_reserved_inode_matches_kernel_contract`) covering ~20
hand-picked values. The full input space (u32 × u32) is unexplored.

Concrete metamorphic relations not yet pinned:

  MR-A — Zero sentinel is always reserved:
         `is_reserved_inode(first_ino, 0)` MUST be true for any
         first_ino, including first_ino == 0.

  MR-B — Cut-off boundary: for any first_ino > 0,
         is_reserved_inode(first_ino, first_ino) == false
         (first_ino itself is the FIRST user inode), and
         is_reserved_inode(first_ino, first_ino - 1) == true
         (the slot immediately below is reserved).

  MR-C — Anti-monotonicity in `first_ino`: for any ino > 0, raising
         the first_ino threshold can only keep `ino` reserved or
         newly-reserve it — never un-reserve. Formally:
         `first_ino_a <= first_ino_b` implies
         `is_reserved_inode(first_ino_a, ino) <= is_reserved_inode(first_ino_b, ino)`
         (where false < true).

A regression that flipped the comparator (e.g., changed `<` to
`<=`) or dropped the zero-sentinel branch would fail at least one
of these MRs. The fixed-input test catches most concrete cases but
proptest scale catches subtle off-by-one regressions across the
full u32 × u32 space.

Acceptance: 3 new proptests in the existing proptest! block in
crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs covering MR-A through MR-C.
notes: Shipped: 3 new MR proptests in crates/ffs-ondisk/src/ext4.rs (ext4_proptest_is_reserved_inode_zero_sentinel for MR-A, ext4_proptest_is_reserved_inode_strict_cutoff for MR-B pinning strict-less-than boundary, ext4_proptest_is_reserved_inode_anti_monotonic_in_first_ino for MR-C). Pairs with bd-3ydm6 (the predicate itself) — those covered ~20 fixed-input cases; these exercise the full u32 × u32 input space. Verified via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-ondisk --lib ext4_proptest_is_reserved_inode (3 passed).

title: [parity][corruption] btrfs file-data writes never populate the csum tree — data unreadable by the kernel on datasum filesystems
description: btrfs_create (crates/ffs-core/src/lib.rs:16109) creates inodes with flags:0 — i.e. WITHOUT BTRFS_INODE_NODATASUM, so they are datasum (the btrfs default, where the kernel verifies a crc32c per data block on every read). The write path emits BTRFS_ITEM_EXTENT_DATA items for the file's data extents (lib.rs ~6126/14522/14566/...), but NOTHING in production ever inserts EXTENT_CSUM items into the csum tree (BTRFS_CSUM_TREE_OBJECTID=7): an exhaustive grep for csum-tree writes (EXTENT_CSUM / csum_tree / CSUM_TREE_OBJECTID) finds only constants, parsing, and verify_tree_block_checksum (metadata, unrelated) — zero data-csum insertion. NODATASUM is only set via the ext4->btrfs flag translation when FS_NOCOW_FL is present (lib.rs:193), not for normal files. CONSEQUENCE: every data block FrankenFS writes to a datasum btrfs has NO checksum-tree entry, so the Linux kernel returns EIO ('csum failed'/'no csum found') when reading it back, and btrfs check reports 'there is no csum item for ...'. FrankenFS-written btrfs file data is effectively unreadable by real btrfs. Same class as the ext4 stamping gaps (bd-o3wif/bd-fwph3/bd-vdi91) but at the DATA level and for btrfs. FIX (large, COW-machinery): during btrfs commit, for each datasum inode's newly-written data extent (disk_bytenr,len), compute crc32c of each sectorsize block and insert BTRFS_EXTENT_CSUM_KEY items (objectid=BTRFS_EXTENT_CSUM_OBJECTID=-10/0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF6, type=EXTENT_CSUM, offset=disk_bytenr, value=packed crc32c array) into the csum tree via the same COW path that builds fs_tree/extent_tree (WriteDependencyDag), track the csum-tree root, and reference it in the superblock (csum_root, already serialized). Honor csum_type (crc32c default; note btrfs tree-block serialize at ffs-btrfs/writeback.rs:1939 also hardcodes crc32c regardless of csum_type — separate smaller gap). Interim option: set BTRFS_INODE_NODATASUM on inodes FrankenFS writes data to (parity-lossy but kernel-readable). 3. COMMIT csum_tree in btrfs_full_transaction_commit, mirroring the EXTENT_TREE block (lib.rs ~15824-15990): WriteDependencyDag -> alloc_metadata_for_* -> serialize+write nodes -> create/patch CSUM_TREE(7) ROOT_ITEM in root_tree (BEFORE root_tree is committed).

title: [parity] ext4 directory-block CRC32C not stamped on dir modifications — e2fsck-dirty on metadata_csum
description: Found while scoping the bd-gauub htree write-half. FrankenFS reserves the 12-byte directory-block checksum tail on metadata_csum images (ext4_dir_reserved_tail=12) but NEVER stamps the actual CRC32C: ffs_dir::add_entry/remove_entry write the tail checksum field as 0 (no csum seed available), and ffs-core had ZERO callers of stamp_dir_block_checksum. So every FrankenFS directory modification leaves a stale/zero dir-block checksum -> e2fsck reports a directory-block CRC32C mismatch. Same class as bd-fwph3 (xattr block csum) and bd-vdi91 (bitmap csum). CONFIRMED by a RED test: after fs.create on a metadata_csum image, verify_dir_block_checksum on the root dir block failed with InvalidField{dir_checksum, CRC32C mismatch}. FIXED for the create/add + entry-removal paths via a stamp_ext4_dir_block helper (gated on has_metadata_csum, keyed on the owning dir inode ino+generation) called before each dir-block write in ext4_add_dir_entry (both the add-to-existing-block and new-block sites) and ext4_unlink_impl; RED->GREEN regression test dir_block_checksum_stays_valid_after_create_metadata_csum_bd_gauub covers create + entry removal. REMAINING (same bug, follow-up): the rename path (ext4_rename) writes several dir blocks (the moved dir dotdot update -> child inode ino/gen; remove old-name from old parent; add new-name to new parent; remove existing target) each needing stamp_ext4_dir_block with the correct owning-dir ino+gen; also verify the e2compr/indirect dir-write paths. Sites identified at lib.rs ~12826 (dotdot update [child]), ~12881 (remove existing [new_parent]), plus old-name removal + new-name add. Needs per-site ino/gen care + rename csum tests + ideally an e2fsck round-trip.
close_reason: Rename-path follow-up landed in 2b2ae110. All four ext4_rename dir-block writes now stamp CRC32C with the correct owning-dir ino+gen before write: moved dir '..' update (child ino, lib.rs:12847->12992), remove-existing-target from new_parent (12889->12894), remove-old-name from src_parent (12963->12964), and new-name add via ext4_add_dir_entry (already stamping at 10976/11085). Regression test rename_keeps_dir_block_checksums_valid_bd_x4icj is GREEN on rch. e2compr dir-write is N/A (e2compr is regular-file-only); indirect-mapped dirs have no metadata_csum (csum mandates extents) so the has_metadata_csum-gated stamp correctly skips them. create/add/remove paths were closed in 5929fd91.

title: ext4 orphan recovery leaks indirect-file blocks on interrupted-truncate path
description: Follow-on to bd-c7t59. maybe_recover_ext4_orphans has two paths: links_count==0 calls delete_inode (fixed by bd-c7t59) but links_count>0 (interrupted-truncate orphan) only completed the truncate for EXTENTS_FL files via truncate_extents. A legacy INDIRECT-mapped file recorded for truncate-completion leaked all its blocks beyond the recorded size on mount recovery. Kernel-image-reachable. FIX: added ffs_inode::truncate_indirect_blocks (device-agnostic range free: free_indirect_subtree_range recursive single/double/triple, frees data+empty-metadata >= cutoff, zeroes slots, returns freed count; self-guards via inode_uses_indirect_blocks) wired into orphan recovery else branch parallel to truncate_extents + i_blocks accounting. PROOF: truncate_indirect_blocks_frees_range_and_zeroes_slots unit test (frees direct[1]+single-indirect data+root=3, slots cleared, free_blocks consistent). ffs-inode 132, ffs-core 964.
close_reason: done

title: add mounted-path ext4 symlink target PATH_MAX boundary and ENAMETOOLONG coverage
description: Survey finding: ext4 symlink creation/readback success is covered on the mounted path, and ffs-core already rejects empty or >PATH_MAX targets with ENAMETOOLONG while accepting the exact PATH_MAX boundary, but fuse_e2e does not freeze that operator-visible contract. Scope: add mounted-path ext4 probes that create a PATH_MAX-sized symlink target successfully, reject an empty target and an over-limit target with ENAMETOOLONG, and verify no stray entries appear after rejection. Acceptance: fuse_e2e proves ext4 symlink target-length boundary behavior on the real mount surface.

title: Tighten btrfs crash-matrix contract ID validation
description: check_e2e_contract accepts malformed crash_matrix IDs whose two-character point token is not numeric, so FEATURE_PARITY drift rows can false-pass when the label appears in backing sources. Require NN_ numeric point IDs and cover malformed IDs.

title: perf(btrfs): bound on-disk read_file walk to the read window (complete bd-4milp)
description: The on-disk (read-only mount) read_file path walked ALL of an inode's items via walk_btrfs_fs_tree_object then filtered EXTENT_DATA, materialising every extent regardless of the read window. The COW path already window-bounds via floor_key (bd-4milp); the on-disk path did not. Fix: walk_btrfs_fs_tree_range over [ (inode,0,0), (inode,EXTENT_DATA,offset+size) ) so the walk fetches the inode item + only the extents that can overlap [offset,offset+size). Asymptotic O(inode extents)->O(extents up to window) for large fragmented files; neutral on small files. Isomorphic (extents past the window cannot overlap; assembly skips non-overlapping; output pre-zeroed for holes) — proven byte-identical by the full from_device read suite (holes/prealloc/offset). Measurement basis: direct analogy to the measured 159x COW upper-bound c98b5291; no isolated on-disk read criterion harness exists yet (see follow-up).

The most important user-facing invariant is that no irreversible image mutation happens until preflight, dry-run evidence, backup/snapshot guidance, confidence threshold, and rollback/refusal policy all agree.

title: perf(extent): evaluate latch-free / RCU-style reader-non-blocking extent tree (alien §8.7 Bw-tree)
description: DEEP STRUCTURAL SWING (alien-graveyard §8.7 Bw-Trees / Latch-Free Delta Trees; the highest-ambition unharvested primitive after cc verified the quick veins are mined W142-146). Hypothesis: the in-memory extent / COW btree path may block concurrent READERS during writes (lock-based). A latch-free delta-update or RCU/epoch-based read path would let readers proceed without blocking on writers, improving concurrent read+write throughput on a multi-threaded FUSE workload. PROOF OBLIGATIONS: (1) FIRST measure — confirm readers actually block writers today (audit the lock model around the extent/COW tree + InMemoryCowBtrfsTree) AND build a CONCURRENT read+write throughput benchmark (N reader threads + M writer threads); a single-thread bench won't show this. (2) Isomorphism: linearizable, same observable order as the lock-based tree; MVCC snapshot semantics preserved. (3) Memory reclamation safe (epoch/EBR — note: artifacts/benchmarks/ebr_memory_usage.json suggests EBR already exists in the codebase, reuse it). CAVEATS: large careful change to a correctness-critical concurrent structure; do deliberately with a design doc, NOT a within-the-hour lever. Target: ≥2.0 on concurrent read throughput under write contention. Alternatives surveyed + rejected this session: bd-jzh0d inline names (MEASURED 1.42x), intra-extent LZO-segment parallelism (ratio≥2.0 but negligible-absolute on small single-extent LZO files = micro-lever), SWAR bitmap (already optimal), O(N2) scans (none in uncontested crates).
close_reason: Delivered the reader-non-blocking goal via RwLock (9bffc877), the pragmatic realization of the §8.7 Bw-tree idea without the lock-free rewrite. Switched OpenFs::{btrfs,ext4}_alloc_state from Mutex to parking_lot::RwLock: 48 read-only paths (read/lookup/getattr/readdir/fiemap) take shared .read() and descend the COW/extent tree concurrently across the 8 FUSE worker threads; 86 mutating sites take .write(). read/write split = existing let/let-mut binding, compiler-enforced. Concurrent A/B (8 threads, btrfs_alloc_rwlock bench): mutex 19.847ms -> rwlock 5.794ms = 3.43x. 1104 ffs-core tests pass, clippy+fmt clean. Full lock-free Bw-tree would add marginal benefit over RwLock at large rewrite cost; not pursuing.

title: perf(io): ext4 read_contiguous_into_with_scope — zero-copy ranged read into output (ext4 data read had 2 allocs + 2 copies/block)
description: ext4 file-data read (extent path ~9711, indirect path ~10893) calls read_contiguous_blocks_with_scope which returns Vec<Vec<u8>>: device read into Vec<BlockBuf> (alloc/block) then .map(as_slice().to_vec()) (2nd alloc+copy/block), then the caller memcpys each Vec<u8> into the output buf (2nd copy/block). So an ext4 sequential read does 2 allocs + 2 copies PER BLOCK on top of the coalesced device read — worse than the btrfs path fixed in bd-dy41g (1 alloc + 1 copy). Add read_contiguous_into_with_scope(cx, scope, start, dst: &mut [u8]) mirroring read_contiguous_blocks_with_scope's two-layer overlay resolution (scope tx-staged/snapshot + dev MvccBlockDevice) but reading base-gap runs DIRECTLY into dst sub-slices via the bd-dy41g read_contiguous_into primitive (zero per-block alloc/copy) and copying overlay blocks into their dst sub-slices. Wire the extent (9711) + indirect (10893) read sites; leave the dir-block caller (9829, needs per-block Vecs for the data-block cache + parse). Same proven primitive (read_contiguous bench 32.8x), ext4 win is larger (extra Vec<Vec<u8>> layer eliminated). Isomorphic: from_device ext4 read suite byte-identical.
close_reason: Shipped read_contiguous_into_with_scope (01fed27d): ext4 extent + indirect file-read sites now read contiguous runs directly into the output buffer (was Vec<BlockBuf>->Vec<Vec<u8>>->copy = 2 allocs + 2 copies/block). Scope-aware overlay (tx-staged + snapshot) preserved, base-gap runs via bd-dy41g read_contiguous_into. A/B (read_contiguous bench, 1MiB): 1.83ms->44.98us (40.7x). title: ffs-types: BTRFS_CSUM_TYPE_* constants lack kernel-conformance test
description:
Finding (via /testing-conformance-harnesses skill, sixth visit,
different target): crates/ffs-types/src/lib.rs declares 4 btrfs
checksum-type constants:

  pub const BTRFS_CSUM_TYPE_CRC32C: u16 = 0;
  pub const BTRFS_CSUM_TYPE_XXHASH64: u16 = 1;
  pub const BTRFS_CSUM_TYPE_SHA256: u16 = 2;
  pub const BTRFS_CSUM_TYPE_BLAKE2B: u16 = 3;

Each mirrors a kernel macro from `fs/btrfs/btrfs_tree.h`. The
btrfs superblock parser uses these for checksum dispatch via
`validate_supported_csum_type` (crates/ffs-ondisk/src/btrfs.rs:249).
Currently only CRC32C is supported by the Rust port; the other 3
are explicitly rejected at parse time.

There is **no kernel-conformance test** pinning the values to their
canonical kernel macros. A regression that swapped, e.g.,
BTRFS_CSUM_TYPE_CRC32C (0) and BTRFS_CSUM_TYPE_XXHASH64 (1) would
make the parser silently reject every CRC32C image and
masquerade-accept every xxhash64 image — both fatal contracts.

Pairs with bd-khzn4 (BTRFS_*_TREE_OBJECTID kernel-conformance test),
bd-f0q7n (BTRFS_ITEM_* item-key constants), bd-k81lq (ext4 reserved-
inode constants), and bd-343v3 (ext4 file-type constants). Same
pattern.

Acceptance: a kernel-conformance unit test in
crates/ffs-types/src/lib.rs's `tests` module that pins each of the
4 constants to its kernel-macro value, plus a strict-monotonic
sortedness invariant 0..=3 that catches any future renumbering.
notes: Shipped: kernel-conformance unit test btrfs_csum_type_constants_match_kernel_header in crates/ffs-types/src/lib.rs's tests module. Pins all 4 BTRFS_CSUM_TYPE_* u16 constants (CRC32C=0 / XXHASH64=1 / SHA256=2 / BLAKE2B=3) against fs/btrfs/btrfs_tree.h, strict-monotonic ascending ordering, and contiguous-range invariant (max - min == 3). Pairs with bd-khzn4 / bd-f0q7n (btrfs tree objectids + item keys), bd-k81lq / bd-343v3 (ext4 reserved inodes + file types). Verified via rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-types --lib btrfs_csum_type_constants_match_kernel_header.

title: btrfs delete/overwrite corrupts SHARED (reflink/snapshot) data extents: free_extent is not refcount-aware
description: free_extent (ffs-btrfs) unconditionally extent_tree.delete(EXTENT_ITEM) + delete_backrefs_for_extent (removes ALL EXTENT_DATA_REF/TREE_BLOCK_REF) + decrements bg used_bytes by the FULL size — it does not honor the EXTENT_ITEM refs count. On a kernel-created image with SHARED data extents (reflink / cp --reflink, snapshots, CoW partial-overwrite where head+tail share one disk extent with refs>1), deleting (btrfs_purge_inode -> btrfs_collect/execute_purge_plan) or overwriting (btrfs_overwrite ~16978) one referencing file frees the extent + all backrefs while OTHER files still reference it -> freed space gets reused, other references read garbage, btrfs check reports backpointer/refcount mismatch = CORRUPTION + data loss. Reachable: load_btrfs_alloc_state (lib.rs 5033) seeds the FULL on-disk extent tree incl backrefs, and btrfs RW has no shared-extent guard. FrankenFS's OWN files are SAFE (insert_data_extent_item sets refs=1/count=1; overwrite-split allocates fresh extents per segment via btrfs_insert_regular_extent_segment, extent_offset=0, distinct disk_bytenr). FULL FIX: make free_extent refcount-aware — read EXTENT_ITEM refs (first u64 of item data) + the specific EXTENT_DATA_REF/SHARED_DATA_REF count; if refs>1 decrement (rewrite EXTENT_ITEM + drop only THIS inode's backref) instead of deleting; only delete EXTENT_ITEM + free space when refs reach 0; adjust bg used_bytes only on true free. Apply to purge AND overwrite paths. INTERIM SAFE GUARD (this commit): atomic preflight in btrfs_collect_purge_plan via alloc.extent_alloc.get_extent_data_refs(disk_bytenr) sum>1 -> refuse the delete with UnsupportedFeature BEFORE any mutation (collect is read-only) so a shared-extent delete fails cleanly instead of corrupting. Guard does not cover SHARED_DATA_REF-only (snapshot) extents (EXTENT_DATA_REF count may be 1); full EXTENT_ITEM.refs read is the complete fix. Overwrite path still needs the same guard/fix (noted).
notes: CLOSED (a98cf97b): all data-extent free paths now refcount-aware. Delete (b779c30b) + overwrite/punch/collapse/insert (a98cf97b) via shared btrfs_free_or_drop_extent_ref helper. Validated on-disk by TWO real-btrfs-check E2Es (delete + overwrite reflink->modify->check clean, refs 2->1, src intact) + 4 in-memory drop tests. ffs-core lib 976/976. The corruption bug (free_extent not refcount-aware orphaning shared reflink/snapshot extents) is fully fixed across every mutation path.
close_reason: done

title: V1.2 waivers are now stale; refine gate detection to use active-row check
description:
# V1.2 waivers are now stale; refine gate detection to use active-row check

Discovered by beads compliance audit pass `2026-05-10T03-20-31Z` after closing `bd-ckivp` (V1.2 program gate completion-debt bead). The waiver document `docs/release/V1.2_test_waivers.md` lists two historical failures that have since been fixed by the swarm; both tests now PASS as of 2026-05-10. The gate's coarse `[[ -s ]]` detection in `scripts/e2e/ffs_v12_program_gate_e2e.sh:242` will keep emitting `PASS-WITH-WAIVERS` until the file is emptied or removed, even though no active waivers exist.

## Verification (this audit)

```
$ rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-alloc proptest_empty_bitmap_nonzero_count_has_no_free
test tests::proptest_empty_bitmap_nonzero_count_has_no_free ... ok
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; ...

$ rch exec -- cargo test -p ffs-core btrfs_write_fallocate
running 28 tests
test tests::btrfs_write_fallocate_basic ... ok
test tests::btrfs_write_fallocate_extends_file ... ok
test tests::btrfs_write_fallocate_keep_size_does_not_extend_file ... ok
test tests::btrfs_write_fallocate_collapse_range_shifts_tail_and_shrinks_file ... ok
test tests::btrfs_write_fallocate_punch_hole_zeroes_data ... ok
... (all 28 pass)
test result: ok. 28 passed; 0 failed
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Refine gate detection.** Update `scripts/e2e/ffs_v12_program_gate_e2e.sh:242` to detect *active waiver rows* rather than file non-emptiness. Suggested implementation: scan the `## Active Waivers` table (or whatever section header is canonicalized) and count data rows; PASS-WITH-WAIVERS only if ≥1 data row.
- [ ] **Update `docs/release/V1.2_test_waivers.md`.** Either:
  - (a) Remove the two stale entries (proptest_empty_bitmap, btrfs_write_fallocate) since both tests now pass, leaving the file with header + explanation + empty `## Active Waivers` table, OR
  - (b) Mark the entries as `RESOLVED` with a citation to the verifying commit + cargo test exit codes, in a separate `## Resolved Waivers (historical)` section that does NOT count toward gate detection.
- [ ] **Re-run V1.2 gate locally.** With the above changes in place, invoke `./scripts/e2e/ffs_v12_program_gate_e2e.sh` (or `FFS_V12_PROGRAM_GATE_SMOKE=1`) and confirm `program_gate_manifest.json` emits `release_recommendation: "PROCEED"` (not `PASS-WITH-WAIVERS`) when all scenarios pass.
- [ ] **Add unit test.** Extend `crates/ffs-harness/tests/program_gate_v12.rs` with a test asserting that an empty waiver doc (or a doc with only resolved entries) produces `release_recommendation: "PROCEED"` while a doc with active entries produces `PASS-WITH-WAIVERS`. The current test only validates manifest schema — extend it to validate the waiver-detection contract.
- [ ] **Update `docs/release/V1.2_release_notes.md`** to reflect the refined waiver-detection contract.
- [ ] Workspace gates: `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`. Must pass with 0 failures.

## Discovery context

This is a follow-on bead from audit pass `2026-05-10T03-20-31Z`. The audit:
1. Identified `bd-m5wf.10` as PARTIAL (V1.2 program gate not actually executed; 2 admitted test failures).
2. Created `bd-ckivp` as completion-debt; the swarm implemented it (commit `0eae8c9d`).
3. The waiver doc was created with the 2 admitted failures so the gate could emit `PASS-WITH-WAIVERS` rather than silently passing.
4. The swarm subsequently fixed both failures (this bead's verification block above).
5. Now the waiver doc is stale — the gate would erroneously report `PASS-WITH-WAIVERS` instead of clean `PROCEED`.

title: [perf][no-gaps] cache Bw-tree chain length for append decisions
description: Profile-backed ffs-btree target from rch Criterion baseline on worker vmi1149989 (2026-06-02). Command: cargo bench --profile release-perf -p ffs-btree --bench bwtree_vs_locked -- --warm-up-time 1 --measurement-time 2 --sample-size 10 --noplot. Ranked gaps: mixed/bwtree/8 mean 11.472 s [11.091,11.861] vs locked_btree/8 mean 13.886 ms [12.655,15.301]; write_heavy/bwtree/8 mean 10.018 s [9.7189,10.265] vs locked_btree/8 mean 26.956 ms [25.864,27.557]; read_heavy/bwtree/8 mean 717.36 ms [695.93,736.03] vs locked_btree/8 mean 17.192 ms [16.569,18.012]. Profile/code-read symptom: MappingTable::append_delta calls chain_length(&snapshot.head) on every append, walking the growing delta chain and making 10k inserts O(n^2) before consolidation. Existing point_lookup/new_direct_lookup is already 3.4255 us vs old_materialize_then_get 4.1211 ms, so lookup is not this lever. Alien-graveyard primitive: §14.2 flat-combining/cache-hot sequential critical sections and §8.7 Bw-Trees + §14.10 EBR; harvest the practical constant-factor fix: cache per-page chain metadata next to the mapping-table head so append/consolidation decisions avoid repeated pointer chasing while retaining EBR/drop invariants. Recommendation card: Impact high because profile rows are 40x-800x slower than locked baseline; Confidence medium-high because the hot path visibly does a redundant full chain walk per append; Effort medium; EV/Score target >=2.0. One lever: add a cached per-page chain length updated only on successful head replacement, use it for append preconsolidation, consolidate skip/report, and scan_for_consolidation. Fallback: if cached length proves hard to keep isomorphic under CAS races, revert and file smaller bounded-chain-depth early-exit target. Proof obligations: identical materialized map, lookup, range_scan ordering, split/delete shadowing, consolidation result semantics, error classes, no FP/RNG; golden bwtree lookup report sha256 unchanged; rch crate-scoped tests/check/clippy/fmt and bwtree_vs_locked rebench; otherwise revert.

comments.text: REJECTED per Score>=2.0 discipline (regression). Verified PlumFern WIP: replace popcount_range with a specialized popcount_aligned_block in SuccinctBitmap::build. title: perf(ffs-core): parallelize lookup_name_with_scope serial dir-block reads (I/O-overlap)
description: ffs-core lookup_name_with_scope (lib.rs ~10876-10894) reads ext4 directory blocks SERIALLY in a for lb in 0..num_blocks loop, calling read_ext4_file_data_block_with_scope per block and searching each for the name. Each block read is independent device I/O that could overlap. The parallel sibling read_dir_with_scope (~10692-10847) already coalesces cold dir-block runs and reads them with rayon (split serial-PLAN + parallel-EXECUTE), shipped as bd-2jurz (6.01x). lookup_name_with_scope remains purely serial — every path-component resolution (FUSE lookup) on a large/cold directory pays O(dir_blocks) serial read latency. LEVER: mirror the read_dir parallel-read pattern — resolve_extent to map each logical block to phys serially (preserve order + error semantics), gather the cold/unwritten-filtered phys block list, parallel-read via rayon over the static pool, then search blocks in order for first match (early-exit semantics must be preserved: a serial search stops at first hit; with parallel reads, read all candidate blocks then scan in logical order and return first match — same result, extra reads bounded by pool). Measure on LatencyBlockDevice (sleep+delegate) like the other I/O-overlap wins. Sibling of bd-2jurz/bd-yg6tk. Target 3-6x on cold fragmented dir lookup.
close_reason: Shipped 01b84302: lookup_name_with_scope's htree-miss linear scan now parallelizes per-block reads via rayon (serial PLAN resolve_extent descent preserves order+lowest-block-error semantics; into_par_iter reads+searches; results consumed in logical-block order so first match / lowest-block error wins — isomorphic to serial early-exit). Targets negative lookups (file-create existence checks) on large non-htree/htree-stale dirs. Score 7.53x (ext4_lookup_run_overlap model: serial 21.2ms vs parallel 2.81ms, 64 blocks x 250us). 1106 ffs-core tests pass, clippy clean.

title: perf(ffs-core): btrfs_fs_tree_root_cache Mutex->RwLock for parallel read-only root resolution

LEVER: RwLock — hit path takes .read() (parallel), miss inserts under .write(). Sibling of bd-xenil (alloc-state Mutex->RwLock, 3.43x). Lower priority than the alloc-state win since the critical section is a single HashMap lookup (very short) — RwLock may be borderline vs sharding; measure A/B at 8 readers, prefer sharding if RwLock dips <2.0 (W148 lesson: short sections want lock-striping not RwLock). Only consulted when btrfs_alloc_state is None (read-only).
close_reason: Rejected borderline sub-2.0 (W148 precedent). Hit-path is a SINGLE HashMap::get of btrfs_fs_tree_root_cache (~1-2 entry subvol map) returning a copied u64 — the too-short-critical-section regime where W148 measured RwLock at 1.84x worst case (reader-count atomic ping-pong dominates); map far too small to shard. Real read cost is device I/O elsewhere. If revisited, fix is eager mount-time resolution into an immutable lock-free map, not RwLock.

CAVEAT (why P3, not shipped): GDs pack ~64/4KB block + sharded cache → only ~group_count/64 DISTINCT cold block reads (rest cache hits), muting the win after warm-up; statfs is also infrequent (df/statvfs/mount-time). title: test(ffs-btrfs): free_extent rejects an unallocated extent without side effects
description: BtrfsExtentAllocator::free_extent calls locate_extent_key first, which returns BtrfsMutationError::KeyNotFound when no EXTENT_ITEM/METADATA_ITEM exists at the given bytenr/len, so a stray or double free errors before touching block-group accounting. The zero-byte rejection is tested (extent_allocator_rejects_zero_byte_free_without_side_effects) but the not-found path is not. A regression that silently freed an unallocated extent would underflow used_bytes / corrupt free-space accounting. Add free_extent_rejects_unallocated_extent_without_side_effects: seed one allocation, free a different (never-allocated) bytenr, assert Err(KeyNotFound) and that used_bytes + delayed_ref_count are unchanged. Pure, no mocks.

title: test(ffs-block): empty contiguous byte-block operations are no-ops
description: ByteBlockDevice contiguous-read/write overrides currently have empty-input fast paths that are not directly covered. Pin the contract that empty read_contiguous_blocks/read_contiguous_into/write_contiguous_blocks are successful no-ops even when start is outside the device range, do not issue inner byte reads/writes, and still preserve cooperative Cx checkpointing on return. Acceptance: add focused ffs-block unit coverage using the existing in-memory byte device helper and mirror entry/exit checkpoint structure in each empty fast path.
close_reason: VERIFIED (cc): byte_block_device_empty_contiguous_ops_are_noops_at_invalid_start (ffs-block:7411) pins empty read/write_contiguous no-op even when start out of range. cargo test: ok.

title: test(ffs-block): pin the specific overflow error in MemIoEngine range-overflow tests
description: mem_engine_rejects_overflowing_read_range/write_range submit offset=u64::MAX (len 1), which makes start+len overflow usize and must return the 'memory I/O range overflows usize' InvalidInput error (the checked_add branch, distinct from the end>capacity out-of-bounds branch). Both tests only assert matches!(_, IoCompletion::Error(_)), so they'd still pass if a regression removed the overflow guard and the request instead fell through to a different error. Strengthen both to assert the error message identifies the range overflow, pinning the specific branch. No mocks.
close_reason: VERIFIED (cc): mem_engine_rejects_overflowing_read_range/write_range (io_engine.rs:487/510) pin checked_add 'memory I/O range overflows usize' InvalidInput. cargo test: 2 passed.

title: fix(ffs-block): default vectored byte reads skip zero-length iovecs
description: ByteDevice::read_vectored_exact_at's default scalar fallback calls read_exact_at for every IoSliceMut, including zero-length slices. Implementers that rely on the default should not observe synthetic scalar reads for empty iovecs; only non-empty ranges should advance through the device. Add focused coverage with a scalar-only byte device that counts read_exact_at calls and verifies zero-length leading/trailing iovecs neither trigger reads nor disturb offsets for following non-empty buffers.
close_reason: VERIFIED (cc): default ByteDevice::read_vectored_exact_at skips zero-length iovecs; test default_vectored_read_skips_zero_length_iovecs (7785). cargo test: ok.

title: test(ffs-error): pin the io::ErrorKind -> errno fallback table in to_errno
description: FfsError::to_errno maps Self::Io(err) via err.raw_os_error(), falling back to an ErrorKind->errno table (NotFound->ENOENT, PermissionDenied->EACCES, AlreadyExists->EEXIST, WouldBlock->EAGAIN, InvalidInput/InvalidData->EINVAL, TimedOut->ETIMEDOUT, Interrupted->EINTR, others->EIO) when the io::Error has no OS errno (synthetic errors from io::Error::new). errno_mapping_covers_all_variants only tests io::Error::other (EIO fallback) and io_error_preserves_raw_os_error tests the raw-OS path; the ErrorKind fallback table is untested. A regression mapping e.g. NotFound->EIO would surface the wrong errno to FUSE/userspace. Add errno_mapping_covers_io_error_kinds asserting each ErrorKind maps to its expected errno. Pure, no mocks.
close_reason: VERIFIED (cc): errno_mapping_covers_io_error_kinds + io_error_kind_mapping_without_raw_errno (ffs-error lib.rs:370/731) pin the io::ErrorKind->errno fallback table. cargo test: ok.

title: fix(ffs-journal): native COW open rejects malformed first record
description: Fallback quality work after clean br ready returned no ready rows. NativeCowJournal::open scans COW records to discover the first free slot, but currently treats any Format error from decode_cow_record as a clean tail. If slot 0 has COW magic with an unsupported version or unknown kind, open incorrectly accepts the corrupted head as an empty journal and can overwrite it. Make open fail closed before any valid record has been observed while preserving clean-tail discovery after existing records. Add a no-mock MemBlockDevice regression.
close_reason: VERIFIED (cc): native_cow_open_rejects_malformed_first_record (ffs-journal lib.rs:3993). cargo test: ok.

title: test(ffs-ondisk): pin dx_hash unknown/HALF_MD4_UNSIGNED version fallback arm
description: dx_hash dispatches hash_version to legacy/half_md4/tea (signed+unsigned), with a  arm that routes DX_HASH_HALF_MD4_UNSIGNED (4) and ANY unknown version to half_md4 unsigned (matching the kernel fallback so dirs with unusual/future hash_version fields still hash deterministically). dx_hash_dispatcher only covers versions 0/1/2; the  fallback arm is untested. A regression that panicked or mis-routed unknown versions would break htree lookups on such directories. Add dx_hash_dispatcher_unknown_version_falls_back_to_half_md4_unsigned: assert version 4 and several unknown versions (6,7,99,200,255) all hash identically (same  arm). Pure, no mocks.
close_reason: VERIFIED (cc): dx_hash_dispatcher_unknown_version_falls_back_to_half_md4_unsigned (ext4.rs:14367). cargo test: ok.

title: test(ffs-ondisk): pin dx_hash legacy-unsigned and tea-unsigned dispatch arms (v3, v5)
description: dx_hash routes hash_version 3 to legacy unsigned and 5 to tea unsigned. dx_hash_dispatcher only covers 0/1/2 and dx_hash_signed_vs_unsigned only exercises the direct half_md4 functions, so the v3/v5 dispatch arms are untested. A regression mis-routing them would corrupt htree lookups on directories using those hash versions. Add dx_hash_dispatcher_legacy_and_tea_unsigned_arms: assert dx_hash(3) equals (normalize(dx_hash_legacy(name,false).major), legacy minor) and dx_hash(5) equals (normalize(dx_hash_tea(name,false).major), tea minor) for a high-bit name, directly verifying the routing. Pure, no mocks.
close_reason: VERIFIED (cc): dx_hash_dispatcher_legacy_and_tea_unsigned_arms (ext4.rs:14386). cargo test: ok.

title: test(ffs-journal): pin FC short-payload guards for DEL_RANGE/CREAT/LINK/UNLINK
description: parse_fc_operation guards each fast-commit tag with a payload-length check (DelRange>=12, Creat/Link>=8, Unlink>=8) and returns None when too short, so replay skips the op and flags fallback instead of panicking on out-of-bounds indexing of a truncated journal record. Short-payload guards are tested only for ADD_RANGE/INODE/HEAD/TAIL; DEL_RANGE(0x02), CREAT(0x03), LINK(0x04), UNLINK(0x05) are untested. A regression removing one guard would panic during recovery of a malformed fast-commit journal. Add replay_short_del_creat_link_unlink_tags_require_fallback: frame each tag in a valid HEAD/TAIL transaction with a too-short payload and assert operations empty + fallback_required. No mocks.
close_reason: VERIFIED (cc): replay_short_del_creat_link_unlink_tags_require_fallback (ffs-journal:2289). cargo test: ok.

title: test(ffs-ondisk): pin validate_mirror_stripes RAID1C3/RAID1C4 insufficient-stripe rejection
description: validate_mirror_stripes (btrfs.rs:866, called from sys_chunk_array parsing) requires RAID1C3 chunks to carry at least 3 stripes and RAID1C4 at least 4, rejecting with a profile-specific InvalidField reason otherwise. It is never called from any test (only its 2 parse callers), so the RAID1C3/RAID1C4 stripe-count arms are untested; only data_copies() is tested for those profiles. A regression mis-counting would let a malformed multi-mirror chunk parse. BtrfsChunkEntry has public fields, so add validate_mirror_stripes_rejects_insufficient_raid1c3_and_raid1c4: build chunks with too few stripes, assert the specific rejections, and assert the minimum valid counts pass. Pure, no mocks.
close_reason: VERIFIED (cc): validate_mirror_stripes_rejects_insufficient_raid1c3_and_raid1c4 (btrfs.rs:6280). cargo test: ok.

title: test(ffs-ondisk): pin validate_superblock_tree_level rejection above BTRFS_MAX_LEVEL
description: validate_superblock_tree_level (btrfs.rs:337) rejects a superblock root_level/chunk_root_level/log_root_level greater than BTRFS_MAX_LEVEL (7), preserving the field name in the InvalidField error. It is called only from superblock parsing and never directly tested; the existing tree-level proptest validates the tree-NODE header level, a different function. So the superblock-level reject branch is untested and the superblock rejection suite has no invalid-tree-level case. A regression accepting an out-of-range level would let a corrupt superblock parse and drive a bad tree descent. Add validate_superblock_tree_level_rejects_above_max: assert levels 0 and 7 pass, 8 and u8::MAX are rejected with the field preserved. Pure, no mocks.

description: validate_dir_block_slice_len rejects a zero block_size and a directory block slice longer than the declared block_size, returning InvalidField. It is called from directory-block parsing but never directly tested, and the parse tests only feed valid slices, so both reject branches are uncovered. A regression would let a malformed/oversized dir block slice through into entry parsing. Add validate_dir_block_slice_len_rejects_bad_inputs: assert block_size 0 rejected, an oversized slice rejected with the specific reasons, and in-range slices (including empty and exactly block_size) accepted. Pure, no mocks.

title: test(ffs-ondisk): pin verify_bitmap_free_count partial-byte masking and short-bitmap rejection
description: verify_bitmap_free_count masks the trailing partial byte when total_bits is not a multiple of 8 (counting only the low rem_bits) and rejects a bitmap shorter than ceil(total_bits/8) with InsufficientData. Both existing proptests use total_bits = byte_len*8 (always a multiple of 8) with full-size bitmaps, so neither the partial-byte mask nor the short-bitmap branch is covered. A mask regression would mis-count free bits in the last group (non-byte-aligned), defeating corruption detection. Add verify_bitmap_free_count_masks_partial_byte_and_rejects_short: total_bits=12 with high-nibble bits set but ignored, a mismatch case, and a short bitmap -> InsufficientData. Pure, no mocks.
close_reason: VERIFIED (cc): verify_bitmap_free_count_masks_partial_byte_and_rejects_short (ext4.rs:9216) + proptest :18770. cargo test: ok.

description: Via the public validate_v1 entry, two reject branches are uncovered: validate_geometry_layout rejects inodes_count greater than group_count*inodes_per_group (s_inodes_count), and validate_v1 rejects a superblock missing the required FILETYPE incompat feature (feature_incompat).
