title: test(harness): --client-threads is accepted and silently discarded on 8 of 9 workloads — fail closed instead of running a different experiment than requested
description:
--client-threads IS ACCEPTED AND SILENTLY DISCARDED for three of the nine workloads.

Workload::client_threads (crates/ffs-harness/src/bin/ffs_mounted_kernel_bench.rs:183)
returns DEFAULT_PARALLEL_THREADS unconditionally for ReaddirStat8, ParallelRead8 and
ParallelRead8ColdCache, and 1 unconditionally for WarmStat, CreateDeleteStorm,
FsyncJournalCommit, BulkDurableWrite and XattrGetListReport. Only ParallelMetadataWrite
returns the configured value.

The CLI parses --client-threads, validates it, and throws it away. Nothing warns.

COST, measured: I ran a 1/2/4/8 thread sweep as the discriminator for bd-o83z3 and every
cell ran at 8 threads. Eight comparator runs, ~15 minutes of a contended host, and an
invalid experiment that would have produced a confident wrong answer had the second
error in that bead not been caught independently.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY A BUG: the hardcoding is deliberate and defensible. These workloads
are DEFINED at a thread count — "readdir-stat-8t" says 8 in its name — and letting the
flag change it would silently redefine the workload and make rows non-comparable across
runs. The bank's comparability depends on that.

SO THE FIX IS NOT "honour the flag". Options, cheapest first:
  1. REJECT the flag when the workload ignores it. `--client-threads 4 --workload
     readdir-stat-8t` should fail closed with "readdir-stat-8t is defined at 8 threads;
     --client-threads applies only to parallel-metadata-write", exactly as the harness
     already fails closed on --managed-unmount-timeout-secs with --runtime-mode standard.
     This is the smallest change and it converts a silent discard into a refusal.
  2. Or accept it and rename the workload per thread count, which is a much bigger
     change to the bank's identifiers and probably not worth it.

MITIGATION THAT ALREADY WORKS: the report is honest. Every run prints
requested_client_threads=N,actual_observed_worker_threads=N with the EFFECTIVE value, so
a reader who checks the output catches it. That is how it was caught. Worth stating in
the harness docs: read requested_client_threads in the report, do not trust the flag.

ACCEPTANCE:
  - --client-threads with a workload that ignores it fails closed, naming the workload
    and the workloads where the flag does apply
  - a test pins that refusal for at least ReaddirStat8 and ParallelMetadataWrite, so the
    two branches cannot drift
  - no change to any workload's effective thread count; this bead is about refusing a
    misleading invocation, not about making the flag work

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED (AzureBay, 2026-08-16, commit f10fbc40). --client-threads now fails closed where it cannot take effect.

THE FIX IS NOT "honour the flag", and that is the point. The hardcoding is deliberate and correct: these workloads are DEFINED at a thread count — "readdir-stat-8t" carries it in the name and in every banked row's identity — so obeying the flag would silently redefine the workload and make rows non-comparable across runs. The bank's comparability depends on it. So the invocation is refused, naming both the workload that discards the flag and the one workload where it applies, in the same shape as the existing --managed-unmount-timeout-secs refusal.

Detecting it needed one new bit: client_threads defaults to DEFAULT_PARALLEL_THREADS, so an explicit --client-threads 8 is indistinguishable from an absent flag by value. client_threads_explicit records whether it appeared on the command line.

TEST pins BOTH branches, because a refusal that silently stops applying is the same defect again: parallel-metadata-write accepts the flag AND the value reaches the workload; the other seven refuse with a message naming the flag, the workload, and where the flag does apply; and the effective thread count does not depend on the discarded value.

MY FIRST VERSION OF THE TEST FAILED FOR A REASON IT WAS NOT ABOUT: it asserted that the same workload without the flag passes validate_config outright, which trips unrelated capacity and durability requirements on several workloads. Narrowed to assert only that the client-threads refusal is ABSENT, which is the actual property under test.

GATE, precisely. The pre-narrowing run compiled on rch worker vmi1293453 and executed the test, reaching line 8333 — the incidental assertion — and failing only there. Everything before it passed: the pre-existing only_metadata_scaling_uses_configured_client_threads test, parallel-metadata-write accepting the flag with the value reaching the workload, and the refusal firing for ReaddirStat8 with a message naming the flag, the workload and parallel-metadata-write. The production change is therefore verified compiled and behaving.

NOT CLAIMED: the narrowed test has not re-run. rch refused nine consecutive attempts (no admissible workers, insufficient_total_slots=4) and the standing disk directive rules out a local build. The single unverified line is the assertion I narrowed, which is strictly weaker than the one that already passed. Worth one rch run when the fleet frees up.

title: perf(read): destination-buffer page churn is the new #1 cold-read frame — 28.91% of cycles, 17,459 faults for a 32,768-page read
description:
CONTEXT (BlackThrush/cc_ffs 2026-07-10). With xa_lock contention capped (bd-ddryj: fan-out 64 -> 16),
the cold-read frame table re-ranks completely. Fresh profile of the prebuilt release-perf binary,
production 128 KiB chunk, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=16, drop_caches per run, zero local cargo builds.

RANKED SELF-TIME, ffs T=16 (>= 0.1%):
   12.28%  _copy_to_iter            [k]  the buffered copy (inherent)
   11.81%  clear_page_erms          [k]  zero-filling fresh anonymous destination pages
    9.32%  native_queued_spin_lock_slowpath  [k]  residual xa_lock (was 42.27% at T=64)
    5.74%  asm_exc_page_fault       [k]
    2.19%  rmqueue_bulk             [k]
    2.02%  __filemap_add_folio      [k]
    1.67%  lru_gen_add_folio        [k]
    1.57%  do_anonymous_page        [k]
    1.44%  mod_memcg_lruvec_state   [k]
    1.13%  crossbeam Stealer::steal [.]  rayon work-stealing
    1.13%  zap_present_ptes         [k]
    0.94%  get_page_from_freelist   [k]
    0.80%  __alloc_frozen_pages     [k]
    0.77%  __mem_cgroup_charge      [k]

ANON-PAGE ALLOC/FAULT/ZERO CLUSTER TOTAL = 28.91% of cycles. This is the destination buffer:
allocate -> page fault -> clear_page (zero-fill) -> immediately overwritten by _copy_to_iter.
Measured: 17,459 page faults (17,385 minor) for a read of 32,768 destination pages.

HONEST WALL BASELINE (9 interleaved reps, quiet box, medians; sha256 identical across arms):
   ffs T=64 (as shipped)          42.94 ms   1.54x kernel
   ffs T=16 (best config)         34.67 ms   1.25x kernel
   raw pread, same fd model+chunk 28.20 ms
   kernel dio loop T=32           27.80 ms
  => of the 6.87 ms residual, +6.47 ms is frankenfs-attributable and only +0.40 ms is the
     buffered page-cache path. The gap has moved OUT of the kernel's page cache and INTO
     frankenfs's own allocation behaviour.

HYPOTHESIS (UNTESTED, do not assume): frankenfs allocates a fresh destination buffer per 128 KiB
chunk, so every chunk faults + zero-fills fresh anonymous pages that are then fully overwritten.
A per-thread reusable read buffer (or a buffer pool, or read_into a caller-owned dst) would keep
those pages mapped and warm, eliminating clear_page + fault + page-alloc + memcg-charge work.

WHY THIS IS NOT YET A REJECT OR A WIN -- PROXY INVALIDITY (ledger-integrity, 5feb977):
I built a raw-pread proxy (alloc-per-chunk vs reused per-thread buffer, 128 KiB, T=16, shared fd,
sha256 identical) and it showed reuse *slower* (0.957x median, 1/7 paired reps, p=1.0). THAT RESULT
IS NOT ADMISSIBLE: the proxy's alloc arm made only 2,364 page faults vs frankenfs's 17,459 (7.4x
fewer), because glibc's DYNAMIC mmap threshold makes CPython recycle the freed 128 KiB block instead
of returning it. The proxy never exercises the mechanism under test, so its null says nothing about
frankenfs. Same class of error as the earlier proxy-chunk artifact -- the arm must reproduce the
mechanism's MAGNITUDE, not just its shape.

WHAT TO DO:
 1. Find the per-chunk destination allocation in the read path (ffs-core read fan-out, and
    ffs-block BlockBuf / read_block). Confirm with a fault counter that it is the source of the
    17,459 faults (e.g. count faults for a 1-chunk read and scale).
 2. Prototype a per-thread reusable buffer / pool, or push `read_into(&mut dst)` all the way down.
 3. Measure IN-TREE, cold, arms interleaved per rep, sha256 parity, self-time recorded.
    A proxy is not acceptable for this lever -- see above.
 4. Do NOT project the wall win from the 28.91% cycle share. Projecting wall from cycle share was
    already proven invalid on this exact workload (bd-kdmu4: Model A/B predicted 1.12-1.85x,
    measurement was 1.00x; spin-wait and much of this cluster overlap device I/O).

BLOCKED ON: the same build blocker as bd-ddryj. In-tree measurement needs a modified binary run
locally under drop_caches (root). `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo build`
still does not return the artifact. Unblock by fixing rch retrieval or granting one local build.
notes:
HARNESS OVERHEAD MEASURED 2026-07-10 (BlackThrush/cc_ffs): 3.10 ms = 41% of the best-config cold-read
gap vs kernel ext4. Measured, not projected.

METADATA: binary sha256=03b7456d8cd6fa118bd214b2fdf8a03e56cac79e6768b7311613b039c8ae81eb (release-perf,
55,453,584 B); allocator tikv_jemallocator; worker = local host (perf + drop_caches need root, so no
remote worker is possible for this measurement); rch verify worker vmi1149989; cv per arm below.

REBUILT HARNESS (preader5.py). The earlier bigbuf floor was inadmissible -- it timed SLOWER than the
thing it floored. Two bugs, both mine: CPython's bytearray(n) memsets, and the allocation sat inside the
timed region. Fixes: mmap.mmap(-1,n) (kernel lazily zero-fills, which is what jemalloc alloc_zeroed gets);
destination alloc + chunk-list construction hoisted out of the timed region; one persistent pre-warmed
ThreadPoolExecutor (no thread spawn inside the timer); drop_caches outside the timer; result consumed via
XOR checksum so nothing is elided.

  cold_dst : fresh mmap INSIDE the timer -> pays the 64 MiB first-touch, exactly like ffs-cli read
  warm_dst : mmap allocated + pre-faulted BEFORE the timer -> reads only

VALIDITY GATES (all pass): identity (same XOR checksum; sha256 == kernel mount); magnitude (cold_dst
18,090 faults vs ffs 17,467); impossibility (cold_dst 31.10 ms < ffs 35.77 ms).

MEASUREMENT (9 interleaved reps, medians):
   ffs T=64 (as shipped)       42.88 ms  cv 7.7%
   ffs T=16 (best config)      35.77 ms  cv 8.6%
   floor cold_dst              31.10 ms  cv 10.7%
   floor warm_dst              28.00 ms  cv 5.7%
   kernel dio loop T=32        28.30 ms  cv 8.8%
   => destination first-touch  = 31.10 - 28.00 = 3.10 ms

HONEST GAP:
   ffs T=64: reported 1.52x -> 1.41x   harness = 3.10/14.58 = 21% of the gap
   ffs T=16: reported 1.26x -> 1.15x   harness = 3.10/ 7.47 = 41% of the gap
Also warm_dst (28.00) ~= kernel dio (28.30): a raw parallel pread into a WARM destination is already at
kernel parity. Residual filesystem overhead = 35.77 - 3.10 - 28.00 = 4.67 ms.

TOP FRAME, with the harness attributed. The 28.91% anon alloc/fault/zero cluster IS the harness. What
remains for real filesystem work at T=16:
   _copy_to_iter                     12.28%  <- ALSO paid by the warm_dst floor; cannot explain the residual
   native_queued_spin_lock_slowpath   9.32%  <- residual xa_lock (fan-out cap already cut it from 42.27%)
   crossbeam Stealer::steal           1.13%
   ext4_mpage_readpages               0.69%
The 4.67 ms residual is frankenfs's own userspace work (user CPU at T=16 = 4.5 ms, same order). perf
cannot resolve it above the 0.1% cut. Attributing it needs the harness fixed first.

(a) HARNESS HYGIENE -- do this first, it is small and it unblocks everything else:
    crates/ffs-cli/src/main.rs:2403-2407, STREAM_CHUNK = 64 MiB, `vec![0_u8; 64 MiB]`.
    Either shrink STREAM_CHUNK to the comparator's granularity, or pre-fault the buffer before the

(b) STILL OPEN: does the FUSE read path allocate per-chunk destinations? Profile through the mount,

It does NOT show that bd-kdmu4's "~2.9x slower than kernel" is an artifact: that came from a different
harness (multi-file parallel read, in-process threaded; claimed 41% pread copy tax + 27% nested-rayon

title: btrfs send drops additional hard links (only the first name is emitted)
description: generate_send_stream built inode_parents with one (parent,name) per inode (last INODE_REF item's first name won), and build_path used it for a single path. A file with multiple hard links (multiple INODE_REF items / multiple names) was thus created at only ONE path; the other hard links were silently dropped from the send stream, so the received subvolume has fewer links than the source. FIX: collect ALL (parent,name) links per inode (inode_links); the first is the primary (drives path/mkfile), and each additional link emits a Link command (newpath -> primary path) for non-directory inodes (dirs cannot be hard-linked). All parent dirs are emitted first (bd-7ucz7) so link paths resolve. Test generate_send_stream_emits_link_for_additional_hardlinks.
close_reason: done

title: symbol exchange store can rewrite an existing generation
description: Phase B audit follow-up in crates/ffs-repair/src/exchange.rs. InMemoryStore::put_symbols treats only current.generation > generation as stale; a second PutSymbols with the same group/generation but different symbols overwrites the existing repair generation. Repair generations are durable identity for self-healing symbols, so same-generation puts should be idempotent only when the payload is byte-identical and should reject conflicting payloads instead of silently changing later GetSymbols results. Fix by making same-generation same-payload puts return Stored without mutating, and same-generation different-payload puts return RepairFailed/Response::Error. Add focused tests for idempotent repeat and conflicting rewrite rejection. Validate with rch crate-scoped ffs-repair exchange tests/check/clippy and fmt.
close_reason: Completed: InMemoryStore same-generation put is now idempotent for identical symbol payloads and rejects conflicting same-generation rewrites before mutating stored symbols. Added focused exchange store tests for idempotent replay and rewrite rejection. title: [code-review] dominating_set(start_with) port still 4.84x slower than nx — wrapper overhead in G[u] access
description:
br-r37-c1-lj6bo just shipped a native port for dominating_set(start_with=...). Profile on BA200 (500 calls, 278ms total) shows G[u] access dominates:

  ncalls  cumtime  function
  35500   0.142 s  _graph_getitem_from_adj
  35500   0.078 s  __getitem__ (AtlasView)
  35500   0.072 s  __iter__   (AtlasView)
  35500   0.057 s  _atlas
  35500   0.045 s  _private_adj_mapping

~50% of total time is in the AtlasView wrapper around G[u]. Same wrapper-bypass opportunity that closed the find_cliques gap (br-r37-c1-lgyq8) and square_clustering (br-r37-c1-7t95c).

Apply same fix: when graph has no nx-private-storage and isn't a multigraph, replace set(G[start_with]) and set(G[v]) with set(_GRAPH_NEIGHBORS(G, start_with)) and set(_GRAPH_NEIGHBORS(G, v)). The set-comprehension form preserves nx's iteration order, but here we're just consuming the set so order doesn't matter for correctness — only the SET contents need to match nx.

Estimated speedup: 1.5-2x based on profile (the per-call overhead of AtlasView is a fixed cost). Combined with the prior delegate→native port (14x), final speedup vs delegate would be ~25-30x.

P1 because the dominating-set call is a frequently-used primitive and the bypass pattern is now mature (3 prior applications).

title: dijkstra_predecessor_and_distance pred dict iteration order drifts from nx
description:
fnx.dijkstra_predecessor_and_distance returns the predecessor dict with keys in distances iteration order, but nx returns it in insertion order during traversal (which differs because pred entries are populated when an edge relaxation finds a tentative path, not when the node is finalized).

Repro:
  edges = [(a,b,1),(b,c,2),(c,d,1),(a,d,5),(b,d,3)] (weighted)
  fnx.dijkstra_predecessor_and_distance(g, 'a')[0] -> {'a':[], 'b':['a'], 'c':['b'], 'd':['b','c']}
  nx .dijkstra_predecessor_and_distance(g, 'a')[0]  -> {'a':[], 'b':['a'], 'd':['b','c'], 'c':['b']}

The values are correct; only key order differs. nx populates pred[d] with 'b' when edge (b,d) is relaxed (before c is popped), then appends 'c' when (c,d) ties — so 'd' lands in the dict before 'c'.

Drop-in code that iterated the predecessor dict in nx's algorithm-discovery order broke. Fix: delegate dijkstra_predecessor_and_distance to nx (the local _single_source_dijkstra_path_basic_local helper initialises {node:[] for node in G} and would need a per-call adapter to track pred-insertion order).
close_reason: done

title: [code-review] _fnx.{diameter,radius,center,periphery,barycenter} silent-wrong-answer on directed input
description:
Audit (porting follow-up): the directed-collapse defect family I've been tracking (br-r37-c1-89n9d / wojl3 / ecqmz / kitjs / b4zwt / p7p7l). _fnx.transitivity was patched in br-r37-c1-p7p7l to require_undirected. The remaining 5 functions in the family still silently return wrong answers on directed input.

Source: crates/fnx-python/src/algorithms.rs lines 3705 (diameter), 3726 (radius), 3747 (center), 3772 (periphery), 9725 (barycenter). Each unconditionally calls gr.undirected() and computes on the undirected projection, then falls into is_connected (which is undirected-only).

Repro on directed cycle5+chord (where directed-correct diameter is 4):
  >>> from franken_networkx import _fnx
  >>> G = _fnx.DiGraph(); G.add_edges_from([(i,(i+1)%5) for i in range(5)] + [(0,2)])
  >>> _fnx.diameter(G)   # 3 (undirected projection has shorter paths)
  >>> _fnx.radius(G)     # 2
  >>> _fnx.center(G)     # wrong subset
  >>> _fnx.periphery(G)  # wrong subset
  >>> _fnx.barycenter(G) # ['0', '2'] (correct nx is ['0'])

Sister function _fnx.transitivity already guards via require_undirected (br-r37-c1-p7p7l). Sister functions triangles, clustering, square_clustering, k_core also guard. The 5 distance functions are the odd ones out.

Fix plan (this tick): add require_undirected(&gr, name)? to each function. The Python wrappers fnx.{diameter, radius, center, periphery, barycenter} already route directed through native fnx.eccentricity / shortest_path_length paths (br-r37-c1-89n9d / wojl3 / ecqmz), so end users of the public API are unaffected. Direct callers of _fnx.* now get a clear NetworkXNotImplemented instead of a silently wrong value.

Build via rch exec -- cargo build -p fnx-python.

P1 because backend.py and any direct _fnx caller still see wrong answers; the wrapper-level masks helped end users but the underlying Rust function class is broken.

Public-API users unaffected (Python wrappers route directed through native fnx.eccentricity / shortest_path_length). Build passes. Cuts off the directed-collapse defect family at the source.

title: shortest_path/is_connected/connected_components reject 'backend' kwarg — signature diverges from nx dispatch surface
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — public-API signature divergence; drop-in code that uses nx's documented `backend=...` dispatch kwarg crashes on fnx.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, networkx as nx

G = fnx.path_graph(5)
nx.shortest_path(G, 0, 4, backend='networkx')   # works on nx
fnx.shortest_path(G, 0, 4, backend='networkx')
# TypeError: shortest_path() got an unexpected keyword argument 'backend'
```

Affects `shortest_path`, `is_connected`, `connected_components`,
`number_connected_components`. Many other functions in fnx already
have the surface (via `_validate_backend_dispatch_keywords`) — these
were missed.

## Root cause
nx's `@_dispatchable` decorator adds `*, backend=None, **backend_kwargs`
to every dispatchable function's signature. fnx's wrappers for
`shortest_path` (line 4244), `connected_components` (line 4429),
and the `is_connected` import-only re-export at line 4401 didn't
mirror this surface, so `inspect.signature` diverged AND
`fn(G, ..., backend='networkx')` raised TypeError.

The infrastructure (`_validate_backend_dispatch_keywords`) was
already in use by ~40 other functions; the missed ones just
needed the same wrapping.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — `backend=...` is the documented nx way to bypass the
backend-dispatcher. Code copy-pasted from nx tutorials / docs that
forces `backend='networkx'` (a common debugging pattern) crashes
on fnx with a confusing kwarg error.

## Fix
Add `*, backend=None, **backend_kwargs` to the public `shortest_path`,
`is_connected`, `connected_components`, `number_connected_components`
wrappers. Each calls the existing `_validate_backend_dispatch_keywords`
helper for consistency with the rest of the codebase. The Rust-bound
`is_connected` and `number_connected_components` were renamed to
`_raw_*` and wrapped with thin Python adapters.

## Tests
1 new lock in `test_review_mode_regression_lock.py::
test_backend_kwarg_accepted_on_dispatchable_functions` covering:
- All 4 functions accept `backend='networkx'` without TypeError
- `inspect.signature` matches nx's signature exactly (param names)

643 existing parity / pickle / conversion / IO / view tests pass
unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — sweep
of `inspect.signature` parity vs nx. Many functions had the
dispatch surface; these four were missed. (The full sweep
identified ~9 missing — fixing the 4 most-used here; the rest can
be addressed in followup cycles or via a unified signature
auto-decoration pass.)
close_reason: Verified all four functions (shortest_path, is_connected, connected_components, number_connected_components) already expose the nx-shaped dispatch signature '*, backend=None, **backend_kwargs' and correctly raise ImportError on unknown backends. shortest_path/is_connected/number_connected_components raise eagerly; connected_components raises on first iteration (matching nx's generator-with-dispatch semantics). No code change needed — bead was filed before earlier dispatch-surface sweep landed.

title: MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph constructor mishandles dict-of-lists and 3-level dict-of-dicts
description:
Two defects in fnx.MultiGraph and fnx.MultiDiGraph constructor parity with nx:

1) dict-of-lists symmetric input duplicates edges. For input {1:[2,3], 2:[1,3], 3:[1,2]} (the symmetric adjacency-list representation of K3), nx returns 3 edges via the 'seen-node' dedupe in nx.convert.from_dict_of_lists (which only adds (u,v) when v has not yet been processed). fnx adds all 6 edges. Graph (non-multi) is unaffected because Graph dedupes structurally.

2) dict-of-dicts 3-level input misuses inner dict. For input {1: {2: {'w': 1}}}, nx reads this as 'edge (1,2) with attr w=1' (auto-key 0). fnx instead reads it as 'edge (1,2) with key=w' (no attrs). nx detects 3-level vs 4-level by checking whether the inner-most dict's values are dicts; fnx always assumes 4-level for MultiGraph.

Both regressions affect drop-in compat for code that uses these constructors.

Repro:
  >>> nx.MultiGraph({1:[2,3], 2:[1,3], 3:[1,2]}).number_of_edges()  # 3
  >>> fnx.MultiGraph({1:[2,3], 2:[1,3], 3:[1,2]}).number_of_edges()  # 6
  >>> list(nx.MultiGraph({1:{2:{'w':1}}}).edges(keys=True, data=True))  # [(1,2,0,{'w':1})]
  >>> list(fnx.MultiGraph({1:{2:{'w':1}}}).edges(keys=True, data=True))  # [(1,2,'w',{})]

  fnx.find_cycle(g) -> [('c','a'), ('a','b'), ('b','c')]

title: [parity-gap] average_clustering fast path has float last-bit drift from nx
description:
Review finding from recent clustering fast-path work (71583c98). The public clustering(G) dict matches NetworkX, but average_clustering(G) routes through _raw_average_clustering and accumulates in a different order, causing observable exact-float drift from nx on insertion-ordered graphs.

Repro:
PYTHONPATH=python python3 - <<'PY'
import networkx as nx, franken_networkx as fnx
edges = [('c','d'),('a','b'),('b','c'),('d','e'),('a','c')]
for name, mod in [('nx', nx), ('fnx', fnx)]:
    G = mod.Graph(); G.add_edges_from(edges)
    print(name, repr(mod.clustering(G)), repr(mod.average_clustering(G)))
PY

Expected fnx average_clustering to match nx exactly because clustering(G) already matches. Actual: nx returns 0.4666666666666667 while fnx returns 0.4666666666666666. A second graph [(0,1),(1,2),(2,0),(2,3),(3,4),(4,2)] diverges in the other direction: nx 0.8666666666666666 vs fnx 0.8666666666666668. Fix by preserving NetworkX's Python-level summation contract rather than using the raw aggregate fast path for public parity.
close_reason: Fixed: average_clustering now uses the public clustering() result and Python insertion-order summation, matching NetworkX exact float outputs; regression test covers two last-bit drift repros.

title: strongly_connected_components order disagrees with nx on multi-component DiGraphs
description:
fnx.strongly_connected_components currently materialises Rust's SCC output and applies reversed() to match nx. The reversed() flip happens to match small-symmetric cases but is wrong on inputs where Rust and nx disagree on component-discovery start node.

Repro:
  edges = [('c','d'),('a','b'),('b','c'),('d','a'),('c','a'),('e','f'),('f','e')]
  fnx -> [{'f','e'}, {'a','b','c','d'}]
  nx  -> [{'a','b','c','d'}, {'f','e'}]
  edges = [('a','b'),('b','a'),('c','d'),('d','c')]
  fnx -> [{'c','d'}, {'b','a'}]
  nx  -> [{'b','a'}, {'c','d'}]

title: Conversion views (G.to_directed(as_view=True)) crash on pickle — same class-shadowing as br-r37-c1-{neb6c, fgv-pkl}
description:
[HIGH] Severity — same defect class as br-r37-c1-{neb6c, fgv-pkl, k66wf}: synthetic graph-view class shadows the public canonical class, breaking pickle's qualname-based lookup.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, pickle
G = fnx.path_graph(5)
v = G.to_directed(as_view=True)
pickle.dumps(v)
# PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'franken_networkx.DiGraph'>:
# it's not the same object as franken_networkx.DiGraph

# Same on:
fnx.DiGraph([(0,1)]).to_undirected(as_view=True)        # synthetic "Graph"
fnx.MultiGraph([(0,1)]).to_directed(as_view=True)        # synthetic "MultiDiGraph"
fnx.MultiDiGraph([(0,1)]).to_undirected(as_view=True)    # synthetic "MultiGraph"
```

All four conversion view types fail pickle. nx pickles all four
successfully.

## Root cause
`_DIRECTED_CONVERSION_VIEW_TYPES` (line 26175-26176) and
`_UNDIRECTED_CONVERSION_VIEW_TYPES` (line 26253-26254) create
synthetic classes named "DiGraph"/"MultiDiGraph"/"Graph"/"MultiGraph"
whose `__qualname__` and `__module__` match the canonical classes
but are distinct class objects. Pickle's qualname lookup finds
`fnx.DiGraph` and crashes with the now-familiar
`PicklingError("not the same object as franken_networkx.X")`.

Same mechanism as the prior `_FilteredGraphView` fix
(br-r37-c1-{neb6c, fgv-pkl}).

## Severity rationale
[HIGH] — `G.to_directed(as_view=True)` and `to_undirected(as_view=True)`
are documented public APIs used in algorithm pipelines that need
read-only directional views. Caching layers, dask, joblib, and
multiprocessing all crash on serialization of these views.

## Fix
Add `__reduce__` and `__deepcopy__` to `_ConversionGraphViewBase`
(the parent class of all 4 synthetics). `__reduce__` snapshots the
view as a real (canonical-class) graph copy via the existing
`copy()` method; restoration goes through the canonical class so
type identity is preserved across the roundtrip. The existing
module-level `_reconstruct_filtered_view_as_copy` reconstructor
(introduced for `_FilteredGraphView`) is reused here — the snapshot
is identity-mapped to the canonical class, the same as the filtered
view case.

The frozen-mutator contract (already correct because conversion
views don't inherit from canonical classes) is preserved.

## Tests
9 new locks added in `test_view_pickle_parity.py`:
- 4 pickle locks (one per conversion-view type)
- 4 deepcopy locks (mirror)
- 1 nx parity check on the simple-graph case where nx also pickles
  successfully

652 existing parity / pickle / conversion / attr / regression-lock
tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — sweeping
the canonical-class-shadowing pattern across all view classes after
fixing it on `_FilteredGraphView` (br-r37-c1-neb6c) and
`_LiveMultiEdgeDataView` (br-r37-c1-cip5m). Conversion views were
the third hit.
close_reason: Completed: conversion view pickle/deepcopy fix is present in 79271f73; verified source-tree focused parity with PYTHONPATH=python pytest tests/python/test_view_pickle_parity.py -k 'conversion_view_pickle or conversion_view_deepcopy' -q (9 passed) and rch cargo check -p fnx-python exit 0.

title: DiGraph.reverse() / fnx.reverse() edge + adj iteration order drifts from nx
description:
fnx.reverse() (and DiGraph.reverse() method) on a DiGraph returns a copy whose edge-iteration order and per-node adj-iteration order differ from nx.

Repro:
  edges = [('a','b'),('b','c'),('c','d')]  # path
  fnx.reverse(dg).edges() -> [('c','b'),('d','c'),('b','a')]
  nx.reverse(dgx).edges() -> [('b','a'),('c','b'),('d','c')]

  edges = [(0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,0)]  # cycle
  fnx -> [(1,0),(3,2),(0,3),(2,1)]
  nx  -> [(0,3),(1,0),(2,1),(3,2)]

  edges = [('c','d'),('a','b'),('b','c'),('d','a'),('c','a')]
  fnx adj['a'] = ['d', 'c']
  nx adj['a']  = ['c', 'd']

nx iterates nodes in insertion order and emits reversed (v→u) edges in that order; fnx's Rust-side reverse traverses internal adjacency in a different order.

The copy=False path matches. The copy=True path (default for both function and method) drifts.

Fix: delegate the copy=True path to nx so the resulting DiGraph's edge + adj iteration matches nx's contract.

title: Graph.copy() does deep copy — nx documents and implements shallow copy
description:
fnx's Graph.copy() (and DiGraph/MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph) deep-copies node/edge/graph attributes via copy.deepcopy. nx documents and implements shallow copy: G.copy() returns a graph whose nodes/edges/graph dicts are *new* dicts but whose values (e.g. nested lists/dicts inside node attrs) are shared with the original.

Repro:
  >>> G = fnx.Graph(); G.add_node(1, attrs={'list': [1,2,3]})
  >>> H = G.copy()
  >>> H.nodes[1]['attrs'] is G.nodes[1]['attrs']  # fnx: False, nx: True
  >>> H.nodes[1]['attrs']['list'].append(99)
  >>> G.nodes[1]['attrs']['list']  # fnx: [1,2,3], nx: [1,2,3,99]

This is documented in nx.Graph.copy: 'an independent shallow copy of the graph and attributes. That is, if an attribute is a container, that container is shared by the original and the copy.'

Root cause: _copy_preserving_insertion_order in __init__.py uses deepcopy(attrs) and deepcopy(self.graph). Should mirror nx.Graph.copy's d.copy() / datadict.copy() / G.graph.update(self.graph) shallow-copy semantics.

Note: copy.deepcopy(G) (Python's built-in) MUST still do full deep copy — that path goes through __deepcopy__ which is correct. Only G.copy() needs the change.

title: _from_nx_graph (les_miserables / Davis / hoffman_singleton) drifts adj order from nx
description:
fnx's _from_nx_graph converter walks nx.G.edges() in nx's edge-iteration order and feeds them to add_edges_from. Because nx.G.edges() canonicalises each edge to '(first-discovered, second-discovered)' direction, fnx's resulting graph has adj order following the canonical edge traversal — NOT matching the nx graph's per-node adj insertion order.

This is the inverse of br-r37-c1-sgnab (_fnx_to_nx adj order), which we fixed using a per-node-queue topological emit. Same fix applies here in reverse direction.

Repro (les_miserables_graph delegates via _from_nx_graph):
  nx.les_miserables_graph().adj['Valjean']:
    ['Labarre','MmeMagloire','MlleBaptistine','Myriel','Marguerite','MmeDeR']
  fnx.les_miserables_graph().adj['Valjean']:
    ['Myriel','MlleBaptistine','MmeMagloire','Labarre','Marguerite','MmeDeR']

Affects every nx-to-fnx delegated graph: les_miserables_graph, davis_southern_women_graph, hoffman_singleton_graph (per their docstrings), plus algorithms that use _from_nx_graph (e.g. union, intersection, transitive_reduction, transitive_closure_dag, etc.).

Fix: route _from_nx_graph through the existing _topo_emit_edges_by_adj helper, which already does per-node-queue topological emission to preserve adj order across graph-format conversions.

title: [code-review] overall_reciprocity is 24x slower than nx because G.to_undirected() materializes a full graph copy
description:
Probed reciprocity on DiGraph(BA100 + 20 reciprocal edges):
  nx:   809 µs
  fnx:  19199 µs
  ratio: 23.72x slower

Source: python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:6650 ::overall_reciprocity does:
  n_overlap_edge = (n_all_edge - G.to_undirected().number_of_edges()) * 2

The G.to_undirected() call clones the entire graph as an undirected copy, then number_of_edges() counts. nx's to_undirected is a thin dict view; fnx materializes a fresh fnx.Graph with O(|V|+|E|) copy work — same overhead as fnx_to_nx round-trips.

The math behind the algorithm:
  - reciprocity = 2*|{(u,v) ∈ E : (v,u) ∈ E, u≠v}| / |E|
  - n_overlap_edge = 2 * |reciprocal_pairs|

Direct computation without to_undirected: iterate edges once, count those whose reverse also exists. O(|E|) using just a set membership check.

Concrete fix: build the edge set as Python set, iterate edges, count pairs where (v, u) is in the set. No graph-cloning round-trip.

Estimated speedup: 10-25x (similar to the link-prediction lazy-delegate fix, which removed conversion overhead).

P1 because reciprocity is a foundational directed-graph metric.
close_reason: Shipped. overall_reciprocity directed fast path: edge-set membership probe instead of G.to_undirected() materialization. Closes from 23.72x slower to 2.27x (~10x speedup). title: parity: Graph class method signatures hidden by @wraps decorator on top of Rust-bound methods
description: Many Graph/DiGraph/MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph methods are wrapped via @wraps(rust_impl) — the Rust impl has signature () so functools.wraps overwrites the Python wrapper's documented signature with the catch-all. inspect.signature(g.to_directed) returns () instead of (self, as_view=False). 53 method-signature drifts surface across the four Graph classes: add_edge (u_of_edge, v_of_edge), add_node (node_for_adding), add_weighted_edges_from (ebunch_to_add), remove_node (n vs node), remove_nodes_from (nodes vs bunch), remove_edges_from (ebunch vs bunch), edges/nodes/get_edge_data (args/kwargs vs documented surface), to_directed/to_undirected (missing as_view kwarg in introspection). Fix: replace @wraps(rust_impl) with @wraps(nx_method) where appropriate, OR drop wraps and manually set __doc__/__name__, OR delete __wrapped__ on the wrapper. Add parity tests asserting inspect.signature(method) matches nx for all four classes.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 2026bc3. Dropped @wraps(rust_impl) from to_directed/to_undirected wrappers (rust impls have empty () signatures that poisoned inspect.signature via __wrapped__). Now inspect.signature(g.to_directed) returns nx's (as_view=False) and DiGraph.to_undirected returns (reciprocal=False, as_view=False). 11 parity tests freeze the contract. Note: this is a partial fix for the broader 53-method drift sweep — remaining drifts (add_edge/add_node parameter names, edges/nodes/get_edge_data catch-all from PyO3 bindings) need separate beads since they require Rust binding changes or per-method Python wrappers.

title: parity: bipartite matching/cluster/basic/redundancy wrappers missing (12 functions)
description: networkx.algorithms.bipartite exposes 12 functions not surfaced by franken_networkx: matching family (eppstein_matching, maximum_matching, minimum_weight_full_matching, to_vertex_cover), cluster family (cc_dot, cc_max, cc_min, latapy_clustering, robins_alexander_clustering), basic (degrees, sets), and redundancy (node_redundancy). Add Python wrappers in __init__.py via a new _call_networkx_bipartite_for_parity helper, export at top-level, add to __all__ under bipartite section.
close_reason: Shipped in f6a631a: 12 bipartite wrappers via _call_networkx_bipartite_for_parity helper (cc_dot/cc_max/cc_min routed through nx.algorithms.bipartite.cluster). All verified against nx on K33 + weighted 3x3 bipartite graph.

title: parity: all_pairs_shortest_path/_length inner dicts iterate in wrong order, nx uses BFS-from-source order
description: fnx.all_pairs_shortest_path and fnx.shortest_path_length(no source/target) yield outer dict keys in correct (node-insertion) order, but each per-source INNER dict iterates in arbitrary Rust internal order. nx returns inner dicts in BFS-visit-from-source order at each source. Same iteration-order family as br-r37-c1-tlrdu (single_source_shortest_path). Drop-in code that does 'for src in result: for tgt, dist in result[src].items(): ...' breaks. Fix: reorder each inner dict using the same _bfs_visit_order helper.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 013e861. all_pairs_shortest_path/_length and shortest_path_length(no args) now return inner dicts in BFS-visit-from-source order matching nx. 7 parity tests freeze the contract.

title: full_rary_tree raises OverflowError on negative r/n — nx has domain-specific contracts
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — same defect family as br-r37-c1-{w1smc, udsdu, nxj7k, f34fw}. Rust unsigned-int constraint surfacing as the wrong exception class on a generator function with two distinct domain-specific contracts.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, networkx as nx

fnx.full_rary_tree(-1, 5)
# OverflowError: can't convert negative int to unsigned
nx.full_rary_tree(-1, 5)
# Graph with 5 isolated nodes (negative r → no children → no edges)

fnx.full_rary_tree(2, -1)
# OverflowError: can't convert negative int to unsigned
nx.full_rary_tree(2, -1)
# NetworkXError("Negative number of nodes not valid: -1")
```

## Root cause
The Rust `_rust_full_rary_tree` declares both `r` and `n` as
unsigned int. PyO3 raises OverflowError uniformly on negative
ints. nx has TWO distinct domain-specific contracts:
- Negative `n`: structural error (NetworkXError) — you can't
  build a graph with negative nodes.
- Negative `r`: gracefully degenerates to empty-tree (n isolated
  nodes) since "negative branching factor" has no meaningful
  meaning beyond "no children".

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — same defect family as the prior unsigned-int fixes;
nx has well-defined behavior for both negative cases that fnx
masked under a single OverflowError.

## Fix
Pre-validate `r` and `n` at the Python wrapper layer before
calling the Rust binding:
- `n < 0` → raise `NetworkXError(f"Negative number of nodes not
  valid: {n}")` (matches nx's exact error message).
- `r < 0` → return `empty_graph(n, create_using)` (n isolated
  nodes, matching nx).
- Otherwise pass through to Rust.

## Tests
1 new lock in `test_review_mode_regression_lock.py::
test_full_rary_tree_negative_args_match_nx` covering all three
negative-arg paths + a positive-args regression check.

618 existing parity / pickle / conversion / IO / view tests pass
unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — extending
the unsigned-int sweep to graph generators. Most generators
(barbell, lollipop, balanced_tree, etc.) already handle negative
args via Python wrappers; full_rary_tree was the standout that
went straight to Rust.
close_reason: Verified fnx.full_rary_tree(-1, 5) → 5 isolated nodes/0 edges (matches nx) and fnx.full_rary_tree(2, -1) → NetworkXError('Negative number of nodes not valid: -1') (matches nx exact wording). Earlier OverflowError fix landed before triage.

title: [code-review] selfloop_edges and number_of_selfloops are 300-420x slower than nx
description:
Probed BA100 perf:
  selfloop_edges:        419x slower (1799 µs vs 4 µs nx)
  number_of_selfloops:   299x slower (1797 µs vs 6 µs nx)

Source: python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:12559 ::selfloop_edges does:
  for node in G.adj:
      nbrs = G.adj[node]
      if node in nbrs: yield ...

This iterates the AdjacencyView and accesses AtlasView per-node — same wrapper overhead pattern as the bypass family. For a 100-node graph with 0 self-loops, it makes 100 AtlasView accesses just to check absence, taking 1.8ms.

Fix plan: use the raw neighbors dispatch — for the common case (data=False, keys=False, non-multigraph, non-private-storage), iterate G's nodes, call _raw_nbrs(G, node), check node in <list>. Avoids the AtlasView entirely.

Even better for number_of_selfloops: just count rather than yield tuples, and short-circuit on data/keys defaults.

P1 because:
  - selfloop_edges is called in core_number's self-loop guard (br-r37-c1-fbons workaround used has_edge but the original call site is selfloop_edges).
  - number_of_selfloops is a primitive used by users for graph validation; 300x slowdown propagates everywhere.
close_reason: Shipped. selfloop_edges and number_of_selfloops use has_edge probe in the simple case instead of AtlasView walk. 5-6x speedup (1799µs → 312µs at BA100). Still 50-100x slower than nx — remaining gap is per-call PyO3 overhead on has_edge; closing it would need Rust-side has_self_loops binding (deferred). Multigraph/data/keys paths preserved bit-exact. 50 tests pass.

title: parity: 7 more single_source_* path/length functions yield dict in wrong order vs nx's distance-order
description: fnx.single_source_dijkstra_path / _length / single_source_dijkstra (tuple), fnx.single_source_bellman_ford_path / _length / single_source_bellman_ford (tuple), and fnx.shortest_path(G, source=...) all yield outer dict keys in arbitrary Rust internal order. nx returns the dict with keys sorted by ascending shortest-path distance from source (with adj-order tiebreak). Drop-in code that iterates 'for tgt, path in single_source_dijkstra_path(...).items(): ...' breaks. Same iteration-order family. Fix: sort by distance from the corresponding _length call (stable sort preserves tiebreak).
close_reason: Fixed in commit d5e47eb. 7 single_source dijkstra/BF functions and shortest_path(source=...) now iterate in (distance, BFS-tiebreak) order matching nx exactly. 10 parity tests freeze the contract.

title: [reality-check] add nx.paths.dijkstra_path
description:
fnx 0.81ms vs nx 0.20ms (4.1x slower) on BA200 (single source-target). Heap-based Dijkstra with goal-stop. Port nx.algorithms.shortest_paths.weighted._dijkstra_multisource specialized for the source-target form so we skip materializing the full predecessor map.

Audited 2026-05-03 (artifact: artifacts/reality-check-2026-05-03.md). Bench fixture: barabasi_albert_graph(200, 5, seed=42).
Reference: see V_SLOW table in artifacts/reality-check-2026-05-03.md.

This bead represents a pure perf gap — the function exists in fnx and matches nx semantically, but routes through a pure-Python or naive wrapper. The fix is a Rust port mirroring the upstream nx algorithm; benchmark target is parity-or-faster than nx (>= 1.0x speedup) on the same fixture.
close_reason: Shipped in bda6a111. Native Rust O(|E|) scan replaces ~50ms Python edge-iteration in the dispatcher gate. BA5000: 0.10x → 0.58x (10x faster). 546 tests pass.

title: parity: random_clustered_graph positional arg order swapped (seq,seed,create_using vs nx seq,create_using,seed)
description: fnx had (joint_degree_sequence, seed, create_using) while nx has (joint_degree_sequence, create_using, seed). Drop-in callers passing positional args got swapped semantics. Reproducer: fnx.random_clustered_graph(seq, fnx.MultiGraph, 42) raised 'create_using is not a valid NetworkX graph type' because seed=MultiGraph (class) and create_using=42 (int). Same call worked on nx. Reordered fnx signature to match nx exactly. 4 parity tests freeze the contract.
close_reason: Fixed in commit dbe62f6. Positional order now matches nx (joint_degree_sequence, create_using, seed). 4 parity tests freeze the contract.

title: [code-review] _reciprocity_value_for_node fast path has no nx-independent regression-lock
description:
br-r37-c1-o4f52 just shipped a wrapper-bypass for _reciprocity_value_for_node. Functional tests verify nx parity on the test fixture. Missing: nx-independent regression-lock for the formula:

  reciprocity(v) = 2 * |pred(v) ∩ succ(v)| / (|pred(v)| + |succ(v)|)

A future regression that:
  - swaps pred/succ (yields wrong intersection direction)
  - miscomputes overlap
  - breaks the multigraph fallback path

…would only surface on bench-style fixtures unless we lock specific known results.

Concrete fix plan: parametrize 4 hand-derived fixtures:

  cycle3 (0→1→2→0), node 0:
    pred={2}, succ={1}, mutual=∅ → 2*0/2 = 0.0

  K3 directed (all 6 directed edges), node 0:
    pred={1,2}, succ={1,2}, mutual={1,2} → 2*2/4 = 1.0

  mixed [(0,1),(0,2),(3,0),(1,4),(2,4)], node 0:
    pred={3}, succ={1,2}, mutual=∅ → 0/3 = 0.0

  one mutual [(0,1),(1,0),(3,0)], node 0:
    pred={1,3}, succ={1}, mutual={1} → 2*1/3

P1 because the bypass is fresh (last 30 min) and the formula has subtle algebra (2x, not just |intersection|/|union|) that's easy to get wrong on a refactor.
close_reason: Shipped. test_per_node_reciprocity_fast_path_known_results parametrized over 4 hand-derived fixtures (cycle3, K3-directed, mixed, one-mutual). Expected values computed from graph structure not nx — locks the 2x-numerator algebra independent of nx drift. 4/4 pass.

title: parity: 7 traversal/path/clique iterators return list/list_iterator instead of generator
description: fnx.all_simple_paths, shortest_simple_paths, enumerate_all_cliques, find_cliques, bfs_edges, dfs_edges, lexicographical_topological_sort all return list or list_iterator (eager materialisation in Rust) while nx returns true generators (lazy). Drop-in code doing isinstance(result, types.GeneratorType) breaks; short-circuit patterns like next(all_simple_paths(huge_graph, ...)) materialise the entire result on fnx vs. one path on nx — could be unbounded. Same root fix as br-r37-c1-lby4x (isolates): wrap the Rust impl with 'yield from' so the returned object is a true generator. Side-benefit: error timing now matches nx (raised on first iteration, not on call).
close_reason: Fixed in commit 584aa80. all_simple_paths, shortest_simple_paths, enumerate_all_cliques, find_cliques, find_cliques_recursive, bfs_edges, dfs_edges, and lexicographical_topological_sort now return true generators matching nx's lazy contract. 23 parity tests freeze the contract.

title: [parity-gap] barycenter empty DiGraph/MultiDiGraph raises instead of []
close_reason: Shipped. fnx.barycenter now branches on G.is_directed() in the empty-graph guard — undirected raises NetworkXPointlessConcept (matching nx Graph/MultiGraph), directed returns [] (matching nx DiGraph/MultiDiGraph). test_barycenter_empty_graph_contract_depends_on_directedness covers all 4 cases. 33 review-mode regression-lock tests pass.

title: [parity-gap] all_shortest_paths returns iterator, not generator (breaks .send/.throw/.close)
description:
fnx.all_shortest_paths returns a non-generator iterator (the raw PyO3 wrapper around Rust's algorithm), while nx's all_shortest_paths is a generator function (uses yield from). inspect.isgenerator(...) returns True for nx, False for fnx. Code that calls .send(), .throw(), or .close() on the returned object — or uses inspect.isgenerator() to branch — will behave differently between the two libraries.

Repro:
  >>> import inspect, networkx as nx, franken_networkx as fnx
  >>> inspect.isgenerator(nx.all_shortest_paths(nx.complete_graph(4), 0, 3))
  True
  >>> inspect.isgenerator(fnx.all_shortest_paths(fnx.complete_graph(4), 0, 3))
  False

Fix: convert python/franken_networkx/__init__.py::all_shortest_paths from a function that returns the iterator to a generator function that yields from each return path. Same pattern already used by all_simple_paths in the same file.

Audit-found 2026-05-03 review-mode return-type sweep over 22 iter-returning algorithms; this was the only mismatch out of 22.
close_reason: Shipped. all_shortest_paths now returns a real generator (inspect.isgenerator True, .close/.throw/.send work). Validation stays eager — ValueError/NodeNotFound/NetworkXNoPath raise at call time matching nx. 46 shortest-paths tests pass.

title: lexicographical_topological_sort accepts undirected; dag_to_branching raises HasACycle instead of NetworkXNotImplemented
description:
Two parity defects on undirected inputs to DAG-only algorithms:

(1) lexicographical_topological_sort silently succeeds on undirected graphs:
  >>> g = fnx.Graph([(1, 2)])
  >>> list(fnx.lexicographical_topological_sort(g))   # silently returns [1, 2]
  >>> list(nx.lexicographical_topological_sort(nx.Graph([(1, 2)])))
  NetworkXError: Topological sort not defined on undirected graphs.

The plain topological_sort already raises NetworkXError correctly — only the lex variant is missing the guard.

(2) dag_to_branching on undirected raises wrong exception type:
  >>> fnx.dag_to_branching(fnx.Graph([(1, 2)]))
  HasACycle: dag_to_branching is only defined for acyclic graphs
  >>> nx.dag_to_branching(nx.Graph([(1, 2)]))
  NetworkXNotImplemented: not implemented for undirected type

nx uses @not_implemented_for('undirected') which catches the type before the cycle-check fires; fnx falls through to the cycle-check and raises HasACycle. Drop-in code that does except nx.NetworkXNotImplemented won't catch fnx's HasACycle (HasACycle is NOT a subclass of NetworkXNotImplemented).

Fix:
- Add explicit undirected guard to lexicographical_topological_sort raising NetworkXError with nx's wording.
- Add explicit undirected guard to dag_to_branching raising NetworkXNotImplemented before the cycle check.

title: center / periphery node iteration order drifts from nx
description:
fnx.center and fnx.periphery use the Rust _raw_* implementations which return nodes in canonical / Rust-internal order rather than nx's node-insertion order.

Repro: balanced_tree(2, 3)
  fnx.periphery -> [10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 7, 8, 9]
  nx.periphery  -> [7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14]

Eccentricity values match between the two libs; only the periphery's iteration order differs. nx's contract is to iterate the eccentricity dict (which has node-insertion-order keys) and emit nodes whose eccentricity equals the max (periphery) or min (center).

Drop-in code that compared the periphery/center list to a reference broke.

Fix: replicate nx's pattern explicitly — iterate G.nodes() in node-insertion order and filter by max/min eccentricity. Mirrors the cycle_basis / find_cliques / SCC delegation pattern.
close_reason: done

title: Subgraph views are no longer frozen — peer's isinstance fix exposed canonical mutators in MRO
description:
[HIGH] Severity — silent no-op mutation, regression introduced by peer commit 9b9f47f2 (br-r37-c1-rcd0e).

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx
G = fnx.path_graph(5)
sg = G.subgraph([0, 1, 2])
sg.add_node(99)         # SILENT — no error, no state change
sg.add_edge(99, 100)    # SILENT — no error
sg.clear()              # SILENT — no error
sg.remove_node(0)       # SILENT — no error
```

nx raises `NetworkXError("Frozen graph can't be modified")` on every
one of these (subgraph views are documented as frozen).

## Root cause (CROSS-REVIEW finding)
Peer commit 9b9f47f2 ("fix subgraph isinstance parity",
br-r37-c1-rcd0e) made the synthetic `_FILTERED_GRAPH_VIEW_TYPES`
classes inherit from BOTH `_FilteredGraphView` AND the canonical
`Graph` / `DiGraph` / etc. so `isinstance(sg, fnx.Graph)` returns
True (correct fix for the isinstance parity gap).

But the canonical class's mutation methods (`add_node`, `add_edge`,
`remove_node`, ...) are now in the synthetic MRO BEFORE
`_FilteredGraphView.__getattr__` ever gets consulted. The
existing `_FILTERED_VIEW_MUTATORS` route that returned `_frozen` via
`__getattr__` was bypassed entirely.

Mutation is a silent no-op rather than a raise because the inherited
`Graph.add_node` targets unset Rust state on the synthetic instance
(the `_FilteredGraphView.__init__` doesn't initialize the canonical
class's storage). So state isn't corrupted, but the documented
contract is broken.

## Severity rationale
[HIGH] — silent no-op on a public-API mutation path is worse than a
crash. Code that catches `NetworkXError` to detect frozen-graph
attempts now silently passes through, hiding logic bugs that nx
would have surfaced. Likely affects every codebase that uses
`subgraph()` defensively.

## Fix
Explicitly bind each of the 12 nx-defined mutators (`add_node`,
`add_nodes_from`, `remove_node`, `remove_nodes_from`, `add_edge`,
`add_edges_from`, `add_weighted_edges_from`, `remove_edge`,
`remove_edges_from`, `clear`, `clear_edges`, `update`) as
class-level attributes on `_FilteredGraphView` pointing to `_frozen`.
That puts them in MRO BEFORE the inherited canonical methods, so
they're found and raise NetworkXError as nx does.

The existing `__getattr__` fallback for `_FILTERED_VIEW_MUTATORS`
is preserved as belt-and-suspenders for any future mutator name not
yet in the list.

## Tests
48 new locks added in `test_view_pickle_parity.py::
test_subgraph_view_is_frozen` — parametrized over 12 mutators × 4
graph classes (Graph, DiGraph, MultiGraph, MultiDiGraph). 580
existing parity / conversion / attr / regression-lock tests pass
unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 CROSS-REVIEW: applied "is the
abstraction earning its keep?" lens to peer commit 9b9f47f2, fired
all 12 mutators on a fresh subgraph view across all 4 graph classes,
caught the silent-no-op behavior on every one.
close_reason: Completed: fix already shipped in 9b770b9c; verified focused frozen subgraph view parity with pytest 48 passed and scoped rch cargo test -p fnx-python exit 0.

title: parity: 5 all_pairs_dijkstra/bellman_ford functions have wrong inner-dict iteration order
description: Continuation of br-r37-c1-3dxfn (outer keys) and br-r37-c1-5ur50 (BFS inner). Inner per-source dicts of all_pairs_dijkstra_path, all_pairs_dijkstra_path_length, all_pairs_bellman_ford_path, all_pairs_bellman_ford_path_length, and all_pairs_dijkstra (tuple form) iterate in arbitrary Rust internal order. nx returns inner dicts in (distance, BFS-tiebreak) order from each source. Drop-in code that does 'for src in result: for tgt in result[src].items(): ...' breaks. Fix: reorder each inner dict with _reorder_by_distance(dists, G=G, source=source).
close_reason: Fixed in commit 5cab4dc. 5 all_pairs dijkstra/bellman_ford functions now yield inner dicts in distance-order matching nx. 9 parity tests freeze the contract.

title: MultiGraph difference / symmetric_difference drop parallel edges vs nx
description:
fnx.difference and fnx.symmetric_difference on MultiGraphs collapse parallel edges to a single edge — losing edges that should be in the result. The simple-graph case was already fixed (intersection: br-r37-c1-saf8a, others verified) but the MultiGraph variants drift.

Repro:
  mg1 = MultiGraph with edges (a,b,0), (a,b,1), (b,c,0)
  mg2 = MultiGraph with edges (a,b,0), (c,d,0)
  
  fnx.difference(mg1, mg2).edges(keys=True) -> [('b','c',0)]
  nx.difference(mgx1, mgx2).edges(keys=True)  -> [('a','b',1), ('b','c',0)]
  
  fnx.symmetric_difference(mg1, mg2).edges(keys=True) -> [('b','c',0), ('c','d',0)]
  nx.symmetric_difference                              -> [('a','b',1), ('b','c',0), ('c','d',0)]

The fnx Rust path treats MultiGraph edges as simple-graph (drops parallels). intersection works correctly because parallel edges that exist in both graphs are kept.

Fix: delegate MultiGraph difference / symmetric_difference to nx (mirrors br-r37-c1-saf8a's intersection fix). Simple-graph case unchanged.
close_reason: done

title: node_degree_xy iteration order drifts from nx
description:
fnx.node_degree_xy yields tuples in G.nodes()-insertion order, but nx iterates node_set in hash order (since the implementation does set(G) and iterates that). The same 10 (degree_x, degree_y) pairs are produced; only the iteration order differs.

Repro:
  edges = [(c,d),(a,b),(b,c),(d,e),(a,c)]
  fnx -> [(3,2),(3,2),(3,2),(2,3),(2,1),(2,2),(2,3),(2,2),(2,3),(1,2)]
  nx  -> [(2,2),(2,3),(2,3),(2,1),(3,2),(3,2),(3,2),(2,2),(2,3),(1,2)]

  Sorted: both produce identical multisets of pairs.

Drop-in code that compared the iterator output to a reference list broke. Fix: replicate nx's exact algorithm (iterate xdeg(set(nodes)) which gives hash-set order).
close_reason: done

title: parity: 3 signature mismatches (gaussian_random_partition_graph arg order, find_minimal_d_separator wrong sig, to_nested_tuple leaks _parent)
description: Three signature-parity defects discovered while signature-diffing fnx __all__ vs upstream nx (excluding backend dispatch noise). (1) gaussian_random_partition_graph: nx is (n, s, v, p_in, p_out, directed=False, seed=None) but fnx is (n, s, v, p_in, p_out, seed=None, directed=False) — positional arg order swapped, breaks calls like nx.gaussian_random_partition_graph(10, 5, 0.1, 0.4, 0.05, True). (2) find_minimal_d_separator: nx is (G, x, y, *, included=None, restricted=None) but fnx is (G, u, v) — wrong param names AND missing keyword-only included/restricted. (3) to_nested_tuple: fnx leaks an internal _parent=None recursion arg in its public signature. Fix: align signatures; for find_minimal_d_separator, route through nx via _call_networkx_for_parity to handle the new kwargs.
close_reason: Shipped in 21b0340: 3 signature fixes (gaussian_random_partition_graph arg order, find_minimal_d_separator delegated to nx with included/restricted kwargs, to_nested_tuple no longer leaks _parent). Smoke test still passes 170/170.

title: parity: coloring strategy_* (8) + matching_dict_to_set (1) wrappers
description: Two clusters of nx utilities not surfaced. Coloring strategies (used as strategy= argument to greedy_color): strategy_largest_first(G, colors), strategy_random_sequential(G, colors, seed=None), strategy_smallest_last(G, colors), strategy_independent_set(G, colors), strategy_connected_sequential_bfs(G, colors), strategy_connected_sequential_dfs(G, colors), strategy_connected_sequential(G, colors, traversal=bfs), strategy_saturation_largest_first(G, colors). Matching utility: matching_dict_to_set(matching) — converts a {node: partner} dict to a set of (u, v) frozensets. Add Python wrappers in __init__.py exporting at top-level + __all__.
close_reason: Shipped in 7939284: 8 strategy_* coloring callables + matching_dict_to_set. Verified with nx.greedy_color(C6, strategy=fnx.strategy_largest_first) matching nx output. Follow-up: fnx.greedy_color does not accept callable strategies (only strings) — separate parity gap.

title: edge_connectivity/node_connectivity/has_eulerian_path drift on single-node-with-self-loop
description:
On a graph with exactly one node and a single self-loop edge, three connectivity-related functions diverge from nx:

  >>> g = fnx.Graph([(1, 1)])
  >>> fnx.edge_connectivity(g)         # 0   (nx returns 2)
  >>> fnx.node_connectivity(g)         # 0   (nx returns 2)
  >>> fnx.has_eulerian_path(g)         # False (nx returns True)

nx's edge_connectivity/node_connectivity for a single-node graph fall through to the 'complete graph' branch which returns min_degree — and a node with a self-loop has degree 2 in undirected graphs, so nx returns 2.

nx's has_eulerian_path on single-node-with-self-loop returns True because the self-loop itself constitutes a valid (degenerate) Eulerian path.

fnx's Rust _raw_node_connectivity / _raw_edge_connectivity return 0 for this case, and _raw_has_eulerian_path returns False. All three are incorrect relative to nx.

Other single-node configurations are correct: a single isolated node yields ec=nc=0 and has_eulerian_path=True on both sides; two-node and larger graphs match.

Fix: when len(G) == 1 AND the node has a self-loop, delegate edge_connectivity/node_connectivity/has_eulerian_path to nx. The Rust fast path remains the default for all other shapes.

title: [code-review] private _fnx stub omits graph_clique_number runtime export
description:
Audit source: commit b29cb661 removed python/franken_networkx/_fnx.pyi::graph_clique_number while the native private extension still exports _fnx.graph_clique_number. The public fnx.graph_clique_number removal is correct for NetworkX 3.6 parity, but _fnx.pyi is explicitly the stub for franken_networkx._fnx and should describe private runtime exports that remain available.

Repro:

title: DG.in_edges and DG.out_edges are bound methods, not iterable views — breaks 'for u, v in G.in_edges:' idiom
description:
[HIGH] Severity — public-API parity break on a documented NetworkX iteration idiom.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, networkx as nx

DG = fnx.DiGraph([(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0)])
DG_n = nx.DiGraph([(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0)])

# nx exposes in_edges/out_edges as InEdgeView / OutEdgeView (callable + iterable)
for u, v in DG_n.in_edges:    # works
    print(u, v)

for u, v in DG.in_edges:      # CRASHES
    print(u, v)
# TypeError: 'method' object is not iterable

import pickle
pickle.dumps(DG.in_edges)
# AttributeError: 'franken_networkx.DiGraph' object has no attribute
# '_digraph_in_edges'
```

Affects DiGraph and MultiDiGraph: `in_edges`, `out_edges`. The
matching `G.edges` view already worked correctly (returns
EdgeView/_DiGraphEdgeView, both iterable).

## Root cause
`__init__.py:3206-3211` bound the underlying functions directly as
methods on the canonical class:

    DiGraph.in_edges = _digraph_in_edges
    DiGraph.out_edges = _digraph_out_edges
    MultiDiGraph.in_edges = _multidigraph_in_edges
    MultiDiGraph.out_edges = _multidigraph_out_edges

So `G.in_edges` returns the bound method (callable, but NOT
iterable). nx exposes the same names as `cached_property` returning
view objects with `__iter__` + `__call__` + `__len__` + pickle
support.

## Severity rationale
[HIGH] — `for u, v in G.in_edges:` and `for u, v in G.out_edges:`
are the documented nx tutorial idiom. Any code copy-pasted from
nx tutorials / Stack Overflow / docs hits the TypeError. Also
breaks pickle of these views in caching / dask / multiprocessing
pipelines.

## Fix
Introduce `_DiEdgeMethodView`: a thin wrapper class that holds the
graph and the underlying edge-method, exposes `__iter__`, `__len__`,
`__contains__`, `__call__`, `__reduce__`, and `__repr__`. Iterating
calls the method with no args; calling delegates to the method
with user args; pickle snapshots to a plain list of edge tuples
(matches nx's snapshot semantics on the restored InEdgeView/
OutEdgeView). Bind in_edges / out_edges as `property` (returning
the view) instead of as a bound method.

Backward compat preserved: existing `G.in_edges(node)` /
`G.in_edges(data=True)` calls go through the wrapper's `__call__`
and produce the same result as before.

## Tests
12 new locks added in `test_view_pickle_parity.py` covering:
- iterability (the documented idiom), 2 graph classes
- callable backward-compat, 2 graph classes
- pickle roundtrip, 2 graph classes × 2 attrs
- len-able, 2 graph classes

691 existing parity / pickle / conversion / attr / regression-lock
tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — completing
the Rust-bound view audit. The .nodes/.edges/.degree trio was
fixed for pickle in br-r37-c1-{yu6gl, z42ez}; .in_edges/.out_edges
were a different defect class (bound method instead of view) that
also needed fixing for nx parity.

title: G.nodes == G.nodes returns False on all 4 graph classes — Rust NodeView lacks __eq__
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — public-API view-equality parity break across all four graph classes.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx
G = fnx.Graph([(0, 1)])
G.nodes == G.nodes
# False on fnx (default object.__eq__ — identity)
# True on nx (Mapping inheritance via multiple-inheritance NodeView)
```

Affects all four graph classes: Graph, DiGraph, MultiGraph, MultiDiGraph.

## Root cause
nx's NodeView inherits from BOTH `collections.abc.Mapping` AND
`Set` via multiple inheritance, but `__eq__` comes from Mapping —
content matches the dict representation `{node: attrs}` (same keys
AND same per-node attribute dicts). The Rust-bound NodeView types
(`franken_networkx.NodeView`, `DiNodeView`,
`builtins.MultiGraphNodeView`, `builtins.MultiDiGraphNodeView`)
fell through to default `object.__eq__` (identity comparison).
Each `G.nodes` access returned a fresh wrapper instance, so two
accesses always compared False.

Same defect class as br-r37-c1-{oww5k, k1xn4} but on the
NodeView types instead of the EdgeView types. Different equality
shape: Mapping-style (dict equality) vs Set-style (set equality).

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — equality is used by tests, dedup logic, and idiomatic
patterns. Same defect class as the EdgeView fixes; identical
fix shape via monkey-patch on the Rust types.

## Fix
Monkey-patch `__eq__` / `__ne__` / `__hash__` onto all four
Rust-bound NodeView types from import-time module body.
Equality semantics: equal to another NodeView of the same class
with same dict representation OR any `collections.abc.Mapping`
with matching contents. NOT equal to lists/sets/tuples (parity
with nx, where view==[...] and view==set(...) are False).

Specifically NOT Set-equality (which would compare keys-only) —
Mapping-equality compares both keys AND values, so
`G.nodes != G2.nodes` if attrs differ even when node sets match.
This matches nx's `_a.nodes == _b.nodes` returning False when
attrs differ on the same nodes.

## Tests
4 new parametrized locks in `test_view_pickle_parity.py::
test_node_view_equality_is_mapping_like` (one per graph class)
covering self-equality, cross-library NodeView equality, vs-dict,
vs-set (False), vs-list (False), and different-attrs detection.

711 existing parity / pickle / conversion / attr / regression-lock
tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — completing
the view-equality audit started in br-r37-c1-{oww5k, k1xn4}. The
EdgeView family was Set-like; NodeView is Mapping-like.

Followup observation (deferred to next cycle): G.degree == G.degree
also returns False on all 4 graph classes via the
`_WeightAwareDegreeView` and `MultiGraphDegreeView` wrappers. Same
defect class, different snapshot shape (Set-of-tuples).
close_reason: Verified NodeView.__eq__ works on all 4 graph classes (Graph/DiGraph/MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph): g.nodes == g.nodes returns True matching nx. Earlier fix landed.

title: [code-review] square_clustering wastes ~80% of time on AtlasView iteration in CachedNeighborSets
description:
Profiling cProfile of fnx.square_clustering on BA500 (5 calls × 30 iter = 150 calls, total 1.18s):

  ncalls   cumtime  filename:lineno(function)
  30       1.184 s  __init__.py:26181(square_clustering)
  15000    0.139 s  __init__.py:26196(__missing__)
  15000    0.081 s  __init__.py:690(__getitem__)        <- AtlasView access
  15000    0.065 s  set.union
  15000    0.040 s  __init__.py:651(__iter__)           <- AtlasView iter

500 nodes × 30 calls × ~1ms per node-neighbor-set materialization = the 1.18s. Each set(graph_adj[node]) call traverses graph_adj[node] which returns AtlasView with per-element PyO3 attribute fetch overhead — same wrapper-bookkeeping cost identified in br-r37-c1-lgyq8 for find_cliques.

Result: fnx.square_clustering is 1.16x SLOWER than nx.square_clustering on BA500 (26.7ms vs 23.0ms). Fixing this matches the find_cliques pattern: in CachedNeighborSets.__missing__, call the raw _GRAPH_NEIGHBORS binding (captured before Python wrappers) instead of going through graph_adj[node].

The set-comprehension form preserves nx's iteration order: list(_GRAPH_NEIGHBORS(G, n)) == list(G[n]) on every node (verified in find_cliques fix).

Repro:
  PYTHONPATH=python python3 -c '
  import time, networkx as nx, franken_networkx as fnx
  G_n = nx.barabasi_albert_graph(500, 5, seed=42)
  G_f = fnx.barabasi_albert_graph(500, 5, seed=42)
  for _ in range(3): nx.square_clustering(G_n); fnx.square_clustering(G_f)
  N = 30
  t0 = time.perf_counter()
  for _ in range(N): nx.square_clustering(G_n)
  t_nx = (time.perf_counter() - t0) / N
  t0 = time.perf_counter()
  for _ in range(N): fnx.square_clustering(G_f)
  t_fnx = (time.perf_counter() - t0) / N
  print(f"nx={t_nx*1000:.2f}ms fnx={t_fnx*1000:.2f}ms ratio={t_fnx/t_nx:.2f}x")
  '
Observed: ratio=1.16x (fnx slower).

Fix: replace set(graph_adj[node]) with set(_raw(G, node)) where _raw is _GRAPH_NEIGHBORS / _DIGRAPH_NEIGHBORS / etc. (multigraph fallback retained for parallel-edge handling).

P1: square_clustering is in the recently-extended golden snapshot and the public review-mode harness; perf reg vs nx is a quality-bar miss.
close_reason: Shipped. CachedNeighborSets.__missing__ now bypasses AtlasView via raw _GRAPH_NEIGHBORS / _DIGRAPH_NEIGHBORS binding for non-multigraph non-private-storage cases. Closed perf gap from 1.16x slower to 1.04x (within nx parity). Parity bit-exact on BA50/200/500. 22 square_clustering tests pass.

title: G.degree / G.in_degree / G.out_degree views miss __eq__ — same defect class as br-r37-c1-7krwv
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — public-API view-equality parity break across all DegreeView types and directions.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx
G = fnx.Graph([(0, 1)])
G.degree == G.degree
# False on fnx (default object.__eq__ — identity)
# True on nx (DegreeView equality via dict)

DG = fnx.DiGraph([(0, 1), (1, 2)])
DG.in_degree == DG.in_degree   # False on fnx, True on nx
DG.out_degree == DG.out_degree # False on fnx, True on nx
```

Affects all 4 graph classes for `.degree`, plus `.in_degree` /
`.out_degree` on DiGraph and MultiDiGraph = 8 broken view types.

## Root cause
Four DegreeView wrapper classes had no `__eq__`:
- `_WeightAwareDegreeView` (Graph.degree, DiGraph.degree)
- `MultiGraphDegreeView` (MultiGraph.degree)
- `MultiDiGraphDegreeView` (MultiDiGraph.degree)
- `_DirectedDegreeView` (DiGraph.in_degree/out_degree, MultiDiGraph in/out)

Each access to the degree view returned a fresh instance, so default
identity comparison returned False.

Same defect class as br-r37-c1-{oww5k, k1xn4, 7krwv} — completes the
full View-equality audit (NodeView/EdgeView/InEdgeView/DegreeView).

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — equality used by tests, dedup logic, idiomatic patterns.
Same shape as the prior view-equality fixes; identical fix mechanism.

## Fix
Add `__eq__` / `__ne__` / `__hash__` to all four classes matching
nx's DegreeView semantics: equal when the dict representation
`{node: degree}` matches. Cross-class comparison allowed where the
underlying content shape matches (e.g. `_WeightAwareDegreeView` ==
`MultiGraphDegreeView`).

For `_DirectedDegreeView`, equality is gated on the
`_adjacency_attr` matching too — `in_degree != out_degree` because
they iterate different adjacency directions even on the same graph.

## Tests
4 new parametrized locks in `test_view_pickle_parity.py::
test_degree_view_equality_via_dict` (one per graph class) covering
self-equality, different-content detection, and (for directed
classes) in_degree-vs-out_degree disambiguation.

715 existing parity / pickle / conversion / attr / regression-lock
tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — completing
the view-equality audit. The trio
`NodeView (Mapping-equality, br-r37-c1-7krwv) → EdgeView (Set-equality,
br-r37-c1-{oww5k, k1xn4}) → DegreeView (dict-equality, this commit)`
now have full nx-parity equality contracts across all 4 graph classes.

title: [parity-gap] center/periphery delegate directed graphs to nx unnecessarily
description:
Audit source: python/franken_networkx/__init__.py::center (line 5299) and ::periphery (line 5340). Both have a guard if G.is_directed(): return _call_networkx_for_parity(...) that delegates the entire computation to NetworkX for any directed graph, even when fnx's own eccentricity (which they're built on top of) already handles directed graphs natively.

Repro:
  >>> import networkx as nx, franken_networkx as fnx
  >>> G = fnx.DiGraph(); G.add_edges_from([(i,(i+1)%5) for i in range(5)] + [(0,2)])
  >>> fnx.eccentricity(G)   # native, correct
  {0: 3, 1: 4, 2: 4, 3: 3, 4: 3}
  >>> fnx.center(G)         # delegates to nx — needless round-trip
  [0, 3, 4]

Effect: every directed-graph center/periphery call pays the
fnx_to_nx graph-conversion cost (build a fresh nx.Graph, copy nodes
+ edges + attrs) plus nx's own eccentricity loop, instead of
reusing fnx.eccentricity which is already on the fast Rust path.

Fix plan: drop the G.is_directed() short-circuit. The downstream
ecc = eccentricity(G); ... [n for n in G.nodes() if ecc[n] == r]
already works for both directed and undirected G (verified against
nx on cycle3 and 5-cycle-with-chord — bit-exact match).

Tagged P1 because directed-graph callers of fnx.center / fnx.periphery
take a 2-3x slowdown vs the native-eccentricity path with no
correctness benefit.
close_reason: Shipped. center and periphery now natively handle directed graphs by reusing fnx.eccentricity (already directed-aware) instead of converting back to nx. 462 center/periphery tests pass; bit-exact match against nx on cycle3 and 5-cycle+chord. Removes the fnx_to_nx graph-conversion overhead from every directed-graph call.

title: G.nodes(data=True) NodeDataView crashes pickle — wrapper_descriptor class shadowing
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — public-API serialization break on the documented `G.nodes(data=True)` idiom.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, pickle
G = fnx.Graph()
G.add_node(0, color='red')
ndv = G.nodes(data=True)
pickle.dumps(ndv)
# PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'franken_networkx.NodeView'>:
# it's not the same object as franken_networkx.NodeView
```

Affects `G.nodes(data=True)` and `G.nodes(data='attr')` on all 4
graph classes.

## Root cause
`NodeDataView.__init__` stores `self._call`, a `wrapper_descriptor`
on the Rust `NodeView` type (`<slot wrapper '__call__' of
'franken_networkx.NodeView' objects>`). When pickle serializes the
NodeDataView, it tries to serialize the wrapper_descriptor. Pickle's
qualname lookup for `franken_networkx.NodeView` finds the
Python-side `class NodeView(Mapping)` at `__init__.py:23932` —
which is a DIFFERENT class object than the Rust
`_SIMPLE_GRAPH_NODE_VIEW_TYPE` that actually owns the descriptor.
PicklingError("not the same object").

Same class-shadowing defect family as br-r37-c1-{cip5m, k66wf,
neb6c, 2vxhk, ld4oo} — completes the audit on NodeDataView.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — `G.nodes(data=True)` is the documented nx idiom for
iterating nodes-with-attrs, used in tutorials, documentation, and
production code. Serialization across caching / dask / joblib /
multiprocessing breaks.

## Fix
Add `__reduce__` to NodeDataView that snapshots the materialized
list. Restored value is a plain list (matches nx's snapshot
semantics on the restored NodeDataView). Same fix shape as the
prior pickle cycles on Rust-shadowing types.

## Tests
12 new parametrized locks in `test_view_pickle_parity.py`:
- 4 pickle roundtrip locks (one per graph class)
- 4 .data='attr' variant pickle locks
- 4 deepcopy locks

778 existing parity / pickle / conversion / attr / regression-lock
tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — extending
the pickle audit to the NodeDataView wrapper that holds a Rust-side
wrapper_descriptor. The earlier cycles fixed pickle on the
NodeView/EdgeView types directly; the NodeDataView wrapper holding
descriptors needed its own __reduce__.
close_reason: Verified pickle.dumps(g.nodes(data=True)) succeeds for fnx — wrapper_descriptor class shadowing fix landed.

title: [code-review] link-prediction family eagerly converts graph even when caller never iterates
description:
Profiling link-prediction functions on BA fixtures shows extreme slowdown vs nx:

  BA50:  jaccard_coefficient   222x slower (0.621 ms vs 0.003 ms)
  BA50:  preferential_attach   218x slower
  BA100: jaccard_coefficient   486x slower (1.396 ms vs 0.003 ms)
  BA200: jaccard_coefficient  1199x slower (3.520 ms vs 0.003 ms)

Reason: fnx.jaccard_coefficient (line 8548) and siblings (adamic_adar_index, preferential_attachment, resource_allocation_index) all call _call_networkx_for_parity which does the fnx_to_nx graph-conversion EAGERLY at function-call time. Even though nx returns a generator, the conversion happens BEFORE the generator is constructed. So a user who calls fnx.jaccard_coefficient(G) without iterating still pays the full O(|V|+|E|) graph-copy cost.

For BA200: the conversion is 3.5 ms; nx's generator-construction is 3 µs. fnx is 1000+x slower on the call alone.

Concrete fix plan (this tick): wrap each delegation in an inner generator function so the fnx_to_nx conversion only happens when iteration begins. The validation pass at _link_prediction_validate_ebunch already runs eagerly (correct — error contracts must match nx); only the conversion is deferred.

Target functions:
  - jaccard_coefficient
  - adamic_adar_index
  - preferential_attachment
  - resource_allocation_index

P1 because the slowdown is so extreme (1000x) that any user pipeline that probes these functions for any reason — even just feature-detection — pays prohibitive cost. Fix is small and uniform across 4 sister functions.
close_reason: Shipped. _link_prediction_lazy_delegate wraps each of jaccard / adamic_adar / preferential_attachment / resource_allocation in an inner generator that defers fnx_to_nx graph conversion to first iteration. Call-time perf went from 200-1200x slower than nx to 5-7x FASTER (BA200: 3.5ms → 0.6µs). Full-iteration parity preserved bit-exact; eager NodeNotFound validation preserved; 366 tests pass.

title: equivalence_classes returns list instead of nx's set (and wrong iter order)
description:
fnx.equivalence_classes returns a list of frozensets in iteration order (a, b, c, d, e), while nx returns a set of frozensets (which iterates in Python hash order). The return type and iteration order differ.

Repro:
  nodes = ['a','b','c','d','e']; eq = lambda x,y: x == y
  fnx -> [frozenset({'a'}), frozenset({'b'}), ...] (list, input order)
  nx  -> {frozenset({'d'}), frozenset({'a'}), frozenset({'b'}), ...} (set, hash order)
  
  list(nx.equivalence_classes(...)) yields hash-order frozensets.
  list(fnx.equivalence_classes(...)) yields input-order frozensets.

Drop-in code expecting nx's set-of-frozensets return type or its hash-based iteration order broke.

Fix: delegate to nx (small function, simple delegation). Mirrors the cycle_basis / find_cliques / SCC delegation pattern.
