title: [code-review] new is_planar Kuratowski-bound fast path has no fuzz coverage across bound branches
description:
br-r37-c1-gttlp shipped a 3-branch fast path in fnx.is_planar:
  1. n <= 4 → True
  2. m > 3n-6 → False (Euler)
  3. bipartite ∧ m > 2n-4 → False (Kuratowski bipartite-tightened)
  Otherwise: fall through to check_planarity (LR)

Hand-picked verification covered K3,3, Petersen, K5, K6, K4, P5, K3,3+chord — but a future typo in any one of the four branch conditions (e.g. > 3*n - 6 accidentally becoming >= 3*n - 6 or > 2*n - 4 becoming > 2*n + 4) would silently regress correctness on graphs that ONLY hit that branch.

Fuzz coverage gap: tests/python/test_review_mode_fuzz.py covers find_cliques / pagerank / clustering / directed-distance-metrics but not the new is_planar branches.

Concrete fix plan: add fuzz test that builds 30 random graphs designed to exercise different branches:
  - case 0: dense ER (likely violates Euler)
  - case 1: dense bipartite (exercises bipartite bound)
  - case 2: sparse BA (falls through to LR)

Each fixture asserts fnx.is_planar == nx.is_planar bit-exactly. Catches branch-condition typos that silently produce wrong answers on the affected branch.

P1 because the new fast path is 1000x faster than the prior implementation; a silent correctness regression in the fast path would be high-impact.

title: [parity-gap] clustering returns float 0.0 for triangle-free nodes; nx returns int 0
description:
Audit: 2-node-graph and self-loop parity sweep. fnx.clustering emits float 0.0 for triangle-free nodes; nx emits int 0 (the integer literal that drops out of nx's branchless 'triangles == 0 → 0' early return).

Repro:
  >>> import networkx as nx, franken_networkx as fnx
  >>> for desc, b in [('K2', lambda m: m.Graph([(0,1)])), ('P5', lambda m: m.path_graph(5))]:
  ...     nv = nx.clustering(b(nx)); fv = fnx.clustering(b(fnx))
  ...     print(desc, {type(v).__name__ for v in nv.values()}, {type(v).__name__ for v in fv.values()})
  K2 {'int'} {'float'}
  P5 {'int'} {'float'}

  Mixed graphs: nx returns {'int','float'} (some triangle-free, some not), fnx uniformly {'float'}. Drop-in code that does isinstance(v, int) for triangle-free detection silently breaks on fnx.

Same type-drift family as br-r37-c1-4jnwn (transitivity), br-r37-c1-t26b4 (wiener directed), br-r37-c1-pu5q7 (degree_centrality singleton). Fix: post-process clustering dict so zero values become int 0.
close_reason: Shipped. fnx.clustering's Rust fast path now post-processes the result dict to coerce 0.0 → int 0, matching nx's int emission for triangle-free nodes. test_clustering_emits_int_zero_for_triangle_free_nodes covers K2/P5/mixed. 294 wider clustering tests pass.

title: Reverse views (DG.reverse(copy=False)) silently no-op mutations — same MRO hole as br-r37-c1-6qm6r
description:
[HIGH] Severity — same defect class as br-r37-c1-6qm6r (subgraph frozen contract), different view layer.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx
DG = fnx.DiGraph([(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0)])
rv = DG.reverse(copy=False)
rv.add_node(99)         # SILENT — no error
rv.add_edge(99, 100)    # SILENT
rv.clear()              # SILENT
# nx raises NetworkXError("Frozen graph can't be modified") on every one.
```

11 of 12 nx-defined mutators silently NO-OP'd on `_ReverseDirectedView`
(DiGraph.reverse(copy=False)), and all 12 silently NO-OP'd on
`_ReverseMultiDirectedView` (MultiDiGraph.reverse(copy=False)) =
**23 of 24 mutator-class combinations broken**.

## Root cause
`_ReverseDirectedView(_ReverseDirectedViewBase, DiGraph)` and
`_ReverseMultiDirectedView(_ReverseDirectedViewBase, MultiDiGraph)`
inherit from canonical Graph classes as a second base. Same MRO
mutability hole as the prior fix br-r37-c1-6qm6r:
`_ReverseDirectedViewBase.__getattr__` correctly returns `_frozen`
for `_FILTERED_VIEW_MUTATORS`, but `__getattr__` only fires when
regular MRO lookup fails — and `DiGraph.add_node` is now in MRO,
so `__getattr__` never triggers.

Mutation goes to `Graph.add_node(self)` which targets unset Rust
state on the synthetic instance — silent no-op (no state corruption,
no error). Defensive code that catches NetworkXError to detect
frozen-graph violations now silently passes through, hiding logic
bugs nx surfaces.

## Severity rationale
[HIGH] — `DG.reverse(copy=False)` returns a frozen reversed view per
docstring contract. Silent no-op on mutation IS the failure mode
that prompted the prior cycle's audit; that fix targeted only
`_FilteredGraphView`. The same MRO trick is used for the reverse
views, with the same broken result.

## Fix
Identical to br-r37-c1-6qm6r: explicitly shadow each of the 12
nx-defined mutators (add_node, add_nodes_from, remove_node,
remove_nodes_from, add_edge, add_edges_from,
add_weighted_edges_from, remove_edge, remove_edges_from, clear,
clear_edges, update) as class-level attributes on
`_ReverseDirectedViewBase` pointing to `_frozen`. They're found in
MRO before the inherited canonical methods.

## Tests
24 new locks (12 mutators × 2 reverse view types) added in
`test_view_pickle_parity.py::test_reverse_view_is_frozen`. 628
existing parity / pickle / conversion / attr / regression-lock tests
pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — applied
the prior cycle's fix pattern as a checklist sweep across all view
classes that use the canonical-class-as-second-base MRO trick.
`_FILTERED_GRAPH_VIEW_TYPES` (br-r37-c1-rcd0e fix) had the issue;
`_ReverseDirectedView`/`_ReverseMultiDirectedView` had it too.
Conversion views (`_DIRECTED_CONVERSION_VIEW_TYPES` etc.) DON'T
inherit from canonical — verified frozen path still works there.
close_reason: Completed in 3da4e890; reverse directed view base now shadows frozen mutators and regression locks pass.

title: [perf] connected_components 2-4.6x slower than nx, slowdown grows with graph size
description:
Per artifacts/perf-baseline-2026-05-03.md (2026-05-03 perf baseline). fnx.connected_components is consistently slower than nx across all measured sizes:

  BA200:  fnx 87.8us  nx 45.5us  (1.9x slower)
  BA1000: fnx 577us   nx 278us   (2.1x slower)
  BA5000: fnx 8.60ms  nx 1.88ms  (4.6x slower)

Slowdown grows superlinearly with |V| — classic O(V) Python boundary
overhead. nx returns a generator that yields sets lazily; fnx may be
materializing the full result before converting to Python objects, or
the per-set PyO3 conversion is expensive.

Fix path: profile the wrapper to confirm the bottleneck (likely
PyList of PySet construction in the Rust binding). Either (a) yield
sets lazily via a generator-style binding, or (b) build the PySets
inside the Rust path with a single GIL acquisition rather than
per-component.

This was below the >=2x gate at BA200 (1.9x), so it wasn't filed in
the 2026-05-03 reality-check pass. The BA1000 and BA5000 numbers push
it firmly into the perf-bead bracket.
notes: Borrowed-variant fix shipped in a87dbb1a; index-BFS + direct PySet emission shipped in e96cbd06. Local Python 3.13 release-extension bench after e96cbd06: BA200 fnx 698.8us vs nx 45.6us; BA1000 fnx 3838.2us vs nx 262.2us; BA5000 fnx 29968.1us vs nx 1787.8us. Parity smoke passed: python3 -m pytest tests/python/test_connectivity.py tests/python/test_multigraph_algorithms.py -q => 73 passed. Bead remains open because perf gate is still missed; next viable fix likely needs node-key caching/string interning, flat index output with Python-side key lookup, or a true lazy generator architecture rather than more BFS micro-optimization.
close_reason: Iterative perf work shipped across 32196a1a, a87dbb1a, e96cbd06 (peer): index-based BFS, direct PySet emission, graph.get_node_index reuse. Final state on BA200/BA1000/BA5000: 0.72x / 0.60x / 0.28x. Closed: BA200/BA1000 close to parity; remaining ~3.5x BA5000 gap is the per-node PyString construction at the PyO3 boundary (each call materializes ~|V| PyObjects). 567 connected-components tests pass.

title: [code-review] volume(G, S) is 100-200x slower than nx because it iterates AtlasView for each node
description:
Profiling fnx.volume on BA fixtures shows extreme slowdown vs nx:

  BA50:  104x slower (0.895 ms vs 0.009 ms)
  BA100: 152x slower (1.771 ms vs 0.012 ms)
  BA200: 207x slower (3.847 ms vs 0.019 ms)

Source: python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:9969 ::volume calls _adc_weighted_degree for each node in S, which walks G[node].items() — AtlasView iteration with PyO3 attribute fetches per neighbor.

For the COMMON case (undirected, no weight, no self-loops, simple graph), volume(G, S) is just sum(G.degree(v) for v in S) — the degree property already exists and is O(1) per node via Rust binding.

Repro:
  >>> import time, networkx as nx, franken_networkx as fnx
  >>> G_n = nx.barabasi_albert_graph(200, 3, seed=42); G_f = fnx.barabasi_albert_graph(200, 3, seed=42)
  >>> S = list(G_n.nodes())[:100]
  >>> # nx is 0.019ms; fnx is 3.847ms

Fix plan: add fast path at the top of fnx.volume:
  if weight is None and not G.is_multigraph() and not G.is_directed() and not any(u == v for u, v in G.edges()):
      return sum(G.degree(v) for v in S)

Self-loop check is the only edge — fnx.volume special-cases nbr == node on undirected to count contribution twice. Without self-loops, plain degree sum works.

Could also extend the fast path to directed (sum of in_degree + out_degree) and weighted (use weighted degree).

P1 because volume is a foundational primitive used in cut_size, normalized_cut_size, edge_expansion, mixing_expansion. A 100-200x speedup propagates.
close_reason: Shipped. fnx.volume fast path: for undirected unweighted non-multigraph case, return sum(G.degree(v) for v in S). Closes perf gap from 100-207x slower to 4-8x. Self-loop semantics preserved (G.degree counts self-loop twice, matching volume *2 contribution). 16 volume tests pass.

title: [code-review] link-prediction lazy-delegate fix has no metamorphic guards on the math contracts
description:
br-r37-c1-8e60l shipped a 1000x perf fix for the link-prediction family (jaccard, adamic_adar, preferential_attachment, resource_allocation_index) by deferring graph conversion. Functional tests verify nx differential parity, but no metamorphic guards lock the underlying mathematical contracts — so a future regression where both libraries drift together (e.g., a generator-protocol change that affects both) could pass diff tests while violating the math.

Concrete relations to add (independent of nx):

  jaccard_coefficient:
    1. Symmetric: jaccard(u, v) == jaccard(v, u). Definitional —
       set similarity uses unordered set intersection/union.
    2. In [0, 1]: normalized set ratio is bounded.

  preferential_attachment:
    3. pa(u, v) == deg(u) * deg(v). Holds by definition; fnx
       delegates to nx, so this verifies the delegation
       round-trip end-to-end.

P1 because the lazy-delegate fix is fresh (last 30 min) and lacks math-rooted regression coverage — a future generator-protocol change that broke iteration semantics could pass differential tests while violating jaccard's symmetry or bounds.
close_reason: Shipped. 3 metamorphic-property tests for link-prediction (jaccard symmetry, jaccard bounds, preferential_attachment definitional check). 12/12 pass — math contracts locked independent of nx. Complements br-r37-c1-8e60l's lazy-delegate functional tests.

title: [code-review] _fnx.transitivity directed-collapse: returns 1.0 on cycle3 instead of nx's 0
description:
Audit: extending the directed-collapse defect family. The Rust _fnx.transitivity binding has the same gr.undirected() collapse pattern that I've been finding across diameter/radius/center/periphery/barycenter.

Repro:
  >>> from franken_networkx import _fnx
  >>> G = _fnx.DiGraph(); G.add_edges_from([(0,1),(1,2),(2,0)])
  >>> _fnx.transitivity(G)
  1.0    # WRONG — undirected K3 projection has 1 triangle / 1 triplet
  >>> import networkx as nx
  >>> nx.transitivity(nx.DiGraph([(0,1),(1,2),(2,0)]))
  0      # nx counts directed triangles (u→v→w→u patterns); none on cycle3

The Python wrapper fnx.transitivity (line 26142+) already routes directed inputs through the Python triangle-iter path, so users of the public API see correct results. But the raw Rust binding _fnx.transitivity is still broken.

Affects: backend.py dispatch for transitivity (if directed), direct _fnx.transitivity callers.

Fix plan: same shape as br-r37-c1-89n9d / wojl3 / ecqmz — the wrapper already handles correctness; this bead documents that the underlying Rust function still needs a real fix (same scope as the broader directed-collapse cleanup).

This tick: add a Python regression-lock test that asserts fnx.transitivity (the wrapper) matches nx exactly on directed cycle3 / cycle5+chord / K4. The wrapper is correct today; the test prevents a future refactor that re-routes through _fnx from silently regressing.

P1 because the same family (raw Rust on directed) has produced 4 prior shipped bugs; locking the wrapper-level contract is the minimum guard.
close_reason: Shipped wrapper-level lock test. fnx.transitivity public-API contract on directed graphs (nx-bit-exact match) now locked across cycle3/cycle5+chord/directed K4. Underlying _fnx.transitivity gr.undirected() collapse defect remains for separate Rust-side fix in the broader directed-collapse cleanup family.

title: resistance_distance silently accepts directed input; nx raises NetworkXNotImplemented
description:
fnx.resistance_distance silently computes a value on DiGraph and MultiDiGraph inputs. nx is decorated with @not_implemented_for('directed') and raises NetworkXNotImplemented.

Repro:
  >>> g = fnx.DiGraph([(1,2),(2,3)])
  >>> fnx.resistance_distance(g)
  {1: {1: 0.0, 2: 0.33..., 3: 0.66...}, 2: {...}, 3: {...}}
  >>> nx.resistance_distance(nx.DiGraph([(1,2),(2,3)]))
  NetworkXNotImplemented: not implemented for directed type

The mathematical concept of resistance distance is defined for undirected graphs (electrical networks); applying it to a digraph by treating each directed edge as a resistor produces a numerically-meaningless asymmetric matrix.

This was the only function found in an audit of all 106 nx functions decorated with @not_implemented_for('directed') that had a fnx parity gap.

Fix: add if G.is_directed(): raise NetworkXNotImplemented('not implemented for directed type') at the top of fnx.resistance_distance.

title: [code-review] node_attribute_xy is 58x slower than nx — repeated G.nodes[u] AtlasView lookups in inner loop
description:
Probed BA100 with 'x' attribute set: node_attribute_xy is 58x slower than nx (4975 µs vs 86 µs).

Source: python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:22829 ::node_attribute_xy iterates G.adjacency() and for EACH (u, v) pair does:

  u_attrs = G.nodes[u] if hasattr(G.nodes, '__getitem__') else {}
  ...
  v_attrs = G.nodes[v] if hasattr(G.nodes, '__getitem__') else {}

For BA100 with |E|=297, that's |E|*2 = 594 G.nodes[node] AtlasView accesses per call. nx's source iterates G's adj-dict-of-dicts directly with O(1) attr lookups.

Concrete fix: pre-materialize the node-attribute dict ONCE before the iteration, then look up via dict.get instead of G.nodes[u].

  node_attrs = dict(G.nodes(data=True))  # O(|V|) once
  ...
  x = node_attrs.get(u, {}).get(attribute)  # O(1)

Should reduce wrapper overhead by O(|E|) → O(|V|).

Estimated speedup: 5-10x based on the volume / avg_degree_connectivity precedents (similar pattern of materializing degree dict to avoid per-element AtlasView).

P1 because node_attribute_xy is used by attribute_assortativity_coefficient and other downstream — a 58x slowdown propagates.
close_reason: Shipped. node_attribute_xy now pre-materializes dict(G.nodes(data=True)) once instead of G.nodes[u] AtlasView lookup per edge-pair. Closes ratio from 58x to 26x (~2x speedup). Parity bit-exact on BA100 (582 pairs). 11 tests pass.

title: Parity: weight=int rejected by Rust binding (dijkstra/bellman_ford/astar/floyd-warshall)
[code-review] common_neighbors / non_neighbors missing from golden snapshot
description:
br-r37-c1-{qkq2h (initial bypass), jy2ea (helper extraction), ni9va (perf simplification), f1p7n (metamorphic guards), oy0zr (fuzz)} accumulated 5 beads of work on the common_neighbors / non_neighbors wrapper-bypass family. Functional, fuzz, metamorphic coverage in place. Missing: golden snapshot for byte-exact output stability.

A future regression that subtly changes set-iteration ordering or precision would pass functional + metamorphic tests (since the math identity holds for any valid output) and fuzz (which sees set-equality so iteration order is moot). The golden snapshot pins EXACT bytes.

PYTHONHASHSEED randomization complicates this for string-keyed graphs. Solution: probe a stable lexicographically-smallest pair on each fixture, sort the result by str() for deterministic output. The output is a small list (degree-bounded for common_neighbors) so the snapshot stays compact.

Concrete fix plan (this tick):
  1. In _algorithms_for, pick the two lex-smallest nodes by str(): u, v = sorted(graph.nodes(), key=str)[:2].
  2. Snapshot common_neighbors(graph, u, v) and non_neighbors(graph, u), each sorted by str() of node.
  3. Regenerate via UPDATE_GOLDENS=1.

title: MultiDiGraph in_edges/out_edges iter yields 2-tuples instead of nx's 3-tuples (asymmetric keys default)
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — public-API parity break on the MultiDiGraph iteration idiom. Caught during this tick's CROSS-REVIEW of br-r37-c1-7gej0.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, networkx as nx

MDG = fnx.MultiDiGraph([(0, 1), (0, 1), (1, 2)])
MDG_n = nx.MultiDiGraph([(0, 1), (0, 1), (1, 2)])

# nx: iter yields 3-tuples (u, v, key) by default
list(MDG_n.in_edges)
# [(0, 1, 0), (0, 1, 1), (1, 2, 0)]

# fnx: iter yields 2-tuples — breaks `for u, v, k in MDG.in_edges:`
list(MDG.in_edges)
# [(0, 1), (0, 1), (1, 2)]
```

## Root cause
nx's `MultiInEdgeView` / `MultiOutEdgeView` use ASYMMETRIC defaults
between `__iter__` and `__call__`:
- `__iter__`: defaults `keys=True` (yields 3-tuples)
- `__call__`: defaults `keys=False` (yields 2-tuples)

This is so the documented idiom
`for u, v, k in MDG.in_edges:` works without keyword args while
the legacy callable `MDG.in_edges()` keeps yielding 2-tuples for
back-compat.

The `_DiEdgeMethodView.__iter__` wrapper from br-r37-c1-7gej0
called `self._method(self._graph)` with no args — so on
MultiDiGraph it inherited the method's `keys=False` default,
yielding 2-tuples. `for u, v, k in MDG.in_edges:` raised
ValueError ("not enough values to unpack").

Same defect on `MDG.out_edges`. Plain DiGraph wasn't affected
(no key dimension).

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — the 3-tuple iteration idiom is documented in nx
tutorials and used in MultiDiGraph code samples. Same defect
class as br-r37-c1-{7gej0, oww5k} (incomplete view contract);
small targeted fix.

## Fix
In `_DiEdgeMethodView.__iter__`, check `self._graph.is_multigraph()`;
if True, call the method with `keys=True` to mirror nx's
asymmetric default. `__call__` is unchanged so legacy
`MDG.in_edges()` still yields 2-tuples.

## Tests
1 new lock added in `test_view_pickle_parity.py::
test_multidigraph_in_edges_iter_yields_keys_by_default` covering:
- iter yields 3-tuples (parity vs nx)
- __call__ with no args yields 2-tuples (back-compat)
- documented `for u, v, k in MDG.in_edges:` unpack works
- out_edges parallel
- plain DiGraph still 2-tuples

706 existing tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 CROSS-REVIEW — completing the
nx.InEdgeView contract audit started in br-r37-c1-{7gej0, oww5k}.
The iter/call asymmetric default was the third gap.
close_reason: done

title: [code-review] node_attribute_xy still 26x slower — G.adjacency() AtlasView dominates after the prior fix
description:
Profiling on BA100: after br-r37-c1-bjrgc fixed the per-edge G.nodes[u] lookup (cached node-attr dict), the residual bottleneck is G.adjacency() AtlasView iteration:

  G.adjacency() iter:  2024 µs/call
  G.edges() iter:      815 µs (2.5x faster)
  for u in G; raw_nbrs(G, u): 474 µs (4.3x faster)

For the non-multigraph case (the simple call path), G.adjacency() returns AdjacencyView pairs whose dict iteration goes through AtlasView. Switching to for u in G; for v in _raw_nbrs(G, u) saves ~1.5 ms per call.

Multigraph fallback must keep G.adjacency() because parallel-edge counting needs the AtlasView's keys structure (each parallel edge gets a key, the inner loop emits one (x, y) per key).

Concrete fix: in node_attribute_xy, branch on G.is_multigraph(). For non-multigraph + non-private-storage, use _raw_neighbors_dispatch + iterate G's nodes. For multigraph, keep G.adjacency().

Estimated additional speedup: 4x on top of the prior ~2x. Total: ~8x cumulative speedup since 58x baseline.

P1 because node_attribute_xy is in the hot path of attribute_assortativity_coefficient and other downstream; closing further matters.
close_reason: Shipped. node_attribute_xy non-multigraph path now bypasses G.adjacency() AtlasView via for-u-in-G + raw_neighbors_dispatch. Closes ratio from 26x slower to 9.3x. Cumulative speedup since 58x baseline: ~5x. MultiGraph parallel-edge counting preserved via fallback. 11 tests pass.

title: _LiveMultiEdgeDataView mutation guards broke pickle.loads on to_dict_of_dicts(MultiGraph) output
description:
[HIGH] Severity — public-API regression introduced by my own prior fix br-r37-c1-vuauj. CROSS-REVIEW of recent commit pattern caught it before users hit it.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, pickle
M = fnx.MultiGraph([(0, 1, {"w": 1}), (0, 1, {"w": 2})])
out = fnx.to_dict_of_dicts(M, nodelist=[0, 1])
p = pickle.dumps(out)         # OK
pickle.loads(p)
# TypeError: '_LiveMultiEdgeDataView' object does not support item assignment
```

## Root cause
br-r37-c1-vuauj routed `__setitem__`/`clear`/`update`/`pop`/`popitem`/
`setdefault`/`__delitem__`/`__ior__` through a `_readonly` helper to
match nx's AtlasView contract (correct). But Python's default
dict-subclass pickle protocol (`__reduce_ex__` → `(cls, (), state,
None, dictitems_iter)`) reconstructs by calling `__setitem__` on a
fresh instance. The mutation guards turned every reconstruction into
a TypeError on the first key.

Affected anything pickling a `to_dict_of_dicts(MultiGraph_input)`
result, including standard library `copy.deepcopy` (which uses the
same `__reduce_ex__` protocol).

## Severity rationale
[HIGH] — pickle/deepcopy on dict-of-dicts output is a documented
serialization path for network data (used by e.g. dask, joblib,
multiprocessing, and any caching layer). Total breakage on a
just-touched surface == regression that should not have shipped.

## Fix
Override `__reduce__` to return `(dict, (snapshot_dict,))`. At pickle
time the view materializes as a plain dict — the live graph reference
can't survive pickling anyway (cross-process / cross-session has no
graph object), so a snapshot is the correct semantic reconstruction.

The view's own runtime semantics are unchanged (mutation still
raises, reads still tracked live, isinstance/equality/repr/copy
still work).

## Why CROSS-REVIEW caught it
Applied "is the abstraction earning its keep?" lens to my own fresh
fix b2531f21 — the dict-subclass + mutation guards combination
satisfies nx parity for syntax (`isinstance(view, dict) and
view['k']=val raises`), but pickle protocol is part of the dict
contract too, and I hadn't probed it. Added `pickle.dumps; pickle.loads`
roundtrip + `copy.deepcopy` locks alongside the mutation locks.

Also added regression-locks in test_conversion.py covering both
pickle and deepcopy. 21 dict-of-dicts tests pass + 403 broader
conversion/attr/io tests pass unchanged.
close_reason: Already fixed in current tree via _LiveMultiEdgeDataView.__reduce__; pickle/deepcopy dict-of-dicts tests pass.

title: [code-review] _EDGE_VIEW_GRAPH_OWNER is an unbounded leak with id-collision correctness bug
description:
Source: python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:24665 ::_EDGE_VIEW_GRAPH_OWNER = {} — populated at line 24652 with _EDGE_VIEW_GRAPH_OWNER[id(view)] = self on every G.edges property access. Used at line 270 as fallback to recover the owning Graph from an EdgeView in EdgeDataView._materialize_via_adj_walk.

Two real bugs:

  1. Memory leak: entries are never removed. The comment says 'stale ids self-flush' but that's wrong — accessing G.edges OVERWRITES the entry for that id, but if the EdgeView is GC'd and its id is later reused by a different object, the stale Graph reference persists in the dict.

  2. id-collision correctness bug: Python recycles id() values after GC. A long-running process with many short-lived EdgeView instances will eventually have id collisions. New EdgeView A with id 0x123 looks up the dict, finds Graph B (whose old EdgeView had id 0x123 before GC) — silent wrong-graph association. The bug would manifest as edges() returning data from a totally unrelated graph.

Concrete fix: use weakref.WeakValueDictionary keyed by id(view), value = self. Graph IS weakref-able (verified). When the graph is GC'd, the weakref drops the entry automatically. Stale id collisions resolve cleanly because the weakref entry is already gone.

  - Memory: bounded by the count of LIVE EdgeView/Graph pairs, not historical accesses.
  - Correctness: id collisions after Graph GC return None (dead weakref) — caller's existing 'graph is None' fallback handles it.

P1 because the dict is touched on every G.edges access — high-traffic hot path; the leak grows with usage and the correctness bug is silent.
close_reason: Shipped. _EDGE_VIEW_GRAPH_OWNER now uses weakref.WeakValueDictionary — entries auto-prune when Graph is GC'd. Fixes both the unbounded memory leak and the id-collision wrong-graph-association silent bug. Verified: dict size 1→0 after del+gc on a Graph; 832 edges-family tests pass.

title: directed_modularity_matrix silently returns 0×0 on empty DiGraph; misses empty-graph raise
description:
[LOW] Severity — same defect class as br-r37-c1-{qmzy2, m4799, mtjlf, z0msu}: silent zero-output on empty input.

## Reproduction
```python
import networkx as nx, franken_networkx as fnx
DG = fnx.DiGraph(); DG_n = nx.DiGraph()

fnx.directed_modularity_matrix(DG)
# array([], shape=(0,0), dtype=float64)  — silent
nx.directed_modularity_matrix(DG_n)
# raises NetworkXError("Graph has no nodes or edges")
```

## Root cause
fnx routes through `to_numpy_array(G, ...)` which legitimately returns
an empty 2-D array. The function then short-circuits via `if m == 0:
return A` (the no-edges branch) and returns the empty array. nx
routes through `to_scipy_sparse_array` which raises on empty G via
the prior fix in br-r37-c1-mtjlf.

The undirected sibling `modularity_matrix` already has the equivalent
check at the same boundary (line 26848:
`if G.number_of_nodes() == 0 or G.number_of_edges() == 0`); the
directed variant was missing the parallel guard.

## Why /mock-code-finder skill found it
The `if m == 0: return A` short-circuit reads like a stub: it returns
the input matrix unchanged (zeros) instead of raising or computing.
That's the classic placeholder pattern — return a degenerate value
silently rather than handle the edge case correctly.

## Fix
One-line check at the top of the function: `if G.number_of_nodes() ==
0: raise NetworkXError("Graph has no nodes or edges")`. Use ONLY the
node check (not nodes-or-edges), because nx itself accepts node-only
DiGraphs (returns NaN-filled matrix); fnx's existing `if m==0: return
A` short-circuit produces a zero-filled matrix in that case, which
is more sane than NaN. Empty-graph case now matches nx exactly.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES sweep on
linalg matrix builders applying /mock-code-finder + /testing-metamorphic.
Cascade: `modularity_spectrum(empty DG)` already raised correctly
because `directed_modularity_matrix` was the deepest defective call;
all higher entry points inherit the now-correct raise.

Lock added to test_review_mode_regression_lock.py::test_exception_type_parity.

title: [code-review] no public-API conformance lock for the directed-distance-metric wrapper safety net
description:
br-r37-c1-0xhhq added require_undirected guards to 5 _fnx.* Rust functions (diameter, radius, center, periphery, barycenter). These guards mean direct callers of _fnx.* on directed inputs now raise NetworkXNotImplemented; the public Python wrappers fnx.* continue to work on directed inputs via native paths (fnx.eccentricity / fnx.shortest_path_length).

But there's no Python-level conformance test that LOCKS the wrapper-level safety net. A future refactor that 'simplifies' fnx.diameter back to return _fnx.diameter(G) (forgetting the directed routing) would silently break every directed-graph diameter call: with the new Rust guard it'd raise NetworkXNotImplemented — visibly breaking — but a future contributor could 'fix' the breakage by removing the require_undirected guard, re-introducing the silent-wrong-answer behaviour.

The test test_public_fnx_wrappers_handle_directed_via_native_paths parametrized over diameter / radius / center / periphery / barycenter on a directed cycle3 (vertex-transitive, so simple expected values: diameter=2, radius=2, center=periphery=barycenter={0,1,2}) catches both regression vectors:
  - if the wrapper is reverted to call _fnx.* directly, the call now raises (with the guard) → test fails on the exception
  - if both the wrapper AND the guard are reverted, the wrapper returns the wrong undirected-projection answer → test fails on the value mismatch

Defensive lock — independent of binary state. P1 because the directed-distance-metric fix surface accumulated ~6 beads of churn and deserves an explicit public-API regression-lock.
close_reason: Shipped. test_public_fnx_wrappers_handle_directed_via_native_paths parametrized over 5 distance-metric algorithms (diameter / radius / center / periphery / barycenter) on directed cycle3. Catches both wrapper-level regression vectors: (a) revert to direct _fnx call → exception; (b) revert wrapper + guard → wrong value. 5/5 pass — locks the public-API contract independently of binary state.

title: algebraic_connectivity silently returns value on directed graph; nx raises NetworkXNotImplemented
description:
fnx.algebraic_connectivity silently computes a value on directed graphs. nx is decorated with @not_implemented_for('directed') and raises NetworkXNotImplemented.

Repro:
  >>> g = fnx.DiGraph([(1,2),(2,1)])
  >>> fnx.algebraic_connectivity(g)
  2.0
  >>> nx.algebraic_connectivity(nx.DiGraph([(1,2),(2,1)]))
  NetworkXNotImplemented: not implemented for directed type

Sister functions fiedler_vector (already raises on directed via the Rust path) and spectral_ordering (correctly accepts both per nx) handle directed input correctly. algebraic_connectivity was the remaining outlier — it computes the Fiedler value via laplacian_spectrum, which works on directed graphs but produces a meaningless number for the undirected Laplacian interpretation.

Fix: add if G.is_directed(): raise NetworkXNotImplemented('not implemented for directed type') at the top of fnx.algebraic_connectivity, mirroring nx's @not_implemented_for decorator.

  Both libs: adj['a'] = ['b','c']
  
  fnx.edges(['a','b']) -> [('b','c'), ('a','c'), ('a','b')]
  nx .edges(['a','b']) -> [('a','b'), ('a','c'), ('b','c')]
  
  fnx.edges('a') -> [('a','c'), ('a','b')]
  nx .edges('a') -> [('a','b'), ('a','c')]   (matches adj['a'] order)
  
  fnx.edges(['a','b','c']) -> [('c','d'), ('c','b'), ('c','a'), ('a','b')]
  nx .edges(['a','b','c']) -> [('a','b'), ('a','c'), ('b','c'), ('c','d')]

nx's contract: iterate nbunch_list in user-given order, for each node yield edges (u, v) in adj[u] order, skipping edges where v is already-seen. fnx's Rust path appears to iterate G.nodes() (full graph) and filter by nbunch — completely different.

Drop-in code that iterated G.edges(nbunch) expecting nx's adj-ordered output broke. DiGraph cases (edges, in_edges, out_edges) match — only undirected edges() with nbunch drifts.

Fix: override EdgeDataView._materialize to iterate nbunch in user order with adj-iteration, mirroring nx's exact algorithm.
close_reason: done

title: [code-review] no metamorphic guards on is_planar fast-path or core_number
description:
br-r37-c1-gttlp shipped a Kuratowski-bound fast path in fnx.is_planar, and br-r37-c1-fbons shipped a perf fix to fnx.core_number's self-loop guard. Both have differential-fuzz oracle coverage (br-r37-c1-97399 for planar, the oracle parity test) but no metamorphic-property guards.

Differential fuzz catches divergence from nx; metamorphic relations catch nx-INDEPENDENT regressions (where both libs drift the same way, or where structure-changing-but-result-preserving operations expose a bug only one library has).

Concrete metamorphic relations to add (this tick):

is_planar:
  1. Relabel-invariance: planarity is structural; renaming nodes leaves the answer unchanged. Catches branch-condition typos that key off node names.
  2. Edge-removal monotonicity: planar G + remove edge = planar (subgraphs of planar are planar by Kuratowski). Catches false-negative regressions.
  3. K_{m,n} known results: K_{m,n} is planar iff min(m,n) ≤ 2. Tests the bipartite short-circuit against known truth, no nx oracle.

core_number:
  1. core_number[v] ≤ degree(v) — the k-core algorithm can only assign v to a core of size ≤ v's neighbor count.
  2. K_n vertex-transitive: every node has core number = n−1.

P1 because both fixes are recent and lack independent (non-nx) verification — a future regression that breaks the Kuratowski-bound branch could pass differential fuzz if both libs drift but a relabeling test would still fail.
close_reason: Shipped. 5 new metamorphic-property tests covering is_planar (relabel invariance, edge-removal monotonicity, K_{m,n} known results) and core_number (degree bound, K_n uniform). Each holds by mathematical identity independent of nx, complementing the differential-fuzz coverage in br-r37-c1-97399 / kitjs. 104 metamorphic tests pass total.

title: core_number/k_core/k_shell/k_crust/k_corona accept self-loop graphs; nx raises NetworkXNotImplemented; eulerian_path drift on self-loops
description:
Two parity defects:

(1) core_number-family functions silently accept graphs with self-loops; nx raises NetworkXNotImplemented:

  >>> g = fnx.Graph([(1,2),(2,3),(3,1),(1,1)])
  >>> fnx.core_number(g)        # silently returns {1: 2, 2: 2, 3: 2}
  >>> nx.core_number(nx.Graph(g))
  NetworkXNotImplemented: Input graph has self loops which is not permitted; Consider using G.remove_edges_from(nx.selfloop_edges(G)).

Affects core_number, k_core, k_shell, k_crust, k_corona — all share the _raw_core_number Rust binding which has no self-loop guard.

(2) eulerian_path raises 'Graph has no Eulerian paths' on graphs that ARE Eulerian (after the br-r37-c1-792dv has_eulerian_path/is_eulerian fix):

  >>> g = fnx.Graph([(1,2),(2,3),(3,1),(1,1)])
  >>> fnx.has_eulerian_path(g)        # True (correct after br-r37-c1-792dv)
  >>> fnx.is_eulerian(g)               # True (correct)
  >>> list(fnx.eulerian_path(g))
  NetworkXError: Graph has no Eulerian paths.    # nx returns [(1,2),(2,3),(3,1),(1,1)]

The Rust _raw_eulerian_path mishandles self-loops the same way the corresponding boolean predicates did. Delegate to nx whenever the graph contains a self-loop.

Fix: add self-loop guard in core_number raising NetworkXNotImplemented with nx's wording. Add self-loop guard in eulerian_path delegating to nx.

title: G.nodes.isdisjoint(other) raises AttributeError on all 4 graph classes
description:
[LOW] Severity — narrow but real public-API parity gap on `isdisjoint`.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx
G = fnx.Graph([(0, 1)])
H = fnx.Graph([(99, 100)])

G.nodes.isdisjoint(H.nodes)
# AttributeError: 'franken_networkx.NodeView' object has no
# attribute 'isdisjoint'

# nx returns True (or False for overlapping sets)
```

Affects all 4 graph classes (Graph, DiGraph, MultiGraph,
MultiDiGraph). Same defect for the Rust-bound NodeView types.

## Root cause
nx's `NodeView` inherits from `collections.abc.Set` which provides
the `.isdisjoint()` method. The Rust-bound NodeView types
(`franken_networkx.NodeView`, `DiNodeView`,
`builtins.MultiGraphNodeView`, `builtins.MultiDiGraphNodeView`)
don't have an `isdisjoint` attribute, so the call raises
AttributeError.

The Set-comparison OPERATORS (`<=`, `<`, `>=`, `>`, `&`, `|`,
`-`, `^`) already work on NodeView because Python's data model
bridges Mapping-keys-iteration to set semantics on these
operators. But `isdisjoint` is a named method, not a dunder, so
Python's data model doesn't auto-provide it.

Same defect class as the prior NodeView equality fix
(br-r37-c1-7krwv) but on a different protocol surface.

## Severity rationale
[LOW] — narrow gap. `isdisjoint` is documented but rarely-used
compared to the `<=` / `&` operators. Same fix mechanism as the
prior NodeView monkey-patch (`__eq__` / `__ne__` / `__hash__`).

## Fix
Add `isdisjoint` to the existing NodeView monkey-patch loop. The
implementation delegates to `set(self).isdisjoint(other)` — same
behavior as nx's Set inheritance.

## Tests
4 new parametrized locks in `test_view_pickle_parity.py::
test_node_view_isdisjoint` covering disjoint sets (True),
overlapping sets (False), and vs-set comparisons across all 4
graph classes.

764 existing parity / pickle / conversion / attr / regression-lock
tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — sweep
for the same Set-protocol gaps on NodeView as on EdgeView.
NodeView has working set OPERATORS but missing the `isdisjoint`
method; EdgeView (br-r37-c1-fbtk0) was fixed last cycle.

DegreeView audited too — both fnx and nx fail on Set ops there
(DegreeView is NOT Set-like in nx). Parity holds.
close_reason: Verified g.nodes.isdisjoint({99}) returns True without AttributeError on Graph. Earlier fix landed.

Repro: DiGraph with edges 0->1, 0->2, 1->3, 2->3 all weight=1; list(fnx.all_shortest_paths(G, 0, 3, weight='weight')) raises, but nx returns [[0, 1, 3], [0, 2, 3]]. title: [code-review] no metamorphic guards on directed-graph distance metrics
description:
Audit: tests/python/test_review_mode_metamorphic.py covers undirected algorithms (complement involution, cycle_basis circuit rank, etc.) but has zero metamorphic guards on the DIRECTED distance-metric surface that was just patched in br-r37-c1-89n9d (center/periphery) and br-r37-c1-wojl3 (diameter/radius).

A future regression that re-introduces the directed-collapse defect at the wrapper level (e.g., a refactor that re-routes via the buggy raw _fnx) would only be caught by the recently-added differential fuzz test_fuzz_directed_diameter_radius_center_periphery_oracle_match_nx (br-r37-c1-kitjs). That fuzz test compares against nx as oracle — but if BOTH libraries drift the same way (highly unlikely, but possible if nx is pinned to a vulnerable version), the fuzz silently passes.

Metamorphic relations are a complementary guard that catches independent-of-nx drift. Concrete relations to add:

  1. diameter(reverse(G)) == diameter(G) for strongly-connected DiGraphs.
  2. radius(G) <= diameter(G) (fundamental graph-distance inequality).
  3. center(G) == {n : ecc[n] == radius(G)} (definitional, but verifies cross-algo coherence).
  4. periphery(G) == {n : ecc[n] == diameter(G)} (same).

All four hold by mathematical definition independent of any nx implementation; a wrapper that returns garbage for any one of them violates the relation.

Tagged P1 because the directed-distance-metric fix surface is fresh (last 60 min) and lacking metamorphic-test coverage means future regressions could land silently if both libs drift.
close_reason: Shipped 88a10381 successor commit. Adds 4 metamorphic-property tests (20 cases total) for the directed distance-metric surface: diameter(reverse(G)) == diameter(G), radius <= diameter, center == ecc-minimizers, periphery == ecc-maximizers. Each holds by mathematical identity independent of any nx behavior, so they catch both-libs-drift cases that pure nx-oracle differential testing misses. 86 metamorphic tests pass total.

title: G.add_edges_from raises ValueError on bad-arity tuples; nx raises NetworkXError
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — exception type divergence on a documented public API. Same defect class as br-r37-c1-{0xhhq, p7p7l} (exception-type parity).

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, networkx as nx

G_f = fnx.Graph()
G_n = nx.Graph()

G_f.add_edges_from([()])
# fnx: ValueError("edge tuple must have 2 or 3 elements")
G_n.add_edges_from([()])
# nx:  NetworkXError("Edge tuple () must be a 2-tuple or 3-tuple.")
```

Affects Graph and DiGraph for 1-tuple, empty-tuple, 4-tuple,
5-tuple, etc. inputs. MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph already raised
NetworkXError correctly through a different code path (they accept
4-tuples for the key dimension).

## Root cause
The Rust `_GRAPH_RAW_ADD_EDGES_FROM` raises `PyValueError` on
bad-arity tuples (lib.rs:2422). Code catching
`nx.NetworkXError` to detect malformed edge inputs (a documented
nx contract) missed fnx's ValueError, silently propagating the
wrong exception type.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — exception type is part of the public-API contract;
defensive code (try/except NetworkXError) misses the error
class entirely.

## Fix
Pre-validate tuple arity at the Python wrapper layer before
delegating to the Rust raw call. Raise NetworkXError with nx's
exact message format: `"Edge tuple {edge} must be a 2-tuple or
3-tuple."`.

The fix is added inside `_add_edges_from_materialized` (Graph and
DiGraph) — Multi* already has correct NetworkXError validation
through a separate path.

## Tests
3 new locks in `test_review_mode_regression_lock.py::
test_exception_type_parity` covering 1-tuple (Graph), empty-tuple
(DiGraph), 5-tuple (Graph). 803 existing tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — sweep
of edge-input-validation paths after the prior `union` fix
(br-r37-c1-qh17m) on a different operator. `add_edges_from` had

title: [parity-gap] barycenter on directed cycle5+chord returns [0,2], nx returns [0]
description:
Audit: extending the directed-collapse-defect family from br-r37-c1-89n9d / br-r37-c1-wojl3 to the next eccentricity-related algorithm. Found via differential probe.

Repro:
  >>> import networkx as nx, franken_networkx as fnx
  >>> edges = [(i,(i+1)%5) for i in range(5)] + [(0, 2)]
  >>> G_n = nx.DiGraph(edges); G_f = fnx.DiGraph(edges)
  >>> nx.barycenter(G_n)
  [0]
  >>> fnx.barycenter(G_f)
  [0, 2]

Manual verification on this 5-node strongly-connected DiGraph: barycentricity[v] = sum of distances FROM v to every other node:
  bc[0] = 0+1+1+2+3 = 7
  bc[1] = 4+0+1+2+3 = 10
  bc[2] = 3+4+0+1+2 = 10
  bc[3] = 2+3+4+0+1 = 10
  bc[4] = 1+2+2+3+0 = 8
Minimum is 7 at node 0 → barycenter = [0]. fnx incorrectly includes node 2 (which has bc=10).

The fnx wrapper (after br-r37-c1-pooue) calls _raw_barycenter directly for the strongly-connected directed case. The Rust binding has the same gr.undirected() collapse pattern — it computes barycentricity on the undirected projection where node 2 sits symmetrically with node 0, giving them equal undirected barycentricity.

Fix: route directed inputs through the existing Python branch at __init__.py:9629 (which uses fnx.shortest_path_length and sums distances natively, working correctly for both directed and undirected). The Rust fast path stays for undirected graphs.

P1: same risk class as the diameter/radius/center/periphery fixes — directed-graph callers see wrong answers on standard inputs.
close_reason: Shipped. fnx.barycenter on directed graphs now computes barycentricity natively via fnx.shortest_path_length (directed-aware) instead of routing through _raw_barycenter (gr.undirected() collapse defect). Verified bit-exact against nx on directed cycle5+chord (was [0,2], now [0]), cycle5, K4, cycle3. 112 barycenter tests pass; golden snapshot regenerated with corrected dicycle5+chord output.

title: write_adjlist Rust fast path omits header + trailing newline — byte divergence from nx
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — public-API output divergence; tooling that snapshot-diffs across libraries sees spurious differences.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, networkx as nx, io

G = fnx.path_graph(5)
buf = io.BytesIO()
fnx.write_adjlist(G, buf)
print(buf.getvalue())
# fnx: b'0 1\n1 2\n2 3\n3 4\n4'           ← no header, no trailing newline
# nx : b'#\n# GMT ...\n# \n0 1\n1 2\n2 3\n3 4\n4\n'  ← timestamped header + newline
```

## Root cause
`fnx.write_adjlist` defaulted to `_rust_write_adjlist` (via
`crates/fnx-readwrite/src/lib.rs::write_adjlist` → `lines.join("\n")`)
which:
1. Omits nx's timestamped comment header (`#\n# GMT <date>\n# \n`)
2. Omits the trailing newline (uses `join("\n")` not
   `join("\n") + "\n"`)

Both differences are observable byte-level; affects any pipeline
that diffs adjlist output across libraries OR any line-oriented
reader that requires newline-terminated files.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — `write_adjlist` is documented public API; byte-level
parity matters for snapshot-based testing and cross-library
comparison. The behaviour was already locked by a test
(`test_write_adjlist_default_uses_rust_fast_path`) that asserted
the Rust path IS used — but the lock pinned the wrong contract.

## Fix
Remove the Rust fast-path gate from the public `write_adjlist`
wrapper. Always delegate to `_write_adjlist_via_nx` for byte-exact
output. The Rust writer remains available via
`_rust_write_adjlist` for callers that explicitly want the
no-header variant; the public API now matches nx exactly.

Updated `test_write_adjlist_default_uses_rust_fast_path` —
renamed to `test_write_adjlist_default_delegates_for_byte_parity`
and inverted the assertion to lock the new (correct) contract:
the delegate IS invoked on the default path.

## Tests
- 1 new lock in `test_review_mode_regression_lock.py::
  test_write_adjlist_byte_parity_with_nx` covering header presence
  + trailing newline + comment-stripped byte equality.
- Existing `test_write_adjlist_default_*` updated to lock the new
  contract.

844 existing tests pass. Round-trip via read_adjlist still works.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — sweep
of IO write parity across edgelist, adjlist, multiline_adjlist,
pajek, gml, graphml. `write_adjlist` was the one with concrete
byte divergence.

title: Parity: negative_edge_cycle rejects weight=int / weight=None (Rust binding)
[code-review] common_neighbors / non_neighbors lack metamorphic guards on math identities
description:
br-r37-c1-qkq2h shipped wrapper-bypass for fnx.common_neighbors and fnx.non_neighbors. Functional + fuzz tests cover nx differential parity (br-r37-c1-oy0zr); no metamorphic guards on the underlying mathematical identities.

Both functions have unambiguous identities that hold for ANY valid implementation:

  common_neighbors:
    1. symmetric: cn(u, v) == cn(v, u). Set intersection is symmetric.
    2. endpoint-exclusion: u ∉ cn AND v ∉ cn (definitional).
    3. subset: cn(u, v) ⊆ N(u) AND cn(u, v) ⊆ N(v).

  non_neighbors:
    4. complement-partition: non(v) ∪ N(v) ∪ {v} == V(G), pairwise disjoint.

These are nx-INDEPENDENT — even if both libraries drift, the math identities catch the regression. Differential fuzz wouldn't help in the both-libs-drift case.

Concrete fix plan:
  Add 4 metamorphic-property tests parametrized over random ER seeds.
  18 cases total (5+5+3+5 across the 4 properties).

title: eigenvector_centrality raises OverflowError on negative max_iter — nx raises PowerIterationFailedConvergence
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — exception type divergence on a documented public-API edge case. Same defect family as br-r37-c1-{w1smc, udsdu, nxj7k}: Rust unsigned-int constraint surfacing as the wrong exception class.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, networkx as nx
G = fnx.path_graph(5)

fnx.eigenvector_centrality(G, max_iter=-1)
# OverflowError: can't convert negative int to unsigned
nx.eigenvector_centrality(G, max_iter=-1)
# PowerIterationFailedConvergence: power iteration failed to
# converge within -1 iterations
```

## Root cause
The Rust `_raw_eigenvector_centrality` declares `max_iter` as
unsigned int. Negative values raise OverflowError. nx's pure-Python
power-iteration loop uses a `while iter_count < max_iter` exit
condition — on `max_iter <= 0` the loop never enters, raising
`PowerIterationFailedConvergence(max_iter)` to signal that no
iteration ran.

Code that catches `PowerIterationFailedConvergence` to detect
non-convergence (a documented nx contract) silently broke on fnx
— got the wrong exception class.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — same defect family as the prior unsigned-int fixes.
Domain-specific exception class is the correct contract for
"didn't converge" detection.

## Fix
Pre-validate `max_iter` at the Python wrapper layer: if it's an int
≤ 0, raise `PowerIterationFailedConvergence(max(max_iter, 0))`
directly without calling the Rust binding. Matches nx's domain-
specific failure mode exactly. Positive max_iter unchanged.

## Tests
1 new lock in `test_review_mode_regression_lock.py::
test_eigenvector_centrality_negative_max_iter_raises_convergence_failure`
covering negative, zero, and small-positive max_iter inputs.

617 existing parity / pickle / conversion / IO / view tests pass
unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — sweep
of negative-int kwarg defects beyond the depth/cutoff family
(br-r37-c1-{w1smc, udsdu, nxj7k}). `eigenvector_centrality.max_iter`
was the standout — other power-iteration centralities (katz,
pagerank, hits) handle negative max_iter correctly already.
close_reason: Verified fnx.eigenvector_centrality(G, max_iter=-1) now raises PowerIterationFailedConvergence matching nx — earlier OverflowError fix landed before bead triage.

title: parity: second_order_centrality dict iterates in wrong node order
description: fnx.second_order_centrality returns a dict in arbitrary internal order (e.g. for path_graph(5): [2, 4, 0, 1, 3]) instead of nx's node-insertion order [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]. Same iteration-order drift as br-r37-c1-pm78h (communicability_betweenness_centrality). Drop-in code that iterates 'for n, score in centrality.items(): ...' breaks. Values are unchanged. Fix: reorder result dict in iteration order of G.nodes().

title: MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph.nodes() returns frozen list, not live NodeView
description:
fnx.MultiGraph.nodes() and fnx.MultiDiGraph.nodes() return a frozen list snapshot at call time. nx returns a live NodeView. Inconsistent with fnx.Graph.nodes() and fnx.DiGraph.nodes() which DO return live views.

Repro:
  >>> g = fnx.MultiGraph([(1,2)])
  >>> v = g.nodes()
  >>> g.add_node(99)
  >>> 99 in list(v)
  False                  # nx returns True

Root cause: the Rust-side MultiGraphNodeView.__call__ and MultiDiGraphNodeView.__call__ return list when called with default args (data=False). For Graph and DiGraph the Rust call returns self (a live NodeView) — only the multi-variants are wrong.

The Python wrapper _node_view_call_with_attr_support calls node_view_call(self, False, default) for data is False and trusts the Rust impl. Override that branch for Multi* classes to return self instead, matching the simple-graph branch.

Same class as br-r37-c1-msf5j (DiGraph/Multi*.edges() live view) — closes the parallel defect for nodes().

title: link-prediction soundarajan_hopcroft / within_inter_cluster raise wrong type on multigraph
description:
Three link-prediction functions raise NetworkXAlgorithmError('No community information available for Node 1') on multigraph input, masking the real issue. nx is decorated with @not_implemented_for('multigraph') and raises NetworkXNotImplemented FIRST, before any community-attribute check.

Repro:
  >>> g = fnx.MultiGraph([(1,2),(2,3)])
  >>> list(fnx.cn_soundarajan_hopcroft(g))
  NetworkXAlgorithmError: No community information available for Node 1
  >>> list(nx.cn_soundarajan_hopcroft(nx.MultiGraph([(1,2),(2,3)])))
  NetworkXNotImplemented: not implemented for multigraph type

Affects cn_soundarajan_hopcroft, ra_index_soundarajan_hopcroft, within_inter_cluster — all share the same code path that checks community attrs before the type guard. Drop-in code that does pytest.raises(NetworkXNotImplemented) won't trigger.

This is the link-prediction subset scoped out of br-r37-c1-tqimg. Fix: add multigraph guard at the top of each function, before any community-attribute lookup. Also add @not_implemented_for('directed') guards since nx decorates these functions with both.

title: parity: ego_graph node ordering uses set iteration (random) instead of BFS-from-source order
description: fnx.ego_graph node order is the iteration order of a set (arbitrary hash order). nx.ego_graph nodes are in BFS-from-source visit order (source first, then by distance from source). For node 'c' on graph with edges (c,d),(a,b),(b,c),(d,e), radius=2: fnx returns ['d','e','a','c','b'] but nx returns ['c','d','a','b','e']. Drop-in code that relies on iteration order breaks. Fix: iterate the BFS 'seen' dict (which records insertion order) instead of converting to set.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 76c3369. ego_graph now iterates nodes in G's insertion order (filtered to ego set) matching nx's G.subgraph contract. 10 parity tests freeze the contract.

title: [code-review] core_number self-loop guard iterates all edges, 24% of total time
description:
Profiling fnx.core_number on BA200 (30 calls, 33ms total):

  ncalls   cumtime  filename:lineno
  30       0.033 s  __init__.py:13518(core_number)
  6030     0.008 s  __init__.py:36666(__iter__)            <- edges() iteration
  17760    0.002 s  __init__.py:13543(<genexpr>)           <- 'any(u == v for u, v in G.edges())'

The self-loop guard any(u == v for u, v in G.edges()) walks EVERY edge — O(|E|) just to check existence — even though G has 985 edges and only |V|=200 nodes need a has_edge(u,u) probe. ~24% of total time.

Result: fnx.core_number is 2.07-2.35x SLOWER than nx (BA100: 0.36 vs 0.17 ms; BA200: 0.93 vs 0.40 ms).

Bench self-loop detection methods (BA200, 1000 calls):
  any(u==v for u,v in edges):     297 µs  (current)
  number_of_selfloops > 0:        645 µs
  any(has_edge(u,u) for u in G):  117 µs  (2.5x faster, short-circuits)

Fix: replace the guard with any(G.has_edge(u, u) for u in G). O(|V|) instead of O(|E|), short-circuits on first self-loop hit. Same correctness contract.

Same wasteful pattern likely exists in other algorithms with self-loop guards — find_cliques, k_core (delegates to core_number), k_shell, k_crust, k_corona all share this entry path via core_number.

P1: core_number is in the hot path of the kcore family; closing this also speeds up k_core, k_shell, k_crust.
close_reason: Shipped. core_number self-loop guard now uses O(|V|) any(G.has_edge(u,u) for u in G) — 2.5x faster than the O(|E|) edge-walk variant, short-circuits on first hit. Closes ~30% of the prior 2.07-2.35x slowdown vs nx; remaining gap is in the Rust binding + per-node re-keying. 169 core_number/k_core tests pass.

title: Edge views miss Set comparison/algebra operators (<=, <, >=, >, isdisjoint, &|-^)
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — public-API parity break on the documented subset/superset idiom across multiple edge-view types.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx
DG = fnx.DiGraph([(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0)])
DH = fnx.DiGraph([(0, 1)])
DH.in_edges <= DG.in_edges
# TypeError: '<=' not supported between instances of '_DiEdgeMethodView'

MG = fnx.MultiGraph([(0, 1), (0, 1), (1, 2)])
MH = fnx.MultiGraph([(0, 1)])
MH.edges & MG.edges  # TypeError on fnx, returns set on nx
MH.edges.isdisjoint(MG.edges)  # AttributeError on fnx
```

## Root cause
nx's edge view classes inherit from `collections.abc.Set`, so all
9 set operations (`<=`, `<`, `>=`, `>`, `isdisjoint`, `&`, `|`,
`-`, `^`) work. fnx's Python wrappers had partial coverage:
- `_DiGraphEdgeView`: had `|`, `&`, `-`, `^`. Missing `<=`, `<`, `>=`,
  `>`, `isdisjoint`.
- `_MultiGraphEdgeView` and `_MultiDiGraphEdgeView`: had nothing.
- `_DiEdgeMethodView` (in_edges/out_edges, both DiGraph and
  MultiDiGraph): had nothing — the fix from br-r37-c1-7gej0 only
  exposed the iter/call/pickle/len contract, not the Set
  comparison/algebra surface.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — `H.edges <= G.edges` is the documented nx idiom for
subset checking. `G1.edges & G2.edges` is the documented intersection.
Same defect class as the prior view-equality cycles
(br-r37-c1-{oww5k, k1xn4, 7krwv, 86151}) but on the comparison /
algebra surface rather than equality.

## Fix
Add the 9 missing operators to four edge-view wrapper classes:
- `_DiGraphEdgeView`: add `__le__`, `__lt__`, `__ge__`, `__gt__`,
  `isdisjoint` (already had | & - ^).
- `_MultiGraphEdgeView`, `_MultiDiGraphEdgeView`: add all 9.
- `_DiEdgeMethodView`: add all 9.

Each operator delegates via `set(self) OP set(other)` (or
`isdisjoint`-equivalent) — matches nx's Set inheritance behavior
exactly.

## Tests
45 new parametrized locks (5 view types × 9 set operations) in
`test_view_pickle_parity.py::test_edge_view_set_operations_match_nx`.
Each lock asserts the operator returns the same value as nx's
matching view.

719 existing parity / pickle / conversion / attr / regression-lock
tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — completing
the view-protocol audit. Equality contracts were closed in
br-r37-c1-{oww5k, k1xn4, 7krwv, 86151}; this commit closes the
companion comparison/algebra contracts on the EdgeView family.
close_reason: Verified Edge view Set protocol: &, |, <=, isdisjoint all work on g.edges. Earlier fix landed.

title: [reality-check] add nx.coloring.greedy_color
description:
fnx 7.49ms vs nx 0.25ms (30x slower) on BA200. Greedy graph coloring with strategy='largest_first'. nx is just a Python loop over sorted-by-degree nodes; fnx is hitting an O(V^2) wrapper or repeated dict lookups. Port nx.algorithms.coloring.greedy_color (all strategies).

Audited 2026-05-03 (artifact: artifacts/reality-check-2026-05-03.md). Bench fixture: barabasi_albert_graph(200, 5, seed=42).
Reference: see V_SLOW table in artifacts/reality-check-2026-05-03.md.

title: [code-review] link-prediction family missing from golden snapshot — and tuple-orientation drift makes naive snapshot non-deterministic
description:
br-r37-c1-8e60l shipped a 1000x perf fix for the link-prediction family (jaccard, adamic_adar, preferential_attachment, resource_allocation_index). Coverage so far: nx differential parity (functional) + metamorphic relations (br-r37-c1-b1i24). No golden snapshot.

A naive [(u, v, score) for ...] snapshot of jaccard_coefficient on string-keyed graphs (Florentine fixture) is NON-DETERMINISTIC across PYTHONHASHSEED-randomized runs. Verified empirically:

  proc1: [("Acciaiuoli", "Castellani", "0.0"), ...]
  proc2: [("Acciaiuoli", "Bischeri", "0.0"), ...]

nx.non_edges emits each unordered pair once but the orientation (u, v) vs (v, u) depends on the underlying set iteration order, which is hash-randomized for non-int nodes. Both orientations are correct (score is symmetric) but a per-tuple snapshot drifts.

Concrete fix plan (this tick):
  1. Add jaccard_coefficient and preferential_attachment to the per-graph payload.
  2. Canonicalize each pair to (min(u,v), max(u,v)) by string, dedupe, then sort by (score, u, v). Eliminates orientation drift.
  3. Regenerate via UPDATE_GOLDENS=1; verify across 4 runs.

P1 because the lazy-delegate fix is recent and a future regression in the fnx_to_nx conversion path (e.g., a precision drift) would only show in functional tests as a bit-noise difference. The aggregated golden catches it as a visible diff.
close_reason: Shipped. Golden snapshot extended with jaccard_coefficient and preferential_attachment via orientation-stable canonicalization (min(u,v), max(u,v) + dedupe). Verified determinism across 4 consecutive runs (was failing on the naive snapshot due to PYTHONHASHSEED-randomized non_edges orientation). 13359 lines now (was 7051).

title: follow-up: 3 more paths accept unhashable nodes (add_weighted_edges_from, remove_node, ctor)
description:
Follow-up to br-r37-c1-m0io3. Three remaining paths still accept unhashable types (or raise the wrong exception):

(1) add_weighted_edges_from with list endpoint:
  >>> g = fnx.Graph()
  >>> g.add_weighted_edges_from([([1,2], 3, 1.0)])
  # silently accepted
  >>> nx.Graph().add_weighted_edges_from([([1,2], 3, 1.0)])
  TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'

(2) remove_node on unhashable node:
  >>> g = fnx.Graph([(1,2)])
  >>> g.remove_node([1,2])
  NetworkXError: The node [1, 2] is not in the graph.
  >>> nx.Graph([(1,2)]).remove_node([1,2])
  TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'

  >>> nx.Graph([([1,2], 3)])
  NetworkXError: Input is not a valid edge list

Drop-in code that catches TypeError on these paths won't trigger on fnx.

  add_edges_from fix from br-r37-c1-m0io3).
- remove_node: hash-validate before the membership check.

  Rust __new__ override OR in the Python __init__ wrapper that

title: find_cliques iteration order and clique node order drift from nx
description:
fnx.find_cliques iterates cliques in a different order from nx and within each clique returns nodes in canonical/sorted order rather than nx's pivot-based discovery order.

Repro:
  edges = [('c','d'),('a','b'),('b','c'),('d','e'),('a','c')]
  fnx -> [['a','b','c'], ['c','d'], ['d','e']]

  fnx -> [[0,1,2], [2,3,4]]
  nx  -> [[2,0,1], [2,3,4]]

Drop-in code iterating cliques in nx's order (or treating the first node of each clique as the pivot) breaks.

Fix: delegate find_cliques to nx for parity (mirrors articulation_points/bridges/cycle_basis fix pattern).

title: [code-review] is_planar 2-9x slower than nx because wrapper always builds nx graph + computes full LR embedding
description:
Profiling fnx.is_planar on BA fixtures vs nx:

  BA50 m=3:  nx=0.10ms  fnx=0.30ms   ratio=3.0x  🐢
  BA100 m=3: nx=1.23ms  fnx=2.60ms   ratio=2.11x 🐢
  BA200 m=5: nx=0.88ms  fnx=7.75ms   ratio=8.82x 🐢🐢

The wrapper at python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:9557 currently delegates EVERY call to check_planarity(G) which:
  1. Calls _planarity_graph_for_certificate(G) to build a fresh nx.Graph copy of every node/edge/attr — O(|V|+|E|) work that is wasted when the graph is trivially planar or non-planar.
  2. Runs nx's full Hopcroft-Tarjan LR planarity test which ALSO constructs the planar embedding — discarded by is_planar (which only needs the bool).

Easy perf wins via cheap necessary conditions checked BEFORE the conversion+delegation:

  - |V| ≤ 4: always planar (true, no exceptions).
  - Pure Euler bound: |E| > 3|V| - 6 ⇒ non-planar (true).
  - Bipartite + Euler-tightened: |E| > 2|V| - 4 ⇒ non-planar (Kuratowski for bipartite).

These three conditions short-circuit common graphs (small, dense, complete bipartite) without the nx round-trip. For graphs that pass all three, fall back to check_planarity — same correctness contract, but much smaller hot-path overhead on inputs the bound catches.

The bipartite test costs O(|V|+|E|) (a 2-coloring BFS) — same order as the conversion it avoids — so it's amortized free.

Fix plan (this tick):
  1. Add cheap necessary-condition checks at the top of fnx.is_planar.
  2. Only fall through to check_planarity when the bounds don't decide.
  3. Verify K3,3, Petersen, K5 still return False; K4, P5, etc. still return True.
  4. Bench BA50/100/200 to confirm closure.

P1 because is_planar is a basic predicate users call frequently and 8x slowdown on BA200 is a quality-bar miss. Same Kuratowski bounds were already proven correct for the Rust function in br-r37-c1-xdjpt; this lifts them to the Python wrapper layer.
close_reason: Shipped. is_planar wrapper now short-circuits on cheap necessary conditions (n<=4, Euler bound, bipartite-tightened bound) before the expensive nx-graph + LR embedding. Dense graphs (BA200/500 m=5) now instant (0.001ms vs nx's 1-2ms — ~1000x speedup). Sparse graphs unchanged at 2x slowdown (unavoidable LR test). 410 planar tests pass; correctness bit-exact vs nx on K3,3/Petersen/K5/K6/K4/P5/K3,3+chord.

title: [code-review] dominating_set native port has no fuzz coverage of the dominating-property contract
description:
br-r37-c1-lj6bo (native port) and br-r37-c1-02djy (wrapper-bypass perf) both shipped fixes to dominating_set(start_with=...) but coverage is hand-picked fixtures only (K4, P5, BA20, K3,3, DiGraph cycle3 in test_review_mode_regression_lock).

Greedy dominating-set choices aren't unique — different node-iteration orders yield different valid dominating sets — so we can't fuzz with nx as oracle (output is non-deterministic across implementations). But the FUNDAMENTAL contract is bit-exact verifiable on every input:

  Contract 1: result is a set
  Contract 2: start_with ∈ ds
  Contract 3: ∀v ∈ V, v ∈ ds OR ∃ u ∈ ds: (u, v) ∈ E

A fuzz test against random ER graphs (skipping self-loop fixtures since they trivially dominate themselves) verifies the contract directly without an external oracle. Catches regressions like:
  - 'all_nodes - dominated - dominating' typo where remaining set is wrong
  - off-by-one in the while-loop guard
  - wrapper-bypass branch returning a stale set from a different graph

P1 because the dominating-set port is fresh (last 30 min) and lacks oracle-free fuzz coverage that catches contract violations independent of nx's drift.
close_reason: Shipped. test_fuzz_dominating_set_with_start_oracle_dominates_every_node parametrized over 25 random ER graphs verifies the 3 fundamental dominating-set contracts (set type, start_with in result, every node dominated) without an nx oracle. 25/25 pass. Catches contract violations independent of nx — complements the hand-picked fixtures.

title: [code-review] regression-lock test fails because venv _fnx.abi3.so is stale relative to a7c84f89 source

title: Refactor draw_networkx_* re-exports to be classified as PY_WRAPPER (last 4 NX_DELEGATED)
description:

title: write_gexf Rust fast path diverges from nx in XML declaration quoting/encoding case
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — public-API output divergence in XML declaration. Same defect family as br-r37-c1-{eeawk, nlkkm, nhgtp} on the IO writers (write_adjlist / write_graphml / write_multiline_adjlist).

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, networkx as nx, io

G = fnx.path_graph(3)
buf = io.BytesIO()
fnx.write_gexf(G, buf)
buf.getvalue()[:50]
# fnx: b'<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>...'
# nx : b"<?xml version='1.0' encoding='utf-8'?>..."
```

## Root cause
`fnx.write_gexf` defaulted to `_fnx.write_gexf` (Rust path) on the
simple-graph path. The Rust XML writer produced double-quoted
attributes with uppercase encoding name; nx's lxml-based writer
produces single-quoted attributes with lowercase encoding name.

Tooling that snapshot-diffs GEXF output across libraries OR
strict XML canonicalization (xmllint --c14n) saw spurious
differences.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — `write_gexf` is documented public API; byte-level
parity matters for snapshot-based testing and cross-library
validation. Same severity as the prior IO byte-parity fixes.

## Fix
Remove the Rust fast-path gate from public `write_gexf`. Always
delegate to `nx.write_gexf` for byte-exact output. The simple-graph
case routes through a new `_simple_to_nx` helper (parallel to
`_multigraph_to_nx`) that converts the fnx graph to nx's matching
class.

The pre-existing multigraph delegation path is unchanged.

## Tests
1 new lock in `test_review_mode_regression_lock.py::
test_write_gexf_byte_parity_with_nx` covering byte-exact match
(timestamps stripped — nx's `<meta lastmodifieddate=...>`
includes the current date) + XML decl format check.

490 IO/view/regression tests pass unchanged. Round-trip via
read_gexf still works.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — closing
the deferred followup from br-r37-c1-nlkkm. The IO byte-parity
audit is now complete: write_adjlist (eeawk), write_graphml
(nlkkm), write_multiline_adjlist (nhgtp), write_gexf (this commit).
close_reason: Verified write_gexf produces byte-equal output to nx including correct XML declaration encoding case for Graph (640b), MultiGraph, and DiGraph — earlier Rust fast-path fix landed.

title: [code-review] volume fast-path has no nx-independent regression-lock for the degree-sum identity
description:
br-r37-c1-ay2no shipped a fast path: volume(G, S) == sum(deg(v) for v in S) for undirected unweighted non-multigraph case. Functional tests verify nx parity (16 volume tests pass). But there's no regression-lock test pinning the IDENTITY independently of nx — a future regression where both libs drift the same way (e.g. degree counting changes) wouldn't be caught.

Concrete known-result fixtures to lock:

  K_n: every node has degree (n-1), so volume(K_n, S of size k) = k*(n-1)
    K5, |S|=3: 3*4 = 12
    K6, |S|=4: 4*5 = 20

  P_n (linear path): endpoints degree 1, middle nodes degree 2
    P5, S=[0, 4]: 1+1 = 2
    P5, S=[1, 2, 3]: 2+2+2 = 6

  Self-loop semantic: degree counts self-loop twice
    Graph[(0,0),(0,1),(1,2)], S=[0]: deg(0) = 2 (self-loop) + 1 (edge) = 3

  Sum-of-degrees identity: sum over all nodes = 2|E|
    BA(20, m=3, seed=7), S=all: 2 * |E|

These are mathematically derived expected values, not nx output. Catches a future regression that reroutes through slow _adc_weighted_degree path OR breaks the self-loop *2 semantic.

P1 because the volume fast path is recent (last 30 min) and the degree-sum identity is a foundational lemma — testing it independently of nx prevents both-lib drift from going undetected.
close_reason: Shipped. test_volume_fast_path_known_results parametrized over 6 hand-derived fixtures (K5/K6 complete, P5 endpoints/middle, self-loop, BA all-nodes-2m). All expected values computed from graph structure, not nx output — locks the volume fast-path correctness independent of nx drift. 6/6 pass.

Same root cause as approximation namespace fix (functools.wraps). draw also has the variadic-kwarg-name drift (kwargs vs nx's kwds). Fix: apply functools.wraps(nx_func) to each wrapper. Add parity test that asserts inspect.signature(fnx.X) matches inspect.signature(nx.X) for the full drawing namespace.

title: is_chordal/complete_to_chordal_graph silently accept K4+self-loop where nx raises
description:
fnx.is_chordal and fnx.complete_to_chordal_graph silently succeed on graphs where nx's internal _is_complete_graph helper raises NetworkXError('Self loop found in _is_complete_graph()').

Repro:
  >>> g = fnx.Graph([(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(1,2),(1,3),(2,3),(0,0)])  # K4 + self-loop
  >>> fnx.is_chordal(g)                       # True
  >>> nx.is_chordal(nx.Graph(g))
  NetworkXError: Self loop found in _is_complete_graph()

  >>> fnx.complete_to_chordal_graph(g)
  (Graph(nodes=4, edges=7), {0: 0, 1: 0, 2: 0, 3: 0})
  >>> nx.complete_to_chordal_graph(nx.Graph(g))
  NetworkXError: Self loop found in _is_complete_graph()

The drift is selective — nx's _is_complete_graph helper is only called when the algorithm reaches a candidate complete subgraph that happens to contain a self-loop. For triangle + self-loop or chain + self-loop, neither algorithm reaches that branch and both nx and fnx return True / a valid result.

Drop-in code that does pytest.raises(NetworkXError) on the K4+self-loop case won't trigger on fnx. fnx's behavior is more permissive but breaks exact-error parity with nx.

Fix: when the input has any self-loop, delegate is_chordal and complete_to_chordal_graph to nx so the exact raise pattern is preserved.

title: 5+ node-lookup paths raise wrong exception on unhashable input
description:
Follow-up to br-r37-c1-m0io3 / -g438p. Several node-lookup paths still raise the wrong exception class on unhashable inputs — drop-in code that does pytest.raises(TypeError) won't trigger:

  g.neighbors([1,2])    fnx: NetworkXError    nx: TypeError(unhashable)
  g.adj[[1,2]]          fnx: KeyError         nx: TypeError(unhashable)
  g.nodes[[1,2]]        fnx: KeyError         nx: TypeError(unhashable)
  g[[1,2]]              fnx: KeyError         nx: TypeError(unhashable)
  g.remove_edge([1,2], 2)  fnx: NetworkXError    nx: TypeError(unhashable)
  g.remove_nodes_from([[1,2]])  fnx: silently skips  nx: TypeError(unhashable)
  descendants(g, [1,2])  fnx: NetworkXError    nx: TypeError(unhashable)
  ancestors(g, [1,2])    fnx: NetworkXError    nx: TypeError(unhashable)

For the dict-getitem cases (adj/nodes/g[n]), nx's underlying dict access raises TypeError because Python's dict tries hash() first. fnx's wrappers catch KeyError-like cases and translate to KeyError, masking the real type issue.

For neighbors/remove_edge/descendants, fnx falls through to a 'node not in graph' check which silently returns False on unhashable, then raises NetworkXError instead of TypeError.

Skip is_isolate (nx itself has a leaky abstraction — accepts unhashable list as nbunch and returns False; matching this is undesirable).

Fix: call hash(node) at the entry of each affected wrapper before any membership check or dict access.

  barbell_graph(3, 4) adj[3]: fnx=[2,4], nx=[4,2]

title: [code-review] average_degree_connectivity is 680x slower than nx — O(|V|²) AtlasView walks
description:
Probed BA100: average_degree_connectivity is 680x SLOWER than nx (179ms vs 269µs).

Source: python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:8098 ::average_degree_connectivity calls _adc_weighted_degree(G, node, ...) for each source node AND each of its neighbors. Each _adc_weighted_degree call walks G[node].items() — AtlasView with per-element PyO3 fetch. For BA100 |E|=297, that's roughly 100 source iterations × ~6 neighbors × _adc_weighted_degree call (each O(degree) AtlasView walks) = O(|V| · avg_deg²) AtlasView accesses.

For the simple undirected unweighted case (source=target='in+out', weight=None, nodes=None, undirected G), _adc_weighted_degree(G, n) is just G.degree(n). The whole inner loop reduces to 'sum(deg[v] for v in G.neighbors(node))'.

Concrete fix plan: at the top of average_degree_connectivity, detect the simple case and:
  1. Materialize deg = dict(G.degree()) once.
  2. For each node, build the sum via deg dict lookup instead of _adc_weighted_degree per neighbor.
  3. Use raw neighbors dispatch to avoid per-node AtlasView in the inner loop.

Estimated speedup: 50-100x based on the volume fast-path precedent (br-r37-c1-{ay2no, u34tv}) which closed similar O(|V|²) AtlasView walks via materialized degree dict.

P1 because 680x slowdown is the most extreme remaining gap I've found in the recent perf scans, and the fix pattern is well-established (precomputed degree dict + raw neighbors).
close_reason: Shipped. average_degree_connectivity simple-case fast path: dict(G.degree()) materialized once + raw_neighbors_dispatch in inner loop. Closes from 680x SLOWER to 2.5x. ~250-700x speedup. Parity bit-exact; directed/weighted/multigraph fall through to slow path. 3 tests pass.

[code-review] wrapper-bypass pattern duplicated across 4+ sites — extract to a helper
description:
The wrapper-bypass pattern shipped in br-r37-c1-{lgyq8 (find_cliques), 7t95c (square_clustering), 02djy (dominating_set), qkq2h (common_neighbors/non_neighbors)} has the same boilerplate at every site:

  if (
      not _has_networkx_private_storage(G)
      and not G.is_multigraph()
  ):
      if isinstance(G, DiGraph):
          _raw_nbrs = _DIGRAPH_NEIGHBORS
      else:
          _raw_nbrs = _GRAPH_NEIGHBORS
      # fast path using _raw_nbrs(G, u)

A future regression that introduces (e.g.) a MultiDiGraph subclass check, OR a new private-storage flag, would need to be threaded through 4-5 callsites — easy to miss one. DRY refactor: extract a helper _raw_neighbors_dispatch(G) that returns either the raw neighbors function (Graph.neighbors / DiGraph.neighbors UNWRAPPED) or None when the bypass isn't safe.

Concrete fix plan:
  1. Add _raw_neighbors_dispatch(G) -> callable | None that returns:
     - _GRAPH_NEIGHBORS if isinstance(G, Graph) and not multigraph and not private-storage
     - _DIGRAPH_NEIGHBORS if isinstance(G, DiGraph) and not multigraph and not private-storage
     - None otherwise (caller falls back to slow path)

  2. Update find_cliques, square_clustering, dominating_set, common_neighbors, non_neighbors to use the helper. Saves ~10 lines per site, centralizes the safety-check logic.

  3. Verify identical perf (the helper just returns a function reference; no per-call overhead).

P1 because the bypass pattern is the most-used perf primitive in the codebase (5 sites and counting); centralizing prevents a future maintainer from breaking 4 of 5 callsites by updating a private-storage check at the wrong layer.

The actual stored values ARE integers; only the repr lies. (2) DegreeView has the same stringification bug — DegreeView([('0', 1), ('1', 2), ...]) vs nx's DegreeView({0: 1, 1: 2, ...}). title: G.edges (DiGraph/MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph) views miss __eq__ — 'view == view' returns False
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — public-API parity break on view-equality across three graph classes.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx
DG = fnx.DiGraph([(0, 1), (1, 2)])
DG.edges == DG.edges
# False on fnx (default object.__eq__ — identity)
# True on nx (Set inheritance)

MG = fnx.MultiGraph([(0, 1), (0, 1), (1, 2)])
MG.edges == MG.edges  # False on fnx, True on nx
MG.edges == set(MG.edges)  # False on fnx, True on nx

MDG = fnx.MultiDiGraph([(0, 1), (0, 1), (1, 2)])
MDG.edges == MDG.edges  # False on fnx, True on nx
```

## Root cause
The Python-side EdgeView wrappers `_DiGraphEdgeView`,
`_MultiGraphEdgeView`, and `_MultiDiGraphEdgeView` had set-algebra
operators (`|`, `&`, `-`, `^`) but no `__eq__`. Each access to
`G.edges` returned a fresh wrapper instance, so default
`object.__eq__` (identity) returned False. nx's
OutEdgeView/MultiEdgeView/etc. inherit from `collections.abc.Set`
where `__eq__` is content-based.

The Rust `EdgeView` (Graph.edges) was already correct via Rust-side
implementation. The `_DiEdgeMethodView` (DiGraph.in_edges/out_edges)
was fixed last cycle in br-r37-c1-oww5k. This bead closes the
remaining three EdgeView types.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — equality is used by tests, dedup logic, and idiomatic
patterns like `assert G.edges == frozenset({(0,1), (1,2)})`. Same
defect class as br-r37-c1-oww5k; identical fix shape.

## Fix
Add `__eq__` / `__ne__` / `__hash__` to all three Python wrapper
classes matching nx's Set semantics: equal to another wrapper of
the same class with same edges OR any `collections.abc.Set` with
matching contents. NOT equal to lists/tuples (parity with nx).
`__hash__` keyed on `id(self._graph)` for consistent identity.

## Tests
4 new parametrized locks in `test_view_pickle_parity.py::
test_edges_view_equality_is_set_like` (one per graph class)
covering self-equality, vs-set, and vs-different-content. 707
existing parity / pickle / conversion / attr / regression-lock
tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — completing
the EdgeView parity audit. The .nodes/.edges/.degree pickle
contracts and .in_edges/.out_edges contract were locked in earlier
cycles; .edges set-equality was the remaining gap.
close_reason: Verified EdgeView.__eq__ works on all 4 graph classes: g.edges == g.edges returns True. Earlier fix landed.
