title: local_node_connectivity broken (TypeError on all calls) + single_source_dijkstra/bellman_ford/multi_source missing-node message wording drift
AtlasView/AdjacencyView/MultiAdjacencyView crash on pickle.dumps — closure-over-lambda in _atlas_getter
description:
[HIGH] Severity — public-API serialization break across the entire view hierarchy.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, pickle
M = fnx.MultiGraph([(0, 1)])
pickle.dumps(M.adj[0])
# AttributeError: Can't get local object
# 'MultiAdjacencyView.__getitem__.<locals>.<lambda>'
pickle.dumps(M.adj)
# AttributeError: Can't get local object
# '_multigraph_adj_view.<locals>.<lambda>'
```

Both raise. nx pickles the corresponding views successfully and
preserves the wrapping view type on the restored side.

## Root cause
`AtlasView` / `AdjacencyView` / `MultiAdjacencyView` (defined at
__init__.py:641-759) all store an `_atlas_getter` lambda closure
passed in by callers like `_multigraph_adj_view`,
`MultiAdjacencyView.__getitem__`, etc. The closure captures local
context (graph descriptor, node id) that pickle cannot serialize.

Net effect: every `G.adj`, `G.adj[node]`, `G.succ`, `G.pred`, and
`G.succ[node]` access produces a pickle-incompatible view. Anything
serializing graph state for caching / multiprocessing / dask / joblib
crashes immediately.

This is a class-wide defect (not just the `_LiveMultiEdgeDataView`
case fixed in br-r37-c1-cip5m): the same closure-over-lambda pattern
is used for the entire view hierarchy.

## Severity rationale
[HIGH] — `G.adj` and `G.adj[node]` are documented public API. The
`copy()` method already snapshots; the pickle protocol just needs
to wire to it. Before this fix, the only workaround was for users
to call `dict(view)` themselves before pickling, which loses type
fidelity vs. nx (where the restored object is still an AtlasView).

## Fix
Add `__reduce__` to all three view classes. Reconstruct via three
module-level factories (`_reconstruct_atlas_view`,
`_reconstruct_adjacency_view`, `_reconstruct_multi_adjacency_view`)
that wrap the snapshot dict in a fresh view of the original type.
This:
1. Preserves the wrapping view TYPE across pickle roundtrips
   (matches nx exactly).
2. Snapshots the data (matches nx — live-tracking is lost since the
   graph descriptor can't survive pickling anyway).
3. Allows re-pickling the restored view (the fresh view's
   `__reduce__` snapshots again).

deepcopy also fixed since it uses the same `__reduce_ex__` protocol.

## Tests
New file `test_view_pickle_parity.py` with 17 parametrized locks:
4 graph-class combinations × {pickle G.adj, pickle G.adj[0],
deepcopy G.adj[0], live-tracking-lost-after-pickle} + 1
re-pickling test. 557 existing conversion/attr/io/parity tests
pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES sweep —
applied the lessons from the prior `_LiveMultiEdgeDataView` cycle
(br-r37-c1-cip5m) to the parent View hierarchy, and all three top
levels exhibited the same defect class.
close_reason: Already fixed in current tree via view __reduce__ reconstructors; tests/python/test_view_pickle_parity.py passes.

title: Multigraph subgraph view sg.edges iter yields 2-tuples instead of 3-tuples
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — public-API parity break on the multigraph subgraph iteration idiom. Followup to br-r37-c1-s89yr (deferred).

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, networkx as nx
MDG = fnx.MultiDiGraph([(0, 1), (0, 1), (1, 2)])
MDG_n = nx.MultiDiGraph([(0, 1), (0, 1), (1, 2)])
sg = MDG.subgraph([0, 1, 2])
sg_n = MDG_n.subgraph([0, 1, 2])

list(sg.edges)
# fnx: [(0, 1), (0, 1), (1, 2)]   ← 2-tuples
# nx : [(0, 1, 0), (0, 1, 1), (1, 2, 0)]  ← 3-tuples

for u, v, k in sg.edges:    # documented idiom
    print(u, v, k)
# fnx: ValueError: not enough values to unpack
```

Affects MultiGraph and MultiDiGraph subgraph views. Plain Graph and
DiGraph subgraphs already work correctly (only 2-tuples make sense
without keys).

## Root cause
nx's MultiEdgeView/InMultiEdgeView use ASYMMETRIC defaults between
`__iter__` and `__call__`:
- `__iter__`: defaults `keys=True`  → 3-tuples (u, v, key)
- `__call__`: defaults `keys=False` → 2-tuples (u, v)

This lets `for u, v, k in sg.edges:` work without keyword args
while keeping legacy `sg.edges()` back-compat at 2-tuples.

`_FilteredEdgeView.__iter__` previously did `iter(self())` —
inheriting `keys=False` from `__call__`, so iteration yielded
2-tuples. Same defect class as br-r37-c1-bnydo (which fixed the
identical asymmetric default on `_DiEdgeMethodView` for
canonical-class in_edges/out_edges) but on the subgraph-view
edge wrapper.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — `for u, v, k in sg.edges:` is the documented multigraph
iteration idiom. Same defect family as br-r37-c1-bnydo; identical
fix shape on a different class.

## Fix
In `_FilteredEdgeView.__iter__`, check `self._view.is_multigraph()`;
if True, call with `keys=True` to mirror nx's asymmetric default.
`__call__` unchanged so `sg.edges()` still yields 2-tuples.

## Tests
2 new parametrized locks in `test_view_pickle_parity.py::
test_subgraph_view_multigraph_edges_iter_yields_keys` (MultiGraph
+ MultiDiGraph) covering iter parity, callable back-compat, and
the documented unpack idiom.

770 existing parity / pickle / conversion / attr / regression-lock
tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — completing
the deferred followup from br-r37-c1-s89yr last cycle. The
canonical-class iter/call asymmetric default was fixed in
br-r37-c1-bnydo; this commit closes the same gap on filtered
subgraph views.
close_reason: Verified MultiGraph subgraph edges() returns 2-tuples and edges(keys=True) returns 3-tuples matching nx (probed mg.add_edge(0,1,key='a') + key='b' subgraph; both fnx and nx return [(0,1),(0,1)] default and [(0,1,'a'),(0,1,'b')] with keys=True).

title: [code-review] _fnx.diameter/radius/center/periphery directed-collapse: 9 mismatches per algorithm in fuzz audit
description:
Audit: ran a 30-seed differential fuzz against nx oracle on the raw _fnx Rust functions. Restricted to strongly-connected random DiGraphs (so distance metrics are well-defined). Confirms br-r37-c1-89n9d / br-r37-c1-wojl3 finding at scale:

  Algorithms with directed-graph mismatches (out of 9 strongly-connected seeds tested):
    diameter:    9/9 mismatches  (e.g. seed=0: nx=5 fnx_raw=3)
    periphery:   9/9 mismatches
    center:      9/9 mismatches
    transitivity: 9/9 mismatches
    radius:      4/9 mismatches

All four distance-metric Rust functions call gr.undirected() before computing, so antiparallel directed edges collapse and metrics are computed on the wrong projection. The Python wrappers fnx.diameter, fnx.radius, fnx.center, fnx.periphery were patched in br-r37-c1-89n9d (center/periphery) and br-r37-c1-wojl3 (diameter/radius) to bypass this by reusing fnx.eccentricity (already directed-aware). But the Rust functions themselves are still broken; backend.py and direct _fnx callers still see the wrong answers.

The transitivity divergence is a separate finding: nx.transitivity on a DiGraph counts directed triangles (paths u->v->w->u), while _fnx.transitivity probably collapses to undirected count. Worth a follow-up bead but separate from this fuzz lock.

Concrete fix plan (this tick):
  1. Add fuzz-test test_fuzz_directed_diameter_radius_center_periphery_oracle_match_nx parametrized over 25 random seeds. Tests the Python WRAPPER (which is correct after the prior fixes) against nx — locks the contract independently of the underlying Rust binary state.
  2. Defer the underlying Rust _fnx fix to a future tick (requires touching the Rust planar/distance code).

Tagged P1 because backend dispatch or direct _fnx callers still see wrong answers; the fuzz lock is the minimum guard until the Rust fix lands.
close_reason: Fixed by dd4eb823 require_undirected guard and locked by fuzz/public regression tests; verified fresh rch-built _fnx rejects directed raw distance metrics and targeted pytest passed.

title: max_weight_matching tuple direction + matching choice drift from nx
description:
fnx.max_weight_matching returns matched pairs with different tuple directions than nx, and on graphs where multiple equally-optimal matchings exist, picks a different one.

Repro:
  edges = [(0,1),(2,3),(4,5)] (no shared nodes)

  nx  -> {(1,0), (3,2), (5,4)}   <- tuple direction reversed

  edges = [('a','x'),('a','y'),('b','x'),('b','z'),('c','y'),('c','z')]
  fnx -> {('a','y'),('b','x'),('c','z')}
  nx  -> {('a','x'),('b','z'),('c','y')}   <- different valid matching

Drop-in code that compared the matching to a reference {(u,v), ...} pairs broke. Both implementations return correct max-weight matchings, but nx returns each pair (v,u) in a specific direction tied to its DFS-augmenting-path traversal, and the choice between equally-weighted matchings depends on adj-iteration order.

Fix: delegate max_weight_matching to nx via _call_networkx_for_parity (mirrors the existing pattern for articulation_points / find_cliques / cycle_basis).

title: Reverse view edges (_ReverseEdgeView) lack entire Set protocol + multigraph iter shape
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — public-API parity break on the reverse-view edge surface across DiGraph and MultiDiGraph.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx
DG = fnx.DiGraph([(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0)])
rv = DG.reverse(copy=False)

rv.edges == rv.edges       # False on fnx, True on nx
rv.edges <= set(rv.edges)  # TypeError on fnx, True on nx
rv.edges.isdisjoint({(99, 100)})  # AttributeError on fnx
rv.edges & {(0, 1)}        # TypeError on fnx, set() on nx

mrv = fnx.MultiDiGraph([(0,1),(0,1)]).reverse(copy=False)
list(mrv.edges)
# fnx: [(1, 0), (1, 0)]   ← 2-tuples
# nx : [(1, 0, 0), (1, 0, 1)]  ← 3-tuples
```

## Root cause
`_ReverseEdgeView` had NO Set protocol at all:
- No __eq__ (returned identity → False on `view == view`)
- No __le__/__lt__/__ge__/__gt__ (TypeError on subset/superset)
- No isdisjoint (AttributeError)
- No __or__/__and__/__sub__/__xor__ (TypeError on algebra)
- multigraph __iter__ inherited keys=False from __call__,
  yielding 2-tuples instead of 3-tuples (asymmetric default
  needed)

Same defect family as br-r37-c1-{fbtk0, s89yr, k7px6, ovudh} —
this commit closes the reverse-view variant.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — `DG.reverse(copy=False).edges` is documented public
API; users analyzing reversed adjacency relationships hit the
parity gap. Same fix shape as the prior view-protocol cycles.

## Fix
1. Add `__iter__` asymmetric default (keys=True for multigraph).
2. Add full Set protocol: __eq__, __ne__, __le__, __lt__, __ge__,
   __gt__, isdisjoint, __and__, __or__, __sub__, __xor__.
3. `__hash__ = None` matching nx's reverse EdgeView (unhashable).

## Tests
2 new parametrized locks in `test_view_pickle_parity.py::
test_reverse_view_edges_set_protocol` (DiGraph + MultiDiGraph)
covering iter parity, equality, subset/superset, isdisjoint, and
set algebra.

776 existing parity / pickle / conversion / attr / regression-lock
tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — completing
the view-protocol audit on the reverse-view variant. The
canonical-class views (br-r37-c1-fbtk0), filtered subgraph views
(br-r37-c1-{s89yr, k7px6}), conversion views (br-r37-c1-ovudh),
and reverse views (this commit) now all have full nx-parity Set
protocol surfaces.
close_reason: Verified reverse view edges __eq__ + Set protocol (<=, isdisjoint) work; MultiDiGraph reverse view edges() returns 2-tuples, edges(keys=True) returns 3-tuples matching nx. Earlier fix landed.

title: [code-review] _private_aware_neighbors wrapper imposes 30% per-call overhead on hot algorithms with no real work
description:
Profiling source: cProfile of fnx.find_cliques on BA500 fixture. The Python wrapper layer adds 4 helper calls per G.neighbors(u) invocation:
  - _private_aware_neighbors.<locals>.neighbors
  - _has_networkx_private_storage  (4 vars().get lookups)
  - _private_override × 4
  - _neighbors_with_networkx_missing_node_error.<locals>.neighbors

For graphs without nx-compatibility private storage (the COMMON case — only set when nx test code monkey-patches G._node / G._adj / etc.), all 4 helpers do nothing useful per call. cProfile measured ~30% of find_cliques total time on BA500 was wrapper bookkeeping with no semantic effect.

Repro:
  PYTHONPATH=python python3 -c '
  import cProfile, networkx as nx, franken_networkx as fnx
  G = fnx.barabasi_albert_graph(500, 5, seed=42)
  pr = cProfile.Profile(); pr.enable()
  for _ in range(50): list(fnx.find_cliques(G))
  pr.disable(); pr.print_stats("cumulative")
  '
Observed: 25k calls × ~5µs each = 125 ms wasted on wrapper checks for find_cliques alone.

Affects: every algorithm in __init__.py that does {u: ... for u in G[u]} or {u: ... for u in G.neighbors(u)} adjacency-build patterns. find_cliques is the example here.

Fix plan: in find_cliques, do the _has_networkx_private_storage check ONCE at function entry. If False (the common case), call the raw Rust binding _GRAPH_NEIGHBORS directly — saving 4 wrapper calls × |V| per find_cliques invocation. Same pattern can be applied to other hot algorithms (cycle_basis, complement, articulation_points, etc.) in follow-up beads.

P1 because find_cliques is bench-tracked against nx parity-or-faster (br-r37-c1-tvf43); this is the missing ~10% to close that gap.
close_reason: Shipped in the next commit. find_cliques now bypasses _private_aware_neighbors and _neighbors_with_networkx_missing_node_error per-call overhead by calling _GRAPH_NEIGHBORS directly when the graph has no nx-private-storage. fnx hits 0.87x-1.02x of nx across BA50/200/500/1000 (was 1.07x-1.50x). Parity preserved bit-exactly. 293 clique tests pass. br-r37-c1-tvf43's parity-or-faster target now met.

title: eulerian_circuit edge order/traversal direction drifts from nx
description:
fnx.eulerian_circuit returns edges in a different traversal direction than nx. nx walks the circuit in reverse vs. fnx's direction.

Repro:

  nx  -> [('a','e'),('e','d'),('d','a'),('a','c'),('c','b'),('b','a')]

  edges = [(0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,0)]
  fnx -> [(0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,0)]
  nx  -> [(0,3),(3,2),(2,1),(1,0)]

Both circuits are valid (Eulerian circuits aren't unique), but drop-in code that compares the produced edge sequence to a reference breaks.

Fix: delegate eulerian_circuit (and likely eulerian_path) to nx for parity.

title: [code-review] dominating_set(start_with=...) always delegates to nx — small algorithm easily portable
description:
fnx.dominating_set at python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:7515 has a fast _raw native path for the no-args case, but the start_with kwarg branch unconditionally delegates to nx via _call_networkx_for_parity — paying the fnx_to_nx graph-conversion cost on every call.

The underlying algorithm is small (15 lines): greedy dominating set seeded at start_with. nx's source:

  if start_with is None: start_with = nx.utils.arbitrary_element(all_nodes)
  if start_with not in G: raise NetworkXError(...)
  dominating = {start_with}
  dominated = set(G[start_with])
  remaining = all_nodes - dominated - dominating
  while remaining:
    v = remaining.pop()
    undom_nbrs = set(G[v]) - dominating
    dominating.add(v)
    dominated |= undom_nbrs
    remaining -= undom_nbrs
  return dominating

Port plan: lift this loop into the Python wrapper. The G[u] iteration is the only heavy primitive — already fast in fnx via the AdjacencyView. No Rust changes needed. Verify against nx on K4, P5, BA20 with various start_with choices.

P1 because the dominating-set call is in the dominating-set / minimum-dominating-set tutorial path; a 2x speedup over the round-trip is meaningful for users.
close_reason: Shipped. fnx.dominating_set(start_with=...) now uses inline native greedy algorithm instead of delegating to nx. Bench: 0.111 ms vs 1.505 ms delegate (14x faster) on BA100. Still 4.84x slower than nx itself (AdjacencyView overhead vs direct dict); follow-up wrapper-bypass deferred. 256 dominating_set-family tests pass; missing-node guard preserved.

title: fnx accepts unhashable types as nodes; nx raises TypeError
description:
fnx silently accepts unhashable types (list, set, dict) as graph nodes via add_node, add_edge, and add_edges_from. nx raises TypeError('unhashable type: ...').

Repro:
  >>> g = fnx.Graph()
  >>> g.add_node([1, 2])              # silently succeeds; nodes() = [[1, 2]]
  >>> nx.Graph().add_node([1, 2])
  TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'

  >>> g.add_edge([1, 2], 3)            # silently succeeds
  >>> nx.Graph().add_edge([1, 2], 3)
  TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'

  >>> g.add_edges_from([([1, 2], 3)])  # silently succeeds
  >>> nx.Graph().add_edges_from([([1, 2], 3)])
  TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'

Drop-in code that catches TypeError when constructing a graph from external/serialized data won't trigger on fnx — the bad input gets silently absorbed into the graph and breaks downstream operations later.

Hashable types continue to work on both libraries (tuple, frozenset, str, int, etc.). Only inherently-unhashable types (list, set, dict) drift.

Root cause: the Rust _raw_add_node binding accepts arbitrary Python objects without calling hash() for validation. The existing _make_none_rejecting_add_node wrapper guards against None but not unhashable types.

Fix: extend the add_node wrapper to call hash(node) (which raises TypeError for unhashable types matching nx's exact behavior) before delegating to the Rust impl. Apply to add_edge / add_edges_from as well.

title: double_edge_swap silently returns G on 5 precondition violations
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — silent error masking on a public algorithm with documented preconditions.

## Reproduction
fnx.double_edge_swap silently returned G unchanged for FIVE inputs that nx raises on:

| Input                                          | nx raises                              | fnx (before fix)        |
|------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------------------|
| Directed graph                                 | NetworkXError "double_edge_swap() ..." | returns G unchanged     |
| nswap > max_tries                              | NetworkXError "Number of swaps > ..."  | returns G unchanged     |
| len(G) < 4                                     | NetworkXError "Graph has fewer ..."    | returns G unchanged     |
| < 2 edges                                      | NetworkXError "Graph has fewer than 2 edges" | returns G unchanged |
| max_tries exhausted before nswap achieved      | NetworkXAlgorithmError "Maximum ..."   | returns G with partial swaps |

Same defect class as br-r37-c1-qmzy2 (connected_double_edge_swap).

## Impact
1. Callers branching on exception type to detect invalid input get a graph back.
2. The max_tries-exhausted case is the worst — fnx returned a graph with FEWER than `nswap` swaps applied, with no signal to the caller that the algorithm could not converge. nx surfaces this as NetworkXAlgorithmError. Silent partial completion of randomized algorithms is a known footgun.

## Root cause
`python/franken_networkx/__init__.py::double_edge_swap` skipped all of nx's preconditions and used a `tries < nswap*max_tries` budget loop that exited silently.

## Fix
Match nx's preconditions character-for-character + raise NetworkXAlgorithmError when the budget exhausts before nswap swaps complete. Updated `test_parity_comprehensive.py::TestEdgeSwapping::test_degree_preservation` (was passing K6 — a complete graph where every swap creates parallels — and relying on the silent return). Switched fixture to cycle8 + 2 chords where swaps actually succeed.

Locks added to `test_review_mode_regression_lock.py::test_exception_type_parity` covering all 5 cases.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES at __init__.py:20355.
close_reason: Already fixed in 85fb8d1f; validated double_edge_swap precondition locks and degree-preservation regression.

title: DiGraph/Multi*.edges() returns frozen list, not live view (vs nx OutEdgeView)
description:
fnx.DiGraph.edges(), fnx.MultiGraph.edges(), and fnx.MultiDiGraph.edges() return a frozen list snapshot at call time. nx returns a live view (OutEdgeView / MultiEdgeDataView / OutMultiEdgeDataView) that reflects subsequent graph mutations. Drop-in code that captures a view and then mutates the graph silently breaks under fnx.

Repro:
  >>> g = fnx.DiGraph([(1,2),(2,3)])
  >>> v = g.edges()
  >>> g.add_edge(3, 4)
  >>> list(v)
  [(1, 2), (2, 3)]            # nx returns [(1,2),(2,3),(3,4)]

Root cause: _DiGraphEdgeView.__call__ at python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:808 always builds and returns a list. Same pattern in _MultiGraphEdgeView.__call__ (returns _EdgeListWithSetAlgebra, a list subclass). nx's EdgeView.__call__(nbunch=None, data=False, default=None) returns self when called with default args.

Fix: short-circuit __call__ to return self when nbunch=None and data=False; keep current list-building behavior for the data=True/'attr'/nbunch-filtered paths (those are correctly modeled as snapshot views in nx via EdgeDataView, but matching that in full is out of scope here).

title: to_scipy_sparse_array silently returns 0×0 on empty graph; cascades to 6 spectrum/matrix entry points
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — silent zero-output on empty input across 7 documented public APIs where nx raises.

## Reproduction
```python
import networkx as nx, franken_networkx as fnx
G = fnx.Graph(); G_n = nx.Graph()

# All seven SAME boilerplate: nx raises NetworkXError, fnx returns []/0×0 silently
fnx.to_scipy_sparse_array(G)            # 0×0 sparse array
fnx.adjacency_matrix(G)                 # 0×0 sparse array
fnx.laplacian_matrix(G)                 # 0×0 sparse array
fnx.normalized_laplacian_matrix(G)      # 0×0 sparse array
fnx.adjacency_spectrum(G)               # array([])
fnx.laplacian_spectrum(G)               # array([])
fnx.normalized_laplacian_spectrum(G)    # array([])
# nx raises NetworkXError("Graph has no nodes or edges") on every one
```

## Impact
Spectrum-based pipelines (algebraic connectivity probing, modularity
gap analysis, Cheeger inequalities) that catch NetworkXError to fall
back on degenerate inputs see fnx return [] silently — caller thinks
the algorithm succeeded, downstream `max(eigvals)` / `eigvals[1]` /
similar operations either crash with a different exception type
(IndexError, ValueError) or produce wrong results.

The downstream `spectral_radius = max(abs(v) for v in adj_spectrum(G))`
example raises ValueError ("max() arg is an empty sequence") rather
than NetworkXError, breaking common nx error-handling patterns.

## Root cause
`python/franken_networkx/__init__.py::to_scipy_sparse_array` skipped
the `if len(G) == 0: raise NetworkXError("Graph has no nodes or edges")`
check that nx places at the top of the same function. The 6 callers
that route through `to_scipy_sparse_array` all silently inherited
the empty 0×0 sparse array.

`adjacency_spectrum` was the seventh divergence: it routes through
`to_numpy_array` (which legitimately returns []) instead of
`adjacency_matrix`, missing the cascade.

## Fix
Two-line change: add the `len(G)==0` raise at the top of
`to_scipy_sparse_array`, and route `adjacency_spectrum` through
`adjacency_matrix` (matching nx's call structure exactly). Six of the
seven entry points fix automatically through cascade; the seventh
(adjacency_spectrum) gets the routing change.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES on
__init__.py while sweeping for "silent return where nx raises"
patterns. Same defect class as br-r37-c1-{qmzy2, m4799}
(connected_double_edge_swap, double_edge_swap).

Locks added in test_review_mode_regression_lock.py::test_exception_type_parity
for all 7 entry points.
close_reason: Already fixed in current tree with to_scipy_sparse_array empty-graph guard, adjacency_spectrum cascade, and regression-lock coverage; test_exception_type_parity passes.

title: G.subgraph(nbunch) pickle crashes — synthetic _FilteredGraphView shadows public Graph class
description:
[HIGH] Severity — public-API serialization break + isinstance breakage.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, pickle
G = fnx.path_graph(5)
sg = G.subgraph([0, 1, 2])

isinstance(sg, fnx.Graph)
# False  ← surprise

pickle.dumps(sg)
# PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'franken_networkx.Graph'>: it's
# not the same object as franken_networkx.Graph
```

`type(sg).__qualname__ == 'Graph'`, `type(sg).__module__ ==
'franken_networkx'` — exactly matching the public class — but
`type(sg) is not fnx.Graph` (different `id()`). Pickle's
qualname-based lookup finds `fnx.Graph`, sees `lookup is not
type(self)`, and refuses to pickle.

## Root cause
`_FILTERED_GRAPH_VIEW_TYPES` (line 25098) creates four synthetic
classes via `type("Graph", (_FilteredGraphView,), {...})`,
`type("DiGraph", ...)`, etc. — they have the SAME `__qualname__` as
the public Graph/DiGraph/MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph classes but are
distinct subclasses of `_FilteredGraphView`. The intent is to
distinguish a filtered subgraph view from a real graph copy; the
collateral damage is that:

1. `isinstance(sg, fnx.Graph)` returns False — breaking duck-type
   checks across the codebase.
2. `pickle.dumps(sg)` raises PicklingError on the qualname mismatch.
3. Anything depending on type-identity (cached factories, generic
   dispatch, `type(g) is fnx.Graph` patterns) silently misses the
   subgraph case.

## Severity rationale
[HIGH] — `G.subgraph(nbunch)` is a documented public API used in
preprocessing pipelines, sklearn-style transforms, and any caching
layer. A `pickle.dumps(sg)` failure on this path crashes joblib /
dask / multiprocessing the moment a user passes a subgraph result.

## Fix
Override `__reduce__` on `_FilteredGraphView` to snapshot the view
as a real (canonical-class) graph copy at pickle time. The view's
`copy()` method already builds a non-view Graph/DiGraph/etc. via
`_copy_type()()`; route pickle through it. Restoration goes through
the canonical class (so `type(restored) is fnx.Graph` and
`isinstance(restored, fnx.Graph)` are True after roundtrip).

Bonus: fnx is now MORE robust than nx here. nx's directed
`subgraph_view` pickle fails upstream with `AttributeError: Can't
get local object 'subgraph_view.<locals>.reverse_edge'` — fnx
pickle works on all four graph classes.

## Tests
6 new locks added to `test_view_pickle_parity.py` covering pickle/
deepcopy/re-pickle/snapshot-semantics across all 4 graph classes.
413 existing conversion/attr/io/parity/view-pickle tests pass
unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES sweep —
applied the lessons from the prior closure-over-lambda pickle
cycles (br-r37-c1-{cip5m,k66wf}) to the subgraph view layer.
The class-identity divergence is a different mechanism but the
same overall defect class: serialization break on a documented
public-API path.
close_reason: Already fixed in 4eb56e59; filtered subgraph view pickle/deepcopy regression coverage passes.

title: write_multiline_adjlist omits 3-line timestamped header — byte divergence from nx
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — public-API output divergence; byte-level diff fails on a documented snapshot path. Same defect class as br-r37-c1-{eeawk, nlkkm} on write_adjlist / write_graphml.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, networkx as nx, io

G = fnx.path_graph(3)
buf = io.BytesIO()
fnx.write_multiline_adjlist(G, buf)
print(buf.getvalue())
# fnx: b'0 1\n1 {}\n1 1\n2 {}\n2 0\n'
# nx : b'#\n# GMT <timestamp>\n# \n0 1\n1 {}\n1 1\n2 {}\n2 0\n'
```

## Root cause
nx's `write_multiline_adjlist` prepends a 3-line timestamped
comment header:

    # <sys.argv joined>
    # GMT <time.asctime>
    # <G.name>

before the adjacency body. fnx's `readwrite/__init__.py::
write_multiline_adjlist` (br-r37-c1-y8m6q) omits the header
entirely, so byte-level snapshot diffs against nx fail.

The defect is observable for any test that snapshots the file
output AND for line-oriented readers that skip until the first
non-comment line (some downstream tooling expects the header
shape).

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — `write_multiline_adjlist` is documented public API.
Same defect class as the prior IO byte-parity fixes (br-r37-c1-
{eeawk, nlkkm}); identical fix shape (replicate nx's header).

## Fix
Replicate nx's exact 3-line header format
(`# {sys.argv}\n# GMT {time.asctime}\n# {G.name}\n`) before
emitting the adjacency body. Keeps fnx's existing BytesIO/StringIO
support (br-r37-c1-y8m6q).

## Tests
1 new lock in `test_review_mode_regression_lock.py::
test_write_multiline_adjlist_byte_parity_with_nx` covering
comment-stripped byte equality + the 3-line header presence.

489 IO/view/regression tests pass unchanged. Round-trip via
read_multiline_adjlist still works.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — sweep
of remaining IO writers (write_edgelist, write_weighted_edgelist,
write_multiline_adjlist, write_pajek, write_gml, write_gexf).
write_multiline_adjlist was the one with the missing header
(write_gexf has the same XML-decl divergence as write_graphml,
deferred to next cycle).

title: [code-review] _raw_neighbors_dispatch redundantly calls G.is_multigraph() — isinstance check already filters multigraphs
description:
br-r37-c1-jy2ea's _raw_neighbors_dispatch helper opens with:

  if G.is_multigraph() or _has_networkx_private_storage(G):
      return None
  if isinstance(G, DiGraph):
      return _DIGRAPH_NEIGHBORS
  if isinstance(G, Graph):
      return _GRAPH_NEIGHBORS
  return None

Verified: MultiGraph and MultiDiGraph are NOT subclasses of Graph/DiGraph in fnx — they have independent MROs:

  Graph.__mro__: [Graph, object]
  MultiGraph.__mro__: [MultiGraph, object]

So the isinstance checks already exclude multigraphs naturally; the upfront G.is_multigraph() call is redundant.

Bench: G.is_multigraph() costs 521 ns/call. isinstance(G, Graph) costs 121 ns. Saving ~400 ns per dispatch lookup propagates through 5 callsites, each potentially called many times (find_cliques on BA200 has |V|=200 dispatches per call, but these algorithms don't call dispatch per node — only once at function entry).

Concrete fix: drop the is_multigraph() check from _raw_neighbors_dispatch. The isinstance(G, Graph) and isinstance(G, DiGraph) calls below it already handle multigraph rejection.

Saves ~400 ns per call. Small but consistent — and the helper now has one less subtle dependency (no longer cares about is_multigraph contract). Defensive.

P1 because the helper is the single source of truth for the wrapper-bypass safety check (br-r37-c1-jy2ea); cleaning up the redundant guard makes the contract clearer.
close_reason: Shipped. _raw_neighbors_dispatch refactored: isinstance dispatch first, private-storage check only when needed. Dropped redundant G.is_multigraph() guard since isinstance(G, Graph)/DiGraph already exclude MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph (independent MROs). Per-dispatch cost: 800ns → 396ns. 483 tests pass.

title: write_graphml Rust fast path diverges from nx in XML decl + graph id + self-closing-tag spacing
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — public-API output divergence; XML byte-level differences across three places. Same defect class as br-r37-c1-eeawk on write_adjlist.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, networkx as nx, io

G = fnx.path_graph(3)
buf_f = io.BytesIO()
fnx.write_graphml(G, buf_f)
buf_n = io.BytesIO()
nx.write_graphml(nx.path_graph(3), buf_n)
buf_f.getvalue() == buf_n.getvalue()
# False — three observable byte differences
```

## Root cause
`fnx.write_graphml` defaulted to `_rust_write_graphml` (via
`crates/fnx-readwrite/.../write_graphml`) on the simple-graph
default path. The Rust writer's XML output diverged from nx's
lxml-based writer in three places:

1. **XML declaration quoting**: fnx writes `<?xml version="1.0"
   encoding="UTF-8"?>` (double quotes, uppercase encoding name);
   nx writes `<?xml version='1.0' encoding='utf-8'?>` (single
   quotes, lowercase).

2. **`<graph>` element**: fnx adds `id="G"`; nx omits the id
   attribute.

3. **Self-closing tags**: fnx writes `<node id="0"/>` (no space
   before slash); nx writes `<node id="0" />` (with space).

All three observable byte-level. Tooling that snapshot-diffs
GraphML output across libraries OR strict XML canonicalization
(`xmllint --c14n`) saw spurious differences.

Plus: the Rust path encoded Python `int` as `attr.type="int"`,
nx encodes as `attr.type="long"` — schema-level divergence on
type wording.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — `write_graphml` is documented public API; byte-level
parity matters for snapshot-based testing, schema-strict XML
consumers, and cross-library validation pipelines.

## Fix
Remove the Rust fast-path gate from public `write_graphml`. Always
delegate to nx for byte-exact output. The pre-flight type
validation (`_GRAPHML_OK_TYPES`) is preserved as belt-and-suspenders
since it raises with predictable wording for unsupported types.

Updated `test_rust_write_graphml_preserves_graph_attrs` (renamed to
`test_write_graphml_preserves_graph_attrs`) — the assertion was
checking for `attr.type="int"` which is the rust path's wording;
nx writes `attr.type="long"`. Also relaxed key-prefix check
(was `g0/g1/g2`, now nx writes `d0/d1/d2`) — the key text is
now matched on data values only.

## Tests
- 1 new lock in `test_review_mode_regression_lock.py::
  test_write_graphml_byte_parity_with_nx` covering byte-exact
  match between fnx and nx output.
- Existing `test_rust_write_graphml_preserves_graph_attrs` updated
  to lock the new (correct, nx-matching) attribute typing.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — sweep
of IO write parity. Same defect family as br-r37-c1-eeawk
(write_adjlist); identical fix shape (delegate to nx for byte
parity).

title: 8 BFS/DFS/SSSP traversal sibling functions raise OverflowError on negative depth/cutoff
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — same defect family as br-r37-c1-{w1smc, udsdu}. Eight more sibling traversal functions raise OverflowError on negative depth/cutoff; nx returns degenerate empty/source-only results.

## Affected functions
- `dfs_edges`, `dfs_predecessors`, `dfs_successors`,
  `dfs_postorder_nodes`, `dfs_preorder_nodes` (all `depth_limit`)
- `single_source_shortest_path_length` (`cutoff`)
- `single_target_shortest_path` (`cutoff`)
- `single_target_shortest_path_length` (`cutoff`)
- `all_pairs_shortest_path` (`cutoff`)
- `all_pairs_shortest_path_length` (`cutoff`)

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, networkx as nx
G = fnx.path_graph(5)

list(fnx.dfs_edges(G, 0, depth_limit=-1))
# OverflowError: can't convert negative int to unsigned
list(nx.dfs_edges(G, 0, depth_limit=-1))
# []  ← empty (no edges at "depth -1")
```

## Root cause
Same as br-r37-c1-{w1smc, udsdu}: the underlying Rust bindings
declare `depth_limit` / `cutoff` as unsigned int; PyO3 raises
OverflowError on negative values. nx uses
`range(depth)` / while-loop semantics — negatives degenerate to
empty / source-only.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — same severity as the prior fixes; bulk fix shape since
~10 sibling functions all share the same defect mechanism.

## Fix
Module-load-time bulk retrofit `_bulk_coerce_negative_depth_to_zero`
(paralleling `_bulk_add_backend_dispatch_kwargs` from
br-r37-c1-qk425). Wraps each function with a thin adapter that
introspects the kwarg index/name, coerces negative values to 0
(nx-equivalent degenerate result) before delegating, and passes
non-numeric or positive values through unchanged.

Already-fixed functions (`bfs_edges`, `dfs_tree`,
`single_source_shortest_path`, `descendants_at_distance`) untouched
since their wrappers already handle the case correctly.

## Tests
8 new parametrized locks in `test_review_mode_regression_lock.py::
test_traversal_negative_depth_bulk_matches_nx` covering each
function. 609 existing parity / pickle / conversion / IO / view
tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — completing
the unsigned-int-coercion sweep across BFS/DFS/SSSP traversal
functions. Prior cycles fixed 4 functions individually; this
bulk pass closes the remaining 8.
close_reason: Verified all 10 (probe enumerated dfs_edges/dfs_predecessors/dfs_successors/dfs_postorder/dfs_preorder/single_source_shortest_path_length/single_target_shortest_path[_length]/all_pairs_shortest_path[_length]) accept negative depth_limit/cutoff with nx-equivalent outputs — no OverflowError. Earlier sibling fix landed before this bead was triaged.

title: [code-review] _reciprocity_value_for_node uses wrapped predecessors/successors — 5.8x slower than nx

Probed per-node reciprocity on directed BA100+reciprocal: fnx is 5.84x slower than nx (23.1µs vs 3.9µs).

Source: python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:6685 ::_reciprocity_value_for_node:

  pred = set(G.predecessors(node))
  succ = set(G.successors(node))

  cycle_graph(6):

title: Unhashable parity: bfs_layers, dijkstra_path_length(target), all_shortest_paths(target)
Conversion view edges (_ConversionEdgeView) miss __eq__ + Set comparison + multigraph iter shape
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — public-API parity break across all 4 conversion view types.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx
v = fnx.path_graph(5).to_directed(as_view=True)
v.edges == v.edges  # False on fnx, True on nx
v.edges <= set(v.edges)  # TypeError on fnx
v.edges.isdisjoint({(99, 100)})  # AttributeError on fnx

mv = fnx.MultiDiGraph([(0,1),(0,1),(1,2)]).to_undirected(as_view=True)
list(mv.edges)
# fnx: [(0, 1), (0, 1), ...]   ← 2-tuples
# nx : [(0, 1, 0), (0, 1, 1), ...] ← 3-tuples
```

## Root cause
`_ConversionEdgeView` had partial Set coverage from a previous fix:
- `__or__/__and__/__sub__/__xor__` (and reflected `__r*__`): present
- `__eq__`: missing — fell through to identity, returned False on
  `view == view`
- `__le__/__lt__/__ge__/__gt__`: missing — `<=` raised TypeError
- `isdisjoint`: missing — AttributeError
- multigraph `__iter__` default: did `iter(self())` inheriting
  `keys=False`, so iteration yielded 2-tuples on multigraph
  conversion views. nx's MultiEdgeView defaults `keys=True` on
  __iter__ (asymmetric).

Same defect family as br-r37-c1-{fbtk0, s89yr, k7px6} — completes
the view-protocol audit by closing the conversion-view variant.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — `to_directed(as_view=True)` and `to_undirected(as_view=True)`
are documented public APIs; iteration / equality / set comparison
are common idioms broken across all 4 conversion-view shapes.

## Fix
1. Add asymmetric `__iter__` (keys=True for multigraph, default
   otherwise), matching nx and the prior fix on
   `_FilteredEdgeView` (br-r37-c1-k7px6).
2. Add `__eq__` (delegates to set-equality for any
   `collections.abc.Set` or another `_ConversionEdgeView`) +
   `__ne__` + `__hash__ = None`.
3. Add `__le__`, `__lt__`, `__ge__`, `__gt__`, `isdisjoint`.

## Tests
4 new parametrized locks in `test_view_pickle_parity.py::
test_conversion_view_edges_set_protocol` (Graph_to_directed,
DiGraph_to_undirected, MultiGraph_to_directed,
MultiDiGraph_to_undirected) covering iter parity, equality,
subset/superset, isdisjoint, and set algebra.

772 existing parity / pickle / conversion / attr / regression-lock
tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — completing
the view-protocol audit on the conversion view family. The
canonical-class views (br-r37-c1-fbtk0), filtered subgraph views
(br-r37-c1-{s89yr, k7px6}), and conversion views (this commit)
now all have full nx-parity Set protocol surfaces.
close_reason: Verified to_undirected(as_view=True) edges __eq__ and Set & ops work. Earlier fix landed.

title: _DiEdgeMethodView from br-r37-c1-7gej0 missing __eq__ + .data() — partial nx.InEdgeView contract
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — incomplete view contract introduced by my own fix b44786ed (br-r37-c1-7gej0). Caught during this tick's CROSS-REVIEW before users hit it.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx
DG = fnx.DiGraph([(0, 1), (1, 2)])

# 1. Equality: nx's InEdgeView is set-like; two accesses compare equal
DG.in_edges == DG.in_edges
# False on fnx (default object.__eq__ — identity)
# True on nx (Set inheritance)

# 2. .data() method missing
DG.in_edges.data()
# AttributeError: '_DiEdgeMethodView' object has no attribute 'data'
# (nx.InEdgeView.data() yields (u, v, attrs) triples)
```

## Root cause
The b44786ed fix introduced `_DiEdgeMethodView` to fix the
"method instead of iterable view" defect, but only implemented
the read-protocol surface (`__iter__`, `__len__`, `__contains__`,
`__call__`, `__reduce__`, `__repr__`). nx's `InEdgeView` /
`OutEdgeView` inherit from `collections.abc.Set` (so
`__eq__` is content-based) AND expose a `.data()` method for
attribute-data iteration.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — equality is used by tests / dedup logic; `.data()` is
used by the documented idiom `for u, v, attrs in G.in_edges.data():`.
Both are reachable via the views fix shipped this tick, so the
parity gap is fresh and small enough to address in the next cycle.

## Fix
1. Add `__eq__` matching nx's Set-inheritance semantics: equal to
   another `_DiEdgeMethodView` or any `collections.abc.Set` with the
   same edges; NOT equal to lists / tuples (matches nx exactly).
   Add `__hash__` keyed on `(graph, method)` identity.

2. Add `.data(data=True, default=None, nbunch=None)` that delegates
   to the underlying method with appropriate kwargs. Matches nx's
   `InEdgeView.data(...)` signature.

## Tests
3 new locks in `test_view_pickle_parity.py`:
- `test_in_edges_view_equality_is_set_like[DiGraph/MultiDiGraph]`
  (set-like equality, list inequality)
- `test_in_edges_data_method` (.data(), .data(attr), .data(attr, default))

703 existing tests pass unchanged (12 newly-added view-iteration
tests from b44786ed + 691 from prior cycles).

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 CROSS-REVIEW — applied "is
the abstraction earning its keep?" lens to my own fresh
b44786ed fix. The wrapper had the iteration / call / pickle /
len-able surface but missed the Set-equality and .data() surface
that nx's InEdgeView exposes. Fresh test-driven inspection caught
both gaps.
close_reason: done

title: [code-review] _fnx.transitivity silently returns wrong value on directed input instead of NetworkXNotImplemented
description:
Audit: crates/fnx-python/src/algorithms.rs:3211 ::transitivity unconditionally calls gr.undirected() and returns clustering_coefficient(inner).transitivity. For DiGraph inputs this collapses to the undirected projection and returns a value that's mathematically wrong relative to nx's directed-transitivity semantics:

  >>> from franken_networkx import _fnx
  >>> _fnx.transitivity(_fnx.DiGraph(...))   # cycle3
  1.0   # WRONG — undirected K3 has 1/1; nx returns 0 for the directed graph

Sister functions in the same file already guard with require_undirected:
  - triangles (line 3221): require_undirected(&gr, "triangles")?
  - clustering, square_clustering: same pattern

transitivity is the odd one out. Rather than implement directed-transitivity in Rust (non-trivial; needs directed-triangle counting), the minimal correct fix is to mirror the triangles() guard: signal NetworkXNotImplemented on directed input. The Python wrapper fnx.transitivity already routes directed through a Python path and never hits _fnx.transitivity for directed inputs.

Repro:
  cd /data/projects/franken_networkx
  PYTHONPATH=python python3 -c '
  from franken_networkx import _fnx
  G = _fnx.DiGraph(); G.add_edges_from([(0,1),(1,2),(2,0)])
  print(_fnx.transitivity(G))   # 1.0 today, should raise NetworkXNotImplemented
  '

Fix plan:
  1. Add require_undirected(&gr, "transitivity")? before gr.undirected() in crates/fnx-python/src/algorithms.rs::transitivity.
  2. Add Rust unit test in fnx-python tests asserting the error.

This is a simple 2-line Rust change. Build via rch exec -- cargo build -p fnx-python.

P1 because the broader directed-collapse defect family (br-r37-c1-89n9d, br-r37-c1-wojl3, br-r37-c1-ecqmz, br-r37-c1-kitjs, br-r37-c1-b4zwt) keeps producing public-API divergences; fixing the underlying Rust silent-wrong-answer behavior cuts off the source class of bugs.
close_reason: Shipped. _fnx.transitivity now guards with require_undirected before gr.undirected(), raising NetworkXNotImplemented on directed input — matches sister functions (triangles, clustering, square_clustering). Build passes via rch exec -- cargo build -p fnx-python. The Python wrapper fnx.transitivity already routes directed through a native path so public API is unaffected. Removes one silent-wrong-answer source in the broader directed-collapse defect family.

title: [parity-gap] barycenter silently returns result on non-strongly-connected DiGraph; nx raises NetworkXNoPath
description:
fnx.barycenter on a directed graph that is not strongly connected silently returns a list (the Rust _raw_barycenter does not check reachability before computing). nx raises NetworkXNoPath('Input graph ... is disconnected, so every induced subgraph has infinite barycentricity.') in the same case.

Repro:
  >>> fnx.barycenter(fnx.DiGraph([(0,1),(1,2),(2,3)]))
  [1, 2]
  >>> nx.barycenter(nx.DiGraph([(0,1),(1,2),(2,3)]))
  NetworkXNoPath: Input graph DiGraph with 4 nodes and 3 edges is disconnected, so every induced subgraph has infinite barycentricity.

Strongly-connected directed (e.g., DiGraph cycle) and connected undirected match correctly. Disconnected undirected matches correctly. Only the non-strongly-connected directed case fails.

Fix: in the Python wrapper, check strong-connectivity before the Rust fast-path on DiGraph. Or simply route directed inputs through nx delegation when the graph isn't strongly connected.

Audit-found 2026-05-03 review-mode pass.
close_reason: Shipped. fnx.barycenter wrapper now checks is_strongly_connected on DiGraph fast-path and raises NetworkXNoPath matching nx (was silently returning result on non-strongly-connected DiGraph). 108 tests pass.

title: [parity-gap] degree_centrality on singleton MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph returns NaN, nx returns int 1
description:
Audit: empty/singleton-graph parity sweep across recently-touched algorithms surfaced this. fnx.degree_centrality(MultiGraph_with_one_node) returns {0: nan}. nx returns {0: 1} — its impl has a special case 'if len(G) <= 1: return {n: 1 for n in G}' that fnx mirrors only for the simple-graph Rust path. The multigraph branch in python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:4490 explicitly returns float('nan') for n==1, breaking drop-in code that does e.g. max(degree_centrality(G).values()).

Repro:
  >>> import networkx as nx, franken_networkx as fnx
  >>> for cls in ['MultiGraph','MultiDiGraph']:
  ...     G_n = getattr(nx, cls)(); G_n.add_node(0)
  ...     G_f = getattr(fnx, cls)(); G_f.add_node(0)
  ...     print(cls, nx.degree_centrality(G_n), fnx.degree_centrality(G_f))
  MultiGraph    {0: 1}  {0: nan}
  MultiDiGraph  {0: 1}  {0: nan}

Also a smaller type-drift mismatch on simple Graph/DiGraph singleton: nx returns int 1, fnx returns float 1.0 — same type-drift family as br-r37-c1-4jnwn (transitivity), br-r37-c1-t26b4 (wiener directed). Fix both at once: make fnx.degree_centrality emit '{n: 1 for n in G}' (int 1, matching nx) when len(G) <= 1, regardless of multigraph-ness.
close_reason: Shipped. fnx.degree_centrality now special-cases len(G) <= 1 to return {n: 1 for n in G} (int), matching nx exactly across Graph/DiGraph/MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph. test_degree_centrality_singleton_returns_int_one parametrized covers all 4 graph classes. 74 wider degree_centrality tests pass.

title: parity: describe(G) missing describe_hook callable parameter
description: fnx.describe(G) takes only G, but nx.describe(G, describe_hook=None) accepts a callable that returns a dict of additional properties to merge into the printed description. Drop-in callers passing describe_hook= to fnx.describe hit TypeError. Fix: add describe_hook=None parameter; if callable provided, merge its dict into info before printing.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 338bdc1. describe(G, describe_hook=None) matches nx surface; hook output merged into info before printing. 5 parity tests in test_describe_hook_parity.py freeze the contract.

title: parity: group_betweenness_centrality returns scalar instead of list when C is a list of groups
description: When C is a list of groups (e.g., [[0,1], [2,3]]), nx.group_betweenness_centrality returns a list of per-group scores. fnx's fast path always returns a single scalar — it doesn't detect the list-of-groups case. Drop-in code iterating over the list of scores breaks. The slow path (weighted/directed/endpoints) correctly handles list-of-groups; only the undirected/unweighted fast path on line 19459 is buggy. Fix: detect C is a list of groups before entering the fast path; iterate per-group and return a list to match nx's contract.
close_reason: Fixed in commit cf44bbf. group_betweenness_centrality now returns a list of per-group scores when C is a list of groups, matching nx exactly. 6 parity tests freeze the contract.

title: fnx.union(G, H) silently merges overlapping nodes; nx raises NetworkXError
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — silent attribute loss on a documented public-API contract.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, networkx as nx
G = fnx.path_graph(3)  # nodes 0, 1, 2
H = fnx.path_graph(3)  # nodes 0, 1, 2 (overlap)

fnx.union(G, H)
# Returns merged graph silently — node attrs from H may overwrite G silently
# (or be lost entirely depending on order)

nx.union(G, H)
# raises NetworkXError("The node sets of the graphs are not disjoint.\n
# Use `rename` to specify prefixes for the graphs or use
# disjoint_union(G1, G2, ..., GN).")
```

## Root cause
`fnx.union(G, H, rename=())` had no disjoint-nodes guard. The
function went straight to `_raw_union(G, H)` (Rust path) which
silently overwrote attrs on collision. nx's documented contract
requires disjoint node sets and provides a clear error pointing
to `rename` or `disjoint_union` as alternatives.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — silent attribute loss on a public API. Caller intent
matters: if the user wanted to merge with attribute precedence
they should call `compose` (which IS designed for that). `union`
is supposed to fail loudly so callers don't get surprised.

Same defect class as the prior validation-gap cycles (br-r37-c1-
{qmzy2, m4799, mtjlf, z0msu, d22fs}) but on a graph operator
rather than an algorithm.

## Fix
Add `if not set(G).isdisjoint(H): raise NetworkXError(...)` at
the top of the function (after the rename-path early return).
Match nx's exact error message character-for-character (with
the "Use `rename` to specify prefixes / use disjoint_union" hint).

## Tests
1 new lock in `test_review_mode_regression_lock.py::
test_exception_type_parity` covering the overlapping-nodes case.
Existing union test fixtures (disjoint nodes + rename path)
unchanged. 802 existing tests pass.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — sweep
of graph operators (union, disjoint_union, compose, intersection,
symmetric_difference, difference, products, power, ego_graph)
for parity gaps with nx. `union` was the only operator with a
silent-merge defect.
close_reason: Verified fnx.union with overlapping node sets raises NetworkXError with nx-matching wording ('node sets of the graphs are not disjoint'). Earlier fix landed.

title: 20 dispatchable functions still missing backend kwarg surface — sweep followup to br-r37-c1-0z6fh
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — same defect class as br-r37-c1-{spbk, 0z6fh}: dispatch-surface signature divergence on 20 more public-API functions.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx
G = fnx.path_graph(5)
fnx.diameter(G, backend='networkx')
# TypeError: diameter() got an unexpected keyword argument 'backend'
```

20 functions affected (all crash on `backend=...`):
  find_cycle, simple_cycles, diameter, radius, eccentricity,
  average_shortest_path_length, cycle_basis, topological_sort,
  descendants, ancestors, single_source_shortest_path, has_path,
  is_directed_acyclic_graph, is_simple_path,
  minimum_spanning_tree, maximum_spanning_tree,
  is_strongly_connected, strongly_connected_components,
  weakly_connected_components, is_weakly_connected.

## Root cause
nx's `@_dispatchable` decorator adds `*, backend=None,
**backend_kwargs` to every dispatchable function's signature.
fnx's wrappers had this surface on ~40 functions, but ~20 were
missed. Drop-in code that uses nx's documented `backend=...`
kwarg crashes on the missed ones.

br-r37-c1-0z6fh fixed 4 of them; this commit closes the rest.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — same class / severity as the prior 4-function fix.
20× the surface area, so fixing as a bulk retrofit rather than
per-function edits.

## Fix
Bulk module-load-time retrofit: `_bulk_add_backend_dispatch_kwargs`
wraps each missed function with a thin adapter that:
1. Accepts `backend=None` + arbitrary kwargs.
2. Splits unknown kwargs into `backend_kwargs` for validation.
3. Calls `_validate_backend_dispatch_keywords` (raises
   ImportError for unknown backends, TypeError for unexpected
   kwargs).
4. Forwards the rest to the original implementation.

Each wrapper synthesizes a new `inspect.Signature` with
`backend` (KEYWORD_ONLY) and `backend_kwargs` (VAR_KEYWORD)
appended, so signature-introspection parity matches nx exactly.

## Tests
1 new lock in `test_review_mode_regression_lock.py::
test_backend_kwarg_accepted_on_bulk_dispatchable_functions`
covering all 20 functions:
- `inspect.signature` includes `backend` + var-keyword
- Unknown kwargs raise TypeError (validator still active)

606 existing parity / pickle / conversion / IO / view tests
pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — closing
the followup deferred from br-r37-c1-0z6fh. The dispatch-surface
audit on top-level dispatchable functions is now complete.
close_reason: Verified all 20 functions (find_cycle, simple_cycles, diameter, radius, eccentricity, average_shortest_path_length, cycle_basis, topological_sort, descendants, ancestors, single_source_shortest_path, has_path, is_directed_acyclic_graph, is_simple_path, minimum_spanning_tree, maximum_spanning_tree, is_strongly_connected, strongly_connected_components, weakly_connected_components, is_weakly_connected) now expose '*, backend=None, **backend_kwargs' and correctly raise ImportError for unknown backends while accepting backend='networkx'. The bulk retrofit landed before this bead was triaged — confirmed by 20-function parametrized probe (only false positive was find_cycle's expected NetworkXNoCycle on a path graph, which is correct nx behavior, not a backend kwarg gap).

title: [code-review] common_neighbors and non_neighbors are 6-10x slower than nx because of AdjacencyView wrapper
description:
Profiling on BA200:

  common_neighbors:  9.66x slower (15.1µs vs 1.6µs)
  non_neighbors:     6.29x slower (20.5µs vs 3.3µs)

Source: python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:30340 ::common_neighbors uses set(G.adj[u]) & set(G.adj[v]) - {u, v}. nx uses G._adj[u].keys() & G._adj[v].keys() - {u, v} — direct dict access. fnx's G.adj is an AdjacencyView wrapper and G.adj[u] returns AtlasView (per-element PyO3 attribute fetch overhead, same family as br-r37-c1-{lgyq8, 7t95c, 02djy}).

Same fix: when graph has no nx-private-storage and isn't a multigraph, call _GRAPH_NEIGHBORS / _DIGRAPH_NEIGHBORS directly to get a flat list, then build a set. Skip the AdjacencyView entirely.

For non_neighbors: set(graph.adj) - set(graph.adj[node]) - {node} — same pattern. set(graph.adj) iterates the outer view; set(graph.adj[node]) iterates AtlasView for one node. Both can use the raw bindings.

Estimated speedup: ~5-8x based on consistent wrapper-bypass perf wins across find_cliques (lgyq8), square_clustering (7t95c), dominating_set (02djy).

P1 because common_neighbors is a primitive used by jaccard_coefficient, adamic_adar_index, resource_allocation_index (link prediction family) AND any user computing graph similarity. The 10x slowdown propagates.
close_reason: Shipped. common_neighbors and non_neighbors now bypass AdjacencyView via raw _GRAPH_NEIGHBORS / _DIGRAPH_NEIGHBORS for non-multigraph non-private-storage cases. Closes ratios from 9.66x → 3.5-4.0x (common) and 6.29x → 4.0-5.4x (non). Parity bit-exact across BA50-500. 64 tests pass. Speedup propagates to link-prediction family.

title: connected_double_edge_swap silently returns 0 instead of raising on invalid input
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — silent error masking on a public API.

## Reproduction
```python
import networkx as nx, franken_networkx as fnx

# disconnected
G = fnx.Graph(); G.add_edges_from([(1,2),(3,4)])
G_n = nx.Graph(); G_n.add_edges_from([(1,2),(3,4)])
fnx.connected_double_edge_swap(G, nswap=5, seed=42)  # returns 0
nx.connected_double_edge_swap(G_n, nswap=5, seed=42)  # raises NetworkXError("Graph not connected")

# < 4 nodes
fnx.connected_double_edge_swap(fnx.complete_graph(3), nswap=5, seed=42)  # returns 0
nx.connected_double_edge_swap(nx.complete_graph(3), nswap=5, seed=42)
# raises NetworkXError("Graph has fewer than four nodes.")

# empty
fnx.connected_double_edge_swap(fnx.Graph(), nswap=5, seed=42)  # returns 0
nx.connected_double_edge_swap(nx.Graph(), nswap=5, seed=42)
# raises NetworkXPointlessConcept("Connectivity is undefined for the null graph.")
```

## Impact
Callers branching on the exception type to detect invalid input
(common pattern for randomized algorithms with preconditions) silently
get a 0 return instead. The underlying nswap*100 sampling loop spins
the full budget without finding any valid swap candidates and exits
with swaps_done=0.

## Root cause
`python/franken_networkx/__init__.py::connected_double_edge_swap`
omits nx's three preconditions:
- `if not nx.is_connected(G): raise NetworkXError("Graph not connected")`
- `if len(G) < 4: raise NetworkXError("Graph has fewer than four nodes.")`
- empty-graph variant (raised by nx via the is_connected check on an
  empty graph: `NetworkXPointlessConcept`)

## Fix
Add the three preconditions at the top of the function, matching nx's
exact error type and message strings. Existing test
`test_untested_coverage.py::test_connected_double_edge_swap` still
passes (uses cycle5+chord, which is connected and has 5 nodes).

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES on
__init__.py:21725 while comparing fnx algorithm to nx source.
close_reason: Already fixed in 5c968d430 with connected_double_edge_swap precondition guards and regression-lock coverage; verified parity tests pass.

title: [testing-metamorphic] Subgraph views fail graph-class isinstance parity
description:
Found during testing-metamorphic fallback after bv reported actionable=0. Repro: PYTHONPATH=python python3 - <<'PY'
import franken_networkx as fnx, networkx as nx
for lib in (nx, fnx):
    G = lib.path_graph(3)

title: [parity-gap] harmonic_centrality dict iteration order differs from nx
description:
Audit: dict-iteration-order parity sweep across 13 dict-returning recently-touched algorithms. Found one divergence — harmonic_centrality.

nx initializes via 'centrality = {u: 0 for u in nbunch}' where nbunch = set(G.nbunch_iter()), so output dict order is set-iteration order over G's nodes. For small int nodes in CPython (hash(int) == int), this happens to be sorted-like; for str/larger-hashable nodes it's hash-randomized.

fnx's _raw_harmonic_centrality preserves G's insertion order in the output dict.

Repro:
  >>> import networkx as nx, franken_networkx as fnx
  >>> def build(m):
  ...     G = m.Graph()
  ...     for n in [3,1,4,1,5,9,2,6]: G.add_node(n)
  ...     G.add_edges_from([(3,1),(1,4),(4,5),(5,9),(9,2),(2,6)])
  ...     return G
  >>> list(nx.harmonic_centrality(build(nx)).keys())
  [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9]
  >>> list(fnx.harmonic_centrality(build(fnx)).keys())
  [3, 1, 4, 5, 9, 2, 6]

Drop-in code that does e.g. next(iter(harmonic_centrality(G))) to get nx's first-iter node breaks.

Fix: post-process _raw_harmonic_centrality result to iterate via 'set(G.nodes)' so order matches nx exactly. Tagged P3 — code relying on nx's set-iteration order is already brittle (hash-randomized for non-int nodes), but drop-in parity is a stated project goal.
close_reason: Shipped. fnx.harmonic_centrality now re-keys the Rust result through set(G.nodes) to match nx's set-iteration dict order. test_harmonic_centrality_dict_order_matches_nx covers the divergence repro. 74 wider harmonic-centrality tests pass.

title: parity: Graph(numpy_array) / Graph(pandas_df) silently drops edges; nx auto-converts
description: fnx.Graph(numpy.ndarray) and fnx.Graph(pandas.DataFrame) return empty graphs (no edges, no nodes from the matrix). nx.Graph(matrix) auto-detects the type and dispatches to from_numpy_array / from_pandas_adjacency, parsing the matrix as an adjacency matrix. Drop-in code that passes a numpy/pandas matrix to the constructor gets a wrong graph silently. Both fnx.from_numpy_array and fnx.from_pandas_adjacency exist and work; the constructor just doesn't dispatch to them. Fix: extend _init_absorbing_dict_of_dicts to detect numpy.ndarray / pandas.DataFrame inputs and dispatch through the appropriate from_* helper, then copy the result into self.

title: parity: align default-arg sentinels (stoer_wagner heap, capacity_scaling heap, adjacency_data attrs, trophic_* weight)
description: Several fnx wrappers have None defaults where upstream nx uses concrete sentinel values, so default-arg introspection diverges. (1) stoer_wagner(G, weight, heap) — nx default heap=BinaryHeap class, fnx is None. (2) capacity_scaling(G, demand, capacity, weight, heap) — same heap default mismatch. (3) adjacency_data/adjacency_graph attrs — nx default {id: id, key: key} dict, fnx is None (so nx.adjacency_data(G) and fnx.adjacency_data(G) emit different JSON). (4) trophic_levels/trophic_differences/trophic_incoherence_parameter weight — nx default weight=weight, fnx is None (silently ignores edge weights by default). Align defaults; for heap=, accept None and substitute BinaryHeap so the public introspectable default matches nx; for trophic_*, change default to weight. for adjacency_data, default to nx attrs dict.
close_reason: Already fixed in commit 3400846 (re-closing after concurrent agent reverted status to in_progress). 12 parity tests in test_default_arg_sentinel_parity.py freeze the contract.

title: [perf] pagerank scales worse than nx past |V|=1000 (3.3x slower at BA5000)
description:
Per artifacts/perf-baseline-2026-05-03.md (2026-05-03 perf baseline). The perf(pagerank) fix in a04084e0 made fnx pagerank competitive on small graphs but it doesn't scale:

  BA200:  fnx 1.00ms   nx 1.22ms   (0.82x — fnx FASTER)
  BA1000: fnx 5.43ms   nx 4.05ms   (1.34x slower)
  BA5000: fnx 69.9ms   nx 21.1ms   (3.31x slower)

Crossover happens between |V|=200 and |V|=1000. By |V|=5000 fnx is
3.3x slower. Likely root causes (need to profile to narrow):

  1. nx switches to scipy.sparse-based power iteration above some |V|
     threshold; fnx stays on Vec<f64> + HashMap-keyed neighbor lookups.
  2. The Vec<CentralityScore> -> PyDict conversion at the end of
     pagerank() in crates/fnx-python/src/algorithms.rs is O(V) Python
     object creation; for V=5000 with ~70ms total fnx time, that
     conversion alone could be 30-50ms.
  3. The precomputed canonical_out_edges from a04084e0 may have
     suboptimal cache layout at this size (Vec<Vec<(usize, f64)>> —
     each inner Vec is heap-allocated separately, poor locality).

Fix path: profile pagerank on BA5000 with  or pyspy to
identify whether the bottleneck is iteration arithmetic, memory
layout, or PyDict conversion. Address the dominant factor.

Note: this is a regression at scale, NOT a regression vs the
pre-a04084e0 state (which was 0.34x at BA200, getting worse at
larger sizes). The fix improved small graphs but didn't address
scaling.
close_reason: Shipped in 54431019. Native Rust O(|E|) non-finite-weight scan replaces ~42ms Python iteration in the pagerank dispatcher gate. BA200: 0.82x → 2.55x. BA5000: 0.30x → 0.71x (was 3.3x slower than nx, now 1.4x slower). 78 pagerank tests pass; non-numeric weight parity preserved. Remaining BA5000 gap is in the Vec<CentralityScore> → PyDict conversion, not algorithm.

title: fiedler_vector silently returns junk on disconnected graphs; nx raises NetworkXError
description:
fnx.fiedler_vector silently returns a numeric vector for disconnected graphs (with or without self-loops). nx raises NetworkXError('graph is not connected.').

Repro:
  >>> g = fnx.Graph([(1,2),(3,4)])
  >>> fnx.fiedler_vector(g)
  array([-0., -0., -0.70710678, -0.70710678])
  >>> nx.fiedler_vector(nx.Graph([(1,2),(3,4)]))
  NetworkXError: graph is not connected.

  >>> fnx.fiedler_vector(fnx.Graph([(1,1),(2,2)]))
  array([0., 1.])
  >>> nx.fiedler_vector(nx.Graph([(1,1),(2,2)]))
  NetworkXError: graph is not connected.

Drop-in code that does pytest.raises(NetworkXError, match='graph is not connected') won't trigger on fnx — the silent return value is mathematically meaningless (the Fiedler vector is the eigenvector for the second-smallest eigenvalue, and on disconnected graphs the second eigenvalue is 0 so the eigenvector is degenerate).

Sister functions algebraic_connectivity and spectral_ordering already raise correctly on disconnected inputs — only fiedler_vector was the outlier.

Fix: add is_connected(G) guard at the top of fnx.fiedler_vector raising NetworkXError with nx's exact wording.

title: [code-review] _fnx.is_planar binary still returns true for K3,3/Petersen despite d2f5f320 source fix
description:
Audit source: Rust commit d2f5f320 (br-r37-c1-xdjpt) added bipartite + girth-aware bounds to crates/fnx-algorithms::is_planar to catch K3,3 and Petersen. The Rust unit tests test_is_planar_k33_is_non_planar and test_is_planar_petersen_is_non_planar both PASS on rch exec -- cargo test -p fnx-algorithms — confirming the source fix is correct.

But the _fnx.abi3.so binary in the venv has mtime 2026-05-03 19:01, while the source change landed 2026-05-04 17:14. The runtime _fnx.is_planar still returns the broken pre-fix result:

  >>> from franken_networkx import _fnx, _fnx as f
  >>> _fnx.is_planar(_fnx.complete_bipartite_graph(3, 3))
  True   # WRONG — should be False after d2f5f320
  >>> _fnx.is_planar(_fnx.petersen_graph())
  True   # WRONG

The Python wrapper franken_networkx.is_planar already routes around this (delegates to nx.check_planarity), so users of the public API are safe. backend.py registers fnx.is_planar (the wrapper), not _fnx.is_planar, so backend dispatch is also safe.

Impact: callers of _fnx.is_planar directly see wrong answers until the .so is rebuilt + installed. Same class of binary-lag issue as br-r37-c1-hc209 (katz_centrality message) — orthogonal to source correctness, blocked on the build pipeline.

Concrete fix plan:
  1. Add a Python regression-lock test fnx.is_planar(K3,3/Petersen) == False to lock the public-API contract (already correct via the wrapper).
  2. Surface as blocker for whoever owns maturin develop / pip install -e .
close_reason: Added public is_planar K3,3/Petersen regression lock; source planarity tests pass while stale raw _fnx binary remains a rebuild concern.

title: Subgraph view's edges (_FilteredEdgeView) miss __eq__ for self + Set comparison operators
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — public-API parity break on subgraph view edges across all graph classes.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx
G = fnx.path_graph(5)
sg = G.subgraph([0, 1, 2])

sg.edges == sg.edges
# False on fnx (NotImplemented for _FilteredEdgeView, falls through to identity)
# True on nx (Set inheritance)

sg.edges <= G.edges
# TypeError on fnx — `<=` not supported between _FilteredEdgeView instances
# True on nx

sg.edges.isdisjoint(other_set)
# AttributeError on fnx
# True/False on nx
```

## Root cause
`_FilteredEdgeView` (the edges of a subgraph view) had partial Set
coverage:
- `__or__/__and__/__sub__/__xor__`: present (br-filtedgeop fix)
- `__eq__`: handled set/frozenset only, returned NotImplemented for
  another _FilteredEdgeView. Each `sg.edges` access creates a fresh
  instance, so default identity comparison returned False.
- `__le__`, `__lt__`, `__ge__`, `__gt__`: missing entirely.
- `isdisjoint`: missing.

Same defect family as the prior view-equality + set-protocol
cycles (br-r37-c1-{oww5k, k1xn4, 7krwv, 86151, fbtk0, du6d8}) but
on the subgraph-view edge wrapper.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — `H.edges <= G.edges` is documented nx subset-checking
idiom; users analyzing subgraph relationships hit the parity gap.
Same fix shape as the prior wrapper-equality fixes.

## Fix
1. Update `__eq__` to also handle `_FilteredEdgeView` and any
   `collections.abc.Set` (was set/frozenset only).
2. Add `__ne__` (matching pattern from prior fixes).
3. Add `__le__`, `__lt__`, `__ge__`, `__gt__` delegating via
   `set(self) OP set(other)`.
4. Add `isdisjoint` delegating via `set(self).isdisjoint(other)`.

`__hash__ = None` preserved (matches nx's filtered EdgeView, which
is also unhashable).

## Tests
2 new parametrized locks in `test_view_pickle_parity.py::
test_subgraph_view_edges_set_protocol` covering simple Graph and
DiGraph (multigraph case has a separate iter-shape defect deferred
to next cycle — `sg.edges` yields 2-tuples instead of 3-tuples on
MultiDiGraph subgraphs).

768 existing parity / pickle / conversion / attr / regression-lock
tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — extending
the view-protocol audit to subgraph views. The previous cycles
covered the canonical-class views (Graph.edges, DiGraph.edges, etc.)
but the filtered subgraph variant had been missed.
close_reason: Verified _FilteredEdgeView (subgraph view) __eq__ and Set protocol (<=, & set()) work. Earlier fix landed.

title: intersection / difference / symmetric_difference node + edge order drift from nx
description:
fnx.intersection, .difference, .symmetric_difference use the Rust binding's traversal which produces different node and edge iteration order from nx (and different edge tuple direction).

Repro (intersection):
  fg edges = [('a','b'),('b','c'),('c','d')]; fg nodes after sync = [a,b,c,d,e]
  fh edges = [('a','b'),('c','d'),('d','e')]; fh nodes after sync = [a,b,c,d,e]
  fnx.intersection(fg, fh).nodes() -> ['a','b','c','d','e']
  nx.intersection(fg, fh).nodes()  -> ['b','d','c','e','a']
  fnx edges -> [('a','b'),('c','d')]
  nx edges  -> [('b','a'),('d','c')]   <- edge direction also flips

nx implements intersection via set intersection and add_nodes_from(set) / add_edges_from(set), which gives Python-hash-based (but stable, deterministic) order. The Rust binding traverses internal adjacency in a different order.

Drop-in code that iterated R.nodes() or R.edges() of an intersection result drifted. Fix: delegate intersection / difference / symmetric_difference to nx via _call_networkx_for_parity (mirrors articulation_points / cycle_basis / find_cycle pattern).
close_reason: done

title: parity: _fnx_to_nx converter doesn't preserve adjacency-iteration order
description: fnx.G.adj[b] = ['a', 'c'] (matches nx for the same input), but after _fnx_to_nx(G), the converted nx graph has adj[b] = ['c', 'a']. The converter iterates fg.edges (canonical-endpoint form) which feeds add_edges_from with (c,b) instead of (b,c) the user added. nx stores adj in user-call order (asymmetric: add_edge(u,v) puts v in adj[u] first, then u in adj[v]). Converted-via-edges order differs from converted-via-adj-iteration order. This silently breaks BFS/DFS-strategy greedy_color, ego_graph, and any algorithm whose result depends on adj iteration. Fix: rewrite _fnx_to_nx to iterate fg.adj[u] in u's insertion order, matching the user-direct-construction adj order.
close_reason: Fixed in commit f6696a7. _fnx_to_nx now uses per-node-queue topological emit so adj iteration order matches direct nx construction. Self-loops, tuple nodes, and directed graphs all correct. 10 parity tests freeze the contract.

title: [parity-gap] katz_centrality default nonconvergence message wraps message twice
description:
Audit source: commit 8da6d1ac changed the default Rust-backed katz_centrality path to raise PowerIterationFailedConvergence on non-convergence. The class now matches NetworkX, but the PyO3 binding passes a fully formatted message string into NetworkX's PowerIterationFailedConvergence(max_iter) constructor, so NetworkX formats it again.

Repro:
  PYTHONPATH=python python3 - <<'PY'
  import networkx as nx, franken_networkx as fnx
  for mod in (nx, fnx):
      try:
          mod.katz_centrality(mod.complete_graph(20))
      except Exception as exc:
          print(mod.__name__, type(exc).__name__, exc.args[1])
  PY

Observed before fix:
  nx:  power iteration failed to converge within 1000 iterations
  fnx: power iteration failed to converge within power iteration failed to converge within 1000 iterations iterations

Expected: fnx should pass the iteration count into the imported NetworkX exception constructor so args[1] and str(exc) match upstream.
close_reason: Fixed in a7c84f89: PyO3 now passes the raw iteration count to NetworkX's PowerIterationFailedConvergence constructor, and test_review_mode_regression_lock asserts str(exc) and args parity on K20 default non-convergence.

title: parity: 3 more all_pairs_* path functions have wrong outer-key iteration order
description: fnx.all_pairs_bellman_ford_path, fnx.all_pairs_bellman_ford_path_length, and fnx.all_pairs_dijkstra yield outer source keys in arbitrary Rust internal order instead of nx's node-insertion order. Same iteration-order family as br-r37-c1-3dxfn (all_pairs_dijkstra_path). Drop-in code that does 'for source, dists in result: ...' breaks. Fix: iterate via G.nodes() so outer keys come out in node-insertion order.
close_reason: Fixed in commit e702fc7. all_pairs_bellman_ford_path/_length and all_pairs_dijkstra now yield outer keys in node-insertion order matching nx. 9 parity tests freeze the contract.

title: dag_longest_path tie-breaking diverges from nx due to pred-order loss in conversion
description:
fnx.dag_longest_path delegates to nx via _call_networkx_for_parity / _fnx_to_nx, but _fnx_to_nx emits edges via per-node adj iteration (_topo_emit_edges_by_adj) which preserves adj[u] order but scrambles pred[v] order. nx.dag_longest_path's tie-breaking depends on G.pred[v].items() iteration order: max(us, key=lambda x: x[0]) returns the FIRST element with the max key, which is determined by the order of iteration over predecessors.

Repro:
  >>> g = fnx.DiGraph()
  >>> g.add_nodes_from([5,1,3,2,4,6])
  >>> for u,v in [(1,2),(1,3),(2,4),(3,4),(4,5),(4,6)]: g.add_edge(u,v)
  >>> g.pred[4]
  {2: {}, 3: {}}
  >>> fnx.dag_longest_path(g)
  [1, 3, 4, 5]
  >>> nx.dag_longest_path(nx.DiGraph(...same construction...))
  [1, 2, 4, 5]   # tie-break to first-inserted predecessor

After _fnx_to_nx, pred[4] becomes {3:{}, 2:{}} — scrambled because edges() iterates by source-node-order (which puts node 3 before 2 in this case, since the user added [5,1,3,2,4,6] so adj iteration yields 3's edge before 2's).

Fix: implement dag_longest_path natively in fnx using fnx.pred directly, mirroring nx's algorithm but skipping the conversion. This is faster too.

title: [code-review] _link_prediction_lazy_delegate generator-protocol safety untested
description:
br-r37-c1-8e60l shipped _link_prediction_lazy_delegate as a generator-wrapper helper used by 4 link-prediction functions. Functional + metamorphic + golden coverage exists. Missing: direct test that the generator properly handles mid-iteration close().

Risk: if a user calls fnx.jaccard_coefficient(G), iterates partway via next(), then drops the generator OR explicitly calls .close(), the inner _call_networkx_for_parity generator must also close cleanly (via Python's GeneratorExit propagation through yield from). A regression that wraps the inner call in something that catches GeneratorExit could silently leak the inner generator (delaying GC and holding a graph copy).

Concrete fix plan: add a unit test that:
  1. Calls fnx.jaccard_coefficient(G) and verifies isinstance(result, types.GeneratorType).
  2. Calls next() once, verifies a 3-tuple (u, v, score).
  3. Calls .close() on the generator.
  4. Calls next() again, expects StopIteration (generator exhausted via close).

Same pattern test for adamic_adar / preferential_attachment / resource_allocation. 4 quick tests.

P1 because the lazy-delegate is shipped at scale (4 funcs) and a future yield-from refactor that breaks GeneratorExit propagation would silently leak inner generators across the entire link-prediction surface.
close_reason: Shipped. test_link_prediction_lazy_generator_protocol parametrized over 4 link-prediction functions. Each verifies isinstance(GeneratorType), next() yields 3-tuple, close() + next() → StopIteration. 4/4 pass — locks the generator protocol against regressions in _link_prediction_lazy_delegate that would silently leak inner generators.

title: [parity-gap] wiener_index returns float on integer-valued path lengths; nx returns int
description:
fnx.wiener_index returns float when the sum of all-pairs shortest path distances is an integer (typical case for unweighted graphs). nx returns int.

Repro:
  >>> fnx.wiener_index(fnx.DiGraph([(0,1),(1,2),(2,0)]))
  9.0
  >>> nx.wiener_index(nx.DiGraph([(0,1),(1,2),(2,0)]))
  9

Type mismatch breaks drop-in code asserting isinstance(result, int). Same family as br-r37-c1-bctxc (preferential_attachment) and br-r37-c1-4jnwn (transitivity).

Fix: in the Python wrapper, coerce f64 result to int when result.is_integer().
close_reason: Shipped. fnx.wiener_index now coerces directed-graph integral f64 result to int matching nx (was returning float). Undirected case unchanged (nx also returns float there). 382 tests pass.

(2) resource_allocation_index returns -0.0 instead of nx's 0 (also pair order differs). (3) adamic_adar_index returns -0.0 instead of nx's 0. Drop-in code matching exact tuples breaks. Fix: delegate all three to nx for pair-order + type parity (Rust impl is just a small score computation per pair, no real perf benefit).
