title: [code-review] volume fast path uses per-node G.degree(v) calls — materializing the degree dict once is 4x faster
description:
br-r37-c1-ay2no's volume fast path uses sum(G.degree(v) for v in S). Profiling on BA200 (|S|=100) shows per-node access takes 133µs; materializing the full degree dict via dict(G.degree()) once and then summing is 32µs (4.1x faster).

Mechanism: each G.degree(v) call goes through the DegreeView wrapper which does per-call wrapper bookkeeping (similar to the AtlasView overhead I've been tracking). Calling dict(G.degree()) once amortizes the wrapper cost across all nodes via a single batched iteration.

For sparse subsets (|S| << |V|), per-node access could in theory win, but the per-call wrapper overhead is so high that batched materialization wins even at |S| = |V|/2.

Concrete fix: replace sum(G.degree(v) for v in S) with deg = dict(G.degree()); return sum(deg[v] for v in S).

Bench (BA200 m=3, |S|=100, 1000 iter):
  per-node:     133.2 µs (current after ay2no)
  dict cache:    32.4 µs
  nx baseline:   15.9 µs

This closes from 7.75x slower to ~2x slower vs nx.

P1 because volume is in the hot path of cut_size, normalized_cut_size, edge_expansion, mixing_expansion (recall br-r37-c1-ay2no's note); the 4x compounding speedup propagates.
close_reason: Shipped. volume fast path now materializes dict(G.degree()) once instead of per-node G.degree(v) — 4x faster on the inner loop. Closes ratio from 4-8x slower (post-ay2no) to 1.5-2.3x. Total speedup since original slow path: 50-100x. 22 tests pass; self-loop semantic preserved.

title: second_order_centrality silently returns dict on empty/disconnected; nx raises NetworkXException
[parity-gap] katz_centrality silently returns un-converged values; nx raises PowerIterationFailedConvergence
description:
fnx.katz_centrality runs power iteration up to KATZ_DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS (1000) and falls through the loop if convergence isn't reached, returning the un-converged values normalized. nx.katz_centrality raises PowerIterationFailedConvergence(max_iter) in that case.

Repro on BA200, default alpha=0.1, max_iter=1000:
  fnx.katz_centrality(G) → succeeds with normalized but un-converged values
  nx.katz_centrality(G_nx) → raises PowerIterationFailedConvergence

Bug location: crates/fnx-algorithms/src/lib.rs:2442-2473 — power iteration loop has no convergence-failure exit. After KATZ_DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS, the loop ends and the function continues to normalization + return.

Fix: add a convergence flag; if loop ends without delta < tolerance, return Result::Err so the PyO3 binding can raise PowerIterationFailedConvergence matching nx's contract.

Audit-found 2026-05-03 during review-mode pass.

title: BFS/DFS traversals raise OverflowError on negative depth_limit/cutoff — nx returns empty result
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — exception type divergence on documented public-API edge cases. Same defect class as br-r37-c1-w1smc (descendants_at_distance), on three sibling traversal functions.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, networkx as nx
G = fnx.path_graph(5)

list(fnx.bfs_edges(G, 0, depth_limit=-1))
# OverflowError: can't convert negative int to unsigned
list(nx.bfs_edges(G, 0, depth_limit=-1))
# []  ← empty, no edges traversed at "negative depth"

fnx.dfs_tree(G, 0, depth_limit=-1)
# OverflowError
nx.dfs_tree(G, 0, depth_limit=-1)
# DiGraph with [0, 1]

fnx.single_source_shortest_path(G, 0, cutoff=-1)
# OverflowError
nx.single_source_shortest_path(G, 0, cutoff=-1)
# {0: [0]}
```

## Root cause
The Rust bindings (`_bfs_edges_raw`, `_dfs_tree_raw`,
`_raw_single_source_shortest_path`) declare `depth_limit` /
`cutoff` as unsigned int. PyO3 raises OverflowError on negative
ints. nx walks `range(depth)` / while-loop which trivially yields
nothing on negatives — returning empty / source-only results.

Defensive code that treats "no traversal at this depth" as a
valid empty / source-only result silently broke on fnx.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — same defect class as br-r37-c1-w1smc; sibling
traversal functions with the same Rust-side unsigned-int
constraint.

## Fix
Pre-validate `depth_limit` / `cutoff` at each Python wrapper:
- `bfs_edges`: short-circuit to empty generator on negative depth.
- `dfs_tree`: coerce negative to 0 (Rust accepts; nx returns the
  same 2-node tree for both -1 and 0).
- `single_source_shortest_path`: coerce negative cutoff to 0
  (returns {source: [source]} matching nx).

## Tests
1 new lock in `test_review_mode_regression_lock.py::
test_traversal_negative_depth_or_cutoff_matches_nx` covering all
three functions on negative depth/cutoff inputs. 608 existing
parity / pickle / conversion / IO / view tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES sweep —
extending the prior `descendants_at_distance` fix
(br-r37-c1-w1smc) to sibling traversal functions with the same
underlying Rust-side defect.
close_reason: Verified all 3 traversals (bfs_edges/dfs_tree/single_source_shortest_path) accept negative depth_limit/cutoff and return nx-equivalent empty/single-source results without OverflowError. No code change needed — earlier fix already landed.

title: laplacian_matrix returns float64 instead of int64 for unweighted graphs
description:
fnx.laplacian_matrix returns a float64 sparse array even when the graph is unweighted (no edge weights). nx returns int64 in that case (matches the int dtype of nx.to_scipy_sparse_array on a weight-less graph).

Repro:
  >>> g = fnx.Graph([(1,2),(2,3)])
  >>> fnx.laplacian_matrix(g).toarray().dtype
  dtype('float64')
  >>> nx.laplacian_matrix(nx.Graph([(1,2),(2,3)])).toarray().dtype
  dtype('int64')

The values agree element-wise, but downstream code that sizes buffers based on dtype, exports to formats with int constraints (e.g., GraphBLAS bool/int variants), or just uses np.array_equal across libraries gets a divergence.

Root cause: python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:12674 forces dtype=float on the diags_array call:
    D = scipy.sparse.diags_array(
        np.asarray(A.sum(axis=1)).flatten(), dtype=float
    )

nx (lib/python/networkx/linalg/laplacianmatrix.py) uses dia_array without forcing dtype, so D inherits A's dtype.

Fix: drop the dtype= kwarg so D's dtype is inferred from the input vector, which itself derives from the sparse-array sum (same dtype as A).

title: _LiveMultiEdgeDataView dict-subclass silently swallows __setitem__/clear/update/etc. — silent data loss
description:
[HIGH] Severity — silent data loss on a public-API path. Found via /cross-review of peer commit fed1a94e.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx
M = fnx.MultiGraph([(0, 1, {"w": 1})])
view = fnx.to_dict_of_dicts(M, nodelist=[0, 1])[0][1]

view["new_key"] = {"fake": "attrs"}    # SILENT — no error
view                                   # {0: {"w": 1}}  ← assignment vanished
M[0][1]                                # {0: {"w": 1}}  ← graph unchanged
```

The assignment vanished into oblivion: stored in the inherited
(always-empty) dict's underlying storage, but every read method
(`__iter__`, `__len__`, `keys/values/items`, `__getitem__`, `__contains__`)
delegates to `_current()` (the live graph view), so the assignment
is invisible AND the graph is never updated.

Eight mutation methods exhibited this defect:
`__setitem__`, `__delitem__`, `clear`, `pop`, `popitem`, `setdefault`,
`update`, `__ior__`.

By contrast, nx's `AtlasView` raises `TypeError("'AtlasView' object does
not support item assignment")` on the same operations.

## Root cause
br-r37-c1-etbv4 (peer fed1a94e, 19:55 ET) changed
`_LiveMultiEdgeDataView` from `Mapping` → `dict` to make
`isinstance(view, dict)` return True (which DID restore nx parity for
type-checks — that part is correct). But `dict.__init__` allocated
the inherited storage, and the override didn't disable mutation
methods, so they wrote to the inherited slot that nothing reads.

## Severity rationale
Silent data loss on a public-API path is [HIGH] — worse than the
isinstance divergence the prior commit fixed. A user round-tripping
`to_dict_of_dicts → mutate → from_dict_of_dicts` (a documented usage
pattern in nx examples) would silently lose every modification.

## Fix
Override the 8 mutation methods to raise TypeError matching nx's
AtlasView contract. Read paths unchanged. Live-tracking via graph
mutation still works (verified). isinstance/equality/copy/pickle
still work (verified — 11 read locks pass).

Lock added in test_conversion.py::TestDictOfDicts::
test_multigraph_view_mutation_raises_typeerror — parametrized over
all 8 mutation methods.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 CROSS-REVIEW: applying the
"is the abstraction earning its keep?" lens to the fresh peer
commit, I noticed the dict-subclass made `view['k']=val` SYNTAX
type-correct but couldn't actually have semantics — the inherited
storage isn't connected to the live data path. Test confirmed.
close_reason: Already fixed in current tree: _LiveMultiEdgeDataView mutation methods raise TypeError; focused mutation guard tests pass.

title: descendants_at_distance raises OverflowError/TypeError on degenerate distance — nx returns empty set
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — exception type divergence on a documented public-API edge case.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, networkx as nx
G = fnx.path_graph(5)

fnx.descendants_at_distance(G, 0, -1)
# OverflowError: can't convert negative int to unsigned
nx.descendants_at_distance(G, 0, -1)
# set()  ← empty, no nodes at "distance -1"

fnx.descendants_at_distance(G, 0, "foo")
# TypeError: argument 'distance': 'str' object cannot be interpreted as an integer
nx.descendants_at_distance(G, 0, "foo")
# set()
```

## Root cause
The Rust binding `_raw_descendants_at_distance` declares `distance`
as an unsigned int. Negative ints produce OverflowError in PyO3's
type conversion; non-int values produce TypeError. nx's
implementation walks `range(distance)` (or while-loop) which
trivially yields nothing for non-positive or non-int distances —
returning `set()` silently.

Defensive code that treats "no nodes at this distance" as a valid
empty result (a common pattern for distance-bounded queries that
might have invalid distance values from user input) silently broke
on fnx — got an exception instead of empty set.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — exception class divergence on a documented public API.
Same defect class as the prior validation-gap cycles (br-r37-c1-
{ea7eh, qmzy2, m4799}); silent-shape divergence rather than
silent-merge.

## Fix
Pre-validate the `distance` argument at the Python wrapper layer:
- Try `int(distance)`. If it fails (TypeError/ValueError), return
  `set()` — matches nx's degenerate-empty contract.
- If the int is negative, return `set()` — same.
- Otherwise pass the validated int to the Rust binding.
- Source-not-in-graph still raises `NetworkXError` (preserved).
- Unhashable source still raises `NetworkXError` (preserved).

## Tests
1 new lock in `test_review_mode_regression_lock.py::
test_descendants_at_distance_degenerate_distance_returns_empty`
covering negative ints, non-int strings, valid distance, and
missing-source error path.

607 existing parity / pickle / conversion / IO / view tests pass
unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — sweep
of BFS / DFS edge cases found this in
`descendants_at_distance(G, src, distance)`. Prior cycles audited
the more-common path/cycle traversal functions; this completes the
distance-bounded query family.

title: edges nbunch with unhashable element raises TypeError vs nx NetworkXError
G.edges.data() EdgeDataView crashes pickle on Graph — wrapper_descriptor class shadowing
description:
[MEDIUM] Severity — public-API serialization break on the documented `G.edges.data()` idiom for Graph.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, pickle
G = fnx.Graph([(0, 1, {"w": 5})])
edv = G.edges.data()
pickle.dumps(edv)
# PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'franken_networkx.EdgeView'>:
# attribute lookup EdgeView on franken_networkx failed
```

Affects Graph specifically. DiGraph/MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph all
return `list` / `_EdgeListWithSetAlgebra` from `.edges.data()`,
which pickle as their built-in types and therefore work.

## Root cause
`EdgeDataView.__init__` stores `self._call`, a wrapper_descriptor
on the Rust EdgeView type:
`<slot wrapper '__call__' of 'franken_networkx.EdgeView' objects>`.

When pickle serializes the EdgeDataView, it tries to serialize the
wrapper_descriptor. Pickle's qualname lookup for
`franken_networkx.EdgeView` finds the Python-side EdgeView wrapper
(or fails to resolve) — either way, the lookup gets a different
class object than the Rust `_EDGE_VIEW_TYPE` that actually owns
the descriptor. PicklingError.

Same class-shadowing defect family as br-r37-c1-{cip5m, k66wf,
neb6c, 2vxhk, ld4oo, 8crof}. The earlier br-r37-c1-8crof fix
closed the same gap on `NodeDataView`; this commit closes the
parallel `EdgeDataView` gap.

## Severity rationale
[MEDIUM] — `G.edges.data()` is documented nx idiom for iterating
edges-with-attrs; affects Graph specifically (the most common
graph class). Caching / dask / joblib / multiprocessing all crash
on serialization.

## Fix
Add `__reduce__` to `EdgeDataView` that snapshots the materialized
list. Restored value is a plain list (matches nx's snapshot
semantics). Same fix shape as br-r37-c1-8crof on NodeDataView.

## Tests
12 new parametrized locks in `test_view_pickle_parity.py`:
- 4 pickle roundtrip locks (one per graph class)
- 4 .data='attr' variant pickle locks
- 4 deepcopy locks

790 existing parity / pickle / conversion / attr / regression-lock
tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — extending
the wrapper-descriptor pickle audit to EdgeDataView. The earlier
br-r37-c1-8crof fix closed the parallel gap on NodeDataView; this
completes the audit on the *DataView family.

title: [parity-gap] diameter/radius delegate directed graphs to nx, _raw_* mishandles antiparallel directions
description:
Audit source: python/franken_networkx/__init__.py::diameter (line 5233) and ::radius (line 5266). Same defensive 'or G.is_directed(): _call_networkx_for_parity' guard as br-r37-c1-89n9d (center/periphery), but with an additional twist — the underlying Rust _raw_diameter / _raw_radius produce WRONG values on directed graphs because they call gr.undirected() before computing.

Repro:
  >>> from franken_networkx._fnx import diameter as raw_diam
  >>> import franken_networkx as fnx
  >>> G = fnx.DiGraph([(i,(i+1)%5) for i in range(5)])
  >>> raw_diam(G)
  2   # WRONG — should be 4 (length of the directed path around the cycle)
  >>> import networkx as nx
  >>> nx.diameter(nx.DiGraph([(i,(i+1)%5) for i in range(5)]))
  4

Same shape as harmonic_diameter's documented 'directed-collapse defect' (same family as eccentricity, is_eulerian, is_tree, core_number — all fixed previously). The Python wrapper currently masks this by routing directed graphs to nx, paying the fnx_to_nx graph-conversion cost on every directed-graph diameter/radius call.

Fix plan:
  1. For undirected (the original fast Rust path stays): _raw_diameter / _raw_radius.
  2. For directed: reuse fnx.eccentricity (already directed-aware, fast Rust path), then take max for diameter / min for radius.
  3. Other-args delegation (e=, usebounds, weight=) stays unchanged.

This avoids the fnx_to_nx graph-conversion overhead on every directed-graph call AND keeps the undirected fast path. Verified bit-exact against nx 3.6.1 on directed cycle5, directed K5, directed cycle3+chord — diameter and radius all match.

P1 because directed-graph callers of fnx.diameter / fnx.radius pay the round-trip cost on every call; affects every directed-graph user.

title: [code-review] crates/fnx-algorithms is_planar returns true for non-planar K3,3 and Petersen
description:
Source: crates/fnx-algorithms/src/lib.rs:18878 ::is_planar. The function is documented as a planarity check (used by backend.py 'is_planar' dispatch and via _fnx.is_planar) but only verifies the necessary-but-not-sufficient Euler bound |E| <= 3|V| - 6 plus the same bound applied to each biconnected component.

Result: returns true for K3,3 (n=6, m=9, bound 3n-6=12 ✓) and the Petersen graph (n=10, m=15, bound 24 ✓), both of which are non-planar. The Python wrapper franken_networkx.is_planar workarounds this by delegating to networkx's check_planarity, but any direct caller of the Rust function or the backend.py dispatch sees the buggy result.

Repro:
  PYTHONPATH=python python3 -c "
  from franken_networkx import _fnx
  print('K3,3:', _fnx.is_planar(_fnx.complete_bipartite_graph(3,3)))  # → True (WRONG)
  "

Concrete fix plan (this tick):
  1. Add the bipartite-aware bound m <= 2n - 4 (Kuratowski for bipartite graphs); catches K3,3 directly.
  2. Add girth-aware bound m <= (g / (g - 2)) * (n - 2) for graphs with girth g >= 4; catches Petersen (girth=5, bound=13.33 < m=15).
  3. Tighten doc comment: stop claiming this is a full planarity check; rename internally to clarify, OR (preferred) add the stronger bounds and keep the public name with an honest doc.

Both bounds are polynomial-time, mathematically rigorous, and necessary conditions. Still not sufficient (full LR planarity testing requires Hopcroft-Tarjan or Boyer-Myrvold which is ~1000+ LOC), but raises the false-positive rate dramatically and catches the 2 known repro cases.

Tagged P1 because backend.py routes through this function and any user invoking it via fnx.backend gets wrong answers on common non-planar graphs.
close_reason: Shipped in d2f5f320. Rust crate is_planar now applies two additional necessary conditions per biconnected component: bipartite BCC → m <= 2n-4 (catches K3,3 with m=9 vs bound 8) and girth-aware m <= g/(g-2)*(n-2) (catches Petersen with girth 5, m=15 vs bound 13.33). Helpers added: bcc_to_adjacency, bcc_is_bipartite, bcc_girth — all polynomial-time and mathematically rigorous as Kuratowski-style necessary conditions. Tests for K3,3, Petersen, K4, C6 all pass on rch exec -- cargo test -p fnx-algorithms. 407 wider Python planar tests still pass. Not full LR planarity testing (graphs needing Hopcroft-Tarjan still slip through) but catches the canonical Kuratowski-pair cases the bead flagged.

Repro:

  fnx -> [4, 3, 2, 1, 0]

title: [code-review] selfloop_edges/number_of_selfloops fast path has no nx-independent regression-lock
description:
br-r37-c1-61okz shipped a 5-6x perf fix for selfloop_edges and number_of_selfloops. Functional tests verify nx parity. Missing: nx-independent regression-lock for the contract.

A future regression that subtly broke the multigraph FALLBACK path (which the new fast path doesn't exercise — multigraph hits the original AdjacencyView walk) would only surface on multigraph fixtures. Same for the directed path, the empty-graph path, and the parallel-self-loops case.

Concrete known-result fixtures that lock both fast and fallback paths:
  K5 (undirected): no self-loops, count=0, edges=[]
  P5 (undirected): no self-loops, count=0, edges=[]
  Graph[(0,0),(0,1),(2,2)]: 2 self-loops, fast path
  Graph[(0,0)]: singleton self-loop, fast path
  DiGraph[(0,0),(0,1),(1,1)]: 2 self-loops, directed fast path
  MultiGraph[(0,0),(0,0),(0,1)]: 2 PARALLEL self-loops, multigraph fallback
    — count is 2 (parallel edges count separately)
    — edges is [(0,0),(0,0)] (yields each parallel edge)

P1 because the fast path branches on graph type/multigraph; a future regression that misroutes the dispatch (e.g. accidentally using fast path on multigraph) would silently undercount parallel self-loops.
close_reason: Shipped. test_selfloop_fast_path_known_results parametrized over 6 hand-derived fixtures (K5/P5 no-loops, undirected 2-loops, singleton, directed 2-loops, MultiGraph parallel) — exercises BOTH the fast path AND the multigraph fallback. 6/6 pass, all expected values derived from graph structure independent of nx.

close_reason: Fixed in commit 64e1627. Graph/DiGraph/MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph now use object's identity-based __eq__ and __hash__ matching nx exactly. set/dict containing graphs now works on fnx. 29 parity tests freeze the contract.

fnx.write_weighted_edgelist(G, BytesIO()) and fnx.write_multiline_adjlist(G, BytesIO()) raise TypeError('expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not BytesIO'). nx accepts file-like objects (BytesIO) for these functions via the @open_file decorator and writes the encoded bytes directly.

Repro:

  >>> g = fnx.Graph([(1, 2, {'weight': 1.5})])
  >>> nx.write_weighted_edgelist(g, io.BytesIO())  # OK, writes b'1 2 1.5\n'

Drop-in code that streams to BytesIO (very common in tests, network handlers, in-memory pipelines) silently breaks.

title: G.nodes crashes pickle on all 4 graph classes — Rust-bound NodeView types lack __reduce__
description:
[HIGH] Severity — public-API serialization break across all four graph classes.

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, pickle
for cls in (fnx.Graph, fnx.DiGraph, fnx.MultiGraph, fnx.MultiDiGraph):
    pickle.dumps(cls().nodes)
    # TypeError: cannot pickle 'franken_networkx.NodeView' object
    # (and DiNodeView, builtins.MultiGraphNodeView, builtins.MultiDiGraphNodeView)
```

nx's `G.nodes` pickles successfully on every graph class.

## Root cause
The four NodeView types are Rust-bound (PyO3) classes:
- `franken_networkx.NodeView` (Graph.nodes)
- `franken_networkx.DiNodeView` (DiGraph.nodes)
- `builtins.MultiGraphNodeView` (MultiGraph.nodes)
- `builtins.MultiDiGraphNodeView` (MultiDiGraph.nodes)

PyO3-bound types ship with no default `__reduce__`, so pickle's
default `object.__reduce_ex__` falls through to "cannot pickle X
object". Same defect class as the previously-fixed Python view
classes (br-r37-c1-{cip5m, k66wf, neb6c, 2vxhk}) but on Rust types
that need a different fix mechanism (Python monkey-patch instead of
class-level `__reduce__`).

## Severity rationale
[HIGH] — `G.nodes` is the most-used public-API view in
NetworkX-shaped code. Any caching layer / dask / joblib /
multiprocessing pipeline that touches `G.nodes` crashes. The Python
sister types (AtlasView/AdjacencyView/MultiAdjacencyView,
_FilteredGraphView, _ConversionGraphViewBase, _LiveMultiEdgeDataView,
_ReverseDirectedView*) were all fixed in earlier cycles of this
audit; the Rust-bound NodeView types were missed because they don't
appear in `grep ^class`.

## Fix
Monkey-patch `__reduce__` onto the four Rust types from the Python
import-time module body. The reconstructor materializes a plain
dict `{node: attrs}` on the restored side — the Rust-bound view
type can't be reconstructed without a Graph reference, but the
restored dict supports the same iteration / indexing / len / `in`-
test protocol as the live NodeView. Live-tracking is lost (matches
nx — the restored NodeView there is also a snapshot).

The same monkey-patch path was already in use for `__call__`
overrides on these types (line 2652-2656), so the technique is
known to work on Rust-bound classes from this codebase.

## Tests
12 new locks added in `test_view_pickle_parity.py`:
- 4 pickle roundtrip locks (one per graph class)
- 4 snapshot-semantics locks (mutation after pickle doesn't propagate)
- 4 deepcopy roundtrip locks
661 existing parity / pickle / conversion / attr / regression-lock
tests pass unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES — completing
the Rust-bound view audit started in earlier cycles. Followup beads
filed for the other Rust-bound view types that also crash pickle:
G.edges (Graph only), G.degree (Graph and DiGraph). Those are
deferred to next cycle since each needs a slightly different snapshot
shape.
close_reason: Fixed by 9b664637; verified NodeView pickle/deepcopy parity locks.

title: to_scipy_sparse_array with nodelist=[] silently returns 0×0 instead of raising
description:
[LOW] Severity — silent zero-output where nx raises, follow-up to br-r37-c1-mtjlf.

## Reproduction
```python
import networkx as nx, franken_networkx as fnx
G = fnx.path_graph(3); G_n = nx.path_graph(3)

fnx.to_scipy_sparse_array(G, nodelist=[])  # 0×0 sparse array (silent)
nx.to_scipy_sparse_array(G_n, nodelist=[])
# raises NetworkXError("nodelist has no nodes")

# Cascades to adjacency_matrix, laplacian_matrix, normalized_laplacian_matrix:
fnx.adjacency_matrix(G, nodelist=[])         # 0×0 silent
fnx.laplacian_matrix(G, nodelist=[])         # 0×0 silent
fnx.normalized_laplacian_matrix(G, nodelist=[])  # 0×0 silent
```

## Root cause
`to_scipy_sparse_array` checks `len(G) == 0` (the prior fix from
br-r37-c1-mtjlf), but never validates that a user-supplied
`nodelist` is non-empty when the graph itself isn't empty. nx places
the check IMMEDIATELY after the empty-graph check at the same
function boundary.

## Impact
Same defect class as br-r37-c1-{qmzy2, m4799, mtjlf}. Specifically,
this is the precondition path that the prior fix missed because
`len(G) == 0` and `len(nodelist) == 0` are independent — a user
intentionally restricting to a subset that happens to be empty
silently gets a zero matrix instead of an error.

## Fix
One-line addition: `if len(nodelist) == 0: raise NetworkXError("nodelist has no nodes")`
right after the `nodelist = list(nodelist)` materialization, BEFORE
the duplicate / missing-node checks (so the message matches nx
exactly when nlen == 0).

Locks added in test_review_mode_regression_lock.py for all 4
cascade points. 450 existing matrix/conversion/parity tests pass
unchanged.

Discovered during REVIEW MODE Tick 14 EXPLORE+FRESH-EYES sweep on
__init__.py — same audit pass that found the prior 4 silent-return
defects this tick.
close_reason: Already fixed in current tree with nodelist=[] NetworkXError guard and matrix-cascade regression locks; test_exception_type_parity passes.

title: parity: geometric_soft_configuration_graph silently ran wrong algorithm (random_geometric_graph instead of S^1/H^2 model)
description: fnx had geometric_soft_configuration_graph(beta=1, n=100, dim=2, pos=None, seed=None) which silently re-routed to random_geometric_graph(n, 0.3) — a completely different model. nx's S^1/H^2 hyperbolic soft configuration model uses signature (*, beta, n=None, gamma=None, mean_degree=None, kappas=None, seed=None) where beta is required. Drop-in callers expecting the documented Krioukov S^1 model got back a uniform random geometric graph (no degree heterogeneity, no hyperbolic structure, wrong density/clustering). Aligned the signature to nx exactly and delegated the implementation to nx so the well-tested upstream algorithm runs end-to-end. 8 parity tests freeze the contract.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 83b29d5. Signature matches nx (keyword-only, beta required) and implementation delegates to nx so the proper S^1/H^2 hyperbolic model runs end-to-end. Returns fnx.Graph for public type contract. 8 parity tests freeze the contract.

title: G.edges and G.degree crash pickle on Graph/DiGraph — Rust EdgeView/DegreeView/DiDegreeView lack __reduce__
description:
[HIGH] Severity — public-API serialization break, followup to br-r37-c1-yu6gl (G.nodes pickle).

## Reproduction
```python
import franken_networkx as fnx, pickle

# All four classes' G.edges and G.degree are documented public API.
pickle.dumps(fnx.Graph().edges)
# TypeError: cannot pickle 'franken_networkx.EdgeView' object

pickle.dumps(fnx.Graph().degree)
# TypeError: cannot pickle 'franken_networkx.DegreeView' object

pickle.dumps(fnx.DiGraph().degree)
# TypeError: cannot pickle 'franken_networkx.DiDegreeView' object
```

nx pickles all of these successfully on every graph class.

## Root cause
Three more Rust-bound view types missing pickle support, all in the
same family as the NodeView fix from the prior cycle:
- `franken_networkx.EdgeView` (Graph.edges)
- `franken_networkx.DegreeView` (Graph.degree, wrapped by `_WeightAwareDegreeView`)
- `franken_networkx.DiDegreeView` (DiGraph.degree, wrapped by `_WeightAwareDegreeView`)

The Python `_WeightAwareDegreeView` wrapper iterates by delegating
to `self._raw` (the Rust DegreeView/DiDegreeView). When pickle walks
the wrapper, it tries to pickle `self._raw` and crashes.

The MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph .edges/.degree types are Python wrappers
that already pickle naturally — those weren't broken.

## Severity rationale
[HIGH] — `G.edges` and `G.degree` are the most-used view APIs after
`G.nodes`. Caching layers, dask, joblib, and multiprocessing
pipelines that touch these views crash on serialization. The prior
NodeView fix (br-r37-c1-yu6gl) closed one of three faces of the
same defect; this closes the remaining two.

## Fix
Two complementary fixes:

1. Add `__reduce__` to `_WeightAwareDegreeView` (the Python wrapper
   for Graph.degree and DiGraph.degree) — snapshot to a list of

title: eigenvector_centrality{,_numpy} silently returns {} on empty graph; nx raises NetworkXPointlessConcept
description:
fnx.eigenvector_centrality(empty_graph) and fnx.eigenvector_centrality_numpy(empty_graph) silently return an empty dict {}. nx raises NetworkXPointlessConcept('cannot compute centrality for the null graph'). Drop-in code that does pytest.raises(NetworkXPointlessConcept) won't trigger on fnx.

Repro:
  >>> fnx.eigenvector_centrality(fnx.Graph())
  {}
  >>> nx.eigenvector_centrality(nx.Graph())
  NetworkXPointlessConcept: cannot compute centrality for the null graph

Survey of other centralities on empty graphs (degree, in_degree, out_degree, closeness, betweenness, harmonic, load, subgraph, communicability_betweenness, information, current_flow_*, pagerank, hits, katz, katz_numpy) all match nx's behavior — only eigenvector_centrality and eigenvector_centrality_numpy are off.

Fix: add explicit empty-graph guard at the top of both wrappers that raises NetworkXPointlessConcept with nx's wording, before falling through to the Rust/numpy implementation that swallows the case.
